entries.name: Commutes of 45 minutes or more
entries.plain: Out of every 100 workers who travel to a workplace, how many usually need 45 minutes or more to get there. People who work from home are not counted. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico: 18.7% in 2020-2024.
entries.definition: Workers 16 and over who did not work from home and whose usual trip to work takes 45 minutes or more, divided by all such workers, times 100. Source: American Community Survey (ACS) table B08303. The top is cells 11 to 13 (45 to 59, 60 to 89 and 90 or more minutes). The bottom is cell 1, all workers who did not work from home.
entries.unit: % of workers 16 and over who did not work from home

coverage.frequency: Five-year windows, labeled by their last year (2010 = 2006-2010, 2024 = 2020-2024). In the 2026-10 snapshot the windows run from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024, so the Analysis tab's Years line reads 2010-2024 and means fifteen windows, not fifteen calendar years. A new window is added when the Census Bureau publishes it and the file is rebuilt.

entries.method: The observatory reads table B08303 for every five-year window from the Census Bureau's summary files: per-sequence files for windows ending 2010 to 2020 and table-based files for windows ending 2021 and later. It keeps the 78 municipio rows and the Puerto Rico row. It adds cells 11, 12 and 13 and divides by cell 1. The margin of error is calculated by the observatory from the published margins of the cells used: margins of summed cells are combined as the square root of the sum of their squares, and the share's margin uses the Census Bureau's formula for a proportion whose numerator is part of its denominator. If that formula would need the square root of a negative number, the observatory uses the Census Bureau's ratio formula instead. Shares are kept to two decimals; the Analysis tab shows one.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B08303 (Travel Time to Work), cells 001 and 011-013; windows from 2006-2010 to the latest published (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab (group Workers and commuting): shade municipalities by
Map, Analysis tab, view 'Job centres and commuting' (jobs per employed resident, 45-minute commutes, jobs)

entries.how_to_read: A value of 19 means that 19 of every 100 workers who travel to work spend 45 minutes or more getting there. In the 2026-10 snapshot, it fell island-wide from 21.8% in 2006-2010 to 18.7% in 2020-2024. The Analysis tab's view 'Job centres and commuting' shades it next to jobs per employed resident. The number after the plus-minus sign (±) is the margin of error: with 90% confidence, the true value lies within that distance of the estimate. The Analysis tab prints it in percentage points, for example ±0.4 pts. The percentage is not printed in the Census Bureau's table; the observatory calculates it from the cells named in the definition. To cite it: 'Share calculated by Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, from US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table B08303 (Travel Time to Work), cells 11 to 13 divided by cell 1, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' To cite the Census Bureau's own numbers, cite the table cells, not the percentage.
caveats: The base differs from the means-of-transportation shares: it leaves out people who worked from home. The two kinds of shares are not directly comparable.

The base is the Census table's workers 16 and over who did not work from home (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,050,989 for Puerto Rico in 2020-2024): the means-of-transportation total minus those who worked from home. It is not the same count as the civilian employed residents in the class-of-worker table (1,150,831 in the same window). Do not multiply this share by 'Employed residents 16+ (ACS)'.

It is the usual travel time reported by the worker. It does not give distance, mode or the workplace. A worker can live in one municipality and work in another; the value belongs to the home municipality.

Small municipalities are less precise. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the margin of error for 2020-2024 runs from ±0.8 to ±8.7 points across the 78 municipalities, and 19 of the 78 are larger than 30% of the estimate (18 with an estimate above zero, plus Vieques, which shows 0.0% (± 1.8 points), a sample result).

The Puerto Rico share is calculated from the Census Bureau's island-wide counts, not averaged from the 78 municipal shares. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the middle (median) municipality has 18.3% for 2020-2024 and the island value is 18.7%.

Neighboring windows share four of their five years of survey responses, so the change from one window to the next mostly reflects one year of new responses. To judge real change, compare windows that do not overlap, for example 2012, 2017 and 2022. In some municipalities one new year can move the value a lot. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Manatí goes from 31.65% (2007-2011) to 23.58% (2008-2012). Do not read a trend from one small municipality.

Different periods side by side. With Year set to Latest, each layer in the view 'Job centres and commuting' uses its own latest period. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the jobs symbols show the 2025 annual average from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW), while the commute-time and jobs-per-employed-resident layers show the 2020-2024 survey window. Check the year chip in the legend.
entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico, 2020-2024: 18.7% (± 0.35 points); 2006-2010: 21.8%. Highest of the 78 municipalities: Naranjito, 41.0% (± 6.7 points). Lowest: Vieques, 0.0% (± 1.8 points).
entries.plain_es: De cada 100 personas trabajadoras que viajan a un lugar de trabajo, cuántas suelen tardar 45 minutos o más en llegar. No se cuentan las personas que trabajan desde la casa. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, Puerto Rico: 18.7% en 2020-2024.
entries.name_es: Viajes al trabajo de 45 minutos o más
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor de 19 significa que 19 de cada 100 personas trabajadoras que se trasladan al trabajo tardan 45 minutos o más en llegar. En el corte de datos 2026-10, bajó en toda la isla de 21.8% en 2006-2010 a 18.7% en 2020-2024. La vista 'Centros de empleo y viaje al trabajo' de la pestaña Análisis lo sombrea junto a los empleos por residente con empleo. El número después del signo más o menos (±) es el margen de error: con 90% de confianza, el valor real está a esa distancia del estimado o menos. La pestaña Análisis lo muestra en puntos porcentuales, por ejemplo, ±0.4 pts. El porcentaje no aparece en la tabla del Negociado del Censo; el observatorio lo calcula a partir de las celdas que se nombran en la definición. Para citarlo: 'Proporción calculada por Foundation for Puerto Rico, Observatorio de Datos de PR, a partir de Negociado del Censo de EE. UU., Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS), estimados de 5 años 2020-2024, tabla B08303 (Travel Time to Work), celdas 11 a 13 divididas entre la celda 1, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' Para citar las cifras propias del Negociado del Censo, cite las celdas de la tabla, no el porcentaje.

entries.name: Employed residents 16+ (ACS)
entries.plain: How many residents aged 16 and over had a job (not counting the armed forces), from the American Community Survey. It counts people where they live and is an estimate for a five-year window. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico: about 1.15 million in 2020-2024.
entries.definition: The civilian employed population 16 years and over, both sexes and all classes of worker (American Community Survey, ACS, table B24080, cell 1). A person is employed if, in the week before answering the survey (the Census Bureau's reference week), they did any work as a paid employee or in their own business, worked 15 hours or more without pay in a family business, or had a job and were temporarily away. Members of the armed forces are not in the table. It is the base of the class-of-worker shares: government, self-employed and nonprofit.

coverage.frequency: Five-year windows, labeled by their last year (2010 = 2006-2010, 2024 = 2020-2024). In the 2026-10 snapshot the windows run from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024, so the Analysis tab's Years line reads 2010-2024 and means fifteen windows, not fifteen calendar years. A new window is added when the Census Bureau publishes it and the file is rebuilt.

entries.method: The observatory reads table B24080 for every five-year window from the Census Bureau's summary files: per-sequence files for windows ending 2010 to 2020 and table-based files for windows ending 2021 and later. It keeps the 78 municipio rows and the Puerto Rico row. The value and its margin of error are the Census Bureau's published ones (cell 1). The observatory also divides the jobs counted by the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) in a year by this count for the five-year window ending that year to get 'jobs per employed resident' (from 2014, the first QCEW year), so the ratio mixes a one-year numerator with a five-year denominator.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B24080 (Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over), cell 001; windows from 2006-2010 to the latest published (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab (group Workers and commuting): size symbols by

entries.how_to_read: It counts people, not jobs: someone with two jobs counts once. It counts where people live, so a resident who works in another municipality counts at home. As a count it mostly shows the size of a place. On the Analysis tab a shaded layer shows it per 1,000 residents by default. That divides by the total population of all ages for the window's last year, not by residents 16 and over, so it is not an employment rate. The number after the plus-minus sign (±) is the margin of error: with 90% confidence, the true value lies within that distance of the estimate. The Analysis tab prints it in people, like the estimate, for example ±1,965. To cite the source number, give the table, the window and the place, for example: 'US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table B24080 (Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over), Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' If you took the number from the observatory, also cite Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory.
caveats: It is a five-year average, not a single year. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 2006-2010 window gives 1,149,431 employed residents for Puerto Rico, 8% more than the observatory's BLS-based employed count for 2010 (labor force minus unemployed, 1,060,969). For 2024 the two are close: 1,150,831 here and 1,152,370 from the BLS-based count. Do not mix the two series in one comparison. For individual municipalities the 2020-2024 survey count runs from 0.66 times (Culebra) to 1.23 times (Utuado) the BLS-based employed count for 2024, so do not use one series for a place and the other for the island.
It is not the number of jobs located in the municipality. For jobs by workplace, see the QCEW series.
Margins grow with the size of the place. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the margin for 2020-2024 runs from ±135 (Culebra, 710 workers) to ±1,965 (San Juan, 133,578 workers).
The island value is the Census Bureau's own island-wide count, not an average. In the 2026-10 snapshot it equals the sum of the 78 municipal counts in every window.

Neighboring windows share four of their five years of survey responses, so the change from one window to the next mostly reflects one year of new responses. To judge real change, compare windows that do not overlap, for example 2012, 2017 and 2022.
entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico: 1,150,831 (± 6,702) in 2020-2024 and 1,149,431 in 2006-2010. Largest of the 78 municipalities in 2020-2024: San Juan, 133,578 (± 1,965). Smallest: Culebra, 710 (± 135).
entries.plain_es: Cuántas personas residentes de 16 años o más tenían empleo (sin contar las fuerzas armadas), según la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad (ACS). Cuenta a las personas donde viven y es un estimado para un periodo de cinco años. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, Puerto Rico: cerca de 1.15 millones en 2020-2024.
entries.name_es: Residentes de 16 años o más con empleo (ACS)
entries.how_to_read_es: Cuenta personas, no empleos: alguien con dos empleos cuenta una vez. Cuenta donde viven las personas, así que un residente que trabaja en otro municipio se cuenta en el suyo. Como conteo, muestra sobre todo el tamaño de un lugar. En la pestaña Análisis, una capa sombreada lo muestra por cada 1,000 residentes de forma predeterminada. Eso divide entre la población total de todas las edades del último año de la ventana, no entre los residentes de 16 años o más, así que no es una tasa de empleo. El número después del signo más o menos (±) es el margen de error: con 90% de confianza, el valor real está a esa distancia del estimado o menos. La pestaña Análisis lo muestra en personas, igual que el estimado, por ejemplo, ±1,965. Para citar el número de la fuente, indique la tabla, la ventana y el lugar, por ejemplo: 'Negociado del Censo de EE. UU., Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS), estimados de 5 años 2020-2024, tabla B24080 (Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over), Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' Si tomó el número del observatorio, cite también Foundation for Puerto Rico, Observatorio de Datos de PR.

entries.name: Residents working for government
entries.plain: Out of every 100 employed residents aged 16 and over, how many work for a local, Commonwealth or federal government. It counts where people live, not where the government office is. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico: 18.4% in 2020-2024.
entries.definition: Government workers divided by all employed civilian residents 16 and over, times 100. Source: American Community Survey (ACS) table B24080. The top adds local government workers (cells 7 and 17), state government workers (cells 8 and 18; in Puerto Rico, the Commonwealth government) and federal government workers (cells 9 and 19); cells 7 to 9 are for males and cells 17 to 19 for females. The bottom is cell 1, all employed civilians 16 and over.
entries.unit: % of employed civilian residents 16 and over

coverage.frequency: Five-year windows, labeled by their last year (2010 = 2006-2010, 2024 = 2020-2024). In the 2026-10 snapshot the windows run from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024, so the Analysis tab's Years line reads 2010-2024 and means fifteen windows, not fifteen calendar years. A new window is added when the Census Bureau publishes it and the file is rebuilt.

entries.method: The observatory reads table B24080 for every five-year window from the Census Bureau's summary files: per-sequence files for windows ending 2010 to 2020 and table-based files for windows ending 2021 and later. It keeps the 78 municipio rows and the Puerto Rico row. It adds cells 7, 8, 9, 17, 18 and 19 and divides by cell 1. The margin of error is calculated by the observatory from the published margins of the cells used: margins of summed cells are combined as the square root of the sum of their squares, and the share's margin uses the Census Bureau's formula for a proportion whose numerator is part of its denominator. If that formula would need the square root of a negative number, the observatory uses the Census Bureau's ratio formula instead. Shares are kept to two decimals; the Analysis tab shows one.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B24080 (Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over), cells 001, 007-009 and 017-019; windows from 2006-2010 to the latest published (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot).

Related view (it shows the jobs-based government share, not this variable): Map, Analysis tab, view 'Government and self-employment' (government share of jobs and self-employed residents)

entries.how_to_read: A value of 18 means that 18 of every 100 employed residents worked for a government. In the 2026-10 snapshot, it fell island-wide from 25.1% in 2006-2010 to 18.4% in 2020-2024. The Analysis tab does not split local, Commonwealth and federal workers. The number after the plus-minus sign (±) is the margin of error: with 90% confidence, the true value lies within that distance of the estimate. The Analysis tab prints it in percentage points, for example ±0.4 pts. The percentage is not printed in the Census Bureau's table; the observatory calculates it from the cells named in the definition. To cite it: 'Share calculated by Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, from US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table B24080 (Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over), cells 7, 8, 9, 17, 18 and 19 divided by cell 1, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' To cite the Census Bureau's own numbers, cite the table cells, not the percentage.
caveats: It counts residents by where they live, not jobs by where they are. A municipality can host many government jobs and still have a modest share of resident government workers, because workers commute. For government jobs by workplace, see the 'Government share of jobs' series, from the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW).
Government workers are not a share of all adults. The base is employed residents only.

Small municipalities are less precise. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the margin of error for 2020-2024 runs from ±0.9 to ±11.0 points across the 78 municipalities, and 4 of the 78 are larger than 30% of the estimate.

The Puerto Rico share is calculated from the Census Bureau's island-wide counts, not averaged from the 78 municipal shares. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the middle (median) municipality has 19.3% for 2020-2024 and the island value is 18.4%.

Neighboring windows share four of their five years of survey responses, so the change from one window to the next mostly reflects one year of new responses. To judge real change, compare windows that do not overlap, for example 2012, 2017 and 2022. In some municipalities one new year can move the value a lot. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Vieques goes from 32.59% (2015-2019) to 51.97% (2016-2020). Do not read a trend from one small municipality.
entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico, 2020-2024: 18.4% (± 0.3 points); 2006-2010: 25.1%. Highest of the 78 municipalities: Culebra, 42.3% (± 10.4 points). Lowest: Vega Alta, 14.1% (± 2.7 points).

Cuenta donde viven las personas, no donde está la oficina del gobierno. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, Puerto Rico: 18.4% en 2020-2024.

entries.name: Residents working for nonprofits
entries.plain: Out of every 100 employed residents aged 16 and over, how many work for a nonprofit group. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico: 3.5% in 2020-2024. The share is small, so the value for a single municipality is rough.
entries.definition: Private not-for-profit wage and salary workers divided by all employed civilian residents 16 and over, times 100. Source: American Community Survey (ACS) table B24080. The top adds cell 6 (males) and cell 16 (females). The bottom is cell 1, all employed civilians 16 and over. These are employees of organizations that are not run for profit, such as charities, religious groups, and private nonprofit schools and hospitals.

entries.how_to_read: A value of 3 means that 3 of every 100 employed residents worked for a nonprofit. In the 2026-10 snapshot, it fell island-wide from 4.1% in 2006-2010 to 3.5% in 2020-2024. Use it for the island or for large municipalities. The number after the plus-minus sign (±) is the margin of error: with 90% confidence, the true value lies within that distance of the estimate. El número después del signo más o menos (±) es el margen de error: con 90% de confianza, el valor real está a esa distancia del estimado o menos. La pestaña Análisis lo muestra en puntos porcentuales, por ejemplo, ±0.4 pts. El porcentaje no aparece en la tabla del Negociado del Censo; el observatorio lo calcula a partir de las celdas que se nombran en la definición. Para citarlo: 'Proporción calculada por Foundation for Puerto Rico, Observatorio de Datos de PR, a partir de Negociado del Censo de EE. UU., Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS), estimados de 5 años 2020-2024, tabla B08301 (Means of Transportation to Work), celda 19 dividida entre la celda 1, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' Para citar las cifras propias del Negociado del Censo, cite las celdas de la tabla, no el porcentaje.

entries.name: Workers who work from home
entries.plain: Out of every 100 workers aged 16 and over, how many worked from home. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico: 6.1% in 2020-2024, up from 2.2% in 2006-2010.
entries.definition: Workers 16 and over who worked from home, divided by all workers 16 and over, times 100. Source: American Community Survey (ACS) table B08301. The top is cell 21 (labeled 'Worked from home' from the window ending 2019 and 'Worked at home' in earlier windows). The bottom is cell 1.

coverage.frequency: Five-year windows, labeled by their last year (2010 = 2006-2010, 2024 = 2020-2024). In the 2026-10 snapshot the windows run from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024, so the Analysis tab's Years line reads 2010-2024 and means fifteen windows, not fifteen calendar years. A new window is added when the Census Bureau publishes it and the file is rebuilt.

entries.method: The observatory reads table B08301 for every five-year window from the Census Bureau's summary files: per-sequence files for windows ending 2010 to 2020 and table-based files for windows ending 2021 and later. It keeps the 78 municipio rows and the Puerto Rico row. It divides cell 21 by cell 1. The margin of error is calculated by the observatory from the published margins of the cells used: margins of summed cells are combined as the square root of the sum of their squares, and the share's margin uses the Census Bureau's formula for a proportion whose numerator is part of its denominator. If that formula would need the square root of a negative number, the observatory uses the Census Bureau's ratio formula instead. Shares are kept to two decimals; the Analysis tab shows one.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, table B08301 (Means of Transportation to Work), cells 001 and 021; windows from 2006-2010 to the latest published (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot).

view.label: Map, Analysis tab (group Workers and commuting): shade municipalities by

entries.how_to_read: A value of 6 means that 6 of every 100 workers worked from home. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the island share stays between 2.15% and 2.34% in every window from 2006-2010 to 2015-2019, then rises: 3.1% in 2016-2020 and 6.1% in 2020-2024. A five-year window blends earlier and later years, so while the share is rising it lags behind the latest level. The number after the plus-minus sign (±) is the margin of error: with 90% confidence, the true value lies within that distance of the estimate. The Analysis tab prints it in percentage points, for example ±0.4 pts. The percentage is not printed in the Census Bureau's table; the observatory calculates it from the cells named in the definition. To cite it: 'Share calculated by Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, from US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table B08301 (Means of Transportation to Work), cell 21 divided by cell 1, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' To cite the Census Bureau's own numbers, cite the table cells, not the percentage.
caveats: The shares are small in most municipalities, so values are imprecise. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Vieques has the highest value for 2020-2024, 24.0%, with a margin of ± 10.9 points, and three municipalities (Jayuya, Maunabo and Yabucoa) show 0.0%, a sample result and not proof that nobody works from home.

Small municipalities are less precise. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the margin of error for 2020-2024 runs from ±0.1 to ±10.9 points across the 78 municipalities, and 59 of the 78 are larger than 30% of the estimate (56 with an estimate above zero, plus the 3 that show 0.0%).

The base is the Census table's 'workers 16 and over': people who worked at some time in the reference week, according to the Census Bureau's subject definitions (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,119,495 for Puerto Rico in 2020-2024). The class-of-worker table counts all civilian employed people, including those with a job who were temporarily away (1,150,831 in the same window). Do not multiply this share by 'Employed residents 16+ (ACS)'.
Workers who worked from home are also in the base of the other means-of-transportation shares (drive alone, public transportation, walk), but not in the base of the commute-time share.

The Puerto Rico share is calculated from the Census Bureau's island-wide counts, not averaged from the 78 municipal shares. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the middle (median) municipality has 4.4% for 2020-2024 and the island value is 6.1%.

Neighboring windows share four of their five years of survey responses, so the change from one window to the next mostly reflects one year of new responses. To judge real change, compare windows that do not overlap, for example 2012, 2017 and 2022. In some municipalities one new year can move the value a lot. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Vieques goes from 6.53% (2015-2019) to 17.54% (2016-2020). Do not read a trend from one small municipality.
entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Puerto Rico, 2020-2024: 6.1% (± 0.2 points); 2006-2010: 2.2%. Highest of the 78 municipalities: Vieques, 24.0% (± 10.9 points). Lowest: Jayuya, 0.0% (± 0.6 points).
entries.plain_es: De cada 100 personas trabajadoras de 16 años o más, cuántas trabajaron desde la casa. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, Puerto Rico: 6.1% en 2020-2024, más que el 2.2% de 2006-2010.
entries.name_es: Personas que trabajan desde el hogar
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor de 6 significa que 6 de cada 100 personas trabajadoras trabajaban desde el hogar. En el corte de datos 2026-10, la proporción de la isla se mantiene entre 2.15% y 2.34% en todas las ventanas de 2006-2010 a 2015-2019, y luego sube: 3.1% en 2016-2020 y 6.1% en 2020-2024. Una ventana de cinco años mezcla años anteriores y posteriores, así que, mientras la proporción sube, se queda por detrás del nivel más reciente. El número después del signo más o menos (±) es el margen de error: con 90% de confianza, el valor real está a esa distancia del estimado o menos. La pestaña Análisis lo muestra en puntos porcentuales, por ejemplo, ±0.4 pts. El porcentaje no aparece en la tabla del Negociado del Censo; el observatorio lo calcula a partir de las celdas que se nombran en la definición. Para citarlo: 'Proporción calculada por Foundation for Puerto Rico, Observatorio de Datos de PR, a partir de Negociado del Censo de EE. UU., Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS), estimados de 5 años 2020-2024, tabla B08301 (Means of Transportation to Work), celda 21 dividida entre la celda 1, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico.' Para citar las cifras propias del Negociado del Censo, cite las celdas de la tabla, no el porcentaje.

entries.name: Lodging places in the barrio
entries.plain: How many places to stay (hotels, inns, guest houses, resorts, vacation properties and other lodging) have their map pin inside the barrio.
entries.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio (see boundaries.barrio_assets) in the ACCOMMODATIONS category. The category holds these types: Lodging, Hotels, Vacation Properties, Inns, Guest Houses and Resorts.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: build_barrios in landuse.py adds 1 for each counted place whose category is ACCOMMODATIONS.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places, mapped to the observatory's ACCOMMODATIONS category; Census TIGERweb county subdivisions
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see where lodging listings cluster. It counts listings, not rooms or beds. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the island has 1,831 lodging places: Hotels (1,029), Vacation Properties (426), Lodging (234), Inns (70), Guest Houses (36) and Resorts (36). Barrio values run from 0 to 137 and add up to 1,809.
caveats: It is not an inventory of licensed rooms. Listings in Overture may be incomplete or out of date.

These are listings from Overture Maps, not a count of short-term rentals and not an official room inventory. The type Lodging also holds campgrounds, RV parks and other accommodation that the observatory could not classify more closely.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, barrio totals (1,809) are lower than the island count of lodging places (1,831) because 22 lodging places fall in no barrio.
entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares para hospedarse (hoteles, posadas, casas de huéspedes, complejos turísticos, alquileres vacacionales y otros alojamientos) tienen su marcador dentro del barrio.
entries.name_es: Lugares de alojamiento en el barrio
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver dónde se agrupan los listados de alojamiento. Cuenta listados, no habitaciones ni camas. En el corte de datos 2026-10, la isla tiene 1,831 lugares de alojamiento: Hoteles (1,029), Alquileres vacacionales (426), Alojamiento (234), Posadas (70), Casas de huéspedes (36) y Complejos turísticos (36). Los valores por barrio van de 0 a 137 y suman 1,809.

entries.name: Tourism places in a flood hazard area (barrio count)
entries.plain: How many of the barrio's tourism places sit inside an area the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as high flood risk, the area with a 1% chance of flooding in any year.
entries.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio (see boundaries.barrio_assets) whose pin lies inside a polygon of the Federal Emergency Management Agency's National Flood Hazard Layer with SFHA_TF = T. That is a Special Flood Hazard Area: zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and the coastal V zones (VE in the data).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Each place is tested against the flood polygons when places are flagged (point_flags in build.py). Where polygons overlap the Special Flood Hazard Area wins. The barrio adds up the flags.
entries.source_detail: Overture places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%'; Census TIGERweb county subdivisions
entries.how_to_read: A high number means many listed places lie in an area FEMA maps as having a 1% chance of flooding in any year (about 1 in 4 over 30 years). It is not a forecast of when flooding happens, and it says nothing about the building's elevation or insurance. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 150 and add up to 4,216.
caveats: It describes the mapped hazard at the pin, not the building.
Areas outside the mapped flood zones are not necessarily safe; flood maps may be out of date.
Places in zones where FEMA has not determined the hazard, and places outside the mapped polygons, count as not in a flood hazard area.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, barrio totals (4,216) are lower than the municipality total (4,468) because 325 places fall in no barrio. Almost all of those pins are at or just off the coast, where mapped flood zones are common: 252 of the 325 are in a flood hazard area. The barrio counts therefore leave out 5.6% of flood-zone places (252 of 4,468), against 1.3% of all places (325 of 24,209).

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Barrios (click inside a barrio)

entries.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos del barrio están dentro de un área que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca como de alto riesgo de inundación: el área con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos en zona de riesgo de inundación (conteo por barrio)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un número alto significa que muchos lugares listados están en un área que FEMA mapea con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año (alrededor de 1 en 4 en 30 años). No es un pronóstico de cuándo ocurrirá una inundación, y no dice nada sobre la elevación del edificio ni sobre su seguro. En el corte de datos 2026-10, los valores van de 0 a 150 y suman 4,216.

entries.name: Tourism places in the barrio
entries.plain: How many tourism places (restaurants, attractions, lodging and visitor services) have their map pin inside the barrio.
entries.definition: Count of listings in places.json with confidence of 0.50 or more and a type other than Places of Worship whose pin lies inside the barrio polygon. The places are gastronomy, attractions, accommodations and visitor services together.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: See boundaries.barrio_stats. Places come from Overture Maps and carry a confidence score from the source.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Places (in the 2026-10 snapshot, listing update dates run from November 2020 to September 2026); Census TIGERweb county subdivisions
entries.how_to_read: A high count means many listed businesses and sites in that barrio. It does not say how many visitors they receive. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,884 places are counted in a barrio, and the count runs from 0 (24 barrios) to 1,233 (Santurce, San Juan).
caveats: The file calls this field assets. It counts listed places, not financial or physical assets, and only places the observatory classes as gastronomy, attractions, accommodations or visitor services; other businesses are not counted.
Overture coverage is uneven; barrios with few listings may have businesses that are not in the source.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, listings were last updated between November 2020 and September 2026; some businesses may have closed.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places (1.3%) fall in no barrio and are not counted here.
Barrios are different sizes. Compare with places per km².

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Barrios (click inside a barrio)

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos (restaurantes, atracciones, alojamientos y servicios para visitantes) tienen su marcador dentro del barrio.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos en el barrio
entries.how_to_read_es: Un conteo alto significa muchos negocios y sitios listados en ese barrio. No dice cuántos visitantes reciben. En el corte de datos 2026-10, 23,884 lugares se cuentan en algún barrio, y el conteo va de 0 (24 barrios) a 1,233 (Santurce, San Juan).

entries.name: Tourism places per km² (barrio)
entries.plain: Tourism places in the barrio divided by its area in square kilometers. It shows how crowded a barrio is with listed places, whatever its size.
entries.definition: assets divided by km2, using the unrounded area, rounded to 2 decimals.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: build_barrios in landuse.py: round(assets / km2, 2), where km2 is the unrounded polygon area.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places divided by Census-based polygon area
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 322.19 (the barrio Barceloneta, in Barceloneta: 33 places in about 0.1 km²). The highest values are in small barrios. The top five are Barceloneta, Cabo Rojo, Luquillo, Dorado and Quinto (in Ponce); all but Quinto are barrios-pueblo (town centers) in the Census layer. Compare barrios of similar size.
caveats: Very small barrios can show large values from a handful of places.
The area can include some inland water, which lowers the density slightly.

Do not compare it with places per km² in municipalities.json. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the barrio value uses the observatory's polygon area, which can include inland water, and counts only the 23,884 places inside a barrio. The municipality value uses the 2020 Census land area and counts all 24,209 places.
entries.plain_es: Los lugares turísticos del barrio divididos entre su área en kilómetros cuadrados. Muestra qué tan lleno de lugares listados está un barrio, sea cual sea su tamaño.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos por km² (barrio)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, los valores van de 0 a 322.19 (el barrio Barceloneta, en Barceloneta: 33 lugares en unos 0.1 km²). Los valores más altos están en barrios pequeños. Los cinco primeros son Barceloneta, Cabo Rojo, Luquillo, Dorado y Quinto (en Ponce); todos menos Quinto son barrios-pueblo (centros urbanos) en la capa del Censo. Compare barrios de tamaño parecido.

entries.name: Tourism places within 400 m of any mapped stop (barrio count)
entries.plain: How many of the barrio's tourism places have a mapped bus stop, train station or ferry terminal within 400 m (a quarter mile), measured in a straight line. It counts stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped.
entries.definition: Count of tourism places in the barrio whose nearest mapped stop of any kind (transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal) is 400 m or less away in a straight line. Stops come from the ATI timetable feed (the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado), municipal timetable feeds and OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus and rail stations and ferry terminals. Taxi stands, charging stations, airports and helipads do not count. The field transit minus acc_cur400 is the number of the barrio's places within 400 m of a mapped stop but of no stop with a current timetable.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each full build. The nightly transit refresh does not rebuild barrios.geojson.

entries.method: access.py finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind for each place and sets transit_400m when the distance is 400 m or less (see places.transit_400m). build_barrios in landuse.py adds up the flags of the counted places in each barrio.
entries.source_detail: Overture places; ATI and municipal GTFS feeds; OpenStreetMap; Census TIGERweb county subdivisions
entries.how_to_read: A high number means many places are near a mapped stop. It does not say whether buses run often or at useful hours. For places near a stop whose timetable has not ended, see acc_cur400. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 1,218 and add up to 11,429.
caveats: Distance is a straight line, not the walking route.

Stops from expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops still count, so real service may be thinner. In the 2026-10 snapshot 131 barrios have a value above 0 but no place near a stop with a current timetable.
A barrio with no stop in the data shows 0, which can mean no data rather than no service.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, barrio totals (11,429) are lower than the island count (11,507) because 78 places near a mapped stop fall in no barrio. The barrio counts are rebuilt only at a full build; the nightly refresh does not update them.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Barrios (click inside a barrio)

entries.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos del barrio tienen una parada de guagua, estación de tren o terminal de lancha del mapa a 400 m (un cuarto de milla) o menos, medidos en línea recta. Cuenta las paradas cuyo horario ya terminó y las que mapearon personas voluntarias.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos a 400 m o menos de cualquier parada mapeada (conteo por barrio)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un número alto significa que muchos lugares están cerca de una parada mapeada. No dice si las guaguas pasan a menudo ni a horas útiles. Para los lugares cerca de una parada cuyo horario no ha terminado, vea acc_cur400. En el corte de datos 2026-10, los valores van de 0 a 1,218 y suman 11,429.

entries.name: Tourism places in a flood hazard area (%)
entries.plain: Out of every 100 counted tourism places in the municipality, this many sit in a high-risk flood area. The US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps that area with a 1% chance of flooding each year.
entries.definition: in_sfha divided by assets, times 100, rounded to one decimal. The build leaves it empty when a municipality has no counted places. In the 2026-10 snapshot, all 78 have a value, the island share is about 18.5% (4,468 of 24,209, from the municipality counts) and the median municipality is 14.2%.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot; flood polygons downloaded 2026-10-01

entries.method: round(in_sfha / assets x 100, 1) in build.py. Places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50 are excluded from both numbers.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%'.
entries.how_to_read: A high value means many of the municipality's counted places sit in the mapped 1% flood area. This is the share of counted tourism places with a pin in that area. It is not the share of the municipality's land, homes or residents in a flood area. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Salinas (73.7%), Cataño (73.0%), Guayanilla (63.1%), Loíza (54.5%) and Guánica (52.6%) are highest. Florida is 0%. The Municipality tab also ranks municipalities by this share (1 = highest).
caveats: A municipality with few places can swing widely. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Maricao has 36 counted places and 4 in a flood hazard area (11.1%): one more place in the area would raise its share by about 2.4 points, and one more place outside it would lower the share by about 0.3 points. In Salinas (213 places) one place moves the share by about 0.1 to 0.3 points.
It describes the mapped hazard at a point, not the building. It says nothing about elevation, flood-proofing or insurance.
The Municipality tab's 'in flood hazard area' tile is counted live from the places the map shows and follows the filters. The map hover, the shading and the Rankings tab use this stored value.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: shade municipalities by '% of places in flood hazard area'
Map, Rankings tab: rank by '% of places in flood hazard area'
3D view: Columns by municipality, '% of places in flood hazard area'
Map, Municipality tab: tile 'in flood hazard area'

entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Ponce: 540 of 1,041 counted places, so 51.9%.
entries.plain_es: De cada 100 lugares turísticos contados en el municipio, cuántos están en un área de alto riesgo de inundación. FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca esa área con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse cada año.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos en zona de riesgo de inundación (%)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor alto significa que muchos de los lugares contados del municipio están en el área de inundación de 1% mapeada. Es la proporción de lugares turísticos contados cuyo marcador está en esa área. No es la proporción de la tierra, las viviendas ni las personas residentes del municipio que están en un área inundable. En el corte de datos 2026-10, Salinas (73.7%), Cataño (73.0%), Guayanilla (63.1%), Loíza (54.5%) y Guánica (52.6%) tienen los valores más altos. Florida tiene 0%. La pestaña Municipio también ordena los municipios por esta proporción (1 = la más alta).

entries.name: Tourism places in a flood hazard area (count)
entries.plain: How many counted tourism places sit inside an area that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as having a 1% chance of flooding in any year. This is the Special Flood Hazard Area, often called the 100-year floodplain.
entries.definition: Number of the counted places (assets) whose pin (the point where Overture places the listing) lies inside a FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer polygon marked as a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA_TF = 'T'). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). It is a part of in_flood_zone, which also counts the 0.2% area. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 4,468, and the counted places fall in zones A, AE, AO, A99 and VE (AE includes regulatory floodways).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot; flood polygons downloaded 2026-10-01

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test of each place against the FEMA flood polygons, then a count per municipality of the counted places that tested inside. See 'How flood and protected-area exposure is counted' for the rules on overlaps and ignored zones.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF; 4,894 polygons in the layer downloaded 2026-10-01.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Ponce has the most places in a flood hazard area (540), then San Juan (473), Carolina (194) and Cabo Rojo (181). Florida has none: in the FEMA layer the observatory used, one polygon of minimal flood hazard covers all of Florida. Use sfha_pct for the share of a municipality's places.
caveats: It tests the pin only. It says nothing about the building's elevation, floor level, flood-proofing or insurance, or about past flooding.
A 1% annual chance does not mean the area floods once in 100 years. It can flood in any year, and over 30 years the chance is about 26%.

These flags are a screening count from map pins. They are not a flood zone determination for any property: FEMA's metadata names its Flood Insurance Rate Map, database and Flood Insurance Study as the official designation.
It uses FEMA's mapped zones only. Flooding outside them, for example from heavy rain, can still happen.
A pin close to a zone edge can fall on either side, and FEMA revises its maps over time. The 2026-10 snapshot uses the layer downloaded on 1 October 2026.
Large municipalities have more places, so more places in a hazard area. Compare shares, not only counts.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: shade municipalities by 'Places in flood hazard area'
Map, Rankings tab: rank by 'Places in flood hazard area'

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados están dentro de un área que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca con 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año. Es el Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación (SFHA), conocida como la zona inundable de 100 años.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos en zona de riesgo de inundación (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, Ponce tiene la mayor cantidad de lugares en zona de riesgo de inundación (540), seguido de San Juan (473), Carolina (194) y Cabo Rojo (181). Florida no tiene ninguno: en la capa de FEMA que usó el observatorio, un solo polígono de riesgo mínimo de inundación cubre todo Florida. Use sfha_pct para la proporción de los lugares de un municipio.

entries.name: Tourism places in a mapped 1% or 0.2% flood zone (count)
entries.plain: How many counted tourism places sit in the 1% flood area of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) or in its lower-risk 0.2% flood area. It is always at least as large as the count for the 1% area alone.
entries.definition: Number of the counted places whose pin (the point where Overture places the listing) lies inside a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area (the same test as in_sfha) or inside a FEMA polygon whose subtype is '0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD' (a shaded zone X). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). So in_flood_zone equals in_sfha plus the places that are in the 0.2% area only. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 5,668: 4,468 in a Special Flood Hazard Area and 1,200 in the 0.2% area only.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot; flood polygons downloaded 2026-10-01

entries.method: A place gets a flood zone recorded only when its pin is in a Special Flood Hazard Area or in a polygon whose subtype contains '0.2'. The build counts, per municipality, the counted places with a recorded flood zone. Unshaded zone X (minimal hazard) and zone D leave a place with no flood zone. See 'How flood and protected-area exposure is counted'.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places; FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (676), and Florida has none. The difference between this field and in_sfha is the number of places in the 0.2% area only. In that snapshot the two counts are equal in 20 municipalities, because no counted place there lies in the 0.2% area alone. The observatory's maps and rankings do not show this field. It is in the data file and the CSV (comma-separated values) download.
caveats: A 0.2% annual chance area is lower risk than the 1% area, but flooding there is still possible.

entries.name: FEMA flood zone at the place
entries.plain: The flood zone that FEMA (the US Federal Emergency Management Agency) maps at the place's pin. It is shown only when the pin is in a mapped high-risk area (1% annual chance of flooding) or in the 0.2% annual chance area.
entries.definition: The FEMA flood zone code of the flood-map polygon that contains the pin. It is published only for places inside a Special Flood Hazard Area (the zones that occur in the 2026-10 snapshot are A, AE, AO, A99 and VE) or inside the shaded 0.2% annual chance zone (zone X with that subtype). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 7,266 of 32,541 places have one (22.3%).

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the flood polygons of the National Flood Hazard Layer for Puerto Rico, which FEMA publishes. The observatory skips polygons marked open water or area not included (the 2026-10 download has none). When a pin lies in overlapping polygons, a Special Flood Hazard Area wins over the 0.2% zone. Unshaded zone X (minimal hazard) is not recorded. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
entries.source_detail: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, MapServer layer 28 (flood hazard zones), polygons with DFIRM_ID starting with 72 (Puerto Rico); fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY and SFHA_TF.
entries.how_to_read: Zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and VE all mean a 1% chance of flooding in any given year, often called the 100-year flood. A 1% annual chance does not mean one flood every 100 years. It is a 1-in-100 chance each year, and it repeats every year. X with the 0.2% subtype is the 500-year area. A place with no flood zone is in neither mapped area. That does not mean it cannot flood.
caveats: This is the mapped hazard at one point. It does not describe the building, its floor height or its insurance.

Missing means the pin is in no mapped Special Flood Hazard Area or 0.2% annual chance area. It may be in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places in the 2026-10 snapshot), or outside the area FEMA mapped.
FEMA revises its maps. The 2026-10 snapshot used the layer as downloaded on 1 October 2026.
The descriptions in the codes below are plain-language summaries. The FEMA definitions are the reference.
FEMA's printed Flood Insurance Rate Map and Flood Insurance Study are the official designation. This is a database copy and not a flood determination for any property.
The file does not carry the effective date of the flood map at each place. The observatory downloads only the fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF and STATIC_BFE.

entries.name: How a tourism place is assigned to a municipality
entries.group: How places and points are built
entries.plain: A tourism place belongs to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin (the point where Overture places the listing). The town named in the address does not decide. If the pin is outside every boundary, the place goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest.
entries.definition: The build tests each listing's pin (the point where Overture places the listing) against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipality polygons. A pin inside none goes to the municipality whose polygon is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the one with the nearest centre point). The result is the municipality field of places.json and the basis of every municipality count of tourism places. The full steps are in 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Function make_muni_locator in build.py, applied to every place after de-duplication. The steps, the part the address town plays while duplicates are folded, and the counts of pins outside every polygon are in 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps place coordinates; Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k boundaries clipped to the shoreline); centre points from the observatory's list in municipalities.py.
entries.how_to_read: Counts agree with the polygons the map draws. A place counted for San Juan has its pin inside San Juan's boundary unless it was one of the few pins outside every boundary. The town named in a listing's address does not decide: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 863 of the 32,541 listings (2.7%) have an address that names a different municipality from the one their pin falls in. Counts of places by municipality in the observatory all follow the pin.
caveats: A wrong pin in Overture puts a place in the wrong municipality.

The boundaries are clipped to the shoreline, so pins on piers, marinas and beaches can fall outside. They are then assigned to the nearest polygon. The 2026-10 build still assigned them by nearest centre, which can be a different municipality from the one the pin is next to. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most such counted places (51).

The boundary drawn on the map is simplified by about 20 metres (0.0002 degrees) for display, so a place very near a border can look as if it is on the wrong side. The build used the same Census generalized 500k layer before this display simplification.

entries.plain_es: Un lugar turístico pertenece al municipio cuyo límite contiene su marcador en el mapa (el punto donde Overture ubica el listado). El pueblo que aparece en la dirección no decide. Si el marcador está fuera de todos los límites, el lugar se asigna al municipio cuyo límite está más cerca.
entries.name_es: Cómo se asigna un lugar turístico a un municipio
entries.how_to_read_es: Los conteos coinciden con los polígonos que dibuja el mapa. Un lugar contado para San Juan tiene su marcador dentro del límite de San Juan, a menos que fuera uno de los pocos marcadores fuera de todos los límites. El pueblo que aparece en la dirección de un listado no decide: en el corte de datos 2026-10, 863 de los 32,541 listados (2.7%) tienen una dirección que nombra un municipio distinto de aquel en que cae su marcador. Todos los conteos de lugares por municipio del observatorio siguen el marcador.

entries.name: How flood and protected-area exposure is counted
entries.group: How places and points are built
entries.plain: The observatory checks the map point of each counted tourism place against federal flood-zone maps and protected-area maps, then adds up the places that fall inside, for each municipality.
entries.definition: Each counted place's pin (the point where Overture places the listing) is tested against the flood polygons of the US Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) National Flood Hazard Layer and the protected-area polygons of the Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) of the US Geological Survey (USGS). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship. The results are added up for each municipality in four fields: in_sfha (places in a Special Flood Hazard Area, the area with a 1% yearly chance of flooding), in_flood_zone (places in that area or in the 0.2% area), sfha_pct (in_sfha as a percent of counted places) and in_protected (places inside a protected area). The tests are described in 'How flood exposure of a place is flagged' and 'How a place is flagged as inside a protected area'.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot; FEMA and PAD-US layers downloaded 2026-10-01

entries.method: Function point_flags in build.py runs the two point-in-polygon tests for every place. Function municipality_stats in build.py then counts, for each municipality, the counted places with each flag. The rules for overlapping polygons, ignored zones and proclamation boundaries are in the two entries named in the definition.

values.A: FEMA zone in the 1% flood area (Special Flood Hazard Area), with no base flood elevation given. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 210 counted places.
values.AE: Zone in the 1% flood area with base flood elevations. Includes regulatory floodways. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 3,255 counted places, of which 505 in a floodway.
values.AO: Zone in the 1% flood area for shallow flooding that spreads over the ground. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 490 counted places.
values.AH: Zone in the 1% flood area for shallow ponding. The layer downloaded 2026-10-01 holds one such polygon, and no counted place falls in it.
values.A99: Zone in the 1% flood area that FEMA expects a federal flood-protection system under construction to protect. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 68 counted places.
values.VE: Coastal zone in the 1% flood area with extra hazard from storm waves (zone V is not present in the layer downloaded 2026-10-01). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 732 counted places.
values.X, 0.2 PCT ANNUAL CHANCE FLOOD HAZARD: Shaded zone X: area with a 0.2% yearly chance of flooding. Counted in in_flood_zone only. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,309 counted places.
values.X, AREA OF MINIMAL FLOOD HAZARD: Unshaded zone X: minimal flood hazard. Not counted as flood exposure. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 20,491 counted places.
values.D: Possible but undetermined flood hazard: FEMA has not determined the hazard, which is not the same as no hazard. Not counted as flood exposure. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 15 counted places.
values.No FEMA polygon: The pin lies outside every FEMA polygon used in the test. Not counted as flood exposure. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 9 counted places.

entries.source_detail: FEMA NFHL layer 28, DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%', fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF, 4,894 polygons, downloaded 2026-10-01. USGS PAD-US 4.1, Protection Mechanism Category layer, State_Nm = 'PR', 665 polygons, downloaded 2026-10-01. Zone meanings are FEMA's.
entries.how_to_read: The test says whether the pin falls inside a mapped hazard area in the layers downloaded for the snapshot (1 October 2026 for the 2026-10 snapshot). It does not say how likely a particular building is to flood. Read the zone letters in the 'values' list as FEMA defines them and check FEMA's own zone definitions for the exact wording.
caveats: The test uses the pin only. It says nothing about building elevation, floor level, flood-proofing, insurance or past flooding.

The test used the full-detail polygons downloaded from FEMA and USGS. The published flood.geojson and protected.geojson are simplified by about 5 metres (0.00005 degrees) for display, so repeating the test on the published files can give slightly different results for pins near an edge.

The observatory does not store the effective date of any FEMA map (the build keeps only the zone, subtype, Special Flood Hazard Area flag and base flood elevation of each polygon), so the flags can reflect maps older than the snapshot date.
A place with no flood flag is not shown to be safe. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 15 counted places are in zone D and 9 are outside every FEMA polygon; none of them is counted as exposed.
Only FEMA's mapped zones count. Flooding outside them, for example from heavy rain, can still happen.
Only counted places (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) enter the municipality figures. Another filter gives other numbers.
entries.plain_es: El observatorio compara el punto en el mapa de cada lugar turístico contado con los mapas federales de zonas inundables y de áreas protegidas, y luego suma los lugares que caen dentro, por municipio.
entries.name_es: Cómo se cuenta la exposición a inundaciones y a áreas protegidas
entries.how_to_read_es: La prueba indica si el marcador cae dentro de un área de riesgo mapeada en las capas descargadas para el corte de datos (el 1 de octubre de 2026 para el corte de datos 2026-10). No indica qué tan probable es que un edificio en particular se inunde. Lea las letras de las zonas en la lista de 'valores' tal como las define FEMA y revise las definiciones de zonas de la propia FEMA para la redacción exacta.

entries.name: How points, stops and blocks are assigned to a municipality
entries.group: How places and points are built
entries.plain: A tourism place or a transit stop belongs to the municipality whose boundary contains its map point. If the point is outside every boundary, such as on a pier, the municipality whose boundary is nearest takes it. Census blocks and barrios use their Census county code.
entries.definition: The observatory assigns a municipality in four ways, by kind of record. (1) Tourism places and transport features (stops, stations, terminals, airports, taxi stands, electric vehicle (EV) charging points): the full build tests the point against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipio polygons (a generalized 1:500,000 layer, boundaries as of January 1, 2023); a point inside no polygon takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest (muni_locate.py). The published tourism places still carry the earlier rule, the nearest centre point listed in municipalities.py, until the next full build. (2) Scheduled transit stops after a nightly transit refresh: tested against the published municipios.geojson, a simplified copy of the polygons; a stop outside every polygon takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest, as in the full build. (3) Census blocks: the municipality comes from the county code in the block's ID. (4) Barrios: the municipality comes from the county code in the barrio's GEOID, and a tourism place gets its barrio from a point-in-polygon test against the barrio polygons. Only counted places (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) get a barrio, and only when their point falls inside a barrio polygon.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot; transit stops also refreshed nightly

entries.method: Functions make_muni_locator and nearest_muni in build.py; the refresh in refresh_network.py; network.coverage for blocks; build_barrios in landuse.py. The address town in Overture's records is used only while duplicate listings are folded, so that listings in different towns are not merged.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps place coordinates; Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county boundaries (layer 11) and 2020 blocks; transit stops from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and municipal General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) feeds and from OpenStreetMap.
entries.how_to_read: A municipal count agrees with the polygon drawn on the map. A place counted for San Juan has its point inside San Juan's boundary, unless it is one of the few points outside every boundary. The town named in an address does not decide. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 348 of the 32,541 place listings (324 of the 24,209 counted places) lie outside every polygon and took the nearest centre point (the next full build gives them the nearest polygon, which moves 60 listings, 59 of them counted); for all the others the point-in-polygon result is the published municipality. Of the counted places, 23,884 fall inside a barrio polygon and have a barrio.
caveats: A wrong point in the source puts a place in the wrong municipality.

Boundaries are clipped to the shoreline, so points on piers, marinas and beaches can fall outside. They then go to the municipality whose polygon is nearest. Until the 2026-11 fix they went to the nearest centre point, which can be a different municipality from the one the point is next to: it put the Cataño ferry and bus terminals in San Juan. Scheduled stops follow the new rule since that fix, tourism places from the next full build.
The boundary drawn on the map is simplified for display (about 22 metres, 0.0002 degrees), so a place very near a border can look as if it is on the wrong side.

The nightly refresh tests stops against the simplified copy of the boundaries and the full build against the full-detail ones, so a stop within about 22 metres of a border can land in a different municipality in the two. Both give a stop outside every polygon the municipality whose polygon is nearest. Until the 2026-10 access update the nightly refresh left such a stop without a municipality.
entries.plain_es: Un lugar turístico o una parada de transporte colectivo pertenece al municipio cuyo límite contiene su punto en el mapa. Si el punto queda fuera de todos los límites, como en un muelle, se le asigna al municipio cuyo límite está más cerca. Los bloques censales y los barrios usan su código de condado del Censo.
entries.name_es: Cómo se asignan a un municipio los puntos, las paradas y los bloques

entries.name: Which places each municipality count includes
entries.group: How places and points are built
entries.plain: Three counts describe the tourism listings in a municipality. They differ only in whether places of worship and low-confidence listings are included. The default, assets, leaves out both.
entries.definition: All counts start from the same list: Overture listings that fell into the observatory's four tourism categories, after de-duplication, without the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services; since 2026-10-18). listings_all counts every one of them (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot). assets_all_confidence drops the places of worship (27,509 in that snapshot). assets also drops the listings with an Overture confidence score below 0.50 (24,209 in that snapshot). The other tourism counts in municipalities.json (by_category, in_sfha, in_flood_zone, in_protected, with_website, avg_confidence, sfha_pct and both density ratios) are calculated from the assets places only.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Steps in build.py. (1) parse_places keeps Overture records whose category maps to one of the observatory's tourism categories and drops the rest. (2) dedup folds duplicate listings: two listings in the same municipality (at this step the town in the address, or the nearest centre point when the address names none) and the same category are merged when their names are alike and they are close together (within 600 m, or 1,000 m when either listing is a beach, park, nature reserve, scenic area, historic site or tourist attraction, with a tighter limit when the names are only partly alike), or when they share a phone number, have partly matching names and lie within 500 m. The record with the highest confidence and the most complete details is kept. Then the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing, care services and numbered homes filed under tourism categories; places_privacy.not_tourism) are left out of every count (HANDOFF decision 47, 2026-10-18). (3) Each place gets a municipality from its pin. (4) Flood and protected-area flags are added. (5) municipality_stats counts. The confidence cutoff is MIN_CONF = 0.50. A place of worship is any listing of the type 'Places of Worship'.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01.
entries.how_to_read: Use assets for tourism supply. Use assets_all_confidence to see how much a municipality's count depends on the 0.50 cutoff. Use listings_all only to reconcile with the full list of places in places.json (32,541 rows in the 2026-10 snapshot).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 99,323 Overture places lay in the bounding box, 36,206 matched a tourism category, and 1,088 of those were folded into other listings as duplicates; 2,577 more are not tourism and were left out (since 2026-10-18). The largest single group of dropped records, 3,388, has no Overture category at all.

Places of worship are the only type left out by name. All are Attractions. In the 2026-10 snapshot there are 5,032 such listings, of which 4,758 have confidence of 0.50 or higher. Foundation for Puerto Rico's (FPR) keyword rule for this type also matches the word 'religious', so besides churches and other places of worship it holds 1,169 listings that Overture calls religious organizations and 67 religious schools. All 5,032 are left out of assets.
The map's category chips, confidence slider and worship toggle change what the map draws and what the Municipality tab counts live. They never change the stored counts.

Transit access (transit_pct, access_n and the acc_ shares) and the barrio counts use the same counted places. The municipality land-use place figures (places_urban_pct, places_on_protected_land and places_on_protected_land_pct) differ: they use all listings in listings_all, including places of worship and listings below 0.50. Each is documented in its own entry.
entries.plain_es: Tres conteos describen los listados turísticos de un municipio. Solo se diferencian en si incluyen los lugares de culto y los listados de baja confianza. El conteo predeterminado, assets, deja fuera ambos.
entries.name_es: Qué lugares incluye cada conteo municipal
entries.how_to_read_es: Use assets para la oferta turística. Use assets_all_confidence para ver cuánto depende el conteo de un municipio del punto de corte de 0.50. Use listings_all solo para cuadrar con la lista completa de lugares de places.json (32,541 filas en el corte de datos 2026-10).

entries.name: Land-use group at the place
entries.plain: The broad group of the land-use plan class at the place's pin: urban, urbanizable, rustic (ordinary rural), protected, water or road.
entries.definition: One of six groups that the observatory derives from the plan class (land_use). In the 2026-10 snapshot, it is present for the same 32,369 places as land_use.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Set from the plan class: SU is urban; SURP and SURNP are urbanizable; SRC is rustic; any class starting with SREP is protected; AGUA is water; VIAL is road.
entries.source_detail: Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos de Puerto Rico (PUT), version of 30 November 2015, from a copy of the Junta's official shapefile that Foundation for Puerto Rico holds; fields CLASIPUT and DESCRIPPUT.
entries.how_to_read: Use it for quick counts, for example places on urban land. Protected here means rural land under special protection in the plan. It is a different thing from a protected area in PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States).
caveats: The group name protected can mislead. The plan's special protection and the PAD-US protected-area database are two separate sources, so a place can be in one and not the other.
Water and road mean the pin sits on a mapped water or road polygon.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its website footer reads Todos los derechos reservados (all rights reserved). Check the Junta's terms before you reuse this field.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

entries.name: Land-use plan class (PUT 2015) at the place
entries.plain: The class of Puerto Rico's 2015 land-use plan (Plan de Uso de Terrenos, PUT) at the place's pin, such as urban land or ordinary rural land.
entries.definition: The class code (CLASIPUT) of the Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT) polygon that contains the pin. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 32,369 of 32,541 places have one. The other 172 fall outside every plan polygon; the largest groups are in San Juan (25), Fajardo (19), Culebra (18) and Cabo Rojo (13), and all 4 places on Mona Island are among them.

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the plan's polygons at full detail. If polygons overlap, the first one found is used. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
entries.source_detail: Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos de Puerto Rico (PUT), version of 30 November 2015, from a copy of the Junta's official shapefile that Foundation for Puerto Rico holds; fields CLASIPUT and DESCRIPPUT.
entries.how_to_read: The plan classes land by what the plan intends or allows: urban, urbanizable (future growth), rural or specially protected rural. It is a planning class. It is not the actual use of the building, and it is not zoning (calificación).
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 5,858 places (18.0%) sit in road (VIAL) polygons, because the plan maps roads as their own polygons. Such a place is usually next to the road.
The plan dates from 2015. Land can have changed class since then.
Zoning districts (calificación) are not in the observatory's data: the Junta de Planificación's online service did not return them when the 2026-10 snapshot was built.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its website footer reads Todos los derechos reservados (all rights reserved). Check the Junta's terms before you reuse this field.

entries.name: Place listings on specially protected rural land (%)
entries.plain: Out of every 100 place listings in the municipality that fall inside the 2015 land use plan, how many sit on specially protected rural land.
entries.definition: places_on_protected_land divided by the municipality's listings whose point falls inside any plan polygon (urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural, protected, water or road), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Listings that fall in no polygon are not counted in the denominator.
entries.unit: % of place listings inside a plan polygon

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full snapshot build (Snapshot 2026-10); the plan itself dates from 2015.

entries.method: Listings in protected polygons divided by listings in any plan polygon, per municipality, times 100. Water and road polygons count in the denominator. See land.put_statistics.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026); Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT 2015); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: A high value means many of the municipality's listings stand on protected rural land; a low value means few do. It is a share of listings, not of land area (see protected_land_pct). In the 2026-10 snapshot the value ranges from 0.0% to 44.7% (Maricao); Adjuntas 34.9%, San Juan 0.3%. Of the island's 32,541 listings in that snapshot, 172 fall in no polygon.
caveats: The Housing page profile shows this figure under the label "Tourism places on protected rural land". The figure counts all place listings (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50, so it is not a count of tourism places alone (24,209 in that snapshot, the number counted in assets). See municipalities.counting_rules.
The denominator includes listings on road and water polygons, so shares are lower than a share of places on land only.
A plan designation from 2015: it shows how the Junta de Planificación classified the land, not today's land cover or what stands on it.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it.

entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor alto significa que muchos de los listados del municipio están en suelo rural protegido; un valor bajo significa que pocos lo están. Es una proporción de listados, no de superficie (vea protected_land_pct). En el corte de datos 2026-10 el valor va de 0.0% a 44.7% (Maricao); Adjuntas 34.9%, San Juan 0.3%. De los 32,541 listados de la isla en ese corte, 172 no caen en ningún polígono.

entries.name: Place listings on specially protected rural land (count)
entries.plain: How many place listings in the municipality sit on land the 2015 land use plan classes as specially protected rural land. It counts all listings, not only tourism places.
entries.definition: Number of place listings whose point falls inside a plan polygon of class SREP (Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido) or one of its subtypes, among the listings that the point-in-polygon test assigns to the municipality. Listings are the Overture Maps places that the observatory keeps after classification and de-duplication: they include places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full snapshot build (Snapshot 2026-10); the plan itself dates from 2015.

entries.method: landuse.py tests each listing's point against the plan polygons and takes the first polygon that contains it. A listing in a protected group polygon is counted for the municipality where its point falls. See land.put_statistics.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026); Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT 2015); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: It shows how many listed places stand on land the plan protects. A listing on protected land is not necessarily a problem: nature reserves, parks and scenic areas are listed places too. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 2,151 such listings, in 77 of the 78 municipalities.
caveats: The Housing page profile shows this figure under the label "Tourism places on protected rural land". The figure counts all place listings (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50, so it is not a count of tourism places alone (24,209 in that snapshot, the number counted in assets). See municipalities.counting_rules.
Not the same as in_protected, which counts tourism places inside protected areas of the US Geological Survey (USGS) Protected Areas Database (PAD-US).
A plan designation from 2015: it shows how the Junta de Planificación classified the land, not today's land cover or what stands on it.
A point near a polygon edge can fall in either polygon; the first polygon found is used.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it.
