entries.name_es: Listados de lugares en suelo rústico especialmente protegido (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Muestra cuántos lugares listados están en terreno que el plan protege. Un listado en terreno protegido no es necesariamente un problema: las reservas naturales, los parques y las áreas escénicas también son lugares listados. En el corte de datos 2026-10 la isla tiene 2,151 listados de este tipo, en 77 de los 78 municipios.

entries.name: Place listings on urban land (%)
entries.plain: Out of every 100 place listings in the municipality that fall inside the 2015 land use plan, how many sit on land the plan classes as urban.
entries.definition: Listings whose point falls inside a plan polygon of class SU (Suelo Urbano), divided by the municipality's listings whose point falls inside any plan polygon (urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural, protected, water or road), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Listings in no polygon are not counted.
entries.unit: % of place listings inside a plan polygon

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full snapshot build (Snapshot 2026-10); the plan itself dates from 2015.

entries.method: Listings in urban polygons divided by listings in any plan polygon, per municipality, times 100. Road and water polygons count in the denominator and never in the numerator. See land.put_statistics.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026); Junta de Planificación, Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT 2015); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: A high value means most listings stand on urban land. In the 2026-10 snapshot the value ranges from 29.8% (Maricao) to 81.6% (Guaynabo), and 66.2% of listings island-wide (21,418 of 32,369) stand on urban land. Listings on a street polygon (5,858 of those 32,369, 18.1%) are not counted as urban, even in a town centre. The value therefore understates the share of listings in built-up areas.
caveats: This count uses every place listing in the municipality (32,541 on the island in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and listings below confidence 0.50, not only the tourism places counted in assets. See municipalities.counting_rules.
Not the same as urban_pct, which is a share of land area.
A plan designation from 2015: it shows how the Junta de Planificación classified the land, not today's land cover or what stands on it.
The Junta de Planificación states no data license, and its site footer reads "Todos los derechos reservados". Check its terms before reusing the plan or figures computed from it.
entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: Guaynabo 81.6%; San Juan 78.3%; Maricao 29.8%.
entries.plain_es: De cada 100 registros de lugares del municipio que caen dentro del Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015, cuántos están en terreno que el plan clasifica como urbano.
entries.name_es: Listados de lugares en suelo urbano (%)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor alto significa que la mayoría de los listados están en suelo urbano. En el corte de datos 2026-10 el valor va de 29.8% (Maricao) a 81.6% (Guaynabo), y el 66.2% de los listados de toda la isla (21,418 de 32,369) están en suelo urbano. Los listados en un polígono de calle (5,858 de esos 32,369, 18.1%) no se cuentan como urbanos, ni siquiera en un casco urbano. Por eso el valor subestima la proporción de listados en áreas construidas.

entries.name: Tourism places inside protected areas (count)
entries.plain: How many counted tourism places have their map pin (the point where Overture places them) inside a protected area in PAD-US, the US Geological Survey's Protected Areas Database of the United States. Many of these areas are local parks.
entries.definition: Number of the counted places (assets) whose pin lies inside a polygon of the US Geological Survey's (USGS) Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) in Puerto Rico, other than a proclamation boundary (designation type PROC). Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). A place that is inside several polygons counts once. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 869, and five municipalities have none: Añasco, Las Marías, Maricao, Maunabo and Moca.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot; PAD-US downloaded 2026-10-01

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test of each place against the PAD-US polygons, then a count per municipality of the counted places that tested inside. See 'How flood and protected-area exposure is counted'.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places; USGS PAD-US 4.1, Protection Mechanism Category layer, State_Nm = 'PR'; 665 polygons in the layer downloaded 2026-10-01.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (134), then Río Grande (50), Guánica (38) and Ponce (36). Of the 869 counted places inside a protected area in that snapshot, the strictest status of the area is 4 for 509 places, 2 for 252, 1 for 62 and 3 for 46. This is the GAP code of the US Geological Survey's Gap Analysis Project: 1 = managed for biodiversity, natural disturbance allowed; 2 = managed for biodiversity, disturbance held back; 3 = managed for several uses, such as mining or logging; 4 = no known requirement to protect biodiversity. The map words these codes differently (it labels GAP 1 'strict nature reserve'); see 'Protection level, GAP status (GAP_Sts)'.
caveats: 'Protected' refers to the land's conservation or management status. It does not mean the place is protected from flooding, storms or other hazards.

'Protected' here means any area listed in PAD-US. The layer downloaded for the 2026-10 snapshot includes local parks (411 of its 665 polygons), marine protected areas, conservation easements, wildlife refuges and military lands. It does not mean the place is in a nature reserve.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, one PAD-US record named 'Unknown Local Park' covers 117 of the 869 places (13%), 12 of them in San Juan. That record is a set of 534 separate local-park areas (managing agency unknown), not one park. Counts for municipalities with many local-park places partly reflect it.
Being inside the polygon does not say whether the public can enter. Access differs by area, and the map pop-up for an area shows it.
It is not the same as the share of land in 'Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido' in the Junta de Planificación's 2015 land-use plan, which is a different source and a different field.
It tests the pin only and counts places, not hectares.

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados tienen su marcador en el mapa (el punto donde Overture los ubica) dentro de un área protegida de PAD-US, la base de datos de áreas protegidas de Estados Unidos del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). Muchas de estas áreas son parques locales.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos dentro de áreas protegidas (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, San Juan tiene la mayor cantidad (134), seguido de Río Grande (50), Guánica (38) y Ponce (36). De los 869 lugares contados dentro de un área protegida en ese corte, el estado más estricto del área es 4 para 509 lugares, 2 para 252, 1 para 62 y 3 para 46. Es el código GAP del Gap Analysis Project del Servicio Geológico de EE. UU.: 1 = manejada para la biodiversidad, se permiten las perturbaciones naturales; 2 = manejada para la biodiversidad, se contienen las perturbaciones; 3 = manejada para varios usos, como la minería o la tala; 4 = sin requisito conocido de proteger la biodiversidad. El mapa describe estos códigos con otras palabras (llama al GAP 1 'reserva natural estricta'); vea 'Nivel de protección, estatus GAP (GAP_Sts)'.

entries.name: Protected area containing the place
entries.plain: The name of the protected area that contains the place's pin. The names come from PAD-US, the US Geological Survey's Protected Areas Database. In the 2026-10 snapshot, about 3% of places have one.
entries.definition: The unit name (Unit_Nm) of the PAD-US area that contains the pin. If several areas contain it, the one with the strictest GAP (Gap Analysis Project) status is named. Proclamation boundaries, which outline whole islands or refuges, do not count. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,013 places have one (3.1%), 869 of them on the default basis, and 307 different names occur.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against the PAD-US polygons of Puerto Rico. Of the areas that contain the pin, the one with the lowest GAP status number is used. See 'How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set'.
entries.source_detail: USGS Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US 4.1; USGS data release, digital object identifier (DOI) 10.5066/P96WBCHS), Protection Mechanism Category feature service, records with State_Nm = PR; fields Unit_Nm, Des_Tp and GAP_Sts. Downloaded on 1 October 2026. Version 4.1 was released in March 2025 and USGS cites it as a 2024 data release, so use the year given on the DOI page when you cite it.
entries.how_to_read: PAD-US lists land that is public or held for conservation or recreation. Being inside one does not mean the place is in a nature reserve: PAD-US also lists local parks, plazas and military land. Read the protection level (GAP status) next to it. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 140 places show the name 'Unknown Local Park'. PAD-US records those local parks without a name.
Only one area is named even when the pin lies in several.
This is a database match, not a legal or zoning finding. The land-use plan class is a separate field.

Map, Map layers tab: Protected areas layer

entries.plain_es: El nombre del área protegida que contiene el marcador del lugar. Los nombres vienen de PAD-US, la base de datos de áreas protegidas del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). En el corte de datos de 2026-10, alrededor del 3% de los lugares tiene una.
entries.name_es: Área protegida que contiene el lugar
entries.how_to_read_es: PAD-US lista terrenos que son públicos o que se dedican a la conservación o la recreación. Estar dentro de uno no significa que el lugar esté en una reserva natural: PAD-US también lista parques locales, plazas y terrenos militares. Lea el nivel de protección (estatus GAP) que aparece al lado. La base predeterminada son los lugares con una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más, sin los lugares de culto.

entries.name: Protection level (GAP status) of that area
entries.plain: The protection level, from 1 (strictest) to 4 (no known mandate to protect nature), of the area named in the protected area field. The scale is the GAP status of the USGS (US Geological Survey) Gap Analysis Project.
entries.definition: The USGS GAP status code of the PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) area named in protected_area, written as the digit 1, 2, 3 or 4. It is published together with protected_area: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,013 places have both.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Copied from the GAP_Sts field of the PAD-US area chosen for protected_area, which is the area with the lowest GAP number among those containing the pin.
entries.source_detail: USGS Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US 4.1; USGS data release, digital object identifier (DOI) 10.5066/P96WBCHS), Protection Mechanism Category feature service, records with State_Nm = PR; fields Unit_Nm, Des_Tp and GAP_Sts. Downloaded on 1 October 2026. Version 4.1 was released in March 2025 and USGS cites it as a 2024 data release, so use the year given on the DOI page when you cite it.
entries.how_to_read: GAP 1 and 2 areas are managed for biodiversity. GAP 4 means no known mandate to protect biodiversity. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 608 of the 1,013 places with a value are GAP 4, so most places with a protected area are on land with no known biodiversity mandate. The place pop-up shows the area name only. The GAP status is in the downloaded file, in the CSV (comma-separated values) download and in the Protected areas layer pop-up.
caveats: GAP status describes protection of biodiversity. It does not describe public access. PAD-US has a separate access field that the observatory does not publish for each place.
The descriptions in the codes below paraphrase USGS. The PAD-US data dictionary is the reference. "Strict nature reserve" is the map's label for code 1, not PAD-US wording.
The place counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.1: GAP status 1: managed for biodiversity. Natural disturbance, such as fire or flooding, is allowed to happen or is imitated by management. The pop-up of the Protected areas layer labels it "strict nature reserve", but PAD-US does not use that term. 67 places.
values.2: GAP status 2: managed for biodiversity, but natural disturbance is suppressed, for example fires are put out. The Protected areas layer pop-up calls it managed for biodiversity. 285 places.
values.3: GAP status 3: managed for multiple uses. Extractive uses such as mining or logging, or off-highway vehicle use, may be allowed. The Protected areas layer pop-up calls it multiple use, some extraction. 53 places.
values.4: GAP status 4: no known requirement to protect biodiversity. The land is recorded in PAD-US (for example local parks, plazas, a national historic site and military land) but is not protected for biodiversity. The Protected areas layer pop-up calls it no known biodiversity mandate. 608 places.

Map, Municipality tab: a municipality's places, with a CSV download that has a protected_gap column (example: San Juan)

entries.plain_es: El nivel de protección, de 1 (el más estricto) a 4 (sin mandato conocido de proteger la naturaleza), del área que nombra el campo de área protegida. La escala es el estatus GAP del Gap Analysis Project del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos).
entries.name_es: Nivel de protección (estatus GAP) de esa área
entries.how_to_read_es: Las áreas GAP 1 y 2 se manejan para la biodiversidad. GAP 4 significa que no hay un mandato conocido de proteger la biodiversidad. En el corte de datos 2026-10, 608 de los 1,013 lugares con un valor son GAP 4; por lo tanto, la mayoría de los lugares con área protegida está en terrenos sin mandato conocido de biodiversidad. La ventana emergente del lugar muestra solo el nombre del área. El estatus GAP está en el archivo descargado, en la descarga CSV (valores separados por comas) y en la ventana emergente de la capa Áreas protegidas.

entries.name: All tourism listings (count)
entries.plain: Every tourism listing in the municipality after de-duplication, including places of worship and low-confidence listings. It is the largest of the three place counts.
entries.definition: Number of de-duplicated listings attached to the municipality in any of the observatory's four tourism categories, including places of worship (a type of Attractions) and listings of every confidence score. It equals the number of rows of places.json for that municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 32,541: 27,509 other places plus 5,032 places of worship.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (this entry describes the 2026-10 snapshot)

entries.method: Count of all places attached to the municipality after classification, de-duplication and municipality assignment, with no further filter.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k boundaries clipped to the shoreline).
entries.how_to_read: Use it to reconcile with the full list of places in places.json. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has 4,597 listings and Maricao 47. For tourism supply use assets.
caveats: It includes churches and other places of worship, which are mapped as landmarks but are mostly not tourism supply, and records Overture rates below 0.50.

The type Places of Worship comes from the observatory's keyword rule, which also matches the word 'religious'. In the 2026-10 snapshot it holds 5,032 listings: besides churches and other places of worship, 1,169 listings that Overture calls religious organizations and 67 religious schools.
It does not include every Overture place. Records with no tourism category (for example salons, clinics or gas stations) were dropped before counting.
The map does not display this field; it is in the data file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download.

entries.name: Average Overture confidence of counted places
entries.plain: The average of Overture's own confidence scores for the municipality's counted tourism places. A score is a number from 0 to 1, and a higher number means Overture is more sure the listing is a real place.
entries.definition: Mean of the Overture confidence scores of the places counted in assets, rounded to three decimals. Counted places all score 0.50 or higher, so the mean cannot fall below 0.50. All 78 municipalities have a value.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (this entry describes the 2026-10 snapshot)

entries.method: Sum of the confidence of each counted place divided by the number of counted places, per municipality, rounded to three decimals in build.py. The observatory does not compute the confidence itself.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; field confidence of each place.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the averages run from 0.780 (Peñuelas) to 0.850 (San Juan). The range is narrow because only scores of 0.50 or higher are averaged. Treat it as a rough data-quality signal, not as an accuracy rate.
caveats: The score is produced by Overture, and the observatory has not checked it against the real places.
It is calculated after the 0.50 cutoff, so it cannot show how many weaker listings were left out. See assets_all_confidence for that.
The map does not display this field; it is in the data file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download.

entries.plain_es: El promedio de las puntuaciones de confianza que el propio Overture da a los lugares turísticos contados del municipio. La puntuación es un número de 0 a 1; mientras más alto, más seguro está Overture de que el listado es un lugar real.
entries.name_es: Confianza promedio de Overture de los lugares contados
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, los promedios van de 0.780 (Peñuelas) a 0.850 (San Juan). El intervalo es estrecho porque solo se promedian las puntuaciones de 0.50 o más. Trátelo como una señal aproximada de la calidad de los datos, no como una tasa de exactitud.

entries.name: Tourism places (count)
entries.plain: How many tourism places the municipality has: attractions, food and drink, lodging and visitor services. Places of worship are left out. A place counts only if Overture Maps, an open map-data project, gives it a confidence score of 0.50 or higher.
entries.definition: Number of de-duplicated Overture Maps listings in the municipality that (1) fall into one of the observatory's four tourism categories (Attractions, Gastronomy, Accommodations, Visitor Services), (2) are not places of worship and (3) have an Overture confidence score of 0.50 or higher. This is the default basis for the tourism statistics in the observatory. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 24,209.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (this entry describes the 2026-10 snapshot)

entries.method: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Overture had 99,323 places inside Puerto Rico's bounding box. The rules of Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) matched 36,206 of them to a tourism category and dropped the rest. Duplicates were folded (1,088), leaving 35,118 listings, and the 2,577 that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services filed under tourism categories) were left out, leaving 32,541 (since 2026-10-18, HANDOFF decision 47). Each listing was attached to a municipality by its pin, the point where Overture places the listing (see 'How a tourism place is assigned to a municipality'). The build then counts, per municipality, the listings that are not places of worship and have confidence of at least 0.50 (MIN_CONF in build.py). See 'Which places each municipality count includes'.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01 with the overturemaps command-line tool for the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57. Municipality boundaries: Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k boundaries clipped to the shoreline).
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most counted places (3,424) and Maricao the fewest (36). Large municipalities have more, so compare places per 1,000 residents or per km² before ranking places against each other. The Municipality tab's first tile, 'tourism places (current filters)', is counted live from the places the map shows, so it changes when you change the category chips or the confidence slider; this stored value does not. In municipalities.json and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download, this count is the column 'assets'. A snapshot is one build of the observatory. The 2026-10 snapshot (label 'Snapshot 2026-10') was generated on 2 October 2026 (UTC) from Overture release 2026-09-23.1.
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, nearly two thirds of the counted places (17,170 of 24,209) are food and drink places such as restaurants, bars and cafés, which serve residents as well as visitors. 'Tourism places' is FPR's label for the four categories. It does not count only places that visitors use.
A low count can mean that Overture lists fewer places there. The count is not an inventory and does not match official hotel, room or business counts, which use other records and definitions.

Overture builds its listings from several sources and some are wrong, closed or missing. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,618 of the 24,209 counted places come from Meta, 250 from Foursquare, 238 from Microsoft and 103 from AllThePlaces. The confidence score is Overture's, and FPR has not checked it on the ground.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the sources last updated the counted listings between November 2020 and September 2026, so the count does not describe one date.

Overture records whose category is outside the four groups are not counted at all. Among the most common dropped categories are beauty salons, grocery stores, professional services, auto repair, doctors' offices, gas stations, spas and schools.
One business can appear twice if its records differ more than the de-duplication rules allow, and two real places can be folded into one.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, about 1% of the counted places (324 of 24,209) have a pin outside every municipal boundary polygon, such as pins at the shoreline. That build counted them for the municipality with the nearest centre point; the next full build counts them for the municipality whose boundary is nearest.
Do not read two snapshots as growth or decline. Each snapshot uses a new Overture release and a new run of FPR's matching and de-duplication rules.

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos tiene el municipio: atracciones, lugares de comida y bebida, alojamientos y servicios para visitantes. Quedan fuera los lugares de culto. Un lugar cuenta solo si Overture Maps, un proyecto abierto de datos de mapas, le da una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, San Juan tiene la mayor cantidad de lugares contados (3,424) y Maricao, la menor (36). Los municipios grandes tienen más, así que compare los lugares por cada 1,000 residentes o por km² antes de ordenar unos municipios frente a otros. El primer recuadro de la pestaña Municipio, 'lugares turísticos (filtros actuales)', se cuenta en vivo a partir de los lugares que muestra el mapa, así que cambia cuando se cambian los botones de categoría o el control deslizante de confianza; este valor guardado no cambia. En municipalities.json y en la descarga CSV (valores separados por comas), este conteo es la columna 'assets'. Un corte de datos es una compilación del observatorio. El corte de datos 2026-10 (etiqueta 'Corte 2026-10') se generó el 2 de octubre de 2026 (UTC) a partir de la versión 2026-09-23.1 de Overture.

entries.name: Tourism places by category (counts)
entries.plain: Four counts for each municipality: its attractions, its food and drink places (gastronomy), its lodging (accommodations) and its visitor services. Together they add up to the municipality's tourism places.
entries.definition: An object with four keys, ATTRACTIONS, GASTRONOMY, ACCOMMODATIONS and VISITOR_SERVICES. Each holds the number of the counted places (assets) in that category. Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). All four keys are present for all 78 municipalities (the value is 0 when there is none), and the four numbers add up to assets.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (this entry describes the 2026-10 snapshot)

entries.method: The observatory assigns each Overture listing to a category and a type by matching Overture's category names against keyword rules in build.py (RULES). The build then counts the places counted in assets by category. Places of worship, which are Attractions, are excluded.

values.ATTRACTIONS: Attractions: 4,591 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: historic sites, parks, beaches, tourist attractions, cultural attractions (such as galleries, theatres and cinemas), scenic areas, museums and nature reserves. Places of worship are not counted here.
values.GASTRONOMY: Gastronomy, meaning food and drink: 17,170 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: restaurants, bars, cafés, bakeries, nightlife and food experiences.
values.ACCOMMODATIONS: Accommodations: 1,831 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: lodging (the general type, including campgrounds), hotels, vacation properties, inns, guest houses and resorts.
values.VISITOR_SERVICES: Visitor services: 617 places island-wide in the 2026-10 snapshot. Types present: transportation (such as airports, bus stations and taxi services), adventure operators, tour operators, cultural experience providers, marinas and visitor centers.

entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; categories assigned by the observatory (RULES in build.py).
entries.how_to_read: Use it to compare the mix of supply: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 2,421 of San Juan's 3,424 places are Gastronomy, while 51 of Culebra's 136 are Accommodations. In the CSV (comma-separated values) download the object is split into four columns: by_category_ATTRACTIONS, by_category_GASTRONOMY, by_category_ACCOMMODATIONS and by_category_VISITOR_SERVICES. The Analysis tab maps the four counts as separate layers.
caveats: The category comes from the observatory's keyword rules on Overture's category names, not from the business. A place can be put in a category that a visitor would not choose.
Accommodation listings are not rooms or beds. A hotel with 400 rooms is one place.
The Municipality tab's 'By category' bars are counted live from the places the map shows. They do not read this object and change with the filters.

Map, Rankings tab: download the municipality table (CSV)

entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan: ATTRACTIONS 645, GASTRONOMY 2,421, ACCOMMODATIONS 224, VISITOR_SERVICES 134 (total 3,424).
entries.plain_es: Cuatro conteos para cada municipio: sus atracciones, sus lugares de comida y bebida (gastronomía), sus alojamientos y sus servicios para visitantes. Juntos suman los lugares turísticos del municipio.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos por categoría (conteos)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para comparar la composición de la oferta: en el corte de datos 2026-10, 2,421 de los 3,424 lugares de San Juan son de Gastronomía, mientras que 51 de los 136 de Culebra son Alojamientos. En la descarga CSV (valores separados por comas), el objeto se divide en cuatro columnas: by_category_ATTRACTIONS, by_category_GASTRONOMY, by_category_ACCOMMODATIONS y by_category_VISITOR_SERVICES. La pestaña Análisis muestra los cuatro conteos en el mapa como capas separadas.

entries.name: Tourism places with a website (count)
entries.plain: How many of the counted tourism places list a website in their Overture record.
entries.definition: Number of the counted places (assets) whose Overture record lists at least one website. Counted places are Overture listings with a confidence score of 0.50 or higher, without places of worship (see 'Which places each municipality count includes'). The build keeps the first website Overture gives and counts only whether one is present. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 7,210, which is 30% of the 24,209 counted places.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (this entry describes the 2026-10 snapshot)

entries.method: Count of places in assets with a non-empty website field. The website addresses themselves are published in places.json, except that the build removes a few that contain an email address.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; first value of the websites field.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most places with a website (1,597) and Florida the fewest (7). As a share of counted places, the range in that snapshot is from about 8% in Maunabo to 47% in San Juan (worked out from the municipal values). Use it as a rough sign of how visible a place is online, not as a measure of quality.
caveats: The address is not checked. It may be out of date or lead to a page that no longer exists.

A website can be a social page or a booking listing. Before 2026-10-18, among the 7,440 website addresses then published for counted places (26,579 then counted), 527 contained instagram.com or facebook.com and 293 contained airbnb.com (42 more used Airbnb's abnb.me short link). Website addresses are no longer published.

In the 2026-10 snapshot a recount of has_website in places.json gives the same value for every municipality. Before 2026-10-18 the recount was 1 lower in Ponce, because one website was counted before the build removed an address holding an email address; that listing is no longer counted.
On the Municipality tab, the 'with a website' tile is counted live from the places the map shows and follows the filters.

Map, Municipality tab: tile 'with a website'

entries.plain_es: Cuántos de los lugares turísticos contados tienen un sitio web en su registro de Overture.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos con sitio web (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, San Juan tiene la mayor cantidad de lugares con sitio web (1,597) y Florida, la menor (7). Como proporción de los lugares contados, en ese corte va de alrededor del 8% en Maunabo al 47% en San Juan (calculado a partir de los valores municipales). Úselo como una señal aproximada de qué tan visible es un lugar en internet, no como una medida de calidad.

entries.name: Tourism places, all confidence levels (count)
entries.plain: Tourism places counted at every confidence score, still without places of worship. It is a larger count that includes the listings Overture is less sure about.
entries.definition: Number of de-duplicated listings in the municipality that fall into one of the observatory's four tourism categories and are not places of worship, whatever their Overture confidence score (0 to 1). It is never lower than assets. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 78 values add up to 27,509, against 24,209 for assets.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (this entry describes the 2026-10 snapshot)

entries.method: Same listings and municipality assignment as assets, without the confidence cutoff of 0.50. Places of worship are still left out.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k boundaries clipped to the shoreline).
entries.how_to_read: The gap between this field and assets is the number of listings with confidence below 0.50. In the 2026-10 snapshot it is 3,300 on the whole island, 639 in San Juan and 2 in Maricao. A big gap means the municipality's count depends more on where the cutoff is set.
caveats: Listings below 0.50 are the ones Overture rates as less likely to be real places. The observatory does not use this count for its tourism supply figures.

The map does not display this field; it is in the data file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download. The map's confidence slider recounts places in the browser and never changes this stored value.

entries.plain_es: Los lugares turísticos contados con cualquier puntuación de confianza, todavía sin los lugares de culto. Es un conteo mayor que incluye los listados de los que Overture está menos seguro.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos, todos los niveles de confianza (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: La diferencia entre este campo y assets es el número de listados con una confianza menor de 0.50. En el corte de datos 2026-10 es 3,300 en toda la isla, 639 en San Juan y 2 en Maricao. Una diferencia grande significa que el conteo del municipio depende más de dónde se fije el punto de corte.

entries.name: Tourism places per 1,000 residents
entries.group: Tourism places relative to people and land
entries.plain: How many counted tourism places there are for every 1,000 people who live in the municipality.
entries.definition: assets divided by population_2020, times 1,000, rounded to two decimals. For comparison, in the 2026-10 snapshot the whole island has about 7.37 (24,209 places for 3,285,874 residents, worked out from the municipal values, not stored in the file).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (places: 2026-10 snapshot; residents: 2020 Census)

entries.method: round(assets / population_2020 x 1000, 2) in build.py. It uses the default places basis (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship) and the 2020 Census population.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1) divided by Census TIGERweb 2020 counties layer 82, field POP100.
entries.how_to_read: A higher number means more tourism places for each resident. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Culebra (75.89), Rincón (29.10) and Vieques (28.73) are highest. Trujillo Alto (2.73) and Toa Alta (2.92) are lowest. The ratio does not measure visitors or demand. In the 2026-10 snapshot, nearly two thirds of the counted places are food and drink places, which serve residents too.
caveats: It divides by residents on census day 2020. Visitors, seasonal residents and people who work there but live elsewhere are not in the denominator.
Small populations make the ratio jump. Culebra had 1,792 residents in the 2020 Census.
The Municipality tab shows this stored value. It does not change with the map's filters, unlike the tiles for the number of places, flood share, protected places and websites.

The Analysis tab's 'Per 1,000 residents' option for tourism layers divides by the Census Bureau's latest population estimate in the observatory (July 1, 2025), not the 2020 count, so its values differ from this field (in the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan is 10.38 there and 10.00 here). Do not mix the two.

Places are from 2026 and residents from 2020. Puerto Rico's July 2025 estimate (3,184,835) is 3.1% below the 2020 count (3,285,874), so island-wide this ratio would be about 3% higher with 2025 residents. Municipalities differ.

entries.how_to_read_es: Un número más alto significa más lugares turísticos por residente. entries.name: Tourism places per square kilometre of land
entries.group: Tourism places relative to people and land
entries.plain: How many counted tourism places there are on each square kilometre of the municipality's land.
entries.definition: assets divided by land_km2, rounded to two decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the whole island has about 2.7 (24,209 places on 8,868.5 km², worked out from the municipal values, not stored in the file).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (places: 2026-10 snapshot; land: 2020 Census)

entries.method: round(assets / land_km2, 2) in build.py, using the default places basis and the 2020 Census land area.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1) divided by Census TIGERweb 2020 counties layer 82, field AREALAND.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan is densest (27.59 places per km²), then Rincón (11.95) and Cataño (11.84). Maricao is least dense (0.38). Places cluster in town centres, so the average over a whole municipality hides how crowded the centre is. The Barrios layer on the map shows places per km² for smaller areas, on a different basis, so do not compare the two values (see 'Tourism places per km² (barrio)').
caveats: It uses land area only. Water inside the boundary does not lower the density.
Mayagüez's land area includes Isla de Mona and Monito. In the 2026-10 snapshot, only 3 of its 589 counted places sit there, which lowers its density.
The Municipality tab shows this stored value. It does not change with the map's filters.

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos contados hay en cada kilómetro cuadrado de tierra del municipio.
entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos por kilómetro cuadrado de superficie terrestre
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, San Juan tiene la mayor densidad (27.59 lugares por km²), seguido de Rincón (11.95) y Cataño (11.84). Maricao tiene la menor densidad (0.38). Los lugares se agrupan en los centros urbanos, así que el promedio de todo un municipio oculta cuán concentrado está el centro. La capa Barrios del mapa muestra los lugares por km² para áreas más pequeñas, con otra base, así que no compare los dos valores (vea 'Lugares turísticos por km² (barrio)').

entries.name: Accommodations (tourism category)
entries.plain: Places to stay: hotels, resorts, inns, guest houses, vacation rentals and other lodging.
entries.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code ACCOMMODATIONS, gold pins on the map). It holds 6 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Hotels (1,165), Vacation Properties (586), Lodging (301), Inns (88), Resorts (45), Guest Houses (40). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 2,225 places in the file and 1,831 on the default basis.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Every listing in Overture's lodging group maps here (2,225 places in the 2026-10 snapshot). Its type comes from the first rule that fits, or Lodging when none fits. Listings outside that group never become Accommodations.
entries.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: Counts are listings, not rooms or beds. A large hotel and a small guest house count once each.
The observatory does not use an official lodging register, and lodging that no source lists is missing. See the Vacation Properties type for what it does not count.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: category chips, Minimum confidence slider and the places-of-worship box
Map: click a pin to open the place's pop-up

entries.plain_es: Lugares para hospedarse: hoteles, complejos turísticos, posadas, casas de huéspedes, alquileres vacacionales y otros alojamientos.
entries.name_es: Alojamientos (categoría turística)
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare las cuatro categorías para ver la composición de la oferta, y abra los tipos para ver el detalle. Los conteos son de lugares (uno por cada listado que se conserva después de combinar los duplicados), no de visitantes, habitaciones ni tamaño. La base predeterminada son los lugares con una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más, sin los lugares de culto.

entries.name: Attractions (tourism category)
entries.plain: Places to see or visit: beaches, parks, museums, historic sites, scenery, cultural venues and similar places. It also holds places of worship, which the observatory does not count by default.
entries.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code ATTRACTIONS, blue pins on the map). It holds 9 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Places of Worship (5,032), Historic Sites (1,098), Tourist Attractions (972), Parks (969), Beaches (840), Cultural Attractions (555), Scenic Areas (398), Museums (173), Nature Reserves (60). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 10,097 places in the file, 5,065 without places of worship, and 4,591 on the default basis.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Listings in Overture's cultural_and_historic, arts_and_entertainment and geographic_entities groups map here (6,123, 1,508 and 1,443 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot). Beaches, parks, nature reserves, scenic areas, historic sites, museums and places of worship are also accepted from other Overture groups (sports_and_recreation gives 947 places in that snapshot, mostly parks), because those types may stand alone. The other 76 places come from education (67, religious schools), shopping (7), services_and_business (1) and travel_and_transportation (1). Overture's group is not published in places.json; these counts come from the Overture records used for the 2026-10 snapshot.
entries.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Places of worship are not counted by default. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, places of worship (5,032 listings) are in this category but are left out of counts by default.
Historic Sites and Tourist Attractions are broad types. Read their entries before you draw conclusions.

entries.plain_es: Lugares para ver o visitar: playas, parques, museos, sitios históricos, paisajes, lugares culturales y similares. También incluye los lugares de culto, que el observatorio no cuenta por defecto.

entries.how_to_read_es: Compare las cuatro categorías para ver la composición de la oferta, y abra los tipos para ver el detalle. Los lugares de culto no se cuentan de forma predeterminada. Los conteos son de lugares (uno por cada listado que se conserva después de combinar los duplicados), no de visitantes, habitaciones ni tamaño. La base predeterminada son los lugares con una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más, sin los lugares de culto.

entries.name: Gastronomy (tourism category)
entries.plain: Places to eat and drink: restaurants, bars, cafes, bakeries, lounges, distilleries and wineries.
entries.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code GASTRONOMY, green pins on the map). It holds 6 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Restaurants (11,471), Bars (3,876), Cafes (2,848), Bakeries (1,100), Nightlife (106), Food Experiences (28). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 19,429 places in the file and 17,170 on the default basis.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Every listing in Overture's food_and_drink group maps here (19,429 places in the 2026-10 snapshot). Its type comes from the first rule that fits, or Restaurants when none fits. Listings outside that group never become Gastronomy.
entries.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Gastronomy is the largest category: 60% of all places in the file and 71% of those on the default basis.
Food Markets is a defined type with no places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Grocery stores (1,478) and farmers markets (61) were left out in that snapshot.

entries.name: Visitor services (tourism category)
entries.plain: Businesses that serve visitors: tour operators, marinas and boat businesses, adventure operators, transportation, visitor centers and cultural experience providers (in the 2026-10 snapshot, all of these providers are dance studios). The map writes this category as Visitor Services.
entries.definition: One of the observatory's four tourism categories (code VISITOR_SERVICES, red pins on the map). It holds 6 types (places in the file, 2026-10 snapshot): Transportation (204), Tour Operators (192), Adventure Operators (172), Cultural Experience Providers (121), Marinas (96), Visitor Centers (5). In the 2026-10 snapshot the category has 790 places in the file and 617 on the default basis.

entries.method: Overture has no matching group, so a listing is included only when a Visitor services rule fits its category name. In the 2026-10 snapshot the places come from Overture's travel_and_transportation (445), sports_and_recreation (264), shopping (63), services_and_business (15) and lifestyle_services (3) groups.
entries.how_to_read: Compare the four categories to see the mix of supply, and open the types for detail. Counts are places (one per listing kept after duplicates are folded), not visitors, rooms or size. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, this is the smallest category (790 places in the file, 617 on the default basis). Visitor services that fit no rule are left out.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, car rental offices (174 listings) and other rental businesses are left out. See the classification entry.
Some types hold shops and offices, not only operators, for example surf stores, boat dealers and ferry company offices.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the Cultural Experience Providers type holds only dance studios. It is 101 of the 617 places of this category on the default basis.

entries.name: Overture category (original)
entries.plain: The category Overture gave the place, such as restaurant, beach or hotel. The observatory keeps it so you can see how each place was classified.
entries.definition: Overture's primary category for the listing: lowercase words joined by underscores. 265 different values occur in the 2026-10 snapshot (268 before the listings that are not tourism were left out on 2026-10-18). The observatory uses it, with the parent groups above it in Overture's category tree, to set the category and type.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Copied from the Overture record (taxonomy.primary, or basic_category when the primary is missing). The map pop-up shows it with the underscores replaced by spaces.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to check or redo the classification: find the code below, then the rule words in the type's entry. The same Overture category can land in a different type when its parent group differs; in the 2026-10 snapshot every code maps to one type.
caveats: The category names and their meaning are Overture's. Overture can rename or add categories between releases.
Some records carry only one of Overture's broad group names (arts_and_entertainment, geographic_entities, food_and_drink, lodging) instead of a specific category.
The place counts in this entry, including those in the table of codes, are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

A few codes sit under an unexpected type because of the text rules. See the notes on trailer_dealer, airport_lounge, marina, the religious codes and the food shops (candy_store, chocolatier, delicatessen).

entries.how_to_read: Use it to filter places and to compare the mix of supply. Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) set the four groups. They are not an official or industry classification. entries.name: Fields the observatory does not publish
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: The observatory does not publish the phone, email, social-media links, street address, website, postcode, brand name or source license label of an Overture record, and it removes a telephone number written into a name.
entries.definition: Eight fields of Overture's records are read by the build but never written to places.json: phone, email, socials (social-media links), address (the street address), website, postcode, brand (the brand name) and source_license (the license label of the contributing source). Only whether a website is listed is kept (has_website). The field region is not written either: the map works it out from the municipality. A place the map does not draw also loses its name, Overture ID, coordinates, nearest stop and update date (see Counted but not drawn).
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The build removes these eight fields when it writes each place (places_privacy.py). Phone numbers are used only to match duplicate listings. The counts of phone, website, email, address and social links decide which duplicate is kept. Postcode, brand and license label are read and dropped without use. The build also leaves out any field that is empty or false, and removes a telephone number or an email address written into a name. Until 2026-10-18 the street address and the website were published; the owner rule of that date is never to publish business contact details or any personal data.
entries.how_to_read: Contact details of individual businesses can identify people, so the observatory leaves these fields out. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the 32,541 published places, the Overture record holds a phone number for 24,077 (74%), an email address for 12,711 (39%), social-media links for 32,104 (99%), a street address for 27,235 (84%), a website for 9,416 (29%), a postcode for 26,760 (82%) and a brand name for 1,963 (6%). Those fields are not in the observatory's data. Names are copied as the source wrote them, apart from a telephone number or an email address (see the caveats).
caveats: None of the eight fields is written to the published file. Phone numbers are used only to match duplicate listings. Phone, website, email, address and social links are counted to decide which duplicate is kept.

Names are free text. A telephone number or an email address written into a name is removed (4 names in the 2026-10 snapshot); names are not otherwise scrubbed. The street addresses and websites published until 2026-10-18 held telephone numbers (at least 6 addresses, and 28 websites pointed to WhatsApp) and social-media pages that can belong to individuals; they are no longer published, but copies made before that date can still hold them.
CSV (comma-separated values) downloads from the map hold only the published fields.
The source license label is not published for each place. The labels per source are listed in the codes of the contributing data source entry.

entries.plain_es: El observatorio no publica el teléfono, el correo electrónico, los enlaces a redes sociales, la dirección, el sitio web, el código postal, el nombre de marca ni la etiqueta de licencia de la fuente de un registro de Overture, y quita el número de teléfono escrito en un nombre.
entries.name_es: Campos que el observatorio no publica
entries.how_to_read_es: Los datos de contacto de negocios individuales pueden identificar a personas, por eso el observatorio deja fuera estos campos. En el corte de datos 2026-10, entre los 32,541 lugares publicados, el registro de Overture tiene un número de teléfono para 24,077 (74%), una dirección de correo electrónico para 12,711 (39%), enlaces a redes sociales para 32,104 (99%), una dirección de calle para 27,235 (84%), un sitio web para 9,416 (29%), un código postal para 26,760 (82%) y un nombre de marca para 1,963 (6%). Esos campos no están en los datos del observatorio. Los nombres se copian tal como los escribió la fuente, salvo un número de teléfono o una dirección de correo electrónico (vea las precauciones).

entries.name: How duplicate listings are folded
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: When several listings look like the same place, the observatory keeps the one with the highest confidence and counts the others in the duplicates field. In the 2026-10 snapshot, this folded 1,088 listings.
entries.definition: Two listings count as the same place when they share a municipality (taken from the address town, see step 1) and a category, sit close together, and have alike names (or the same phone number and somewhat alike names). Matches chain: if A matches B and B matches C, all three become one place.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The build groups listings by municipality and category, compares nearby pairs, and joins pairs whose names are alike. It keeps the listing with the highest confidence and counts the others in the duplicates field. The steps are listed below.
entries.how_to_read: A place with a duplicates value above 0 stands for several listings. The map pop-up shows the count. Rankings and counts use the kept listing only.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, most groups are small: 574 of the 691 places with folded listings have exactly one.

A few groups are large. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the two largest groups (43 and 36 folded listings) are built on neighborhood names (Condado and Isla Verde) and mix beaches, parks, condominiums and other places that share the name. The kept listing is only one of them.
Folded listings can have different types (for example a beach and a park), and the type of the kept listing is the one published. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 290 groups mix types.
Listings in different municipalities or different categories are never compared, so some real duplicates remain.
The step runs before the confidence cut and before the municipality is set from the pin, so a low-confidence listing can be folded into a higher one, and the group uses the address town.

Folding can remove places from the default count. It is done within a category, not a type, and the highest-confidence listing is kept. Places of worship share the Attractions category, so in the 2026-10 snapshot 74 listings of other types (67 with confidence 0.50 or higher) were folded into a kept place of worship, which is not counted by default. The other way round, 19 places of worship were folded into a kept listing of another type. These figures come from re-running the folding step on the Overture release used for that snapshot, for the places in the file.

view.label: Map: click a pin to open the place's pop-up

values.Step 1: Group listings: Same municipality and same category. The municipality here is the address town when it names one of the 78 municipalities (accents and capital letters ignored). Otherwise it is the nearest municipality center. In the 2026-10 snapshot, among the 32,541 published places, 325 have no address town and 590 have a town text that is not a municipality name.
values.Step 2: Compare pairs: Pairs within 1,000 m if either listing is a Beach, Park, Nature Reserve, Scenic Area, Historic Site or Tourist Attraction; within 600 m for all other types.
values.Step 3: Same place when: The name similarity is 0.95 or more; or it is 0.80 or more and the listings are within 600 m (those natural types) or 150 m (all other types); or the listings share the same phone number, the similarity is 0.50 or more and they are within 500 m.
values.Step 4: Chain the matches: Matching pairs are joined into groups. If A matches B and B matches C, all three are one place.
values.Step 5: Keep one: The listing with the highest confidence is kept. Ties go to the listing with more contact details on file (website, phone, email, address), then to the one with more social links. The duplicates field is the group size minus 1.
values.Name similarity: Names are compared as sets of words. Accents and capital letters are ignored, words shorter than 3 letters are dropped, and common words are dropped (for example the, de, playa, hotel, restaurante, church and the names of the 78 municipalities). The two names must share a word of 4 letters or more. The score is the shared words divided by all words, or, when the shorter name has two or more words (or both names are short), the shared words divided by the shorter name's words times 0.9, whichever is higher.

entries.plain_es: Cuando varios listados parecen ser el mismo lugar, el observatorio se queda con el de mayor confianza y cuenta los demás en el campo de duplicados. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, esto unió 1,088 listados.
entries.name_es: Cómo se combinan los listados duplicados
entries.how_to_read_es: Un lugar con un valor de duplicados mayor que 0 representa varios listados. La ventana emergente del mapa muestra el conteo. Las posiciones y los conteos usan solo el listado que se conservó.

entries.name: How flood, protected-area, land-use and transit flags are set
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: Flood zone, protected area, land-use class, barrio and municipality are set by checking which map polygon contains the place's pin. Transit access is the distance to the nearest mapped stop and to the nearest stop with a current timetable.
entries.definition: Each flag is a spatial test of the pin (latitude and longitude) against another dataset. Nothing is read from the place's name, address or category.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The build checks whether the pin lies inside a polygon of each of these datasets: FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) flood polygons (flood zone, subtype and Special Flood Hazard Area flag), PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) polygons (protected area and GAP (Gap Analysis Project) status), the land-use plan polygons (land use and group), Census barrio polygons (barrio) and Census municipality polygons (municipality). A pin exactly on a polygon's edge does not count as inside. Where polygons overlap, a Special Flood Hazard Area wins over the 0.2% zone for flood; the lowest GAP number wins for protected areas, and proclamation boundaries are ignored; the first polygon found is used for land use and barrio. The tests use the polygons at the detail the sources give them, not the simplified copies drawn on the map. Transit is different: access.py finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind and stores its distance, its name and the 400 m flag in places.json (see places.transit_m), and finds the nearest stop with a current timetable, which it stores in place_access.json (see place_access.ts_m).
entries.how_to_read: Read each flag as 'the dataset says this about the spot where the pin is'. It is not a finding about the building or the lot.
caveats: The result depends on how accurate the pin is and on how detailed and how current each polygon dataset is. A pin near an edge can fall on either side.
Only one value is kept per field, even when several polygons overlap the pin.
The Census boundaries are generalized by the Census Bureau, so pins close to the coast or to a boundary can fall on the other side of the true line.

view.label: Map: click a pin to open the place's pop-up

entries.plain_es: La zona inundable, el área protegida, la clase de uso de terrenos, el barrio y el municipio se asignan buscando qué polígono del mapa contiene el marcador del lugar. El acceso al transporte colectivo es la distancia a la parada más cercana del mapa y a la parada más cercana con horario vigente.
entries.name_es: Cómo se asignan las marcas de inundación, área protegida, uso de terrenos y transporte colectivo
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea cada marca como "el conjunto de datos dice esto sobre el punto donde está el marcador". No es una conclusión sobre el edificio ni sobre el solar.

entries.name: How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: The municipality comes from where the map pin sits, tested against Census boundaries. The barrio comes from the same kind of test against Census barrio boundaries.
entries.definition: The municipality and the barrio are set from the pin, not from the address text. The address town is used only while duplicate listings are folded.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Step 1 (used only to fold duplicates): the municipality is the address town when it matches one of the 78 municipality names (ignoring accents and capital letters). Otherwise it is the nearest municipality center. Step 2 (published): after folding, each pin is tested against the Census Bureau's shoreline-clipped municipality polygons. The polygon that contains the pin gives the municipality. Step 3: a pin that is inside no polygon (offshore, or at a gap in the shoreline) takes the municipality whose polygon is nearest (in the 2026-10 snapshot, the nearest municipality center). Step 4: for places counted by default only (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship), the pin is tested against the Census barrio polygons. The first polygon that contains it gives the barrio.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county boundaries and county subdivisions (500k, shoreline-clipped); municipality centers from the observatory's own list.
entries.how_to_read: The published municipality is where the pin is, so counts agree with the boundaries drawn on the map. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 863 places have an address town that names another municipality. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 348 places fall in no municipality polygon and took the nearest center. For example, one beach pin on Mona Island falls outside every polygon and took Rincón, while the other three listings on the island are in Mayagüez. The next full build gives such a pin the nearest polygon instead, which puts that beach in Mayagüez too.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places on the default basis have no barrio, and places of worship and places below the confidence cut never get one.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the barrio layer has 901 polygons and 694 different names, so a barrio name alone can point to several municipalities.

view.label: Map: click a pin to open the place's pop-up

entries.plain_es: El municipio sale de dónde está el marcador del mapa, comparado con los límites del Censo. El barrio sale de la misma prueba con los límites de barrios del Censo.
entries.name_es: Cómo se asignan el municipio y el barrio a un lugar
entries.how_to_read_es: El municipio publicado es donde está el marcador, así que los conteos coinciden con los límites dibujados en el mapa. En el corte de datos 2026-10, 863 lugares tienen en su dirección un pueblo que corresponde a otro municipio. La base predeterminada son los lugares con una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más, sin los lugares de culto.

entries.name: How Overture categories become tourism categories
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: The observatory reads each Overture category and files the place under one of four tourism categories and one type within it (27 types occur in the 2026-10 snapshot). Places that fit none of them are left out, and so are listings that fit a category but are not tourism: homes, housing and care services (since 2026-10-18).
entries.definition: A set of 28 ordered text rules plus a mapping of Overture's top-level groups, both set by the observatory's build script (the tourism taxonomy of Foundation for Puerto Rico). Overture sorts its categories in a tree, and the top level is called a group here (for example food_and_drink). The rules look for words inside Overture's category names, so a match is by text, not by an official code list.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The observatory tests each listing's Overture category name against 28 ordered text rules, and then the listing's Overture group can override the result. The five steps and the 28 rules are listed below.
entries.how_to_read: Read the rules as a ladder: the first match wins, and then the Overture group can override it. When a result looks odd, find the place's Overture category in the Overture category entry, then the rule words in the type's entry.
caveats: The rules match words inside longer words. For example the word trail also matches trailer dealers (6 places in Scenic Areas in the 2026-10 snapshot).

Rule order changes results. Amusement parks and water parks are filed as Parks, bar-and-grill restaurants as Bars, and beach resorts as Lodging. Rental businesses outside the lodging group are not kept, because the word rental matches a Vacation Properties rule before the Transportation or Marinas rule. So the keywords car_rental, bike_rental and scooter_rental in rule 27 never decide a result.
The word plaza in rule 9 does not keep a listing by itself. In the 2026-10 snapshot, public plazas (114) were left out because Overture does not file them under an attractions group.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, 63,117 of 99,323 Overture places are left out (63.5%), among them 3,388 with no category. After duplicates are folded, 2,577 more listings that fit a category are left out because they are not tourism (homes, housing estates, condominiums and care services; see Counted but not drawn). The most common left-out categories are beauty salon (3,167), grocery store (1,478), professional service (1,419), automotive repair (1,419), doctors office (1,280), auto dealer (1,279), gas station (1,250), spa (1,189). Some visitor-related categories are also left out: travel service (295), car rental service (174), travel and transportation with no finer category (146), public plazas (114), farmers markets (61), souvenir stores (53), boat rental and training (23), flea markets (22), travel companies (19), train stations (18), airlines (18), jet skis rental (14), golf courses (13), all-terrain vehicle (ATV) rental tours (9), motorcycle rental service (8) and bike rental (7). Visitor services counts do not include these businesses.

Food Markets is a defined type with no places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Gastronomy is accepted only for listings in Overture's food_and_drink group, and grocery stores and farmers markets sit in Overture's shopping group.
Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) set this grouping. It is not an official or industry classification.
The counts in this entry are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

values.Step 1: Take the category name: Take Overture's primary category for the listing, or its basic category when there is no primary. A listing with neither is left out.
values.Step 2: Test the rules: Test that category name against the 28 rules in order: Attractions rules first, then Gastronomy, Accommodations and Visitor services. The first rule that matches gives a category and a type. If no rule matches the name, test the full category path (the group and parent names joined) the same way.
values.Step 3: Find the Overture group: Find the listing's Overture group: the first of lodging, food_and_drink, cultural_and_historic, arts_and_entertainment or geographic_entities in its path (the rules also recognize the older names accommodation, eat_and_drink and attractions_and_activities). Lodging maps to Accommodations, food_and_drink to Gastronomy and the other three to Attractions.
values.Step 4: Let the group decide: If the listing has such a group, keep it. When the rule's category equals the group's category, the rule's type is used. Otherwise the group's category is used with its default type: Lodging, Restaurants or Tourist Attractions.
values.Step 5: Listings with no group: If the listing has no such group, keep it only when a rule puts it in Visitor services, or in Beaches, Nature Reserves, Scenic Areas, Historic Sites, Museums, Parks or Places of Worship. Everything else is left out.
values.Rule 1: Places of Worship: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains place_of_worship, church, cathedral, chapel, synagogue, mosque, temple or religious.
values.Rule 2: Beaches: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name starts with beach.
values.Rule 3: Parks: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name is exactly park, ends with _park, starts with park_, or contains playground, national_park or state_park.
values.Rule 4: Nature Reserves: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains nature, forest, wildlife, reserve or botanical.
values.Rule 5: Museums: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains museum.
values.Rule 6: Historic Sites: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains historic, monument, fort, castle or ruin.
values.Rule 7: Cultural Attractions: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains art_gallery, theater, theatre, performing_arts, cultural_center, cinema or movie_theater.
values.Rule 8: Scenic Areas: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains scenic, lookout, viewpoint, waterfall, cave, lake, river, island, mountain, hiking_trail or trail.
values.Rule 9: Tourist Attractions: Attractions. Applies when the Overture category name contains tourist, attraction, amusement, zoo, aquarium, water_park, theme_park, observatory, plaza or landmark.
values.Rule 10: Bakeries: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains bakery, pastry, patisserie or donut.
values.Rule 11: Cafes: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains cafe, coffee, tea_room, ice_cream, dessert, juice_bar or bubble_tea.
values.Rule 12: Nightlife: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains night_club, nightclub, karaoke, lounge, dance_club or live_music.
values.Rule 13: Bars: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains the word bar on its own, ends with _bar, starts with bar_, ends with pub, or contains brewery, brewpub, beer_garden, cocktail, sports_bar or wine_bar.
values.Rule 14: Food Markets: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains farmers_market, food_market, public_market or grocery, or ends with market.
values.Rule 15: Food Experiences: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains winery, distillery, coffee_roaster, food_tour or cooking.
values.Rule 16: Restaurants: Gastronomy. Applies when the Overture category name contains restaurant, food_truck, food_stand, diner, pizzeria, steakhouse, seafood, fast_food, cafeteria, eatery, taqueria, bistro, kiosk or chinchorro.
values.Rule 17: Resorts: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains resort.
values.Rule 18: Inns: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains the word inn on its own or bed_and_breakfast.
values.Rule 19: Guest Houses: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains guest_house, guesthouse, hostel or boarding.
values.Rule 20: Vacation Properties: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains vacation, villa, cottage, cabin, holiday, rental, apartment_hotel or condo.
values.Rule 21: Hotels: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains hotel or motel.
values.Rule 22: Lodging: Accommodations. Applies when the Overture category name contains lodging, accommodation, campground, camping or rv_park.
values.Rule 23: Tour Operators: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains tour, travel_agen, excursion or sightseeing.
values.Rule 24: Visitor Centers: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains visitor, tourist_information or information_center.
values.Rule 25: Marinas: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains marina, boat, yacht, harbor, harbour, dock or ferry.
values.Rule 26: Adventure Operators: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains surf, dive, scuba, snorkel, kayak, zipline, zip_line, rafting, horse, adventure, paddle, sailing, fishing_charter or climbing.
values.Rule 27: Transportation: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains car_rental, airport, taxi, bus_station, transit, shuttle, limo, bike_rental or scooter_rental.
values.Rule 28: Cultural Experience Providers: Visitor services. Applies when the Overture category name contains cooking_class, art_class, dance_studio, workshop or artisan.

entries.plain_es: El observatorio lee cada categoría de Overture y clasifica el lugar en una de cuatro categorías turísticas y en un tipo dentro de ella (en el corte de datos de 2026-10 aparecen 27 tipos). Los lugares que no caben en ninguna quedan fuera, y también los listados que caben en una categoría pero no son turismo: viviendas, complejos de viviendas y servicios de cuido (desde el 2026-10-18).
entries.name_es: Cómo las categorías de Overture se convierten en categorías turísticas
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea las reglas como una escalera: gana la primera coincidencia, y luego el grupo de Overture puede cambiarla. Cuando un resultado parezca raro, busque la categoría de Overture del lugar en la ficha de la categoría de Overture y luego las palabras de la regla en la ficha del tipo.

entries.name: How the tourism places file is made
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: The observatory takes the places that Overture Maps lists in Puerto Rico and keeps those that fit four tourism categories. It folds duplicates, adds location and hazard flags, and does not copy the phone, email or social-media fields.
entries.definition: places.json is a list of 32,541 places built from 99,323 Overture records (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026). It is rebuilt with each snapshot of the observatory (Snapshot 2026-10 here). The file is a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) list in UTF-8 text with one object for each place and up to 23 fields per place (26 field names occur in the file). It is not GeoJSON: the position is in the separate fields lat and lng.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Step 1: download every Overture place inside the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57 (all of Puerto Rico, including Mona, Culebra and Vieques) as GeoJSON points (99,323 records in the 2026-10 snapshot). Step 2: classify each record (see the classification entry): in the 2026-10 snapshot, 36,206 fit one of the four categories, and 63,117 are left out. Step 3: fold duplicates (see the duplicates entry): in the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,088 listings are folded into others, which leaves 35,118 listings. Then leave out the listings that are not tourism (homes, housing and care services; see Counted but not drawn): 2,577 in the 2026-10 snapshot, which leaves 32,541 places (since 2026-10-18). Step 4: set the municipality from the pin position. Step 5: test each pin against the FEMA (Federal Emergency Management Agency) flood zones, the PAD-US (Protected Areas Database of the United States) protected areas, the 2015 land-use plan, the transit stops and the barrio boundaries. Step 6: remove the phone, email, social-media, postcode, brand and license fields (see the unpublished fields entry), and write places.json.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026 and cut to the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57. The observatory's build is labeled Snapshot 2026-10.
entries.how_to_read: The file is a snapshot of one Overture release. Places that opened, closed or moved after that release are not in it.
caveats: Coverage depends on what Overture's sources list. A place that no source lists is missing, and a place that has closed can still be listed. The observatory does not check places on the ground.

Licenses: Overture's place records carry the license of each contributing source. In the 2026-10 snapshot the labels are CDLA-Permissive-2.0 (Meta and Microsoft records), Apache-2.0 (Foursquare) and CC0-1.0 (AllThePlaces). Read Overture's terms and each source's terms before you reuse or redistribute the records.
The map credits Overture Maps Foundation contributors for place data.

Counts from two snapshots are not comparable as a time series. A new Overture release can add or drop listings from its sources without any business opening or closing, and the observatory does not track openings and closures.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, coverage follows Meta's: 98.2% of the places (31,945 of 32,541) list Meta as the source, so the mix of categories mostly reflects what Meta lists.
