entries.plain_es: El observatorio toma los lugares que Overture Maps lista en Puerto Rico y se queda con los que caben en cuatro categorías turísticas. Une los duplicados, agrega indicadores de ubicación y de riesgo, y no copia los campos de teléfono, correo electrónico ni redes sociales.
entries.name_es: Cómo se hace el archivo de lugares turísticos
entries.how_to_read_es: El archivo es un corte de datos de una versión de Overture. Los lugares que abrieron, cerraron o se mudaron después de esa versión no están en él.

entries.name: How to read a missing value in the places file
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: A field that is empty for a place is left out of the file instead of being written as blank or false. So a missing flood zone, protected area or barrio means no value was found, not that the value is zero.
entries.definition: The observatory does not write a field when its value is missing, false, an empty text or an empty list. That is why the yes flags (sfha and transit_400m) appear only as true, and why optional fields appear on some places and not on others.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The build removes every field whose value is missing, false, an empty text or an empty list, when it writes each place. Numbers, including 0, are kept.
entries.how_to_read: A missing value is not a measured zero and is not a promise of safety. Read the notes below for each field. In a spreadsheet, an empty cell means the same as a missing field.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot every place has category, type, overture_category, municipality, confidence, source, duplicates and transit_m, and every place the map draws also has oid, name, lat, lng, nearest_stop and updated. The build would leave out name, source or updated for a record that has none.

values.sfha: Missing means the pin was not found inside a Special Flood Hazard Area. Present only as true.
values.transit_400m: Missing means the nearest mapped stop of any kind is more than 400 m away. Present only as true.
values.flood_zone: Missing means the pin is in no mapped Special Flood Hazard Area or 0.2% annual chance area. It may be in unshaded zone X (minimal hazard), in zone D (possible but undetermined flood hazard; 17 places in the 2026-10 snapshot), or outside the area FEMA mapped.
values.flood_subtype: Missing means the place has no flood zone, or its zone has no subtype.
values.protected_area: Missing means the pin is in no PAD-US area (proclamation boundaries do not count).
values.barrio: Missing means the place is not counted by default (worship or below the confidence cut), or its pin is in no barrio polygon.
values.land_use: Missing means the pin is in no land-use plan polygon (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 173 places; the largest groups are in San Juan, Fajardo, Culebra and Cabo Rojo, and all 4 places on Mona Island are among them).
values.has_website: Missing means no source gave a website, or the value held an email address. The web address itself is never published.
values.withheld: Missing means the map draws the place. Present on the places counted but not drawn, which also have no oid, name, lat, lng, nearest_stop or updated.
values.hub_400m: Present only as true, and only on a place the map does not draw.
values.duplicates: Never missing. A place with no folded listings shows 0.
values.transit_m: Never missing. A place at a stop shows 0.
values.ts_m, ts_calls and ts_we (place_access.j: Never missing: the file holds one value for each place, in the order of places.json. ts_calls 0 means no stop with a current timetable within 400 m. ts_we 0 means no stop with a current timetable within 400 m, or no Saturday or Sunday service in the published timetable. ts_m is 99,999 at most.

entries.plain_es: Un campo vacío para un lugar se omite del archivo en vez de escribirse en blanco o como falso. Así que, si falta la zona inundable, el área protegida o el barrio, significa que no se encontró un valor, no que el valor sea cero.
entries.name_es: Cómo leer un valor que falta en el archivo de lugares
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor que falta no es un cero medido ni una garantía de seguridad. Lea las notas de cada campo más abajo. En una hoja de cálculo, una celda vacía significa lo mismo que un campo que falta.

entries.name: Which places the observatory counts (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship)
entries.group: Tourism places: how the data are made
entries.plain: Unless you change the filter, the observatory counts a place only when Overture's confidence score is 0.50 or higher and it is not a place of worship. In the 2026-10 snapshot, that gives 24,209 tourism places.
entries.definition: The default basis is: confidence of 0.50 or higher, and a type other than Places of Worship. In the 2026-10 snapshot, of the 32,541 places in the file, 5,032 are places of worship and 3,300 more score below 0.50, which leaves 24,209. In this entry a listing is one record about a place in Overture's data (name, location, category, source), and a pin is the point on the map where a place's coordinates sit. After duplicates are folded, the observatory keeps one listing for each place.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The observatory's build sets the minimum confidence to 0.50. The place counts and shares in municipalities.json (assets, by_category, in_sfha, in_flood_zone, in_protected, with_website, avg_confidence, sfha_pct, places_near_transit, transit_pct, access_n, the acc_ shares and the per-resident and per-km2 rates) and every count in barrios.geojson use that basis. Three exceptions: assets_all_confidence and listings_all, which are meant to show other bases, and places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct, which count every listing in the file that has a land-use class (32,369 of 32,541 in the 2026-10 snapshot), including places of worship and places below 0.50. meta.json records the cut as min_confidence. The 2D map starts at the same value: the Minimum confidence slider runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05, and the Include places of worship box starts off. The 3D view always uses 0.50 and hides places of worship. A place that scores exactly 0.50 is counted.
entries.how_to_read: Use the slider when you want a stricter or looser list. On a municipality profile, the place count, flood share, protected share, website count and transit share follow your filters. Places per 1,000 residents, places per km2 and the ranks always use the default basis, so they can disagree with the count beside them. The CSV (comma-separated values) of one municipality's places follows your filters. The CSV of all municipalities (rankings and shading) uses the default basis. In the 2026-10 snapshot, a basis with no confidence cut and no worship holds 27,509 places.
caveats: The 0.50 cut is the observatory's own choice, not an Overture rule.
The cut matters. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory counts 24,209 places at 0.50. With no cut and no places of worship it would count 27,509.
The cut removes more places of some types than others, and in the 2026-10 snapshot all 3,574 places below 0.50 are Meta records. See the confidence score entry.
The municipal land-use place shares (places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct) do not follow this basis.
Folding duplicates can also remove places from the default count. See the duplicates entry.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: category chips, Minimum confidence slider and the places-of-worship box

entries.plain_es: Si no se cambia el filtro, el observatorio cuenta un lugar solo cuando la puntuación de confianza de Overture es de 0.50 o más y no es un lugar de culto. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, eso da 24,209 lugares turísticos.
entries.name_es: Qué lugares cuenta el observatorio (confianza de 0.50 o más, sin lugares de culto)
entries.how_to_read_es: Use el control deslizante para obtener una lista más estricta o más amplia. En el perfil de un municipio, el conteo de lugares, la proporción en zonas inundables, la proporción en áreas protegidas, el conteo de sitios web y la proporción con acceso al transporte colectivo siguen los filtros elegidos. Los lugares por cada 1,000 residentes, los lugares por km² y las posiciones siempre usan la base predeterminada, así que pueden no coincidir con el conteo que aparece al lado. El CSV (valores separados por comas) de los lugares de un municipio sigue los filtros elegidos. El CSV de todos los municipios (posiciones y sombreado) usa la base predeterminada. En el corte de datos 2026-10, una base sin límite de confianza y sin lugares de culto tiene 27,509 lugares.

entries.name: Barrio of the place
entries.plain: The barrio where the place's pin sits. A barrio is a sub-municipal district that the Census Bureau calls a county subdivision. Only places counted by default have one.
entries.definition: The name of the Census barrio (the Census Bureau calls it a county subdivision) that contains the pin. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 23,884 places have one: every place on the default basis except 325. Places of worship and places below the confidence cut have none.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test against Census barrio boundaries, run only for places counted by default (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship). The first matching polygon is used. See 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county subdivisions (barrios), 500k, shoreline-clipped; field BASENAME.
entries.how_to_read: Always read the barrio together with the municipality. Many barrio names repeat: in the barrio layer of the 2026-10 snapshot, 133 of the 694 barrio names occur in more than one municipality (for example Collores or Playa). Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 325 places on the default basis have no barrio because their pin falls in no barrio polygon. Almost all of them (323) are also outside the shoreline municipality polygons, that is offshore or at the shoreline.
The barrio is the Census Bureau's subdivision. It is not always the neighborhood name people use.
The place pop-up does not show the barrio. It is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download of a municipality's places.

view.label: Map, Municipality tab: a municipality's places, with a CSV download that has a barrio column (example: San Juan)
Map, Map layers tab: Barrios layer (click inside a barrio for its counts)

entries.plain_es: El barrio donde está el marcador del lugar. Un barrio es una división dentro del municipio que el Negociado del Censo llama subdivisión de condado. Solo lo tienen los lugares que se cuentan con los filtros predeterminados.
entries.name_es: Barrio del lugar
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea siempre el barrio junto con el municipio. Muchos nombres de barrio se repiten: en la capa de barrios del corte de datos 2026-10, 133 de los 694 nombres de barrio aparecen en más de un municipio (por ejemplo, Collores o Playa). La base predeterminada son los lugares con una puntuación de confianza de 0.50 o más, sin los lugares de culto.

entries.name: Counted but not drawn: the reason
entries.plain: Why a place is counted in its municipality but not shown on the map: a holiday rental, or a rented unit named by its street address or unit number. Homes, housing and care services are not tourism and are not in the file at all (since 2026-10-18).
entries.definition: One of two reasons, present only on places the map does not draw: holiday_rental (a holiday rental: an entire home, cabin, cottage or apartment rented for short stays) and address (the name is a street address, a house, lot or unit number, or holds a postcode, and the listing is filed as a hotel, B&B, holiday rental, cabin or campground, or as a business such as a restaurant). In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,005 of 32,541 places are withheld (holiday_rental 971, address 34), and 742 of them are among the 24,209 places on the default basis (holiday_rental 715, address 27). Three more reasons, residence (a private home, or a listing named after a private person), residential (a residential building, condominium, housing estate or subdivision, or a lodging listing that names no accommodation) and sensitive (an elderly or children's home, a shelter, rehabilitation or addiction treatment, a hospice and similar), and an address-named listing filed where homes are filed, mean the listing is not tourism: since 2026-10-18 it is left out of the file and of every count (HANDOFF decision 47). That left out 2,577 listings (residential 2,301, residence 157, address 67, sensitive 52), 2,370 of them on the default basis.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: places_privacy.py decides from the Overture category and the name, with a reviewed list of exceptions (places_review.json): a sensitive word or a street address in the name withholds a place in any category; home words (Casa, Residencia, Hacienda, Villa...) and housing words (Urb., Residencial, Condominio, Apartments...) withhold it in the categories where Meta users file homes (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar), unless the name also names an accommodation business or a public venue; and a lodging listing must name an accommodation. Holiday rentals (owner decision of 2026-10-18, HANDOFF decision 48) are withheld by category (holiday rental home, cabin, cottage, service apartment) and, in the lodging categories, by a name that says so (Vacation Rental, Beach House, Airbnb, Short Term Rental, Tiny House, ... Rentals, ... Stays) and, in the hotel, B&B, hostel and campground categories, by a name that rents a unit (... Apartment, Casita ..., Penthouse ..., Studio, Bungalow, Cabin, Chalet, Cottage, Villa 12, ... House, ... Home, ... Villa), a run of units (... Apartments, Condominio ...) or a house called Casa or Villa and one word, alone or followed by a town, municipio or neighbourhood, unless the name also names a hotel, guest house, inn, B&B, hostel, posada, parador or resort; hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs stay drawn, and real guest houses, hostels and aparthotels with such names are drawn by review. A home word followed by a unit or house number (Casa ... 28) withholds a place in any category. A listing withheld as residence, residential or sensitive, or as address in a category where homes are filed (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar; a numbered holiday rental there is recorded as holiday_rental), is not tourism and is dropped before every count (places_privacy.not_tourism, decision 47 of 2026-10-18). A listing whose name also says holiday rental is recorded as holiday_rental (counted, not drawn) unless the name says housing clearly: a subdivision or estate word (Urb., Residencial, Estancias, Villas de...), a condominium or apartment building named as such (Condominio, Edificio, Torre), or a neighbourhood, sector or barrio of the gazetteer within 3 km. Outside the lodging category, Edificio, Edif. and Building alone do not say housing. A withheld place keeps the fields the counts use (municipality, barrio, category, type, Overture category, confidence, source, flood, protected-area, land-use and transit fields) and loses its name, Overture ID, coordinates, nearest stop and update date; its confidence is cut down to a multiple of 0.05, the step of the map's filter, and its distances to a stop and departures (transit_m here, ts_m, tw_m, ts_calls and tw_calls in place_access.json) to one value per class, so every count stays the same. The withheld rows come after all the drawn ones, sorted by their own fields, because Overture's order follows location. hub_400m (true or missing, only on a withheld place) says whether a rail station or ferry terminal is within 400 m, so the nightly transit refresh can still count the place. Owner rule of 2026-10-18; guide: docs/places-privacy.md.
entries.how_to_read: These places are in every count and share (the Municipality tab, the choropleths of places shown, municipalities.json, barrios.geojson). They are not pins, hexagons, search results, list rows or CSV rows. They are tourism supply: 3.1% of the counted places in the 2026-10 snapshot. Until 2026-10-18 the counts also included the homes, housing and care services that Overture's sources filed under tourism categories: 2,370 of the 26,579 places then counted (8.9%). Since then they are left out, and every count and share was rebuilt without them (decision 47).
caveats: Overture gives no ownership or use field. The patterns can miss a home or hold back a public place; places_review.json lists the reviewed exceptions with their reasons.
A withheld place keeps the transit distances of the last full build: the nightly refresh cannot measure it again without its point.

values.holiday_rental: A holiday rental: an entire home, cabin, cottage or apartment rented for short stays, by its Overture category or a name that says so (971 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Hotels, guest houses, inns and B&Bs are drawn.
values.residence: A private home, or a listing named only after a private person. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (157 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.residential: A residential building, condominium, public housing estate or subdivision, or a lodging listing that names no accommodation. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (2,301 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.address: The name is a street address, a house, lot or unit number, or holds a postcode, and the listing is filed as a hotel, B&B, holiday rental, cabin or campground (a numbered unit rented to visitors) or as a business (34). The same names filed where homes are filed (lodging, historic site, park, beach and similar) are numbered homes and flats: not tourism, left out since 2026-10-18 (67).
values.sensitive: An elderly or children's home, a shelter, rehabilitation or addiction treatment, a hospice, a care, foster or recovery home (including one named 'Hogar ...' and filed under a lodging category) or a similar service. Not in the file since 2026-10-18: not tourism, so left out of every count (52 listings in the 2026-10 snapshot). The observatory publishes treatment facilities as counts only (community_series.json).

entries.name: Latitude and longitude of the place
entries.plain: The position of the place's pin on the map, as latitude and longitude.
entries.definition: Latitude and longitude of the listing's point, in decimal degrees (WGS 84, the World Geodetic System 1984 that GPS (Global Positioning System) and web maps use), rounded to 6 decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, latitudes run from 17.884134 to 18.515153 and longitudes from -67.940187 to -65.227658. The 1,005 places the map does not draw have no coordinates in the file (see Counted but not drawn).

entries.method: Copied from the Overture record's point and rounded to 6 decimals. Every flag in the file (municipality, barrio, flood zone, protected area, land-use class and transit distance) is computed from this point.
entries.how_to_read: The pin is where a source says the place is. It can sit on the street, at an entrance or in the middle of a lot.
caveats: Six decimals show the precision of the number, not the accuracy of the position. The source decides how accurate the pin is, and the observatory does not check it on the ground.
A place is one point. A beach, a river or a park appears as one pin, not as its shape or length.
Because every flag uses the pin, a pin a few meters off can change a flag, for example when it sits near the edge of a flood zone or a barrio.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, 2,012 of the 31,536 places with a pin (6.4%) share an exact pin with at least one other place, at 614 locations (up to 23 places on one pin). The distance-based flags treat such places as being at the same spot, and the map groups close pins into clusters, so the pins you can see are fewer than the places.

entries.method: Set by the build from the first website of the Overture record (websites[0]). The web address is not written to the file: the observatory publishes no business contact detail (owner rule of 2026-10-18; see Fields the observatory does not publish). entries.how_to_read: A website means at least one source lists an online address for the place. It does not mean the place is open, that the site works or that it is the business's own site. caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot as first built (35,118 places, before 2026-10-18), many listed websites were not a business's own site: 886 (9.1%) were Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or X (Twitter) pages, 175 were Google Maps or goo.gl short links and 28 were WhatsApp links. The count of places with a website is therefore not a count of places with their own site.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, the municipal figure with_website adds up to the same 7,210 places on the default basis. Before 2026-10-18 it was one more than this field (7,441 against 7,440), because one website was counted before an email address was removed from it; that listing is no longer counted.

entries.name: Municipality of the place
entries.plain: The municipio where the place's pin sits, using Census boundaries. It can differ from the town named in the address.
entries.definition: The name of one of Puerto Rico's 78 municipalities, spelled with accents (for example Bayamón or Mayagüez). Every place has one.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Point-in-polygon test of the pin against Census municipality boundaries that are generalized and clipped to the shoreline. A pin that falls in no boundary takes the municipality whose boundary is nearest (muni_locate.py); in the 2026-10 snapshot it took the nearest municipality center. See 'How municipality and barrio are assigned to a place'.
entries.source_detail: Overture places; US Census Bureau TIGERweb generalized county boundaries (500k, shoreline-clipped, Generalized_ACS2023 service); municipality centers from the observatory's own list of 78 municipalities.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to count or compare places by municipality. Every count of places per municipality in the observatory uses this field. Default basis means a confidence score of 0.50 or higher and no places of worship.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the address names a different municipality than the one the pin falls in for 863 places (2.7% of the file). 325 places have no town in the address, and 590 more have a town text that is not one of the 78 municipality names.

Pins just offshore or at the shoreline can fall outside every boundary polygon. In the 2026-10 snapshot that is 348 places (1.1%). The 2026-10 build gave them the nearest municipality center, which can differ from the municipality next to the pin; the next full build gives them the nearest boundary, which moves 60 of them.
Boundaries are the Census Bureau's generalized lines, not legal survey lines.

A count of places is not a rate. Larger and more populous municipalities have more places: in the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has 3,424 places on the default basis and Maricao 36. To compare municipalities, use places per 1,000 residents or per km2. A rate per resident is high where visitors are many compared with residents.

entries.name: Place ID (Overture)
entries.plain: A long code that identifies the place in Overture Maps. Use it to find the same place in Overture's own data.
entries.definition: The Overture Maps identifier of the listing the observatory kept for the place: a 36-character code. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 31,536 places have one and all are different. The 1,005 places the map does not draw have none (see Counted but not drawn).

entries.method: Copied from the Overture record. When duplicate listings are folded into one place, the kept listing's ID is published and the IDs of the folded listings are not.
entries.how_to_read: Treat it as a label. The code says nothing about the place itself.
caveats: Overture sets its own rules for how an ID carries from one release to the next. Read Overture's documentation before you match the 2026-10 snapshot to another release.

The map's pop-ups do not show the ID. It is in the downloaded file and in the CSV (comma-separated values) download of a municipality's places. That CSV holds the places that pass your current filters.

entries.name: Place name
entries.plain: The name Overture lists for the place, as its sources wrote it. A place the map does not draw has no name in the file.
entries.definition: Overture's primary name for the listing. Every place the map draws has one; the 1,005 places it does not draw have none (see Counted but not drawn). In the 2026-10 snapshot, the file holds 28,775 different names for 31,536 places, because chains such as fast-food brands have many outlets.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Copied from the Overture record (names.primary). The observatory does not translate names, fix spelling or change capital letters. It removes a telephone number or an email address written into a name (4 names held a telephone number in the 2026-10 snapshot).
entries.how_to_read: The map search matches names. Two places can share a name, so use the place ID or the coordinates to tell them apart.
caveats: Some names carry extra words that a source added, such as a town or the country (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 537 names contain 'Puerto Rico' in any capital letters, for example 'Jardín Japonés, Ponce, Puerto Rico').
Spanish and English spellings both occur, so one place can be listed under different names. The observatory folds only some of these as duplicates.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 353 names start or end with a blank space (351 end with one and 2 start with one), because the observatory does not clean names. Trim them before you match or join on name.

Names are copied as written, except that a telephone number or an email address is removed. A listing named only after a private person, or by a street address, and a holiday rental are not drawn and have no name in the file; a few names may still look like the names of individual professionals who run a business. Check a name before you republish it outside the observatory.

Every record also lists Overture's own confidence calculation, and in the 2026-10 snapshot 11 records add an Overture-signals entry (an Overture operating-status signal, with version dates 2026-05-11 and 2026-06-15). The observatory does not publish those entries.

The observatory's build is labeled Snapshot 2026-10. Field: the dataset name of the first entry in the record's sources list (sources[0].dataset).

Overture's places theme is open data under the licenses of its sources. It is not public-domain government data.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, coverage follows Meta's: 31,945 of the 32,541 places (98.2%) list Meta as the source, so the mix of categories mostly reflects what Meta lists.

entries.plain: How many other listings the observatory folded into this place because they looked like the same place. Most places have 0.
entries.definition: A whole number, 0 or more. A value above 0 means the place stands for that many extra listings that the observatory merged. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 43, 691 places have at least one folded listing, and the folded listings add up to 1,005.

entries.method: Set by the de-duplication step: the size of the group of matching listings minus 1, because the kept listing is not counted. See 'How duplicate listings are folded'.
entries.how_to_read: The map pop-up says how many duplicate listings were folded. A high number often means a neighborhood or landmark name that many listings share, not one busy place. A value above 0 means listings were removed from the count. It does not mean the place is large or popular.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, places by number of folded listings: 0: 31,850; 1: 574; 2: 69; 3: 23. The largest values are 43 and 36, and 7 places have 10 or more.
Large groups can merge different places that share a neighborhood word. See 'How duplicate listings are folded'.

Un número alto suele indicar un nombre de vecindario o de lugar emblemático que comparten muchos listados, no un solo lugar muy concurrido. Un valor mayor que 0 significa que se quitaron listados del conteo. No significa que el lugar sea grande o popular.

entries.name: Overture confidence score
entries.plain: Overture's own score, from 0 to 1, for a listing. The map's Map layers tab describes it as Overture's estimate that a listing is a real, current place. The observatory counts places at 0.50 or higher by default.
entries.definition: A number from 0 to 1 with three decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, it runs from 0.024 to 1.000, the middle value is 0.83, 128 places score exactly 1, 14 score exactly 0.50 and 3,574 (11.0%) score below 0.50.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Copied from the Overture record and rounded to 3 decimals. Each record names an Overture 'confidence calculation' as the source of this value. In the 2026-10 snapshot, for 30,817 places (94.7%) it equals the score on the record from the contributing source (mostly Meta), and for the other 1,724 it differs. The observatory does not change it, except on a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn): there the score is cut down to a multiple of 0.05, the step of the map's confidence filter (0.57 is written 0.55), so every count at every filter setting is the same and the exact score is not published. The figures in the definition are for the scores Overture gives.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1 (downloaded 1 October 2026); field confidence. The Overture documentation (docs.overturemaps.org/guides/places/) explains how the score is built. The confidence-calculation entry on each record has version 2026-09-17.
entries.how_to_read: A higher score means Overture is more confident in the listing. It is an estimate, not a rating of quality and not a measure of how many people visit.
caveats: The observatory does not check places on the ground, so a high score does not prove that a place is open today. The map's Map layers tab describes the score as an estimate that a listing is a real, current place.
The observatory's default cut at 0.50 is its own choice, not an Overture rule. See 'Which places the observatory counts'.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, all 3,574 listings below 0.50 are Meta records (11.2% of Meta's 31,945). No Foursquare, Microsoft or AllThePlaces record scores below 0.50, so the cut filters only Meta records.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, scores look different by source: 251 of 252 Foursquare places score exactly 0.77, 137 of 241 Microsoft places score 0.85 and 77 of 103 AllThePlaces places score 0.80, while Meta scores take 948 different values. The score does not rank places within those three sources.
The cut also removes more places of some types than others. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 0.50 cut removes 27% of Vacation Properties and 3% of Beaches.

entries.plain_es: La puntuación propia de Overture, de 0 a 1, para un listado. La pestaña Capas del mapa la describe como el estimado de Overture de que un listado es un lugar real y actual. El observatorio cuenta por defecto los lugares con 0.50 o más.
entries.name_es: Puntuación de confianza de Overture
entries.how_to_read_es: Una puntuación más alta significa que Overture tiene más confianza en el listado. Es un estimado, no una calificación de calidad ni una medida de cuántas personas visitan el lugar.

entries.name: Source record update date
entries.plain: The date a data source last updated its record for the place. For most places it is the date of the source's data version, not the date anyone checked the place.
entries.definition: A date (YYYY-MM-DD) taken from the update time of the first source record in the Overture record. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the dates of the 31,536 places the map draws run from 2020-11-19 to 2026-09-14, 31,109 (98.6%) show a date in 2026, and 30,057 (95.3%) share the single date 2026-09-14. A place the map does not draw has no date in the file (see Counted but not drawn): with the other fields it could single the place out.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: The first 10 characters of the update time of the first source record in the Overture record.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026 and cut to the box west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57. The observatory's build is labeled Snapshot 2026-10. Field: the first 10 characters of sources[0].update_time.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, for the 31,049 drawn places (98.5%) that come from Meta or AllThePlaces, the date equals the version label of the source record (for example 2026-09-14), so it marks a data version, not a visit to the place or a change to it. For Foursquare and Microsoft records the date differs from the version label. Do not use the date to judge whether a listing is current or stale.
caveats: A source can update a record without anyone visiting the place.
The map pop-up does not show this date. It is in the downloaded file and in CSV (comma-separated values) exports. The CSV of a municipality's places holds the places that pass your current filters.

entries.plain_es: La fecha en que una fuente de datos actualizó por última vez su registro del lugar. Para la mayoría de los lugares es la fecha de la versión de datos de la fuente, no la fecha en que alguien verificó el lugar.
entries.name_es: Fecha de actualización del registro de origen
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, para los 31,049 lugares dibujados (98.5%) que provienen de Meta o AllThePlaces, la fecha es igual a la etiqueta de versión del registro de origen (por ejemplo, 2026-09-14). Por eso marca una versión de los datos, no una visita al lugar ni un cambio en él. En los registros de Foursquare y Microsoft, la fecha es distinta de la etiqueta de versión. No use la fecha para juzgar si un listado está vigente o desactualizado.

entries.name: Attraction listings
entries.plain: How many attractions (historic sites, parks, beaches, museums, venues and similar) Overture Maps lists in each municipality. Places of worship are not counted.
entries.definition: The Analysis tab's 'Attraction listings' dataset. It reads the key ATTRACTIONS of the field by_category in municipalities.json: counted places (confidence 0.50 or higher) that the observatory's keyword rules (RULES in build.py) put in the Attractions category, with places of worship left out. Types present: historic sites, parks, beaches, tourist attractions, cultural attractions (galleries, theatres, cinemas), scenic areas, museums and nature reserves. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 municipalities.
entries.method: site/js/economy.js, function ecLoad, helper snap. When the Analysis tab opens, the browser reads municipalities.json (key ATTRACTIONS of by_category) and builds a one-year series for each of the 78 municipalities. The Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78 values. The only year is the year of the snapshot date in meta.json (2026 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Nothing is stored in economy_series.json. The observatory assigns each listing to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin; a pin outside every boundary, such as one offshore, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment). See economy.tourism_supply_layers.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; classified and de-duplicated by the observatory (build.py); placed in municipalities by map pin with Census TIGERweb generalized 500k boundaries. The Analysis tab reads the key ATTRACTIONS of the field by_category of municipalities.json in the browser (Snapshot 2026-10).
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (645), then Ponce 198, Carolina 157; the fewest are Las Marías and Naranjito, 12 each, then Florida 13. Divide by residents or land area before comparing places.
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors. Overture builds its listings from several sources, and some are closed, moved, wrong or missing; the confidence score is Overture's and has not been checked on the ground.

Listings whose Overture category contains words such as church, chapel, temple or religious are left out of every count, even when a visitor would count a church as a sight. In the 2026-10 snapshot, that is 5,032 listings island-wide, including 1,169 religious organizations and 67 religious schools (see municipalities.counting_rules).

In the same snapshot, the type Tourist Attractions (783 listings) is a catch-all that includes, among the counted listings, arts and entertainment venues (234), stadiums and arenas (159), dance clubs (81), bridges (38) and casinos (26). The type Historic Sites is 22% of the category (1,010 listings), almost all of them Overture's generic 'historic site' label (952). The 24 counted listings that Overture classes as marinas (26 in the places file) are filed here, not under visitor services.
The de-duplication rules can leave two listings for one place (see municipalities.counting_rules), so the count is not a count of distinct sites.

The data come from Overture release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026. Listings were last updated by their sources between November 2020 and September 2026, so the count does not describe a single date.

There is only one snapshot, so these layers show no growth or decline. The tab's year control does not change them, and they have no 'change since the base year' option, no trend chart and no small trend line. The '% of the Puerto Rico total' option compares municipalities within the same snapshot.

The source record states Overture's licenses as CDLA-Permissive 2.0 (Meta, Microsoft and others), Apache 2.0 (Foursquare) and CC0 1.0 (AllThePlaces); which applies depends on who contributed the record. Check the source's terms and credit line before reuse.

entries.name: How the Analysis tab builds its tourism supply layers
entries.group: Tourism supply layers on the Analysis tab
entries.plain: The five tourism supply layers on the Analysis tab count Overture Maps listings in each municipality. The page works them out from the municipality data when the tab opens. They are not stored with the other Economy series.
entries.definition: Five datasets in the Analysis tab's 'Tourism supply' group: economy.tourism_places (field assets), and economy.lodging_places, economy.gastronomy_places, economy.attractions_places and economy.visitor_services_places (the keys ACCOMMODATIONS, GASTRONOMY, ATTRACTIONS and VISITOR_SERVICES of the field by_category). Each is a count of listings per municipality in one snapshot. Each is marked 'static' in the code: it has one year, the year of the snapshot date, and the tab shows it whichever year is chosen.
entries.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (the sum of the 78)

coverage.frequency: One snapshot, rebuilt with each snapshot (current: Snapshot 2026-10).

entries.method: site/js/economy.js, function ecLoad, helper snap. Municipality values come from S.muni, which is municipalities.json read by the map page; the Puerto Rico value is the sum of the 78. The year of the series is the first four characters of generated_at in meta.json (2026 in the 2026-10 snapshot). Because each layer is static, the year control does not change it; 'change since the base year', the trend chart and the small trend line are not offered; and 'same classes in every year' does not apply. Options for counts: as published; per 1,000 residents (the default when shading; population from the Housing series for the latest year at or before the snapshot year, which is 2025 in the 2026-10 snapshot); per km² (land_km2 of municipalities.json); % of the Puerto Rico total; percentile among municipalities. The 'location quotient' and '% of the municipality's jobs' options are offered for jobs series only, not for these counts.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; classified and de-duplicated by the observatory (build.py); placed in municipalities by map pin with Census TIGERweb generalized 500k boundaries. The Analysis tab reads the fields assets and by_category of municipalities.json in the browser (Snapshot 2026-10).
entries.how_to_read: Use these layers to see where visitor-facing places are concentrated, and put them next to jobs, income or hazard layers. Shade them per resident or per square kilometre, because raw counts mostly show which municipalities are big; raw counts suit sized symbols. The year control does not change these layers: when you pick an earlier year for another layer, you are pairing it with the listings of the 2026-10 snapshot.
caveats: They are not jobs, sales or visitors. For visitor-economy jobs see economy.tourism_jobs.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the four category layers add up to the tourism places layer in every municipality.

The observatory holds one snapshot, so these layers have no earlier value to compare with. If a later snapshot is added, a change between snapshots will partly reflect changes in Overture's sources and in the observatory's rules, not only places opening or closing.

A listing is placed by its map pin; in the 2026-10 snapshot, 324 of the 24,209 counted listings have pins outside every municipal boundary and went to the municipality with the nearest centre; the next full build gives them the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment and municipalities.counting_rules).

The data come from Overture release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026. Listings were last updated by their sources between November 2020 and September 2026, so the count does not describe a single date.

The source record states Overture's licenses as CDLA-Permissive 2.0 (Meta, Microsoft and others), Apache 2.0 (Foursquare) and CC0 1.0 (AllThePlaces); which applies depends on who contributed the record. Check the source's terms and credit line before reuse.

entries.name_es: Cómo construye la pestaña Análisis sus capas de oferta turística
entries.how_to_read_es: Use estas capas para ver dónde se concentran los lugares orientados a visitantes, y póngalas junto a las capas de empleos, ingreso o riesgos. Sombréelas por residente o por kilómetro cuadrado, porque los conteos absolutos muestran sobre todo qué municipios son grandes; los conteos absolutos se prestan para símbolos de tamaño variable. El control de año no cambia estas capas: si elige un año anterior para otra capa, la está combinando con los listados del corte de datos 2026-10.

The observatory assigns each listing to the municipality whose boundary contains its map pin; a pin outside every boundary, such as one offshore, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest (see methods.municipality_assignment). See economy.tourism_supply_layers.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01; classified and de-duplicated by the observatory (build.py); placed in municipalities by map pin with Census TIGERweb generalized 500k boundaries. The Analysis tab reads the field assets of municipalities.json in the browser (Snapshot 2026-10).
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan has the most (3,424, 14.1% of the island) and Maricao the fewest (36). A shaded map of raw counts mostly shows which municipalities are big. On the Analysis tab, shading starts at 'per 1,000 residents', which divides by the latest population estimate in the Housing series (July 2025 in the 2026-10 snapshot); it differs slightly from municipalities.assets_per_1000_residents, which divides by the 2020 Census count. 'Per km²' divides by land area in square kilometres (municipalities.land_km2).
caveats: It counts listings, not businesses, rooms, beds or visitors. Overture builds its listings from several sources, and some are closed, moved, wrong or missing; the confidence score is Overture's and has not been checked on the ground.
Places of worship and listings with a confidence below 0.50 are left out, so the count is lower than the number of all listings (see municipalities.counting_rules).

In the 2026-10 snapshot, about two in three counted places are restaurants, bars and cafés (17,170 of 24,209), so this is not a measure of visitor demand. In the same snapshot, per-resident values are highest in small, visitor-heavy municipalities (Culebra 78.4, Vieques 30.1 and Rincón 28.4 per 1,000 residents, against 7.6 for Puerto Rico) because visitors and second-home owners are not in the denominator.

The data come from Overture release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026. Listings were last updated by their sources between November 2020 and September 2026, so the count does not describe a single date.

There is only one snapshot, so these layers show no growth or decline. The tab's year control does not change them, and they have no 'change since the base year' option, no trend chart and no small trend line. The '% of the Puerto Rico total' option compares municipalities within the same snapshot.

The source record states Overture's licenses as CDLA-Permissive 2.0 (Meta, Microsoft and others), Apache 2.0 (Foursquare) and CC0 1.0 (AllThePlaces); which applies depends on who contributed the record. Check the source's terms and credit line before reuse.
These counts and the tourism jobs series (economy.tourism_jobs) measure different things: listings in a snapshot versus employees at covered employers over a year.

entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, la isla tiene 617 listados de seis tipos: transporte 173 (aeropuertos 112, estaciones de guaguas 24, terminales de aeropuerto 13, servicios de taxi 10, helipuertos 8, servicios de limosina 3 y servicios de transporte al aeropuerto 3), operadores de aventura 148, operadores turísticos 116, proveedores de experiencias culturales 101, marinas 74 y centros de visitantes 5. San Juan tiene la mayor cantidad (134), seguido de Carolina con 58 y Fajardo con 49. Nueve municipios no tienen ninguno: Aguas Buenas, Barranquitas, Corozal, Florida, Hormigueros, Juana Díaz, Maricao, San Lorenzo y San Sebastián. Un cero aquí significa que Overture no registra ningún lugar de este tipo en el conjunto contado; no significa que los visitantes no puedan encontrar estos servicios allí. entries.name: Date the access fields are computed as of (date)
entries.plain: The date against which the observatory judged whether each operator's timetable had ended when it computed the access fields. Quote it with any access figure.
entries.definition: A date written YYYY-MM-DD. The observatory counts a stop as having a current timetable when its operator's feed end date is on or after this date. It applies to acc_cur400_pct, acc_cur800_pct, acc_freq400_pct, acc_sat400_pct, acc_sun400_pct, acc_paper_pct, stops_current and stops_expired. All 78 municipalities carry the same date. The same date is as_of in place_access.json and as_of in the access part of meta.json.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access is as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

entries.method: access.py sets it to the build date at a full build and to the run date in the nightly refresh. When a run changes no value, the files are not rewritten and the date does not move.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026; tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR)); stops and feed end dates from transport.json and operators.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot it is 2026-10-06, four days after the feeds were read (2026-10-02). A feed that ends after this date counts as current in the stored values. An older date means that no value has changed since then, not that the refresh did not run.
caveats: The stored values describe timetables on this date. They can be out of date by the time you read them if a feed has ended since and the next run has not written the change yet.
entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2026-10-06 in all 78 municipalities.
entries.plain_es: La fecha con la que el observatorio juzgó si el horario de cada operador había terminado cuando calculó los campos de acceso. Cítela junto con cualquier cifra de acceso.
entries.name_es: Fecha de referencia de los campos de acceso (fecha)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10 es el 2026-10-06, cuatro días después de que se leyeron las fuentes de horarios (2026-10-02). Una fuente de horarios que termina después de esta fecha cuenta como vigente en los valores guardados. Una fecha más antigua significa que ningún valor ha cambiado desde entonces, no que la actualización no se haya ejecutado.

entries.name: Distance to the nearest mapped stop of any kind (m)
entries.plain: The straight-line distance in meters from the place to the nearest mapped stop, station or terminal of any kind in the observatory's stop data, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. For the nearest stop with a current timetable, see ts_m.
entries.definition: Whole meters (cut, not rounded) from the pin to the nearest stop of any kind in the observatory's list: scheduled bus, train and ferry stops from the timetables (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and of municipal systems, whether or not the timetable has ended, plus bus stops, bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals mapped in OpenStreetMap. Every place has one. In the 2026-10 snapshot, values run from 0 to 77,841 m, and the middle value is 466 m (447 m on the places the map draws). On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class, so that it cannot single the place out: 400 (within 400 m), 700 (more than 400 and less than 800), 800 (exactly 800, cut) or 1000 (more than 800). Every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); places.json is rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access fields are as of 2026-10-06 (see place_access.json).

entries.method: access.py compares each place with every stop of kind transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal, finds the nearest in meters with a flat-earth formula (111,320 m per degree of latitude, with longitude shortened by the cosine of the mean latitude) and cuts the distance to whole meters. Airports, helipads, taxi stands and electric-vehicle chargers are not counted as stops.
entries.source_detail: Scheduled stops from the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and from municipal GTFS feeds (all feeds the build read, expired timetables included), plus OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals not already in a feed.
entries.how_to_read: A smaller number means a stop of some kind is closer. 400 m (a quarter mile) is the planning distance for a walk to a bus stop. This is the distance to any mapped stop, which can be a stop whose timetable has ended or one that volunteers mapped. For the nearest stop with a current timetable, use ts_m in place_access.json. The map pop-up shows it on the line 'Any mapped stop (expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included)', as meters or kilometers, when a stop without a current timetable is closer than the nearest stop with one. Hovering over that line shows the stop's name. Earlier versions of the observatory labelled the field 'distance to the nearest transit stop'.
caveats: In the 2026-10 access update the field was recomputed from today's stop list for all places: 1,204 of the 35,118 places changed, 892 of them by more than 2 m (always shorter), among them all 183 places in Jayuya. See municipalities.transit_data_updates.
It is a straight line, not a walking route. Rivers, highways and hills are ignored.

A stop counts if it is on the list, even when its timetable has expired or when it comes from OpenStreetMap and has no timetable. A stop on the list is not always served today. In the 2026-10 snapshot 3,717 of the 11,507 default-basis places within 400 m of a stop have no stop with a current timetable within 400 m.
The nearest stop is found by comparing the distance in meters to every stop, so the stop named in nearest_stop is the nearest by the formula above.
The field is recomputed from the stop list at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, so it follows the stops shown on the map.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the largest values (68,541 to 77,841 m) belong to the four places on Mona Island.

The stop list mixes sources with different terms: the ATI feed (provided as is, with no warranty), municipal GTFS feeds (no license stated) and OpenStreetMap (Open Database License, ODbL; credit OpenStreetMap contributors). Check each source's terms before you reuse stop names or distances.

view.label: Map: click a pin to open the place's pop-up
3D view: tourism places (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship)

entries.plain_es: La distancia en línea recta, en metros, desde el lugar hasta la parada, estación o terminal de cualquier tipo más cercana en los datos de paradas del observatorio, incluidas las paradas cuyo horario terminó y las que mapearon personas voluntarias. Para la parada más cercana con horario vigente, vea ts_m.
entries.name_es: Distancia a la parada mapeada más cercana de cualquier tipo (m)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un número más pequeño significa que hay alguna parada más cerca. 400 m (un cuarto de milla) es la distancia de planificación para caminar hasta una parada de guagua. Esta es la distancia a cualquier parada mapeada, que puede ser una parada cuyo horario terminó o una que mapearon personas voluntarias. Para la parada más cercana con horario vigente, use ts_m en place_access.json. La ventana emergente del mapa la muestra en la línea "Cualquier parada mapeada (con horarios vencidos y paradas mapeadas por voluntarios)", en metros o kilómetros, cuando una parada sin horario vigente está más cerca que la parada con horario vigente más cercana. Al pasar el cursor sobre esa línea se ve el nombre de la parada. Versiones anteriores del observatorio llamaban a este campo "distancia a la parada de transporte colectivo más cercana".

entries.name: Distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (m)
entries.plain: How far, in a straight line, a tourism place is from the nearest stop whose published timetable has not ended. It is the distance behind the access class in the map pop-up.
entries.definition: Meters from the place's map point to the nearest scheduled stop whose operator's timetable feed has an end date on or after the as-of date (the field as_of of place_access.json). A scheduled stop is a stop in the timetable feed (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or of a municipal transit system. Stops of feeds that have ended, stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap, airports, taxi stands and chargers are not used. The distance is rounded up to whole meters, so a value of 400 or less is exactly the test behind the shares of places near a stop with a current timetable. 99,999 is the largest value the file can hold. The file has one value for each place of places.json, in the same order. It carries no place ids, so a page joins the two files by position and checks that its count n equals the number of places and that the build time in its field built matches generated_at in meta.json. On a place the map does not draw (see Counted but not drawn) the value is coarsened to one value per class: 400 (400 m or less), 800 (more than 400, up to 800), 1000 (more than 800, up to 1,000) or 99,999 (more than 1,000); every count and share reads the same class as before (owner decision of 2026-10-18).
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities (32,541 places)

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the file is rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the stops were read on 2026-10-02 and the access is as of 2026-10-06 (as_of in the file).

entries.method: access.py compares every place with every scheduled stop of an operator whose feed has not ended, in blocks of 500 places. It uses the flat-earth formula that the observatory uses everywhere (111,320 m per degree of latitude, longitude shortened by the cosine of the mean latitude), keeps the smallest distance and rounds it up. A feed counts as current when its end date (feed.end in operators.json) is on or after the as-of date; a feed with no end date does not count. The as-of date is the build date at a full build and the run date in the nightly refresh. Against a computation in projected meters the formula is about 0.6% long north to south, so a share can read up to 0.1 point lower (32.0% instead of 32.1% of places near a stop with a current timetable).
entries.source_detail: Place coordinates: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026), tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR). Stops: scheduled stops in transport.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02). Feed end dates: operators.json.
entries.how_to_read: A smaller number means a stop whose timetable is still in force is closer. 400 m or less is the test for a stop within 400 m; 400 to 800 m is the 'Stop 400–800 m away' class of the pop-up. It says how far the stop is. It does not say how often vehicles come (see ts_calls), whether the walk is safe, or that the service runs today. In the 2026-10 snapshot the middle value is 3,924 m across all 32,541 places. 10,491 places (32.2%) are 400 m or less from such a stop, and so are 7,790 of the 24,209 places on the default basis (32.2%). For the nearest stop of any kind, use transit_m.
caveats: Straight line, not a walking route. It ignores hills, rivers, highways and fences. The walk along mapped roads is place_access.tw_m, which the map's access classes use.
A stop with a current timetable is not proof of service. A timetable is a schedule: it does not show that vehicles run on time or at all. The observatory has no real-time data.

Stops of expired timetables are left out. In the 2026-10 snapshot 966 stops of 7 operators have an expired timetable (Ponce ended 2024-12-31, Hatillo 2025-12-31, Cidra 2026-01-15, Caguas 2026-01-31, San Lorenzo 2026-02-28, Fajardo 2026-06-15 and Juncos 2026-07-31). Buses can still run there, so a long distance near one of these towns can reflect a feed that was not renewed, not a lack of service.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable, so they are not counted.
The values change on the day a feed ends. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed (see methods.access_profile).
The nearest stop can lie in another municipality.
ts_m is rounded up and transit_m is cut to whole meters, so for the same stop the two can differ by 1 m.
In the 2026-10 snapshot the largest values (68,542 to 77,943 m) belong to the four places on Mona Island.
Each distance starts at the place's listed point, which can be wrong in the source (Overture Maps).

entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 7,790 of the 24,209 places on the default basis are 400 m or less from a stop with a current timetable; the middle value over all 32,541 places is 3,924 m.
entries.plain_es: Qué tan lejos, en línea recta, está un lugar turístico de la parada más cercana cuyo horario publicado no ha terminado. Es la distancia en la que se basa la clase de acceso de la ventana emergente del mapa.
entries.name_es: Distancia a la parada con horario vigente más cercana (m)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un número más pequeño significa que hay más cerca una parada cuyo horario sigue vigente. 400 m o menos es la prueba para una parada a 400 m o menos; de 400 a 800 m es la clase "Parada a 400–800 m" de la ventana emergente. En el corte de datos 2026-10, el valor del medio es 3,924 m entre los 32,541 lugares. 10,491 lugares (32.2%) están a 400 m o menos de una parada así, y también 7,790 de los 24,209 lugares de la base predeterminada (32.2%). Para la parada más cercana de cualquier tipo, use transit_m.

entries.name: How the observatory describes a tourism place's access to transport (the access profile)
entries.plain: The observatory describes a tourism place's access to transport as a profile, not a score: the nearest stop whose timetable has not ended, how many weekday departures it has and whether it has weekend service. Walking distance and gateways such as airports and ferry terminals are planned and not published yet.
entries.definition: The profile has three layers. Layer 1 is published: the straight-line distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (ts_m), the most weekday calls at such a stop within 400 m (ts_calls) and the Saturday and Sunday service at those stops (ts_we). The stops come from the GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) timetable feeds of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and of the municipal transit systems. Layer 2, the walking distance along mapped roads, and layer 3, the nearest gateways (airport, ferry terminal, rail station and bus terminal) and scheduled journey times from a gateway, are planned. They are not published, and nothing in the map or the data files measures them yet. From layer 1 each place falls in one of five access classes, which use the distances 400 m and 800 m and the threshold of 20 weekday calls (see Codes). The older measure, within 400 m of any mapped stop (transit_m, transit_400m and transit_pct), stays and is labelled as what it is: it also counts stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. The pop-up of a place shows the class as a badge, then the line 'Nearest stop with a current timetable' with its distance (and, within 400 m, the weekday departures and the weekend service). A third line, 'Any mapped stop (expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included)', appears when such a stop is closer than the nearest stop with a current timetable.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py). In the 2026-10 snapshot the access is as of 2026-10-06 and the stops were read on 2026-10-02.

entries.method: access.py computes the profile from places.json, transport.json and operators.json. A stop has a current timetable when it is a scheduled stop (source ATI or a municipal GTFS feed) and its operator's feed end date is on or after the as-of date; a feed with no end date does not count. For every place it finds the nearest such stop (ts_m, rounded up to whole metres), the largest number of weekday calls at such stops within 400 m (ts_calls) and the Saturday and Sunday flags (ts_we). It also finds the nearest mapped stop of any kind (transit_m, cut to whole metres, and the flag transit_400m). Distances are straight lines from the flat-earth formula that the observatory has always used. Against a computation in projected metres the formula is about 0.6% long north to south, so a share can read up to 0.1 point lower than a projected computation (32.0% instead of 32.1% of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable). Shares count the default basis: tourism places with confidence 0.50 or higher and no places of worship. The municipal fields, the barrio counts and the access part of meta.json add up the same flags. The class of a place follows access_class in access.py, and the map applies the same rule in site/js/access.js.
entries.source_detail: access.py (compute, access_class, island_summary); Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026); stops and feed end dates from transport.json and operators.json (ATI and municipal GTFS feeds read on 2026-10-02); OpenStreetMap extract of 1 October 2026 for the mapped stops
entries.how_to_read: Read it as a profile: first the distance, then how often, then weekends. The observatory does not combine them into one score. A score would need weights (how much a Saturday service is worth against a closer stop), and the weights would be a policy choice that has not been made. A score would also hide the main finding: in the 2026-10 snapshot 64% of the 24,209 places on the default basis have no stop with a current timetable within 800 m. Island figures on the default basis, as of 2026-10-06: 47.5% of places are within 400 m of any mapped stop and 32.2% of a stop with a current timetable; 21.3% are within 400 m of a frequent stop; 22.4% are within 400 m of a stop with Saturday service and 6.4% of one with Sunday service. Of the 11,507 places within 400 m of any mapped stop, 7,790 (67.7%) have a stop with a current timetable and 3,717 (32.3%) rest on stops whose timetable has ended or that have none.
caveats: Schedule-based, not real time. The observatory has no live vehicle positions. A stop with a current timetable is a stop in a published schedule, not proof that vehicles run, on time or at all.
Straight line, not walking distance. It ignores hills, rivers, highways, fences and missing sidewalks. A walking distance along mapped roads would be an estimate, and it is not published yet.
Públicos (shared taxis and vans), taxis, ride-hailing, rental cars and tour shuttles are in no timetable. A place with no stop within 800 m can still be reachable by them.

Missing is not zero. A feed with no weekend calls does not prove that there is no weekend service, and a municipality with no feed does not lack transport. In the 2026-10 snapshot 25 operators publish a feed (ATI and 24 municipal systems). No feed was found for 15 municipal systems and the públicos authority. Only 3 of the 18 current feeds list Saturday calls and only 1 lists Sunday calls.

An expired timetable is not an absence of buses. Ponce's figures (0.1% of its places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable, 79.1% within 400 m of any mapped stop) reflect a feed that ended on 2024-12-31. Do not compare municipalities as if their feeds were equally complete.

The profile depends on the date. It is computed as of a date (2026-10-06 in the 2026-10 snapshot) and changes on the day a feed ends: 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31, among them San Juan's municipal feed on 2027-01-31. Computed as of 2027-02-01 with the same feeds, 26.1% of the places would be within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable, instead of 32.2%. That is arithmetic on the end dates, not a forecast of service: operators can publish new feeds.
Weekday calls are a proxy for frequency, not a headway (the time between vehicles). The busiest single stop within 400 m is used, not the sum of the stops.
Counts are listings from Overture Maps, not businesses, rooms or visitors. The distance is measured from a place's listed point.
The barrio counts are rebuilt only at a full build, so between full builds they can lag the municipal fields.

values.Frequent stop within 400 m: A stop with a current timetable is 400 m or less away and the busiest such stop within 400 m has 20 or more weekday calls. 5,163 places (21.3%) in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.Stop within 400 m: A stop with a current timetable is 400 m or less away, and the busiest such stop within 400 m has fewer than 20 weekday calls. 2,627 places (10.9%).
values.Stop 400–800 m away: The nearest stop with a current timetable is more than 400 m and at most 800 m away. 964 places (4.0%).
values.Only expired or unscheduled stops within: No stop with a current timetable within 800 m, but a mapped stop within 800 m: a stop whose timetable has ended, or one that volunteers mapped, with no timetable. 4,690 places (19.4%).
values.No stop within 800 m: No mapped stop of any kind within 800 m. 10,765 places (44.5%).

entries.plain_es: El observatorio describe el acceso de un lugar turístico al transporte como un perfil, no como una puntuación: la parada más cercana cuyo horario no ha terminado, cuántas salidas tiene en días de semana y si tiene servicio el fin de semana. La distancia a pie y los puntos de entrada, como los aeropuertos y las terminales de lanchas, están planificados y aún no se publican.
entries.name_es: Cómo describe el observatorio el acceso al transporte de un lugar turístico (el perfil de acceso)
entries.how_to_read_es: Léalo como un perfil: primero la distancia, luego la frecuencia y luego los fines de semana. El observatorio no los combina en una sola puntuación. Una puntuación necesitaría pesos (cuánto vale un servicio los sábados frente a una parada más cercana), y esos pesos serían una decisión de política pública que no se ha tomado. Una puntuación también ocultaría el hallazgo principal: en el corte de datos 2026-10, el 64% de los 24,209 lugares de la base predeterminada no tiene ninguna parada con horario vigente a 800 m o menos. Cifras de la isla con la base predeterminada, al 2026-10-06: el 47.5% de los lugares está a 400 m o menos de cualquier parada mapeada y el 32.2% de una parada con horario vigente; el 21.3% está a 400 m o menos de una parada frecuente; el 22.4% está a 400 m o menos de una parada con servicio los sábados y el 6.4% de una con servicio los domingos. De los 11,507 lugares a 400 m o menos de cualquier parada mapeada, 7,790 (67.7%) tienen una parada con horario vigente y 3,717 (32.3%) dependen de paradas cuyo horario terminó o que no tienen horario.

entries.name: Nearest mapped stop of any kind (name)
entries.plain: The name of the stop, station or terminal of any kind that is closest to the place, whether or not its timetable has ended.
entries.definition: The name of the nearest stop used for the transit distance (transit_m). When the stop has no name, the text is its kind, such as bus stop. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 3,020 different values occur. A place the map does not draw has none (see Counted but not drawn).
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); places.json is rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the access fields are as of 2026-10-06 (see place_access.json).

entries.method: Taken from the stop found for transit_m: its name, or its kind with underscores replaced by spaces when it has no name.
entries.source_detail: Scheduled stops from the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and from municipal GTFS feeds (all feeds the build read, expired timetables included), plus OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals not already in a feed.
entries.how_to_read: The map shows it as a tooltip on the 'Any mapped stop' line of a pop-up. Many names are terminals, for example públicos terminals. It names the nearest stop of any kind, which may have no current timetable. The observatory does not publish the name of the nearest stop with a current timetable.
caveats: In the 2026-10 access update the names were recomputed from today's stop list. The 183 places in Jayuya now name stops of Jayuya's own feed; before, all 183 named a stop in another municipality because 58 Jayuya stops had a wrong longitude.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1,041 of the places the map draws show only 'bus stop', 85 show 'bus station' and 57 show 'ferry terminal', because the nearest stop has no name in its source.
Names are as the feeds or OpenStreetMap wrote them, in Spanish or English. The observatory does not check that a stop is in service.

The stop list mixes sources with different terms: the ATI feed (provided as is, with no warranty), municipal GTFS feeds (no license stated) and OpenStreetMap (Open Database License, ODbL; credit OpenStreetMap contributors). Check each source's terms before you reuse stop names or distances.

view.label: Map: click a pin to open the place's pop-up

entries.plain_es: El nombre de la parada, estación o terminal de cualquier tipo más cercana al lugar, haya terminado o no su horario.
entries.name_es: Parada mapeada más cercana de cualquier tipo (nombre)
entries.how_to_read_es: El mapa lo muestra como texto flotante sobre la línea "Cualquier parada mapeada" de una ventana emergente. Muchos nombres son terminales, por ejemplo, terminales de públicos. Indica la parada más cercana de cualquier tipo, que puede no tener horario vigente. El observatorio no publica el nombre de la parada más cercana con horario vigente.

entries.name: Places measured in a straight line (no walkable road within 150 m)
entries.plain: The list of places that have no mapped road within 150 m, so their walking fields keep the straight-line values. The map pop-up says so for these places.
entries.definition: Positions (0-based, in the order of places.json) of the places whose map point has no walkable road of roads.bin within 150 m. For each of them tw_m equals ts_m, tw_calls equals ts_calls and tw_we equals ts_we.
entries.unit: positions in places.json (a place that is listed is measured in a straight line)
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: point locations in all 78 municipalities (32,541 places)

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py), from the road file the site publishes (roads.bin); the file is rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the stops were read on 2026-10-02 and the access is as of 2026-10-06 (as_of in the file).

entries.method: walknet.py snaps each place to the nearest road of the walking network within 150 m (shapely's nearest-geometry search). A place with no road in that distance is listed here and access.py copies its straight-line values.
entries.source_detail: Place coordinates: Overture Maps places (release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026), tourism places as classified by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR). Stops: scheduled stops in transport.json (the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feeds of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and of municipal systems, read on 2026-10-02). Feed end dates: operators.json. Roads: OpenStreetMap (roads.py builds site/data/roads.bin from the Geofabrik extract; ODbL).
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot 1,210 places are listed, 1,074 of them on the default basis (4.4%): 622 attractions, 325 gastronomy places, 78 visitor services and 49 accommodations. The most are in San Juan (114), Carolina (103), Fajardo (63) and Ponce (59). Beaches, trails and parks inside large grounds are typical. For these places the walking share counts the straight line, which can only understate the walk.
caveats: 150 m is the connector the visitor-access study tested, not a standard. A wider limit would join more places to a road across a barrier.
A place can be on a footpath, a beach or a private road that the road file does not hold.
