coverage.frequency: Rebuilt when the route analysis is rebuilt (docs/analysis/route-analysis-2026-10/); weekday timetables of 2026-10-19.

entries.method: Count of trips.json trips with the route's operator and label and mode bus.

view.label: Knowledge Area: Route analysis, route comparison

entries.plain_es: Cuántos viajes hace la ruta en un día de semana típico, sumadas las dos direcciones.
entries.name_es: Viajes en un día de semana

entries.name: Connections at the ends and stops along the route
entries.plain: Two checks: whether the start and the end are within 300 m of a scheduled stop, and how many scheduled stops lie within 250 m of the route, by operator.
entries.definition: Start and End: the scheduled stop nearest to the first and to the last point you chose, if one lies within 300 m in a straight line. The card shows the stop name, its operator and the distance in metres, or 'no scheduled stop within 300 m'. Existing stops within 250 m of the route: the number of scheduled stops within 250 m of the route line, grouped by operator. A scheduled stop is a stop in a public timetable feed (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) from ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or from a municipal system.
entries.unit: stop name, operator and metres; stops per operator (count)
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js looks at the scheduled stops in the transit features file. For the first and last chosen points it keeps the nearest stop within 300 m. For the route line it counts the stops within 250 m of the simplified line and groups them by operator's short name.
entries.source_detail: transport.json (stops from ATI and municipal feeds); operators.json (operator names); site/js/plan.js (score, endTxt)
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see where a new route could join an existing one. A stop near the end is a place to connect, not proof that a rider can transfer.
caveats: Only the first and last points are tested. Points you add between them are not.
Stops of operators whose timetables have expired are counted.
It does not say whether the lines at that stop go where you need, or how often.
The distance from an end is measured from the point you chose, not from the road it is snapped to.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): Start: a City of San Juan stop 50 m away. End: a Municipality of Caguas stop 51 m away. Stops within 250 m of the route: ATI 20, San Juan 29, Caguas 37. From Mayagüez (municipality) To Aguadilla (municipality): no scheduled stop within 300 m of either end.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)
Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example with no overlap: Mayagüez to Aguadilla)

entries.plain_es: Dos verificaciones: si el origen y el destino están a 300 m o menos de una parada con horario, y cuántas paradas con horario hay a 250 m o menos de la ruta, por operador.
entries.name_es: Conexiones en los extremos y paradas a lo largo de la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver dónde una ruta nueva podría unirse a una existente. Una parada cerca del extremo es un lugar para conectar, no una prueba de que una persona pueda hacer trasbordo.

entries.name: Distances used by the planner and the Transit tab
entries.plain: The route planner and the Transit tab use a few fixed distances, all in a straight line: 150, 250, 300, 400, 500 and 800 metres. This entry says what each is for.
entries.definition: Each distance is a setting chosen for this tool. 400 m (about a quarter mile) is a common rule of thumb for walking access to a stop. Check any agency's or programme's own definition before comparing. All are straight-line distances calculated with a flat-earth approximation, not walking distances along streets.
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: The route planner (plan.js) and the road router (roads.js) compute distances in the browser from longitude and latitude with a flat-earth approximation: 111,320 m per degree of longitude at the equator, scaled by the cosine of the latitude, and 110,574 m per degree of latitude. The distance from each census block to its nearest scheduled stop (the basis of the 400 m and 800 m rules) and the 250 m integration-point test are computed at build time by network.py with a similar formula: 111,320 m per degree of latitude, and the same figure scaled by the cosine of the latitude for longitude. North-south distances in the build are therefore up to about 0.7% longer than in the browser. network.js and plan.js read those stored results: network.js applies the 800 m test to them and plan.js applies the 400 m test when it counts residents with no stop near a route.
entries.source_detail: site/js/plan.js, site/js/network.js, network.py (WALK_M = 400, TRANSFER_M = 250), roads.js
entries.how_to_read: Read each distance as a catchment around a line or a stop. A longer distance includes more people and places and says less about how easy it is to reach them.
caveats: A straight line ignores rivers, hills, fences and the street pattern.
The 400 m walking distance is about a quarter mile. The 800 m distance for service gaps is about half a mile.

values.12 m: Tolerance for simplifying the route line before it is measured.
values.100 m, 250 m, 500 m: Spacing of sample points along the route: up to 30 km, over 30 up to 100 km, over 100 km.
values.150 m: A route 'runs alongside' an existing route when a published line is within 150 m of a sample point.
values.250 m: Scheduled stops within 250 m of the route are counted. Stops of two operators within 250 m of each other make an integration point.
values.300 m: Connections at the ends: the nearest scheduled stop to the first or last point, if within 300 m.
values.400 m: Residents and tourism places counted near the route. Residents counted as served when a scheduled stop is within 400 m. The test for 'no scheduled stop within 400 m'.
values.500 m: Snap radius from a chosen point to a road.
values.800 m: Service gap: a block whose nearest scheduled stop is more than 800 m away.

entries.plain_es: El planificador de rutas y la pestaña "Transporte" usan unas pocas distancias fijas, todas en línea recta: 150, 250, 300, 400, 500 y 800 metros. Esta entrada explica para qué sirve cada una.
entries.name_es: Distancias que usan el planificador y la pestaña Transporte
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea cada distancia como un área de captación alrededor de una línea o una parada. Una distancia mayor incluye más personas y lugares, y dice menos sobre qué tan fácil es llegar a ellos.

entries.name: How the planner samples a route
entries.plain: The flood, protected-area, overlap and municipality measures check points along the route, not the whole line. The spacing depends on the route's length.
entries.definition: The route line is simplified to a 12 m tolerance. Points are then placed along it every 100 m for routes up to 30 km, every 250 m for routes over 30 km and up to 100 km, and every 500 m for longer routes. Every straight piece of the simplified line gets at least one point. The overlap, flood and protected-area measures are each the share of sample points that meet their test, rounded to a whole percent. The municipalities measure is the number of different municipalities that contain at least one sample point.
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js applies Douglas-Peucker simplification (a method that drops points that lie close to a straight line between their neighbours) with a 12 m tolerance, then calls samples() with a step of 100, 250 or 500 m chosen from the route length.
entries.source_detail: site/js/plan.js (simplifyLine, samples, score)
entries.how_to_read: A percentage is a share of points, not a share of kilometres. Short features between points can be missed.
caveats: A curvy stretch has many short pieces, each with at least one point, so it weighs a little more than a straight stretch of the same length.
Residents, tourism places and stops use the distance to the line, not these points.
entries.plain_es: Las medidas de inundación, áreas protegidas, coincidencia con otras rutas y municipios revisan puntos a lo largo de la ruta, no la línea completa. La distancia entre los puntos depende del largo de la ruta.
entries.name_es: Cómo el planificador toma muestras de una ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Un porcentaje es una proporción de puntos, no de kilómetros. Los elementos cortos entre puntos pueden no detectarse.

entries.name: Indicative running time
entries.plain: A rough driving time for the route, in minutes, at fixed planning speeds by road class. It leaves out stops, traffic and waiting. Use it to compare routes, not as a bus timetable.
entries.definition: The sum over legs of the time at planning speeds. On a leg that follows roads: the time along each road piece (its length divided by the speed of its road class), plus the straight-line gap between each chosen point and its road, counted at walking pace (1.4 m/s). On a leg that cannot follow roads: its straight-line length at 8 m/s (28.8 km/h). Shown as '~N min', rounded to whole minutes, at least 1.
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: roads.js adds the seconds of every leg. plan.js shows the total only when Follow roads is on and at least one leg follows roads; otherwise it shows a dash. In the list of legs, minutes appear only for legs that follow roads.
entries.source_detail: site/js/roads.js (path, SPEED_MS) and site/js/plan.js (renderResult)
entries.how_to_read: The number is the time at these planning speeds, for example 25 km/h on residential streets and 90 km/h on motorways. It is closer to a free-flow driving time than to a bus timetable: in the example (snapshot 2026-10, Río Piedras to Caguas) the average speed is about 76 km/h (24.3 km in about 19 min). A real bus trip is longer: it has stops, boarding, signals and traffic. Use the number only to compare routes.
caveats: The speeds are planning values by road class, not observed or posted speeds.
When some legs cannot follow roads, the total time still includes them, as straight lines at 8 m/s (28.8 km/h). The list of legs shows minutes only for legs that follow roads.
The time is not a prediction of a real service and does not depend on the day or the hour.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): about 19 min for 24.3 km.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: Un tiempo aproximado de manejo para la ruta, en minutos, a velocidades fijas de planificación según la clase de carretera. No incluye paradas, tráfico ni esperas. Sirve para comparar rutas, no como horario de guaguas.
entries.name_es: Tiempo de recorrido indicativo
entries.how_to_read_es: El número es el tiempo a estas velocidades de planificación, por ejemplo 25 km/h en calles residenciales y 90 km/h en autopistas. Se acerca más a un tiempo de manejo sin congestión que a un horario de guagua: en el ejemplo (corte de datos 2026-10, de Río Piedras a Caguas), la velocidad promedio es de unos 76 km/h (24.3 km en unos 19 min). Un viaje real en guagua es más largo: tiene paradas, abordaje, semáforos y tráfico. Use el número solo para comparar rutas.

entries.name: Municipalities crossed
entries.plain: How many municipalities the planned route passes through. The card lists the first four names and then says 'and N more'.
entries.definition: The number of different municipalities whose boundary contains at least one sample point of the route, with their names.
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js finds, for each sample point, the municipality polygon that contains it and collects the distinct names. See the entry on how the route is sampled.
entries.source_detail: municipios.geojson: TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (Counties 500K, shoreline-clipped); site/js/plan.js (score)
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see which local governments a route involves. A route that only grazes a municipality can be missed.
caveats: A municipality touched between two sample points (100 to 500 m apart) is not counted.
The boundaries follow the shoreline, so a sample point on a bridge or offshore can belong to no municipality.
The boundaries are simplified by about 22 m (0.0002 degree), so a sample point near a boundary can be assigned to the neighbouring municipality.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 3 (San Juan, Trujillo Alto, Caguas).

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: Por cuántos municipios pasa la ruta planificada. La tarjeta da los primeros cuatro nombres y luego dice "y N más".
entries.name_es: Municipios que cruza
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver qué gobiernos locales abarca una ruta. Una ruta que solo roza un municipio puede no detectarse.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of the route
entries.plain: How many people live in census blocks whose point is within 400 metres of the planned route. It shows who lives near the line, not who would ride it.
entries.definition: The sum of the 2020 Census resident counts of every census block with residents whose internal point lies within 400 m (straight line) of the route line. A block counts whole when its point qualifies. Blocks are not split.
entries.geography: Census blocks of Puerto Rico (36,570 blocks have residents in the 2020 Census)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: population_blocks.json lists, for every block with residents, its longitude and latitude (the Census internal point, rounded to 4 decimals), its residents and its distance to the nearest scheduled stop. plan.js simplifies the route line to a 12 m tolerance and adds the residents of each block whose point is within 400 m of any piece of it.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10 (2020 Census blocks), fields POP100, INTPTLAT, INTPTLON; site/js/plan.js (score)
entries.how_to_read: Use it as a catchment: the number of people close to the line. It is not ridership or demand.
caveats: The distance is in a straight line, not along streets. A person can be within 400 m and still face a long walk.
A block is counted whole or not at all. A large block whose point is farther than 400 m is left out even if part of it is near.
The counts are from April 2020 and have not been updated.
400 m is about a quarter mile, the walking distance the observatory uses for access to a stop.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 26,723 residents.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: Cuántas personas viven en bloques censales cuyo punto está a 400 metros o menos de la ruta planificada. Muestra quién vive cerca de la línea, no quién la usaría.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo como un área de captación: el número de personas cerca de la línea. No es el número de pasajeros ni la demanda.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of the route who have no scheduled stop within 400 m
entries.plain: Of the people who live within 400 m of the route, how many live more than 400 m from every scheduled stop in the observatory's data. These people have no scheduled stop near them.
entries.definition: Residents counted in 'Residents within 400 m of the route' whose census block has its nearest scheduled stop more than 400 m away (straight line). A scheduled stop is a stop in a public timetable feed (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) from ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or from a municipal system. The result card calls them 'of them have no scheduled stop within 400 m today'.

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: population_blocks.json gives each block's distance in metres to its nearest scheduled stop, capped at 9,999. plan.js adds the residents of the blocks near the route whose distance is above 400. The distances are recomputed by the transit refresh.
entries.source_detail: population_blocks.json (network.py, coverage); site/js/plan.js (score)
entries.how_to_read: Compare it with 'Residents within 400 m of the route'. A high share means the route passes many people who have no stop nearby today. The distances were last computed on 2026-10-02.
caveats: 'Today' means the build or refresh date. Stops of operators whose timetables have expired still count as stops, so the true number with no service now is larger.
Only stops in public timetable feeds count. Routes that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap have no stops here, so público service is not counted as service.
A stop within 400 m says that a stop exists. It does not say how often vehicles come or when.
The distance is in a straight line, not along streets.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 13,301 of the 26,723 residents.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: De las personas que viven a 400 m o menos de la ruta, cuántas viven a más de 400 m de todas las paradas con horario en los datos del observatorio. Estas personas no tienen una parada con horario cerca.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de la ruta que no tienen ninguna parada con horario a 400 m o menos
entries.how_to_read_es: Compárelo con 'Residentes a 400 m o menos de la ruta'. Una proporción alta significa que la ruta pasa cerca de muchas personas que hoy no tienen una parada cerca. Las distancias se calcularon por última vez el 2026-10-02.

entries.name: Route length
entries.plain: How long the planned route is, in kilometres, along the roads it follows. The label under the number says 'by road', 'partly by road' or 'straight line'.
entries.definition: The sum of the lengths of all legs between the points you chose (From, any added stops and To; 8 points at most). A leg that follows roads counts the length of its road path plus the straight-line gap from each chosen point to the nearest point on a road. A leg that cannot follow roads counts its straight-line length.
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: roads.js finds the fastest road path for each leg and measures the drawn line with a flat-earth approximation. plan.js adds the legs. With more than one leg, the card also lists each leg with its length and, for legs on roads, its minutes. The label is 'by road' when every leg follows roads, 'partly by road' when some do not, and 'straight line' when Follow roads is switched off.
entries.source_detail: site/js/roads.js (path) and site/js/plan.js (renderResult); roads.bin from OpenStreetMap
entries.how_to_read: It is the length of the path the planner drew, not a measured distance on the ground. It is not the fastest or shortest real bus route.
caveats: A leg that cannot follow roads, for example a leg to another island, counts at its straight-line length, so it can be much shorter than any real trip by sea or air.
If the road file cannot be loaded, the route is drawn as straight lines and a note under the numbers says so.
In the GeoJSON download the same number is called length_km and has two decimals.
The points you choose are stored in the page address (after #r=) to about 11 m. A shared link shares them. Do not choose a home address if you plan to share the link.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 24.3 km, by road.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: Cuánto mide la ruta planificada, en kilómetros, por las carreteras que sigue. La etiqueta debajo del número dice "por carretera", "en parte por carretera" o "en línea recta".
entries.name_es: Largo de la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Es el largo del camino que dibujó el planificador, no una distancia medida en el terreno. No es la ruta de guagua real más rápida ni la más corta.

entries.name: Share of the route in a flood hazard area
entries.plain: The share of the planned route that crosses areas the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as high-risk for flooding, which have a 1% chance of flooding in any year. The card turns amber above 20%.
entries.definition: The share of the route's sample points that fall inside a polygon of the National Flood Hazard Layer of FEMA (the Federal Emergency Management Agency) flagged as a Special Flood Hazard Area (SFHA_TF = T), rounded to a whole percent. In the published file these are zones A, AE, AH, AO, A99 and VE. Zone X and zone D are not counted.
entries.unit: % of sample points along the route
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js tests each sample point against the polygons of the flood file with a point-in-polygon test (checking whether the point lies inside the polygon). See the entry on how the route is sampled.
entries.source_detail: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer, layer 28 (flood.geojson, field SFHA_TF); site/js/plan.js (score)
entries.how_to_read: A high value means much of the route lies in mapped flood hazard. It does not say how deep water would get or whether the road is raised.
caveats: The flood polygons are simplified by about 5 m for display, so points near a boundary can be misplaced.
It is a share of sample points, not of length.
The map shows hazard at a point. It does not describe bridges, culverts or the road surface.
The 20% amber threshold is this tool's own choice, not a standard.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 8%.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: La proporción de la ruta planificada que cruza áreas que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) marca como de alto riesgo de inundación, que tienen 1% de probabilidad de inundarse en cualquier año. La tarjeta se pone ámbar por encima del 20%.
entries.name_es: Proporción de la ruta en una zona de riesgo de inundación
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor alto significa que gran parte de la ruta está en un riesgo de inundación cartografiado. No indica qué profundidad alcanzaría el agua ni si la carretera está elevada.

entries.name: Share of the route in protected areas
entries.plain: The share of the planned route that passes through protected areas in the USGS Protected Areas Database. The card shows it only when it is above 0%.
entries.definition: The share of the route's sample points that fall inside any polygon of the protected-areas file (USGS, the United States Geological Survey), rounded to a whole percent. Every designation is counted, including the proclamation boundaries (PROC) such as El Yunque National Forest and the Culebra and Vieques National Wildlife Refuges.
entries.unit: % of sample points along the route
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js tests each sample point against the polygons of the protected-areas file with a point-in-polygon test (checking whether the point lies inside the polygon). See the entry on how the route is sampled.
entries.source_detail: USGS PAD-US 4.1 (protected.geojson); site/js/plan.js (score)
entries.how_to_read: A value above 0 means the route runs through land with a protected designation. It does not say that the road is closed or that the land is off limits. In the 2026-10 snapshot the protected-areas file has seven proclamation boundaries.
caveats: The statistic for tourism places leaves out the proclamation boundaries (seven records in the 2026-10 snapshot); this route measure counts them, so the two are not on the same basis.
The file includes areas with different levels of protection and public access. The share does not tell them apart.
It is a share of sample points, not of length.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 1%.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)

entries.plain_es: La proporción de la ruta planificada que pasa por áreas protegidas de la base de datos de áreas protegidas del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). La tarjeta la muestra solo cuando es mayor de 0%.
entries.name_es: Proporción de la ruta en áreas protegidas
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor mayor de 0 significa que la ruta pasa por terrenos con una designación de protección. No indica que la carretera esté cerrada ni que el terreno sea de acceso prohibido. En el corte de datos 2026-10, el archivo de áreas protegidas tiene siete límites de proclamación.

entries.name: Share of the route that runs alongside an existing route
entries.plain: The share of the planned route within 150 m of a published transit route; a high share means the route mostly repeats lines that exist. The card turns amber above 50%, a threshold this tool chose.
entries.definition: The share of the route's sample points that have a published route line within 150 m, rounded to a whole percent. Routes that volunteers mapped only in OpenStreetMap (públicos) and ferry routes are not counted. Routes of every other operator are counted, including the Tren Urbano rail line.
entries.unit: % of sample points along the route
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js indexes every segment of the published route lines in grid cells of 0.002 degree (about 220 m) and tests each sample point against the segments in its own and the neighbouring cells. See the entry on how the route is sampled.
entries.source_detail: transit_routes.geojson (all operators except 'osm' and ferries); site/js/plan.js (segments, score)
entries.how_to_read: 100% means the route follows existing lines for its whole length. 0% means no line from an ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or municipal timetable feed is near. Públicos mapped in OpenStreetMap and ferries are not counted. It says nothing about stops or how often vehicles run.
caveats: Lines of operators whose timetables have expired are counted.
A route can run beside a line and still have no stop near it. The measure compares lines, not stops.
It is a share of sample points, not of length. See the entry on sampling.
The 50% amber threshold is this tool's own choice, not a standard.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 100%. From Mayagüez (municipality) To Aguadilla (municipality): 0%.

view.label: Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example: Río Piedras to Caguas)
Map, Transit tab, Plan a route (example with no overlap: Mayagüez to Aguadilla)

entries.plain_es: La proporción de la ruta planificada que queda a 150 m o menos de una ruta de transporte colectivo publicada; una proporción alta significa que la ruta repite mayormente líneas que ya existen. La tarjeta se pone ámbar por encima del 50%, un límite que escogió esta herramienta.
entries.name_es: Proporción de la ruta que corre junto a una ruta existente
entries.how_to_read_es: 100% significa que la ruta sigue líneas existentes en todo su largo. 0% significa que no hay cerca ninguna línea de las fuentes de horarios de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) ni de las municipales. No se cuentan los públicos cartografiados en OpenStreetMap ni las lanchas. No dice nada sobre las paradas ni sobre la frecuencia de los vehículos.

entries.name: Tourism places within 400 m of the route
entries.plain: How many tourism places lie within 400 m of the planned route, and how many of them are lodgings. Tourism places are Attractions, Gastronomy (restaurants, bars and cafes), Accommodations and Visitor services.
entries.definition: The number of listings in the places file with an Overture confidence of at least 0.5, other than places of worship, whose point lies within 400 m (straight line) of the route line. Lodgings are the places in the Accommodations category (the route card calls them lodgings).
entries.unit: tourism places (listings after duplicate folding); lodgings (a part of them)
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Recalculated in your browser each time the route changes, from the data published in the current snapshot. Resident counts are from the 2020 Census

entries.method: plan.js goes through the places file, skips places of worship and listings below 0.5 confidence, and counts those within 400 m of the simplified route line. It counts the lodgings separately.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Places, release 2026-09-23.1, classified by build.py; site/js/plan.js (score)
entries.how_to_read: It says how many visitor places the route passes. A place is a listing, not a verified business.
caveats: The same 0.5 confidence rule as the map statistics applies. The map's own filters (categories, confidence slider) do not change this count.
Listings can be closed, moved or missing.
The distance is in a straight line, not along streets.

Lodgings are listings the observatory's rules file under hotels, resorts, inns, guest houses, hostels, campgrounds and vacation properties (categories such as vacation rental, villa, cottage, cabin, holiday and condo), or under Overture's lodging group. They are Overture listings, not a lodging register.
entries.example: Snapshot 2026-10, From Río Piedras (town) To Caguas (municipality): 400 tourism places, 16 of them lodgings.

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares turísticos hay a 400 m o menos de la ruta planificada, y cuántos de ellos son alojamientos. Los lugares turísticos son "Atracciones", "Gastronomía" (restaurantes, bares y cafés), "Alojamientos" y "Servicios para visitantes".

entries.how_to_read_es: Indica por cuántos lugares para visitantes pasa la ruta. Un lugar es un listado, no un negocio verificado.

entries.name: First and last weekday departure on the route
entries.plain: The earliest and the latest time a weekday trip on the route starts, in seconds after midnight. The map shows them as clock times.
entries.definition: first is the earliest and last is the latest departure from the first stop of any weekday trip on the route. Seconds after midnight, local time (12600 is 03:30). In the 2026-10 snapshot it is present for 149 routes; first runs from 12600 (03:30) to 29700 (08:15) and last from 39600 (11:00) to 84600 (23:30). It is null for the 16 OpenStreetMap (OSM) routes.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.py sorts the time at the first stop of each weekday trip and keeps the smallest and the largest.
entries.source_detail: GTFS stop_times.txt (time at the first stop of each weekday trip), joined to trips.txt and calendar.txt
entries.how_to_read: Divide by 3600 to get hours. last is when the final trip leaves its first stop, not when it arrives. A timetable covers the dates from the operator's feed.start to feed.end in operators.json, not the build date. In the build of 2026-10-02 the earliest start is 2023-01-01 and the latest end is 2029-12-31; Ponce's feed ended 2024-12-31. Cite both the build date and the feed dates.
caveats: For Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and Guaynabo, which list each direction, the two values mix both directions of travel; in the 2026-10 snapshot the other 23 feeds do not separate directions.
They are taken from the stop times as listed, so in the 2026-10 snapshot the five Patillas routes with an inferred stop order also show them even though their times are not used in the replay.

entries.plain_es: La hora más temprana y la más tarde en que sale un viaje de lunes a viernes en la ruta, en segundos después de la medianoche. El mapa las muestra como horas del reloj.
entries.name_es: Primera y última salida de lunes a viernes en la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Divida entre 3600 para obtener horas. last es cuando el último viaje sale de su primera parada, no cuando llega. Un horario cubre las fechas desde feed.start hasta feed.end del operador en operators.json, no la fecha de compilación. En la compilación del 2026-10-02, el inicio más temprano es 2023-01-01 y el final más tardío es 2029-12-31; la fuente de datos de Ponce terminó el 2024-12-31. Cite tanto la fecha de compilación como las fechas de las fuentes de datos.

entries.name: How route lines are drawn
entries.plain: A route line is the operator's own shape when the feed has one, otherwise a path along roads between the stops. If the stop order looks wrong the observatory infers one, and if nothing works it joins the stops with straight dotted lines.
entries.definition: The counts below are for the 2026-10 snapshot. 1. Feed shape: if the feed lists a route shape (the line the operator publishes for the path of a route), the observatory keeps up to the two most used shapes of the route (usually one per direction). 50 routes are drawn this way, including every Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) route. 2. Road-snapped: with no shape, the observatory takes the stops of the longest trip in each direction and links each pair of neighbouring stops by the fastest road path in the OpenStreetMap road network (roads.bin). 94 routes are drawn this way. 3. Inferred order: if a feed lists its stops out of travel order, the observatory picks a plausible order and then snaps it to roads. 5 routes are drawn this way, all from Patillas. 4. Straight dotted: if too little of a route can be snapped, the stops are joined by straight lines and drawn dotted. No route uses this in the 2026-10 snapshot. 5. OpenStreetMap: the 16 públicos and trolley routes are drawn from the lines volunteers mapped.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: Road snapping: each stop is moved to the nearest road within 500 m; a leg is accepted if the road path is no longer than 3 times the straight distance plus 400 m; stops less than 25 m apart are joined directly. A route is kept as road-snapped only if at least 60% of the legs in each direction follow a road; otherwise it falls back to straight lines. The line is then simplified (tolerance about 3 m). Inferred order: a feed is flagged when the stop order has a zig-zag ratio above 2.5 (the length of the path through the stops in listed order divided by the length of a nearest-neighbour tour; real routes sit near 1 to 2) or when the stop names are in alphabetical order. The order is then rebuilt from the terminal or first stop by always going to the nearest unvisited stop by road, improved by reversing stretches of the order while that shortens the road distance, and the line returns to its start; for more than 45 distinct stops the order is not rebuilt and the route falls back to straight lines. A route whose stops did not change keeps its previous line (see the entry on the route line fingerprint).
entries.how_to_read: On the map a solid line follows the operator's shape or the roads, a lighter dashed line is a route with inferred stop order, a dotted line joins stops straight, and a gold dashed line is an OpenStreetMap route. Ferries are dashed teal.
caveats: Only a feed shape is the operator's own alignment. A road-snapped line is an estimate and the real street may differ.
A route with an inferred order shows a plausible path, not the route the operator runs. Its times are left out of the timetable replay.
The feed's route colour is not used on the map; line colour follows the mode and the type of operator.
Road-snapped lines are derived from OpenStreetMap roads, which are under the Open Database License. Credit OpenStreetMap contributors and check the license terms before reuse.

entries.plain_es: La línea de una ruta es la forma del propio operador cuando la fuente de horarios la trae; si no, es un camino por las carreteras entre las paradas. Si el orden de las paradas parece incorrecto, el observatorio deduce uno, y si nada funciona, une las paradas con líneas rectas punteadas.
entries.name_es: Cómo se dibujan las líneas de las rutas
entries.how_to_read_es: En el mapa, una línea continua sigue el trazado del operador o las carreteras; una línea discontinua más clara es una ruta con el orden de paradas deducido; una línea punteada une las paradas en línea recta, y una línea discontinua dorada es una ruta de OpenStreetMap. Las lanchas se muestran con una línea discontinua verde azulada.

entries.name: How the route line was drawn
entries.plain: Says whether the line is the operator's own shape, a path along roads, a path along roads with a guessed stop order, or a volunteer-mapped line.
entries.definition: A code for how the line of a route from Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), a municipality or OpenStreetMap was made. The code stops (a straight dotted line joining the stops) exists in the program but no route uses it in the 2026-10 snapshot.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: Set by network.py (shape, stops), snap_routes (roads, roads_inferred) and load_osm_routes (osm). See How route lines are drawn.
entries.source_detail: GTFS shapes.txt (shape); the OpenStreetMap road network, Geofabrik Puerto Rico extract (roads.bin), for roads and roads_inferred; OpenStreetMap route relations (osm)
entries.how_to_read: Trust shape most. Treat roads as a good estimate, roads_inferred as a rough guess, and osm as a volunteer map.
caveats: The code stops would appear as a dotted straight line; none is present in the 2026-10 snapshot.

entries.definition: Text, present only on routes whose feed lists the stops out of travel order. It states the zig-zag ratio found and that the order of visit is inferred and the times are not usable. The sentence says alphabetically when the stop names are in alphabetical order, and out of travel order otherwise. In the 2026-10 snapshot the five notes give the ratios 2.72, 2.77, 2.93, 4.44 and 4.99, and all five say out of travel order.

entries.name: Públicos and other routes mapped in OpenStreetMap
entries.plain: Bus, público and trolley routes that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap (OSM): 16 in the 2026-10 snapshot. They have no published timetable, so the observatory shows the line but not trips or times.
entries.definition: Route relations in OpenStreetMap tagged route=bus, trolleybus, share_taxi or minibus inside Puerto Rico. Públicos (carros públicos) are shared cars and vans that run set routes. Routes whose network or operator tag names the AMA (Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses), ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or Bayamón are left out, because those come from official feeds. A route needs at least one mapped way to be kept. Each kept route has operator osm, mode bus, trips set to 0 and no first or last time. The label is Público for share_taxi routes or networks whose name contains público, and Bus otherwise (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 9 Público and 7 Bus).

coverage.frequency: Read at each full build. The nightly refresh also asks the OpenStreetMap service (Overpass) for them; when the service does not answer, it keeps the OpenStreetMap routes it already has. Last OpenStreetMap read: 2026-10-02.

entries.method: load_osm_routes in network.py sends one Overpass query and keeps the member ways with roles empty, route, forward or backward. route_id is r followed by the OSM relation number; short_name is the ref tag; long_name is the name, description or network tag, else Unnamed route.
entries.how_to_read: Treat these lines as a volunteer map of where públicos are known to run, not as a service guarantee.
caveats: The routes are incomplete and unscheduled. A público can run without being mapped, and a mapped route may no longer run.
OpenStreetMap data is under the Open Database License (ODbL), which has credit and share-alike terms. Check the terms before reuse.

entries.name: Route line fingerprint
entries.plain: A short technical code used to decide whether a road-snapped line must be redrawn. It has no meaning for readers.
entries.definition: The first 12 hexadecimal digits of an MD5 checksum (a fixed-length fingerprint of text) of the route's stop sequence plus the version of the snapping method. In the 2026-10 snapshot it is present on the 99 routes drawn along roads, all of them municipal routes, and absent on shape and OpenStreetMap (OSM) routes.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: snap_routes in network.py. If a route's sig matches the one in the last published file, the earlier line is reused instead of snapping again.
entries.source_detail: Computed by network.py from the stop sequence of the route (GTFS stop_times.txt and stops.txt)
entries.how_to_read: Ignore it for analysis. A changed sig means the stops of the route or the snapping method changed.
caveats: It is not an identifier. Use operator and route_id to point to a route.

entries.plain_es: Un código técnico corto que se usa para decidir si hay que volver a dibujar una línea ajustada a las carreteras. No tiene significado para el público.
entries.name_es: Huella de la línea de la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: No lo tome en cuenta para el análisis. Un sig distinto significa que cambiaron las paradas de la ruta o el método de ajuste.

entries.name: Routes on the map
entries.plain: In the file of 2026-10-02 the map has 165 transit routes: 149 come from public timetable feeds and volunteers mapped 16 in OpenStreetMap.
entries.definition: The count of route lines in the published routes file: all operators with a feed, plus the routes of the volunteer-mapped OpenStreetMap group. The Transit tab shows the count as 'routes on the map'.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten by each full build and by a nightly transit refresh that finds a changed feed (last write: 2026-10-02)

entries.method: network.py counts the routes it writes to the routes file. Routes in a feed without a shape or stops are not drawn and not counted. The Transit tab reads the count from meta.json.
entries.source_detail: meta.json 'network.routes'; transit_routes.geojson; site/js/network.js (renderNetSummary)
entries.how_to_read: It counts routes, not the trips on them. One route can have two drawn lines, one for each direction.
caveats: The routes that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap have no timetable, so they are not scheduled service.

entries.plain_es: En el archivo del 2026-10-02, el mapa tiene 165 rutas de transporte colectivo: 149 vienen de fuentes públicas de horarios y 16 las mapearon personas voluntarias en OpenStreetMap.
entries.name_es: Rutas en el mapa
entries.how_to_read_es: Cuenta rutas, no los viajes que se hacen en ellas. Una ruta puede tener dos líneas dibujadas, una para cada dirección.

entries.name: Scheduled trips per day on the route
entries.plain: How many trips the operator's timetable has on this route on a typical weekday, a Saturday and a Sunday. Zero means none listed, which for volunteer-mapped routes means no timetable.
entries.definition: Three counts per route: trips_weekday, trips_saturday and trips_sunday. A trip is one scheduled run listed in the feed's trips file (a feed is the set of GTFS files in which an operator publishes its stops, routes, trips and times). Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and Guaynabo list each direction as its own trip, so an out-and-back journey counts as two. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the other 23 feeds give every trip of a route the same direction code, so a trip there may be one leg or a whole loop. The weekday count uses the reference weekday described under Typical weekday. In the 2026-10 snapshot the largest values are 166 on weekdays and 138 on Saturdays and Sundays (Tren Urbano).

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.py counts the trips of the route whose service runs on each day type. Exceptions in calendar_dates.txt (holidays, added or removed dates) are not applied, and the date range of each service pattern is not checked.
entries.source_detail: GTFS trips.txt joined to calendar.txt (service days); calendar_dates.txt only when a feed has no calendar.txt
entries.how_to_read: Compare routes of the same operator. A route with more trips has more scheduled service. The map draws wider lines for higher weekday counts. A timetable covers the dates from the operator's feed.start to feed.end in operators.json, not the build date. In the build of 2026-10-02 the earliest start is 2023-01-01 and the latest end is 2029-12-31; Ponce's feed ended 2024-12-31. Cite both the build date and the feed dates.
caveats: In the ATI feed read on 2026-10-02, route 1 shows 81 weekday trips, but 30 of them belong to a holiday service pattern that the feed removes on most dates. Without them the count is 51.
A feed that gives no Saturday or Sunday service shows 0 for those days. In the 2026-10 snapshot, only ATI, Guaynabo, Juncos and Vega Alta list Saturday service, and only ATI lists Sunday service.
Counts are for the timetable in the feed, whether or not it has expired.

entries.plain_es: Cuántos viajes tiene el horario del operador en esta ruta en un día típico de lunes a viernes, un sábado y un domingo. Cero significa que no hay ninguno en la lista; en las rutas mapeadas por personas voluntarias, significa que no hay horario.
entries.name_es: Viajes programados por día en la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare rutas del mismo operador. Una ruta con más viajes tiene más servicio programado. El mapa dibuja líneas más anchas cuando hay más viajes de lunes a viernes. Un horario cubre las fechas desde feed.start hasta feed.end del operador en operators.json, no la fecha de compilación. En la compilación del 2026-10-02, el inicio más temprano es 2023-01-01 y el final más tardío es 2029-12-31; la fuente de datos de Ponce terminó el 2024-12-31. Cite tanto la fecha de compilación como las fechas de las fuentes de datos.

entries.name: Transit route colour in the feed

In the 2026-10 snapshot it is present on 113 routes (67 different colours) and null for the other 52, including every OpenStreetMap (OSM) route.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: Copied from the feed after checking that it has exactly six hex digits.
entries.source_detail: GTFS routes.txt field route_color
entries.how_to_read: Use it only if you want the operator's own colour scheme.
caveats: The map and the 3D view colour lines by mode and type of operator and ignore this field: rail red, ferries teal, ATI buses blue, municipal buses green and OSM routes gold.

entries.plain_es: El color que el operador le dio a la ruta en su fuente de horarios, como código hexadecimal, por ejemplo #0000FF. El mapa no lo usa.
entries.name_es: Color de la ruta de transporte colectivo en la fuente de datos

entries.name: Transit route id
entries.plain: The id the operator uses for the route. For volunteer-mapped routes, an r followed by the OpenStreetMap (OSM) number.
entries.definition: Text id. Feed routes: the route_id in the operator's routes file (examples from the 2026-10 snapshot: 92, MA004, Rt 1, trolley, Zona Urbana). OSM routes: r plus the OSM relation number (example r938736). It is unique within one operator but not across operators: in the 2026-10 snapshot the 165 routes have 146 different ids in total.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: Copied from the feed, or built from the OSM relation id.
entries.source_detail: GTFS routes.txt field route_id; OpenStreetMap route relation number
entries.how_to_read: Use operator and route_id together to point to one route.
caveats: Two municipal systems can use the same id.
A few route ids lost a letter in the source (in the 2026-10 snapshot, for example, the route id Ruta Marn Bajo, whose name field reads Marin Bajo).
entries.example: MA004

OpenStreetMap (OSM) routes: Público if the OSM route type is share_taxi or the network name contains público, otherwise Bus.

caveats: Any rail route would be labelled Tren Urbano. In the 2026-10 snapshot the only rail route is Tren Urbano.
