entries.name_es: Número o nombre corto de la ruta de transporte colectivo

entries.name: Transit routes
entries.plain: The lines of public transit routes: the Tren Urbano, buses and ferries of Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), municipal routes, and públicos and trolley routes that volunteers mapped. The 2026-10 snapshot has 165 routes. Of these, only 50 lines come from an operator's own route shape; the rest were drawn by the observatory along roads, or by volunteers.
entries.definition: The file transit_routes.geojson has one feature per route. Each is one line made of one or more parts (GeoJSON type MultiLineString; 1 to 94 parts in the 2026-10 snapshot) with properties for the operator, names, mode, trips per day, first and last departure and how the line was drawn. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 38 routes come from the ATI feed, 111 from 24 municipal feeds and 16 from OpenStreetMap (OSM). On the map, line colour follows the mode and the type of operator, line width grows with weekday trips, and the line style shows how the line was drawn.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap routes are read at each full build; the nightly refresh asks for them too and, when the OpenStreetMap service does not answer, keeps the OpenStreetMap routes it already has. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.py builds the routes from each feed (see How route lines are drawn) and load_osm_routes adds the OSM routes. Coordinates have 5 decimals (about 1 m).
entries.source_detail: ATI timetable zip; municipal timetable zips found through the registry of the National Rural Transit Assistance Program portal; OpenStreetMap route relations through the Overpass API; road network from OpenStreetMap (roads.bin)
entries.how_to_read: Open a route to see its operator, trips per day, first and last departure and whether its timetable is current, expiring or expired.
caveats: Routes of expired timetables stay on the map. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 38 of the 165 routes belong to operators whose feed had ended by the build date.
A route in a feed is not proof that the service runs today. Check the feed status.
OSM routes have no timetable. Their trip counts are 0, which means none published, not none running.
Lines and stops of expired timetables look the same as current ones on the map. The Expired badge appears only when a route is opened and in the Operators list.

Terms differ by source. The terms of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) say the data are provided as is, without warranty, and that an app built on them must make clear it is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI. The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. Parts drawn from OpenStreetMap are under the Open Database License (credit and share-alike). Check each source's terms before reuse.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit routes

entries.plain_es: Las líneas de las rutas de transporte colectivo: el Tren Urbano, las guaguas y lanchas de la Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), las rutas municipales, y rutas de públicos y trolleys que mapearon personas voluntarias. El corte de datos de 2026-10 tiene 165 rutas. De ellas, solo 50 líneas vienen de la forma de ruta del propio operador; las demás las dibujó el observatorio por las carreteras, o las dibujaron personas voluntarias.
entries.name_es: Rutas de transporte colectivo
entries.how_to_read_es: Abra una ruta para ver su operador, los viajes por día, la primera y la última salida, y si su horario está vigente, por vencer o vencido.

entries.name: Distance from a census block to the nearest scheduled stop
entries.plain: How many metres in a straight line from the block to the closest scheduled stop. Values above 9,999 are shown as 9,999.
entries.definition: The fourth value of each row in population_blocks.json, in whole metres (the decimals are cut off). It uses every scheduled stop in the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and municipal feeds, whatever the state of the feed. In the build of 2026-10-02, values run from 2 to 9999; 6,419 blocks are capped at 9999; and 925,788 residents (28.2%) are in blocks at 400 m or less.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.coverage uses a spatial index to find the nearest stop and converts the degree difference to metres (111,320 m per degree of latitude, shortened for longitude).
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0; distances use the scheduled stops in transport.json (sources ati_gtfs and muni_gtfs)
entries.how_to_read: A small value means a stop is near. Use 400 m for the walk-access measure and 800 m for the service-gap layer.
caveats: The nearest stop is found in degrees, so a few blocks can have a slightly longer distance than the true nearest stop; recomputing the figures from the published files changes the total near 400 m by under 0.1% in the 2026-10 snapshot.
The distance ignores streets, barriers and the timetable. A stop of an expired timetable counts as a stop.
The distance counts stops of expired timetables. For tourism places, the matching distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable is ts_m in place_access.json.
entries.plain_es: Cuántos metros hay en línea recta desde el bloque hasta la parada con horario más cercana. Los valores mayores de 9,999 se muestran como 9,999.
entries.name_es: Distancia de un bloque censal a la parada con horario más cercana
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor pequeño significa que hay una parada cerca. Use 400 m para la medida de acceso a pie y 800 m para la capa de brechas de servicio.

entries.name: Distances used for walking, gaps, transfers and removing duplicates
entries.plain: The observatory uses fixed straight-line distances. 400 m is a walk to a stop, 800 m is a service gap and 250 m is an integration point. Distances from 30 m to 2 km remove duplicate points.
entries.definition: 400 m: about a quarter mile, used for the walk rings on the map, the shares of tourism places near any mapped stop and near a stop with a current timetable, and the resident coverage. 800 m: a service gap, and the outer limit of the 'Stop 400–800 m away' and 'Only expired or unscheduled stops within 800 m' classes of the access profile. 250 m: two stops of different operators count as an integration point. 30 m: an OpenStreetMap (OSM) stop that close to a scheduled stop is treated as the same stop. 200 m (rail stations and ferry terminals) and 100 m (bus stations): OSM station points that close to a same-kind point are folded together. 2 km: an OSM aerodrome that close to a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airport is dropped. 500 m: how far a stop may be moved to reach a road when a route line is snapped.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the program code

entries.method: Constants in network.py (WALK_M, TRANSFER_M), transport.py (WALK_M, HUB_FOLD_M) and access.py (NEAR_M, FAR_M). Distances are computed on a flat approximation: 111,320 m per degree of latitude, and the same figure scaled by the cosine of the latitude for longitude.
entries.how_to_read: All distances are straight lines, not walking routes.
caveats: The distances are planning conventions chosen for the observatory, not legal or engineering standards.
entries.plain_es: El observatorio usa distancias fijas en línea recta. 400 m es una caminata hasta una parada, 800 m marca una brecha de servicio y 250 m, un punto de integración. Las distancias de 30 m a 2 km sirven para eliminar puntos duplicados.
entries.name_es: Distancias que se usan para caminar, brechas, trasbordos y eliminar duplicados
entries.how_to_read_es: Todas las distancias son en línea recta, no rutas a pie.

entries.name: Integration points
entries.plain: Places where a stop of one transit system lies within 250 m of a stop of another system. They are natural places to coordinate timetables, fares and signs.
entries.definition: Places where scheduled stops of two different operators are 250 m or less apart (straight line). To avoid near-duplicates, the build keeps one pair for each pair of operators in each 0.001-degree cell (about 110 m) of the first stop. One marker is drawn for each kept pair, halfway between its two stops. The map draws at most the 600 closest.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten by each full build and by a nightly transit refresh that finds a changed feed (last write: 2026-10-02)

entries.method: network.py (transfers) compares every scheduled stop with the stops near it, keeps pairs of different operators within 250 m, keeps one pair for each pair of operators and each 0.001-degree cell (about 110 m) of the first stop, sorts by distance and stores the 600 closest with the total (counted after the thinning).
entries.source_detail: operators.json 'transfers' and 'transfers_total' (network.py, transfers); site/js/network.js (setXfer)
entries.how_to_read: Each marker names the two stops and their distance. It marks a candidate for coordination, not a transfer riders can make today. In the data of 2026-10-02 there are 366 such places (1,336 pairs of stops are within 250 m before this thinning), and all 366 are drawn.
caveats: Nothing checks that the routes at the two stops connect, that their times match, or that there is a safe crossing between the stops.
Stops of operators whose timetables have expired are included.
Only timetable stops count. Stops from OpenStreetMap are not included.
Two stops of the same operator never make a pair.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Integration points

entries.plain_es: Lugares donde una parada de un sistema de transporte colectivo está a 250 m o menos de una parada de otro sistema. Son lugares naturales para coordinar horarios, tarifas y rótulos.
entries.name_es: Puntos de integración
entries.how_to_read_es: Cada marcador nombra las dos paradas y la distancia entre ellas. Señala un candidato para la coordinación, no un trasbordo que las personas puedan hacer hoy. En los datos del 2026-10-02 hay 366 de estos lugares (1,336 pares de paradas están a 250 m o menos antes de esta depuración), y se dibujan los 366.

entries.name: Integration points: nearby stops of different operators
entries.plain: Places where a stop of one transit system lies within 250 metres of a stop of another system, a starting point for looking at possible transfers. There are 366 in the 2026-10 snapshot.
entries.definition: The transfers list in operators.json has one record for each pair of nearby stops of different operators; its keys are listed under Codes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the total found is 366 (transfers_total) and the list is cut at 600, so all are present. Most pairs involve Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI): 362 of 366.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.transfers compares every scheduled stop with the others within 250 m, keeps pairs from different operators, keeps only one pair for each pair of operators in each 0.001-degree cell (about 110 m) around the first stop, and sorts by distance.
entries.how_to_read: A short distance means stops of two systems are almost the same place.
caveats: A pair shows that the stops are close. It does not show that riders can transfer: the observatory does not compare timetables, walking routes or fares.
Stops of expired timetables are included; in the 2026-10 snapshot some pairs involve Caguas, Juncos or San Lorenzo, whose feeds had ended.

values.a: Operator id of the first stop (for example ati).
values.b: Operator id of the second stop.
values.lat: Latitude of the midpoint of the two stops (5 decimals).
values.lng: Longitude of the midpoint of the two stops (5 decimals).
values.d: Distance between the two stops in whole metres (0 to 249 in the 2026-10 snapshot).

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Integration points

entries.plain_es: Lugares donde una parada de un sistema de transporte colectivo está a 250 metros o menos de una parada de otro sistema, un punto de partida para estudiar posibles transbordos. Hay 366 en el corte de datos de 2026-10.
entries.name_es: Puntos de integración: paradas cercanas de operadores distintos
entries.how_to_read_es: Una distancia corta significa que las paradas de los dos sistemas están casi en el mismo lugar.

entries.name: Population by census block, with distance to the nearest scheduled stop
entries.plain: A list of the 36,570 census blocks that had residents in the 2020 Census. Each row gives the block's position, its 2020 population and how far it is from the nearest scheduled stop.
entries.definition: The file population_blocks.json is a list of 36,570 rows, one for each 2020 Census block that has residents. Each row is [longitude, latitude, residents, metres], described under Codes. The rows hold 3,285,874 residents in total (2020 Census). The 2D map uses the file for service gaps and the route planner, and the 3D view uses it for the route planner. The coverage figures in operators.json are computed from the same blocks.

coverage.frequency: 2020 population; the distance column is rewritten whenever the stops change

entries.method: load_blocks in network.py reads the 2020 Census block layer of TIGERweb for Puerto Rico (state code 72), keeps blocks with POP100 above 0 and stores the internal point. coverage() then replaces the block's county code with the distance to the nearest scheduled stop.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0; distances use the scheduled stops in transport.json (sources ati_gtfs and muni_gtfs)
entries.how_to_read: Add up residents for blocks that meet a distance rule. For example, blocks with metres of 400 or less hold the residents counted as near a stop.
caveats: The 2020 Census applies privacy protection to block counts, so small blocks are not exact.
Positions are rounded, and the distance is a straight line from the block's internal point, not from where people live in the block.

A row is a statistical block with its internal point, not a home. In the 2020 Census counts used, 50 rows hold exactly one resident. Do not use rows with very small counts to identify or locate any household.
Census Bureau data are a US Government work; the Bureau asks to be cited as the source.

values.1st value: longitude: Longitude of the block's internal point, in decimal degrees, rounded to 4 decimals (about 11 m). The internal point is a point the Census Bureau places inside the block, usually near its centre.
values.2nd value: latitude: Latitude of the block's internal point, in decimal degrees, rounded to 4 decimals.
values.3rd value: residents: The 2020 Census population of the block (the Census field POP100, total people counted in the block). Blocks with 0 residents are left out.
values.4th value: metres: Straight-line distance in whole metres from the internal point to the nearest scheduled stop, capped at 9,999. Stops of expired timetables count. It is a distance, not a count of housing units.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Residents far from service

entries.plain_es: Una lista de los 36,570 bloques censales que tenían residentes en el Censo de 2020. Cada fila da la posición del bloque, su población de 2020 y a qué distancia está de la parada con horario más cercana.
entries.name_es: Población por bloque censal, con la distancia a la parada con horario más cercana
entries.how_to_read_es: Sume los residentes de los bloques que cumplen una regla de distancia. Por ejemplo, los bloques con un valor de metres de 400 o menos contienen a los residentes que se cuentan como cerca de una parada.

entries.name: Residents counted for coverage (by municipality)
entries.plain: How many residents each municipality has in the coverage figures: the 2020 Census count for blocks with at least one resident. For all of Puerto Rico it is 3,285,874 people.
entries.definition: The field pop in each municipality record of operators.json coverage: the sum of the 2020 Census residents (the Census field POP100, total people counted in the block) of the municipality's census blocks that have residents. The 78 values add up to 3,285,874, the Puerto Rico total in population_blocks.json.

coverage.frequency: 2020 Census population; recomputed whenever the stops change

entries.method: network.coverage adds block residents by the first five digits of the block code (the county, which is the municipality).
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0
entries.how_to_read: Use it as the denominator for the share of residents near a stop.
caveats: These are 2020 Census counts, not current estimates. The Census Bureau applies privacy protection to block counts, which can shift small blocks.
Census Bureau data are a US Government work; the Bureau asks to be cited as the source.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: summary figures

entries.plain_es: Cuántos residentes tiene cada municipio en las cifras de cobertura: el conteo del Censo de 2020 para los bloques con al menos un residente. Para todo Puerto Rico son 3,285,874 personas.
entries.name_es: Residentes contados para la cobertura (por municipio)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo como denominador de la proporción de residentes cerca de una parada.

entries.name: Residents far from service (map layer)
entries.plain: Residents who live more than 800 m, in a straight line, from any scheduled stop. The map layer draws a circle for each census block with 40 or more residents that is more than 800 m from a stop. Using 2020 Census counts and the stops of the 2026-10-02 build, 1,986,126 residents (60%) in Puerto Rico live more than 800 m from any stop in a published timetable; the total counts every block, including small ones.
entries.definition: A map layer drawn from population_blocks.json: one circle for each block with more than 800 m to the nearest scheduled stop and at least 40 residents (12,790 blocks in the 2026-10 snapshot). Circle size follows the number of residents. The note on the map counts all residents in blocks more than 800 m from a stop, including blocks with fewer than 40 people.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02); residents are 2020 Census counts

entries.method: The layer filters the rows of population_blocks.json in the browser (network.js, setGaps). 800 m is about half a mile. It is a planning convention chosen by the observatory, not a legal or engineering standard.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0; distances use the scheduled stops in transport.json (sources ati_gtfs and muni_gtfs)
entries.how_to_read: Large circles in low-service areas show many residents far from a scheduled stop. People: 2020 Census. Stops and timetables: build of 2026-10-02.
caveats: Stops from expired timetables still count as stops. Públicos, systems for which no timetable feed was found and stops mapped only in OpenStreetMap are not counted. The true gap could therefore be larger or smaller.
Straight-line distance and 2020 counts. It is a planning aid, not a demand forecast.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Residents far from service

entries.plain_es: Los residentes que viven a más de 800 m, en línea recta, de cualquier parada con horario. La capa del mapa dibuja un círculo para cada bloque censal con 40 residentes o más que está a más de 800 m de una parada. Con los conteos del Censo de 2020 y las paradas de la compilación del 2026-10-02, 1,986,126 residentes (60%) en Puerto Rico viven a más de 800 m de cualquier parada de un horario publicado; el total cuenta todos los bloques, incluso los pequeños.
entries.name_es: Residentes lejos del servicio (capa del mapa)
entries.how_to_read_es: Los círculos grandes en áreas con poco servicio muestran muchos residentes lejos de una parada con horario. Personas: Censo 2020. Paradas y horarios: compilación del 2026-10-02.

entries.name: Residents far from service (service-gap rule)
entries.plain: Residents who live more than 800 m from any scheduled stop. The Transit tab shows the total and draws circles for blocks with 40 or more residents.
entries.definition: The total residents in census blocks whose nearest scheduled stop, of any operator, is more than 800 m away (straight line), and that total as a share of all residents. Blocks with at least 40 residents are drawn as circles. A circle's radius is 2 + 0.45 times the square root of the residents, up to 14 pixels.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten by each full build and by a nightly transit refresh that finds a changed feed (last write: 2026-10-02); the browser calculates the shares when the page opens

entries.method: network.js reads population_blocks.json, adds the residents of blocks whose distance field is above 800, and draws the blocks with 40 or more residents. The distance field is capped at 9,999 m.
entries.source_detail: population_blocks.json (network.py, coverage); site/js/network.js (setGaps)
entries.how_to_read: Larger circles mean more residents far from a stop. The total counts people who live more than 800 m, in a straight line, from any scheduled stop. In the data of 2026-10-02: 1,986,126 residents (60% of 3,285,874) live more than 800 m from a scheduled stop. 12,790 blocks are drawn. 9,808 further blocks with fewer than 40 residents are in the total but not drawn.
caveats: Stops from expired timetables still count as stops, so the real gaps are larger.
800 m is a distance this tool chose (about half a mile), not an official standard. Check any agency's own definition before comparing.
Straight-line distance. A stop 700 m away in a straight line can be far by road.
Residents are the 2020 Census counts, assigned to each census block's internal point.

In the data of 2026-10-02, fifteen municipal systems and the públicos authority report to the federal transit database but publish no timetable feed, so the people they serve count as far from service here. Do not rank municipalities on this figure without checking whether their operator publishes a feed.

In the data of 2026-10-02, the 60% counts residents more than 800 m from a stop. A further 11% (373,960 residents) live 37 to 800 m from a stop and are not in it. It is not the share of residents without transport.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Residents far from service

entries.plain_es: Los residentes que viven a más de 800 m de cualquier parada con horario. La pestaña "Transporte" muestra el total y dibuja círculos para los bloques con 40 residentes o más.
entries.name_es: Residentes lejos del servicio (regla de brecha de servicio)
entries.how_to_read_es: Los círculos más grandes significan más residentes lejos de una parada. El total cuenta a las personas que viven a más de 800 m, en línea recta, de cualquier parada con horario. En los datos del 2026-10-02: 1,986,126 residentes (60% de 3,285,874) viven a más de 800 m de una parada con horario. Se dibujan 12,790 bloques. Otros 9,808 bloques con menos de 40 residentes están en el total, pero no se dibujan.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop
entries.plain: The share of Puerto Rico's residents who live within 400 m of a stop in a public timetable. In the data of 2026-10-02 the Transit tab shows 28%, or 22% when only unexpired timetables count.
entries.definition: Residents (2020 Census) in census blocks whose nearest scheduled stop is 400 m or less away, divided by all residents in blocks. The second figure counts a block only when a stop of an operator whose timetable has not expired lies within 400 m. A scheduled stop is a stop in a public timetable feed (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) from ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or from a municipal system.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico, from the 36,570 census blocks that have residents (2020 Census); also stored for each municipality

coverage.frequency: Rewritten by each full build and by a nightly transit refresh that finds a changed feed (last write: 2026-10-02); the browser calculates the shares when the page opens

entries.method: network.py measures the straight-line distance from each block's internal point to the nearest scheduled stop. It adds the residents of blocks within 400 m, overall and for blocks near a stop of an operator that is not expired. The Transit tab divides the island totals.
entries.source_detail: network.py (coverage, WALK_M = 400); operators.json 'coverage'; site/js/network.js (renderNetSummary)
entries.how_to_read: It says how many people have a stop near their block. It does not say how often vehicles come, where they go, or whether people can reach the stop on foot. In the data of 2026-10-02: 925,788 of 3,285,874 residents, or 28.2%, live within 400 m of a scheduled stop, and 729,507 residents, or 22.2%, live within 400 m of a stop of an operator whose timetable has not expired.
caveats: Straight-line distance, not walking distance.
A stop is a place in a timetable feed. It says nothing about frequency or hours of service.
Residents are the 2020 Census counts, assigned to each block's internal point.
Routes mapped only in OpenStreetMap (públicos) have no stops here, so no resident is counted as served by them.

In the data of 2026-10-02, fifteen municipal systems and the públicos authority report to the federal transit database but publish no timetable feed, so the people they serve count as unserved here. Do not rank municipalities on this figure without checking whether their operator publishes a feed.
The first figure includes stops of operators whose timetables have expired.

In the data of 2026-10-02, of all residents 28% are within 400 m of a stop, 60% are more than 800 m from every stop, and the other 11% (373,960 residents) are 400 to 800 m away. The shares are rounded.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: summary figures

entries.plain_es: La proporción de residentes de Puerto Rico que viven a 400 m o menos de una parada de un horario público. Con los datos del 2026-10-02, la pestaña "Transporte" muestra 28%, o 22% si solo cuentan los horarios que no han vencido.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario
entries.how_to_read_es: Indica cuántas personas tienen una parada cerca de su bloque. No indica con qué frecuencia pasan los vehículos, adónde van ni si las personas pueden llegar a pie a la parada. En los datos del 2026-10-02: 925,788 de 3,285,874 residentes, o el 28.2%, viven a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario, y 729,507 residentes, o el 22.2%, viven a 400 m o menos de una parada de un operador cuyo horario no ha vencido.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (coverage records in the operators file)
entries.plain: How many residents live in blocks within 400 metres (about a quarter mile, in a straight line) of a scheduled stop. Using 2020 Census counts and the stops of the 2026-10-02 build, it is 925,788 of 3,285,874 residents in Puerto Rico: 28.2% counting every scheduled stop, 22.2% counting only operators whose timetable has not ended.
entries.definition: Fields served and served_pct in each municipality record of operators.json coverage. served: residents of census blocks whose nearest scheduled stop (any operator, any feed status) is 400 m or less away in a straight line. served_pct: served divided by pop, times 100, one decimal. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 40 of 78 municipalities have 0 residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop. The same values are copied into municipalities.json as pop_served_400m and pop_served_pct.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02); residents are 2020 Census counts

entries.method: network.coverage finds the nearest scheduled stop of each block and keeps the block if the distance is 400 m or less. The block's position is the Census Bureau's internal point. 400 m is about a quarter mile. It is the walking distance the observatory uses, a planning convention and not a legal or engineering standard.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0; distances use the scheduled stops in transport.json (sources ati_gtfs and muni_gtfs)
entries.how_to_read: A higher share means more residents have a scheduled stop close by. It says nothing about how often vehicles come or where they go. People: 2020 Census. Stops and timetables: build of 2026-10-02.
caveats: Straight-line distance, not walking distance. Hills, rivers, highways and walls can make the real walk longer.
Only scheduled stops count. Stops mapped only in OpenStreetMap are not used.
Stops of expired timetables still count here. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the active figures leave them out: 729,507 residents (22.2%).
A block is counted at one point, so a block that straddles the 400 m line is all in or all out.

If you recompute this from the published block and stop files, the total differs by under 0.1% in the 2026-10 snapshot. Block positions in the file are rounded, and the observatory finds the nearest stop in degrees rather than metres.

A low or zero share can mean that the observatory found no timetable, not that no service runs. In the 2026-10 snapshot, no timetable feed was found in the registry the observatory reads for 15 municipal systems and the públicos authority, and públicos are never counted. Do not rank municipalities by this share without checking each operator's feed status.
Census Bureau data are a US Government work; the Bureau asks to be cited as the source. The stop data carry the terms described in the entry on transit routes.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: summary figures

entries.plain_es: Cuántos residentes viven en bloques a 400 metros o menos (cerca de un cuarto de milla, en línea recta) de una parada con horario. Con los conteos del Censo de 2020 y las paradas de la compilación del 2026-10-02, son 925,788 de 3,285,874 residentes en Puerto Rico: 28.2% si se cuentan todas las paradas con horario, 22.2% si solo se cuentan los operadores cuyo horario no ha terminado.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario (registros de cobertura del archivo de operadores)
entries.how_to_read_es: Una proporción más alta significa que más residentes tienen cerca una parada con horario. No dice nada sobre la frecuencia de los vehículos ni sobre adónde van. Personas: Censo 2020. Paradas y horarios: compilación del 2026-10-02.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop, excluding expired timetables
entries.plain: Like the 400 m measure, but it leaves out stops of operators whose timetable had ended. With 2020 Census counts and the stops of the 2026-10-02 build, it is 729,507 residents (22.2%) in Puerto Rico, compared with 28.2% when every stop counts.
entries.definition: Fields served_active and served_active_pct in each municipality record of operators.json coverage. served_active: residents of blocks with at least one scheduled stop within 400 m that belongs to an operator whose feed status was not expired on the build date. served_active_pct: that number divided by pop, times 100, one decimal. Copied into municipalities.json as pop_served_active_pct.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02); residents are 2020 Census counts

entries.method: network.coverage queries all scheduled stops within 400 m of each block and skips those whose operator id is in the set of expired operators (inactive_ops).
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0; distances use the scheduled stops in transport.json (sources ati_gtfs and muni_gtfs)
entries.how_to_read: Compare with the all-stops measure. The map calls this a stop with a current timetable; for tourism places the matching measure is municipalities.acc_cur400_pct. The gap shows how much of the measured access depends on timetables that have ended. People: 2020 Census. Stops and timetables: build of 2026-10-02. For example, in the 2026-10-02 build Ponce shows 56.6% with every stop and 0.0% with only active timetables, because its feed ended on 2024-12-31.
caveats: The expired set is fixed on the build date. On 2026-10-02 it includes the 7 operators with an expired feed: Caguas, Cidra, Fajardo, Hatillo, Juncos, Ponce, San Lorenzo. An expiring feed still counts as active.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, in Manatí and Carolina this figure is higher than the all-stops figure (by 35 and 223 residents), because the two are found with different search steps.

A low or zero share can mean that the observatory found no timetable, not that no service runs. In the 2026-10 snapshot, no timetable feed was found in the registry the observatory reads for 15 municipal systems and the públicos authority, and públicos are never counted. Do not rank municipalities by this share without checking each operator's feed status.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: summary figures

entries.plain_es: Igual que la medida de 400 m, pero deja fuera las paradas de operadores cuyo horario había terminado. Con los conteos del Censo de 2020 y las paradas de la compilación del 2026-10-02, son 729,507 residentes (22.2%) en Puerto Rico, frente a 28.2% cuando cuentan todas las paradas.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario, sin los horarios vencidos
entries.how_to_read_es: Compárela con la medida de todas las paradas. El mapa llama a esto una parada con horario vigente; para los lugares turísticos, la medida equivalente es municipalities.acc_cur400_pct. La diferencia muestra cuánto del acceso medido depende de horarios que ya terminaron. Personas: Censo 2020. Paradas y horarios: compilación del 2026-10-02. Por ejemplo, en la compilación del 2026-10-02, Ponce muestra 56.6% con todas las paradas y 0.0% solo con los horarios activos, porque su fuente de datos terminó el 2024-12-31.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) stops, municipal stops, or both
entries.plain: How many residents live within 400 metres of a stop of Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), of a municipal system, or of both. With 2020 Census counts and the stops of the 2026-10-02 build, 487,026 residents of Puerto Rico are near an ATI stop, 609,383 are near a municipal stop and 171,389 are near both.
entries.definition: Fields served_ati, served_muni and served_both in each municipality record of operators.json coverage. served_ati: residents of blocks with at least one ATI stop within 400 m. served_muni: residents with at least one stop of a municipal operator (any scheduled stop that is not ATI's) within 400 m. served_both: residents with both. Copied into municipalities.json as pop_served_ati and pop_served_muni.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02); residents are 2020 Census counts

entries.method: network.coverage flags each block for ATI, municipal or both from the stops found within 400 m. Expired municipal feeds still count here.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census Blocks (tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 10), STATE=72, fields GEOID, POP100, INTPTLAT and INTPTLON, blocks with POP100 above 0; distances use the scheduled stops in transport.json (sources ati_gtfs and muni_gtfs)
entries.how_to_read: served_both shows where the two kinds of system overlap, which is where coordination matters. People: 2020 Census. Stops and timetables: build of 2026-10-02.
caveats: Expired municipal timetables are included. See the active measure for the version without them.
A resident near a stop of both counts once in served_both and also in served_ati and in served_muni, so the three do not add up.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, in 11 municipalities the all-stops figure differs from served_ati + served_muni - served_both, by up to 287 residents, because the two are found with different search steps.

A low or zero share can mean that the observatory found no timetable, not that no service runs. In the 2026-10 snapshot, no timetable feed was found in the registry the observatory reads for 15 municipal systems and the públicos authority, and públicos are never counted. Do not rank municipalities by this share without checking each operator's feed status.
entries.plain_es: Cuántos residentes viven a 400 metros o menos de una parada de la Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), de un sistema municipal o de ambos. Con los conteos del Censo de 2020 y las paradas de la compilación del 2026-10-02, 487,026 residentes de Puerto Rico están cerca de una parada de la ATI, 609,383 cerca de una parada municipal y 171,389 cerca de ambas.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de paradas de la Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), de paradas municipales o de ambas
entries.how_to_read_es: served_both muestra dónde se superponen los dos tipos de sistema, que es donde importa la coordinación. Personas: Censo 2020. Paradas y horarios: compilación del 2026-10-02.

entries.name: Bus stations and terminals (count)
entries.plain: How many bus stations and terminals are mapped inside the municipality, from public timetable feeds and from OpenStreetMap. It counts records, not buildings.
entries.definition: Count of features of kind bus station: (1) scheduled stops that no rail or ferry route serves and whose name starts with Terminal or Estación (from the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, ATI, or from municipal feeds), and (2) OpenStreetMap features tagged amenity=bus_station, or public_transport=station without a railway tag, after removing those less than 100 m from a scheduled or already kept bus station. Bus stations are also part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: A scheduled stop becomes a bus station only by its name: the build tests whether the stop name starts with Terminal or Estación (the accent is optional, but a letter missing from the name is not tolerated). OpenStreetMap features are kept when no scheduled stop lies less than 30 m away and no scheduled or already kept bus station lies less than 100 m away. Each feature is assigned to the municipality whose boundary contains it.
entries.source_detail: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stop names (ATI and municipal feeds); OpenStreetMap tags amenity=bus_station and public_transport=station (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see where a town has a central terminal. It is a count, not a rate: larger municipalities and places with more mapping have more. It does not say how many routes the terminal serves, and a count of 8 can be eight records of one terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 91 bus stations: 44 scheduled stops (15 from the ATI feed, 29 from municipal feeds) and 47 from OpenStreetMap. Overture Maps lists 24 places as bus stations in the 2026-10 snapshot (see places.type.transportation); that is a count of place listings, not of the stations counted here.
caveats: The scheduled-stop rule rests on the stop name alone. A stop named Terminal counts as a station whatever it looks like, and a station with another name is missed. In some municipal feeds the accented letter is missing from the name. Examples from the 2026-10 snapshot: San Lorenzo's feed has 8 stops, all named "Terminal" and all at one location, so all 8 count. In Canóvanas, "Estacin Multimodal" stays an ordinary stop. In Guaynabo, "Estacion tren Torrimar" counts as a bus station about 160 m from the rail station "Estación Torrimar", so one place counts twice.

Counts records, not buildings. In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan's 13 include a boarding record and an alighting record of the same terminal (Sagrado Corazón) and two records with the same name, "Estacion Martinez Nadal".
In the 2026-10 snapshot, 39 of the 47 OpenStreetMap bus stations have público or pública in the name (33 say Carros Públicos, shared-taxi terminals); the observatory holds no timetable for them.

Until the 2026-11 fix, the ATI terminal named Terminal de Cataño was counted in San Juan: it falls just outside every municipal boundary, and the build gave such a point the municipality with the nearest centre point, so Cataño showed 0. It now takes the nearest boundary and counts in Cataño.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.

The nightly refresh counts the stations again from transport.json, so the scheduled stations follow the feeds. The OpenStreetMap stations change only at a full build (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: San Juan 13 (some are two records of one terminal); Ponce 2; San Lorenzo 8 (eight records of one terminal).
entries.plain_es: Cuántas estaciones y terminales de guaguas están registradas en el mapa dentro del municipio, según los horarios públicos y OpenStreetMap. Cuenta registros, no edificios.
entries.name_es: Estaciones y terminales de guaguas (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver dónde un pueblo tiene una terminal central. Es un conteo, no una tasa: los municipios más grandes y los lugares más mapeados tienen más. No indica cuántas rutas sirve la terminal, y un conteo de 8 puede ser ocho registros de una sola terminal. En el corte de datos 2026-10 la isla tiene 91 estaciones de guaguas: 44 paradas con horario (15 de la fuente de la ATI y 29 de fuentes municipales) y 47 de OpenStreetMap. Overture Maps lista 24 lugares como estaciones de guaguas en el corte de datos 2026-10 (vea places.type.transportation); ese es un conteo de listados de lugares, no de las estaciones que se cuentan aquí.

entries.name: End date of the stop's timetable feed
entries.plain: The last date covered by the published timetable of the operator that lists the stop. After this date the timetable no longer applies. The stop popup says 'Timetable valid until' this date, or 'Timetable ended' when the date has passed.
entries.definition: A date written YYYY-MM-DD: the end date of the operator's timetable feed (feed.end in operators.json), copied onto each scheduled stop of that operator. All 3,847 scheduled stops have it in the 2026-10 snapshot. It is missing from points that volunteers mapped, from airports, and from a stop of an operator whose feed has no end date (none in the snapshot). The end date is the latest end date among the feed's service calendars, or the feed's own end date when it has no calendar. In the 2026-10 snapshot the 3,847 stops carry 16 different dates, from 2024-12-31 (Ponce, 276 stops) to 2029-12-31 (Bayamón and Jayuya, 186 stops).

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: build_network in network.py writes the feed's end date on each scheduled stop of the operator, and the nightly refresh does the same. The stop popup compares the date with the date on your device. The access fields (ts_m, ts_calls, ts_we, stops_current and the acc_ fields) do not read this field: access.py reads the same end date from operators.json.
entries.source_detail: Timetable feed end date: the latest end_date in calendar.txt, or feed_info.txt when the feed has no calendar (see transit.feed_dates)
entries.how_to_read: Compare the date with today's date. A date in the past means that the published timetable has ended: the stop may still be served, but the file no longer says so. A date far in the future is what the publisher entered, not a promise: Bayamón and Jayuya end on 2029-12-31.
caveats: All stops of one operator share one date. The end date of a single route can be earlier (see transit.feed_dates).

The popup's test uses the date on your device. The stored operator status in operators.json is worked out on the build date, and the Transit tab recomputes it when the page opens (see transit.feed_status).
A feed can run out of dates while buses still run. The date says what the published timetable covers, not whether service stopped.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports (click a stop)

entries.plain_es: La última fecha que cubre el horario publicado del operador que incluye la parada. Después de esa fecha el horario ya no aplica. La ventana emergente de la parada dice "Horario vigente hasta el" esa fecha, o "El horario terminó el" cuando la fecha ya pasó.
entries.name_es: Fecha final de la fuente de datos de horarios de la parada
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare la fecha con la de hoy. Una fecha pasada significa que el horario publicado terminó: puede que la parada todavía tenga servicio, pero el archivo ya no lo dice. Una fecha muy lejana es la que puso quien publica, no una promesa: Bayamón y Jayuya terminan el 2029-12-31.

entries.name: Ferry terminals (count)
entries.plain: How many ferry terminals are mapped inside the municipality. Some come from the public timetable of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and some from OpenStreetMap.
entries.definition: Count of ferry terminal features: (1) scheduled stops served by a ferry route in the ATI feed and (2) OpenStreetMap features tagged amenity=ferry_terminal that lie 200 m or more from a scheduled or kept terminal. Ferry terminals are also part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: A scheduled stop is a ferry terminal when it is served by a ferry route (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, route type 4) and no rail route serves it. OpenStreetMap terminals are dropped when a scheduled stop lies less than 30 m away or a terminal lies less than 200 m away. A terminal over water has no containing boundary, so it goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest.
entries.source_detail: ATI GTFS feed; OpenStreetMap amenity=ferry_terminal (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: A ferry terminal marks a boat connection. This is a count, not a rate, and it does not tell which routes or how many sailings serve the terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 13 ferry terminals: 6 from the ATI feed and 7 from OpenStreetMap.
caveats: OpenStreetMap ferry terminals can include other piers. In the 2026-10 snapshot they include a cruise-ship pier in San Juan and two terminals with no name.

A terminal over water belongs to the municipality whose boundary is nearest. Until the 2026-11 fix it went to the municipality with the nearest centre point, which can differ from the municipality the service is named for: the Cataño ferry terminal (and the Cataño bus terminal) was counted in San Juan, and Cataño showed 0 ferry terminals. Both now count in Cataño.
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.

The nightly refresh counts the terminals again from transport.json, so the scheduled terminals follow the feeds. The OpenStreetMap terminals change only at a full build (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

entries.example: In the 2026-10 snapshot: San Juan 5; Ceiba 3; Vieques 2.
entries.plain_es: Cuántas terminales de lanchas están registradas en el mapa dentro del municipio. Algunas vienen del horario público de la Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) y otras de OpenStreetMap.
entries.name_es: Terminales de lanchas (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Una terminal de lanchas señala una conexión por barco. Es un conteo, no una tasa, y no indica qué rutas ni cuántos viajes sirven la terminal. En el corte de datos 2026-10 la isla tiene 13 terminales de lanchas: 6 de la fuente de la ATI y 7 de OpenStreetMap.

entries.name: Modes served at the stop
entries.plain: The kinds of vehicle that call at a scheduled stop: bus, rail or ferry.
entries.definition: A list of modes taken from the routes that call at the stop. A route's mode comes from its General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) route_type (rail for types 1, 2 and 12; bus for 3 and 11; ferry for 4; other types are mapped to tram, cable, gondola or funicular). The list is sorted and has no repeats. It is empty when no route calls at the stop. Only scheduled stops have it.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.py collects the route ids from stop_times.txt for the stop, then the mode of each route.
entries.source_detail: GTFS routes.txt field route_type, joined to trips.txt and stop_times.txt
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 1 scheduled stop has an empty list because no trip in its feed calls there.

values.bus: A bus route calls here. 3,824 stops in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.rail: A rail route calls here (Tren Urbano). 16 stops in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.ferry: A ferry route calls here. 6 stops in the 2026-10 snapshot.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

entries.plain_es: Los tipos de vehículo que pasan por una parada con horario: guagua, tren o lancha.
entries.name_es: Modos de transporte que sirven la parada

entries.name: Municipality of the transport point
entries.plain: The municipality in which the point lies. In the 2026-10 snapshot every point has one.
entries.definition: Name of the municipality whose boundary contains the point, or the municipality whose boundary is nearest when the point lies inside no boundary (a pier or a shoreline stop, for example). Since the 2026-11 fix there are 64 different names (65 before it, when Maunabo's only stop was counted there) and none is null.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: At a full build, each point is tested against the Census Bureau's generalized (1:500,000) municipality boundaries, clipped to the shoreline (the legal boundaries run 3 nautical miles into the sea, so they are not used). A point outside every polygon is given the municipality whose polygon is nearest (muni_locate.py), so no point is null. The nightly refresh re-tests only the scheduled stops, against the web-simplified copy of those boundaries (municipios.geojson), with the same nearest-centre fallback.
entries.source_detail: TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (counties, 500k, shoreline-clipped), STATE=72
caveats: The municipality of the point is not necessarily the municipality of the operator.

The nightly refresh tests scheduled stops against boundaries simplified for the web (about 20 m), so a stop right on a boundary can fall on either side of the full-detail boundary that a full build uses.
The city field of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airport list can differ: the main San Juan airport (SJU) has city San Juan but lies in the municipality of Carolina.

Until the 2026-10 access update the nightly refresh left a stop outside every polygon without a municipality (11 scheduled stops, 4 of them ferry terminals, were null). It then used the nearest centre point, as the full build did. Since the 2026-11 fix both use the nearest polygon, which moved 7 scheduled stops: 5 on Cataño's waterfront from San Juan to Cataño, one from Carolina to Loíza and one from Maunabo to Patillas.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

entries.plain_es: El municipio donde está el punto. En el corte de datos de 2026-10, todos los puntos tienen uno.
entries.name_es: Municipio del punto de transporte

entries.name: Operator name of the scheduled stop
entries.plain: The name of the transit operator that publishes the timetable for a scheduled stop. Only scheduled stops have it.
entries.definition: Name of the operator, such as Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), City of San Juan or Autonomous Municipality of Ponce. It is the operator's name in operators.json (from the federal transit database list or the feed registry), not the agency name written inside the feed. In the 2026-10 snapshot there are 25 different names, present on 3,847 records.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: Set by network.py when it reads each feed.
entries.source_detail: FTA National Transit Database 2023 GTFS weblinks table, field Agency Name, or the operator name in the Transitland Atlas registry file feeds/nationalrtap.org.dmfr.json; fixed name for ATI
caveats: Names from the federal list and the registry have no accents (for example Municipality of Bayamon).
The name says who publishes the timetable, not who drives the vehicles.

entries.name: Operator of the transport point
entries.plain: Who runs the point. Scheduled stops carry an operator id such as ati or caguas. OpenStreetMap (OSM) points carry whatever operator name volunteers typed. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airports have none.
entries.definition: Scheduled stops: the operator id used in operators.json and in transit_routes.geojson (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 25 different values, for example ati, caguas, san_juan). OSM points: the free text of the operator tag, otherwise the network tag, otherwise null, meaning no value (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 411 points have text and 133 are null). The field is absent from FAA airport records.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: Copied from the feed (scheduled stops) or from the OSM tags.
entries.source_detail: Operator id set by network.py from the feed registry (ati for the ATI file PRITA_GTFS.zip); OpenStreetMap tags operator, then network
entries.how_to_read: Match a scheduled stop to its operator through the operators list. Treat the OSM text as a label, not as an official operator name.
caveats: The same field holds two kinds of value. An id such as ati can be joined to operators.json; OSM text such as Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses cannot.
OSM text is whatever a volunteer typed, so one operator can appear under several spellings (in the 2026-10 snapshot, for example, Tesla, Inc. and Tesla).

Municipal feeds state no license, and the terms of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) ask that an app built on its data say it is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI. See the sources listed for this entry.

entries.name: Rail stations (count)
entries.plain: How many train stations lie inside the municipality. In the 2026-10 snapshot they are all Tren Urbano stations.
entries.definition: Count of scheduled stops served by a rail route (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, route types 1, 2 and 12), plus OpenStreetMap railway stations that lie 200 m or more from a scheduled or kept rail station. Trams (route type 0) are not rail in this count. Rail stations are also part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: A scheduled stop is a rail station when at least one route that serves it has a rail route type in the feed. OpenStreetMap stations tagged railway=station (or public_transport=station with a railway tag) are dropped when a scheduled stop lies less than 30 m away or a rail station lies less than 200 m away. Each station is assigned to the municipality whose boundary contains it.
entries.source_detail: ATI GTFS feed (Tren Urbano); OpenStreetMap railway=station (extract of 1 October 2026); municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 16 rail stations. All come from the feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI): San Juan 12, Bayamón 3, Guaynabo 1. No OpenStreetMap station remains after duplicates are removed. Only three municipalities have a rail station, so 0 is the normal value.
caveats: Counts stations, not lines or service.
The nightly refresh counts the stations again from transport.json, so a change in the ATI feed shows at the next run (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

entries.name: Routes that call at the stop
entries.plain: The routes that call at a scheduled stop, by route number or name. Only scheduled stops have it.
entries.definition: A list of route labels. The label is the route's short name; if the feed has none, its long name; if neither, its route id. In the 2026-10 snapshot a stop lists at most 9 routes. The list is empty when no trip calls at the stop.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.py takes the route of every trip that has a stop time at this stop.
entries.source_detail: GTFS routes.txt fields route_short_name, route_long_name and route_id, joined to trips.txt and stop_times.txt
caveats: A label is only unique within one operator. The label 1 can mean different routes in different municipal systems.
A route can be listed here even if the operator's timetable has ended; check the operator's feed status.

entries.name: Scheduled Saturday calls at the stop (shown on the map as Saturday departures)
entries.plain: How many times the published timetable has a vehicle call at the stop on a typical Saturday. The map popup shows it as Saturday departures. The field is missing when the feed lists no Saturday call at the stop.
entries.definition: Number of stop times at this stop (a stop time is one line in a feed saying that a trip calls at a stop at a given time) for trips whose service pattern runs on Saturday (saturday = 1 in the feed's calendar.txt). A trip that calls at the stop twice counts twice, and every call counts, including the last stop of a trip. The field is left out when the count is 0, so a missing field means that the feed lists no Saturday call at this stop. Only scheduled stops can have it. In the 2026-10 snapshot 1,910 of the 3,847 scheduled stops have it, with at most 276 calls (Terminal Covadonga).

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: parse_gtfs in network.py counts the rows of stop_times.txt for each stop, on trips whose service pattern runs on Saturday, in the same pass that counts the weekday calls. Like the weekday count, it does not apply the exceptions in calendar_dates.txt (holidays, added or removed dates) and does not check the dates when a pattern starts and ends; see Typical weekday.
entries.source_detail: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stop_times.txt, trips.txt and calendar.txt
entries.how_to_read: A higher number means more scheduled Saturday calls. A missing field means that the timetable lists no Saturday call at the stop. It does not prove that no vehicle runs. In the 2026-10 snapshot only four feeds list any Saturday call: ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado; 1,369 stops), Guaynabo (273), Vega Alta (135) and Juncos (133; its feed ended on 2026-07-31). The other 21 feeds list weekday service only. The fields ts_we (place_access.json) and acc_sat400_pct are built from this field.
caveats: It counts calls in the timetable, not vehicles seen.
The stop popup on the map shows this number as Saturday departures even when the operator's timetable has ended. The popup also shows the end date of the timetable (feed_end).
A stop of an expired timetable can carry the field (Juncos, 133 stops). The access fields do not use it, because they read only stops with a current timetable.

entries.plain_es: Cuántas veces el horario publicado tiene un vehículo pasando por la parada un sábado típico. La ventana emergente del mapa lo muestra como salidas del sábado. El campo no aparece cuando la fuente de horarios no tiene ninguna salida en esa parada los sábados.

entries.how_to_read_es: Un número más alto significa más salidas programadas en sábado. Si falta el campo, el horario no indica ninguna salida en sábado por la parada. Eso no prueba que no pase ningún vehículo. En el corte de datos 2026-10, solo cuatro fuentes de datos indican alguna salida en sábado: ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado; 1,369 paradas), Guaynabo (273), Vega Alta (135) y Juncos (133; su fuente de datos terminó el 2026-07-31). Las otras 21 fuentes de datos solo indican servicio de lunes a viernes. Los campos ts_we (place_access.json) y acc_sat400_pct se construyen a partir de este campo.

entries.name: Scheduled stops from timetable feeds (count)
entries.plain: How many boarding points inside the municipality appear in a public timetable. The timetable comes from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) or from a municipal transit system.
entries.definition: Count of features inside the municipality whose source is the ATI GTFS feed or a municipal GTFS feed. GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) is the standard format for public timetable data; ATI is the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado. A feature is a boarding point in the feed's stops file (location type blank or 0) with coordinates inside Puerto Rico. The ATI feed covers Tren Urbano, the buses of AMA (Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses) and the AcuaExpreso ferries. Bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals are included when the feed lists them as stops. Each stop record in a feed counts once, even if no trip serves it on a typical weekday and even if the feed's timetable has expired. It is the scheduled part of transit_stops.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: network.py reads each feed's stops, routes, trips and stop times. A stop whose longitude lacks its minus sign (Jayuya's feed) is corrected, a stop outside Puerto Rico's bounds is dropped, and each remaining stop gets a kind (see municipalities.stop_kinds). transport.py assigns each stop to the municipality whose boundary contains it (or, when it falls outside every boundary, the municipality whose boundary is nearest) and counts the stops whose source is the ATI feed or a municipal feed.
entries.source_detail: ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) GTFS feed (PRITA_GTFS.zip) and the municipal GTFS feeds (24 in the 2026-10 snapshot) listed in the registry of the National RTAP (Rural Transit Assistance Program) portal; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: A scheduled stop has a published timetable entry. The count says nothing about how often vehicles stop there. It is a count, not a rate: large and dense municipalities have more stops. Municipalities with no feed of their own show 0 unless another operator's stops fall inside them. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 3,847 scheduled stop records, and one of them has no trip on a typical weekday. Of these, 2,881 are in a timetable that has not ended and 966 in one that has ended (stops_current and stops_expired add up to this field).
caveats: Stops of expired timetables stay in the count: 7 municipal feeds had expired when the transit data were built on 2026-10-02 (966 stops; see stops_expired).
The observatory has no real-time data. A scheduled stop shows that the timetable lists it, not that vehicles ran.

Records are not merged within a feed or across feeds. In the 2026-10 snapshot, at least 190 of the 3,847 records repeat a location already used by another record of the same feed (coordinates equal to four decimals, about 11 m), for example separate boarding and alighting records. The count is of records, not distinct places. One physical stop that two operators list also counts twice.

The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty, and its terms ask apps built on it to say they are not affiliated with ATI. The observatory is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI.
The nightly refresh rewrites the scheduled stops and counts them again, so this field follows the feeds (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

entries.name_es: Paradas con horario de las fuentes de horarios (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Una parada con horario tiene una entrada en un horario publicado. El conteo no dice nada sobre la frecuencia con que los vehículos se detienen allí. Es un conteo, no una tasa: los municipios grandes y densos tienen más paradas. Los municipios sin una fuente de horarios propia muestran 0, a menos que dentro de ellos haya paradas de otro operador. En el corte de datos 2026-10 la isla tiene 3,847 registros de paradas con horario, y uno de ellos no tiene ningún viaje en un día típico de lunes a viernes. De estos, 2,881 están en un horario que no ha terminado y 966 en uno que ya terminó (stops_current y stops_expired suman este campo).

entries.name: Scheduled Sunday calls at the stop (shown on the map as Sunday departures)
entries.plain: How many times the published timetable has a vehicle call at the stop on a typical Sunday. The map popup shows it as Sunday departures. The field is missing when the feed lists no Sunday call at the stop.
entries.definition: Number of stop times at this stop for trips whose service pattern runs on Sunday (sunday = 1 in the feed's calendar.txt). A trip that calls at the stop twice counts twice, and every call counts, including the last stop of a trip. The field is left out when the count is 0, so a missing field means that the feed lists no Sunday call at this stop. Only scheduled stops can have it. In the 2026-10 snapshot 94 of the 3,847 scheduled stops have it, with at most 138 calls (Estación Cupey).

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: parse_gtfs in network.py counts the rows of stop_times.txt for each stop, on trips whose service pattern runs on Sunday, in the same pass that counts the weekday calls. Like the weekday count, it does not apply the exceptions in calendar_dates.txt (holidays, added or removed dates) and does not check the dates when a pattern starts and ends; see Typical weekday.
entries.source_detail: GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stop_times.txt, trips.txt and calendar.txt
entries.how_to_read: A higher number means more scheduled Sunday calls. A missing field means that the timetable lists no Sunday call at the stop. It does not prove that no vehicle runs. In the 2026-10 snapshot only the feed of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) lists Sunday calls, at 94 of its 1,437 stops: all 16 rail stations, 5 ferry terminals and 73 bus stops and stations. The other 24 feeds list none. The fields ts_we (place_access.json) and acc_sun400_pct are built from this field.
caveats: It counts calls in the timetable, not vehicles seen.
The stop popup on the map shows this number as Sunday departures even when the operator's timetable has ended. The popup also shows the end date of the timetable (feed_end).

En el corte de datos 2026-10, solo la fuente de datos de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) indica salidas en domingo, en 94 de sus 1,437 paradas: las 16 estaciones de tren, 5 terminales de lanchas y 73 paradas y estaciones de guaguas. Las otras 24 fuentes de datos no indican ninguna. Los campos ts_we (place_access.json) y acc_sun400_pct se construyen a partir de este campo.

entries.name: Scheduled versus mapped transit points
entries.plain: A scheduled stop is in a timetable that an operator published; a mapped stop is a point that volunteers drew in OpenStreetMap. Only scheduled stops come with routes, weekday departures and the operator_name field; mapped points can carry operator text that volunteers typed.
entries.definition: Scheduled: a boarding point in the stops file of a public timetable feed in GTFS format (General Transit Feed Specification) from ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) or from a municipality; the source is ati_gtfs or muni_gtfs. The same feed says which routes call at the stop and at what times, so the observatory can count weekday departures. Mapped: a point or area tagged in OpenStreetMap as a bus stop, station, terminal, taxi stand, charger or airport (source osm_transport). The tag says the object exists; it holds no timetable. Airports from the list of the FAA (Federal Aviation Administration; source faa_airports) are a third group: a federal register of airports, not a transit timetable.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: Scheduled stops come from network.py. Mapped points come from transport.py. A mapped bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal that lies next to a scheduled one is dropped and the scheduled record wins (distances are in the entry on distance rules). This check runs only at a full build. Scheduled stops are not merged with each other: the same physical stop can appear once for Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and once for a municipal system, and one operator can list two stops at the same position.
entries.how_to_read: Tools that need a timetable use scheduled stops only: service coverage (residents within 400 m), service gaps, integration points, route counts and the replay of vehicles on their timetable. Tools that only need to know where a stop physically is use scheduled and mapped stops together: the 400 m walk rings on the map and the share of tourism places within 400 m of any mapped stop (kinds transit_stop, bus_stop, bus_station, rail_station and ferry_terminal). The access of tourism places to a stop with a current timetable (place_access.json and the acc_ fields of municipalities.json) uses scheduled stops only, and only those whose operator's feed has not ended.
caveats: A scheduled stop from an expired timetable is not proof of service today, and a mapped stop is not proof of service at all.
How complete the mapped stops are depends on volunteer mapping. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 393 of the 459 mapped bus stops name the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses as operator.
A count of stops is a count of records, not of distinct places. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 167 pairs of scheduled stops of different operators lie within 30 m of each other.

entries.plain_es: Una parada con horario está en un horario que publicó un operador; una parada mapeada es un punto que personas voluntarias dibujaron en OpenStreetMap. Solo las paradas con horario traen rutas, salidas de lunes a viernes y el campo operator_name; los puntos mapeados pueden traer el nombre de operador que escribieron las personas voluntarias.
entries.name_es: Puntos de transporte colectivo con horario frente a puntos mapeados
entries.how_to_read_es: Las herramientas que necesitan un horario usan solo las paradas con horario: la cobertura del servicio (residentes a 400 m o menos), las brechas de servicio, los puntos de integración, los conteos de rutas y la reproducción de los vehículos según su horario. Las herramientas que solo necesitan saber dónde está físicamente una parada usan juntas las paradas con horario y las mapeadas: los aros de 400 m a pie en el mapa y la proporción de lugares turísticos a 400 m o menos de cualquier parada mapeada (tipos transit_stop, bus_stop, bus_station, rail_station y ferry_terminal). El acceso de los lugares turísticos a una parada con horario vigente (place_access.json y los campos acc_ de municipalities.json) usa solo paradas con horario, y solo aquellas cuyo operador tiene una fuente de datos que no ha terminado.

entries.name: Scheduled weekday calls at the stop (shown on the map as weekday departures)
entries.plain: How many times the published timetable has a vehicle call at the stop on a typical weekday. The map popup calls it weekday departures.
entries.definition: Number of stop times at this stop (a stop time is one line in a feed saying that a trip calls at a stop at a given time), counting every trip in the feed whose service runs on the reference weekday (Wednesday, or the first of Tuesday, Thursday, Monday or Friday that the feed serves). A trip that calls at the stop twice counts twice. It counts every scheduled call, including the last stop of a trip, where the vehicle ends its run. Only scheduled stops have it.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.py counts rows of stop_times.txt per stop for trips on the weekday service. It does not apply the feed's calendar_dates.txt exceptions such as holidays; see Typical weekday.
entries.source_detail: GTFS stop_times.txt, trips.txt and calendar.txt
entries.how_to_read: A higher number means more scheduled calls. In the 2026-10 snapshot the largest is Terminal Covadonga with 508 calls. It does not tell how full vehicles are or whether they run on time. A timetable covers the dates from the operator's feed.start to feed.end in operators.json, not the build date. In the build of 2026-10-02 the earliest start is 2023-01-01 and the latest end is 2029-12-31; Ponce's feed ended 2024-12-31. Cite both the build date and the feed dates.
caveats: It counts calls in the timetable, not vehicles seen.

The Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed read on 2026-10-02 includes 30 trips on a holiday service pattern that is counted as ordinary weekday service (see Typical weekday), so stops on ATI route 1 are slightly overstated.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, one scheduled stop has 0 because no trip calls there.
At a terminal the count includes vehicles that arrive and stop there, not only vehicles that leave.

The stop popup on the map shows this number as weekday departures even when the operator's timetable has ended. The popup also shows the end date of the timetable (feed_end) and says 'Timetable ended' when that date has passed.
The same field name, trips_weekday, counts trips on a route in transit_routes.geojson and operators.json. Here it counts stop calls, so the values are not comparable.

entries.plain_es: Cuántas veces el horario publicado tiene un vehículo pasando por la parada en un día típico de lunes a viernes. La ventana emergente del mapa lo llama salidas de lunes a viernes.
entries.name_es: Pasadas programadas de lunes a viernes por la parada (en el mapa: salidas de lunes a viernes)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un número más alto significa más salidas programadas. En el corte de datos 2026-10, el mayor es Terminal Covadonga, con 508 salidas. No dice cuán llenos van los vehículos ni si llegan a tiempo. Un horario cubre las fechas desde feed.start hasta feed.end del operador en operators.json, no la fecha de compilación. En la compilación del 2026-10-02, el inicio más temprano es 2023-01-01 y el final más tardío es 2029-12-31; la fuente de datos de Ponce terminó el 2024-12-31. Cite tanto la fecha de compilación como las fechas de las fuentes de datos.

entries.name: Shelter tagged at the stop
entries.plain: True means volunteers tagged the point as having a shelter; false means it is not tagged that way. Only OpenStreetMap (OSM) points have it.
