entries.name: Stops with a current timetable (count)
entries.plain: How many of the municipality's stops, stations and terminals are in a published timetable that has not ended. With the next two counts it splits transit_stops by the state of the timetable.
entries.definition: Count of the features counted in transit_stops (kinds transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station and ferry terminal) that are scheduled stops (stops in the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feed of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or of a municipal system) of an operator whose feed has an end date on or after access_as_of. stops_current + stops_expired = gtfs_stops, and stops_current + stops_expired + stops_osm = transit_stops in each of the 78 municipalities. A stop belongs to the municipality where it stands, not to its operator's.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the state of each timetable is judged as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

entries.method: access.py sorts each stop of the five kinds by the state of its operator's feed on the as-of date: current (feed end date not before the as-of date), expired (a scheduled stop of a feed that has ended or has no end date) or mapped by volunteers (source OpenStreetMap). It then counts them in each municipality.
entries.source_detail: transport.json (ATI and municipal GTFS feeds read on 2026-10-02) and feed end dates from operators.json; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: A count, not a rate: large and dense municipalities have more stops. It shows where stops with a timetable in force are. It does not show how often vehicles come. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 2,881, in 30 municipalities (San Juan 1,009, Guaynabo 349, Bayamón 276, Carolina 268); 48 municipalities have 0. The Municipality tab shows the three counts in one line.
caveats: The state is judged on the as-of date and changes on the day a feed ends: on that date the stops of the operator move from current to expired. In the 2026-10 snapshot 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31.
Stop records are not merged within a feed or across feeds, so one physical stop with two records counts twice (see municipalities.gtfs_stops).
A timetable that has not ended is not proof of service. The observatory has no real-time data.
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty.

entries.name: Stops with an expired timetable (count)
entries.plain: How many of the municipality's stops, stations and terminals are in a published timetable that has ended. The stop may still be served, but its published timetable no longer covers today.
entries.definition: Count of the features counted in transit_stops that are scheduled stops (stops in the GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification, timetable feed of ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or of a municipal system) of an operator whose feed ended before access_as_of, or has no end date. Stops of a feed that has ended stay in transit_stops, gtfs_stops, transit_pct and pop_served_pct. They are left out of stops_current, of the acc_ fields (except acc_paper_pct, which counts the places near them) and of pop_served_active_pct.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh (access.py); the files are rewritten only when a value changes. In the 2026-10 snapshot the state of each timetable is judged as of 2026-10-06 (see access_as_of).

entries.method: access.py counts, in each municipality, the scheduled stops of the five kinds whose operator's feed end date is before the as-of date (or missing). See municipalities.stops_current.
entries.source_detail: transport.json (ATI and municipal GTFS feeds read on 2026-10-02) and feed end dates from operators.json; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 966 such stops, in 10 municipalities: Caguas 291, Ponce 276, San Lorenzo 159, Juncos 128, Fajardo 81, Cidra 14, Hatillo 11, Gurabo 4, Carolina 1 and Las Piedras 1. They belong to 7 operators whose feeds ended: Ponce on 2024-12-31, Hatillo on 2025-12-31, Cidra on 2026-01-15, Caguas on 2026-01-31, San Lorenzo on 2026-02-28, Fajardo on 2026-06-15 and Juncos on 2026-07-31. A stop can lie in a neighbouring municipality: Gurabo has no feed of its own. A feed can run out of dates while buses still run, so a large count is not proof that service stopped.
caveats: The state is judged on the as-of date. Renewing a feed moves its stops to stops_current at the next run.
Stop records are not merged, so one physical stop with two records counts twice (see municipalities.gtfs_stops).
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it.

entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10 la isla tiene 966 paradas de este tipo, en 10 municipios: Caguas 291, Ponce 276, San Lorenzo 159, Juncos 128, Fajardo 81, Cidra 14, Hatillo 11, Gurabo 4, Carolina 1 y Las Piedras 1. Pertenecen a 7 operadores cuyas fuentes de horarios terminaron: Ponce el 2024-12-31, Hatillo el 2025-12-31, Cidra el 2026-01-15, Caguas el 2026-01-31, San Lorenzo el 2026-02-28, Fajardo el 2026-06-15 y Juncos el 2026-07-31. Una parada puede estar en un municipio vecino: Gurabo no tiene una fuente de horarios propia. Una fuente de horarios puede quedarse sin fechas mientras las guaguas siguen circulando, así que un conteo alto no prueba que el servicio se haya detenido.

entries.name: Transit stops, stations and terminals (count)
entries.plain: How many places to board public transit lie inside the municipality: stops, stations and ferry terminals from public timetables, plus stops, stations and terminals that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. It counts places to board, not routes or trips.
entries.definition: Count of mapped transit features inside the municipality of five kinds: transit stop, bus stop, bus station, rail station and ferry terminal (see municipalities.stop_kinds). It adds (1) every boarding point in the public timetable feeds (GTFS, the General Transit Feed Specification) of ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and the municipal transit systems, and (2) OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, rail stations and ferry terminals that do not duplicate a scheduled stop. Airports, taxi stands and EV (electric vehicle) chargers are not counted. The scheduled part is the field gtfs_stops; the rest comes only from OpenStreetMap.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed at each full build and at each run of the nightly transit refresh, which counts the stops in transport.json again (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: The build reads every GTFS feed (network.py, which also gives each scheduled stop its kind) and an OpenStreetMap query for bus stops, bus stations, railway and public-transport stations and ferry terminals (transport.py). An OpenStreetMap bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal is dropped when the nearest scheduled stop is less than 30 m away. OpenStreetMap stations and terminals are also dropped when a scheduled or already kept feature of the same kind lies less than 200 m away (rail stations, ferry terminals) or less than 100 m away (bus stations), because one station is often mapped as several points. Each remaining feature goes to the municipality whose boundary contains it; a point outside every boundary, such as a pier over water, goes to the municipality whose boundary is nearest. The field is the number of features per municipality.
entries.source_detail: ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) GTFS feed and municipal GTFS feeds (National RTAP, Rural Transit Assistance Program, portal), read by network.py; OpenStreetMap extract of 1 October 2026 (Overpass API, application programming interface), read by transport.py; municipality boundaries from Census TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11 (500k, shoreline-clipped)
entries.how_to_read: A higher count means more places to board. This is a count, not a rate: large and dense municipalities have more stops, and so do places where volunteers have mapped more. The observatory publishes no stops-per-resident rate; for a size-adjusted measure of residents, use pop_served_pct. The count does not measure how often vehicles come, whether a timetable is still valid, or whether people can reach a stop. A value of 0 means no stop appears in these sources; it does not rule out públicos (shared taxis) or informal service that nobody mapped. In the 2026-10 snapshot the island has 4,360 such features: 2,881 in a timetable that has not ended, 966 in a timetable that has ended and 513 that come only from OpenStreetMap (see stops_current, stops_expired and stops_osm).
caveats: Scheduled stops stay in the count when the operator's timetable has ended (966 of them in the 2026-10 snapshot; see stops_expired and municipalities.feed_status).
OpenStreetMap is mapped by volunteers, so coverage is uneven. Its data carry the ODbL (Open Database License); read the license before reusing them.
A stop counts in the municipality where it stands, not where its riders live.
Stop records are not merged within a feed or across feeds, so one physical stop with two records counts twice (see municipalities.gtfs_stops).
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. ATI provides its feed as is, without warranty.
The nightly refresh counts the stops again from transport.json, so the scheduled part follows the feeds. The OpenStreetMap part changes only at a full build (see municipalities.transit_data_updates).

entries.plain_es: Cuántos lugares para abordar el transporte colectivo hay dentro del municipio: paradas, estaciones y terminales de lanchas de los horarios públicos, más las paradas, estaciones y terminales que personas voluntarias registraron en OpenStreetMap. Cuenta lugares para abordar, no rutas ni viajes.
entries.name_es: Paradas, estaciones y terminales de transporte colectivo (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un conteo más alto significa más lugares para abordar. Es un conteo, no una tasa: los municipios grandes y densos tienen más paradas, igual que los lugares donde las personas voluntarias han mapeado más. El observatorio no publica una tasa de paradas por residente; para una medida de residentes ajustada por tamaño, use pop_served_pct. El conteo no mide con qué frecuencia pasan los vehículos, si un horario sigue vigente ni si la gente puede llegar a una parada. Un valor de 0 significa que no aparece ninguna parada en estas fuentes; no descarta los públicos (taxis colectivos) ni un servicio informal que nadie haya mapeado. En el corte de datos 2026-10 la isla tiene 4,360 elementos de este tipo: 2,881 en un horario que no ha terminado, 966 en un horario que ya terminó y 513 que provienen solo de OpenStreetMap (vea stops_current, stops_expired y stops_osm).

entries.name: Transport point id
entries.plain: A unique text id for each transport point. It starts with where the point came from.
entries.definition: Text id, unique in transport.json. Scheduled stops: gtfs, then the operator id, then the stop id used in that operator's feed (example gtfs:ati:1017). OpenStreetMap (OSM) points: osm: followed by n for a node or w for a way, then the OpenStreetMap number (example osm:n368381564). Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airports: faa: followed by the FAA location id (example faa:SJU). The examples are from the 2026-10 snapshot.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: Built by network.py (scheduled stops), transport.py (OSM points) and the FAA loader in transport.py.
entries.source_detail: GTFS stops.txt field stop_id (prefixed gtfs:<operator>:); OpenStreetMap element type (n for node, w for way) and number; FAA location id (loc_id)
entries.how_to_read: Use the id to point to one record in this snapshot.
caveats: A scheduled stop's id contains the feed's own stop id, so it changes if the operator renumbers its stops. Do not use it to follow a stop over time.
Some feed stop ids contain spaces or capital letters. In the 2026-10 snapshot, an example is the Vieques stop gtfs:vieques:EL GALLITO BEACH.

entries.name: Transport point kind
entries.plain: What kind of place the point is: a stop, a bus station, a train station, a ferry terminal, an airport, a taxi stand or a charger.
entries.definition: A code for the type of point. For scheduled stops, which come from the timetables of Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and of municipalities, the kind comes from the feed: a stop served by a rail route is rail_station; one served by a ferry route is ferry_terminal; one whose name starts with Terminal or Estación (and that no rail or ferry route serves) is bus_station; every other scheduled stop is transit_stop. For OpenStreetMap (OSM) points the kind comes from the tags, checked in this order: railway=station (or public_transport=station on an object that also has a railway tag) gives rail_station; amenity=ferry_terminal gives ferry_terminal; amenity=bus_station, or public_transport=station when the point has no railway tag, gives bus_station (in the 2026-10 snapshot, 2 of the 47 mapped bus stations carry only the second tag); highway=bus_stop gives bus_stop; aeroway=aerodrome gives airport; amenity=taxi gives taxi; amenity=charging_station gives ev_charging. The code can also write helipad (aeroway=helipad) and bike_rental (amenity=bicycle_rental) for OSM points; the 2026-10 snapshot has none.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: Rules in network.py (parse_gtfs) and transport.py (osm_kind). The kind decides which map layer shows the point: stops layer (transit_stop, bus_stop), stations layer (bus_station, rail_station, ferry_terminal, airport) and taxi layer (taxi, ev_charging, bike_rental, helipad).
entries.source_detail: GTFS routes.txt field route_type (through trips.txt and stop_times.txt) and stops.txt field stop_name; OpenStreetMap tags railway, public_transport, amenity, highway and aeroway
entries.how_to_read: Kind says what the point is, not whether it is scheduled. Combine it with source.
caveats: A scheduled stop is called a bus_station only when its name starts with Terminal or Estación. A terminal with a different name stays transit_stop.
The map popup labels every transit_stop as “Transit stop (ATI)”, although in the 2026-10 snapshot 2,381 of the 3,781 come from municipal feeds. Use the source field to tell them apart.
The rail_station label on the map reads Tren Urbano station. In the 2026-10 snapshot the only rail route is Tren Urbano.

The airport kind counts mapped aerodromes, not airports with service. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 11 from OpenStreetMap include two seaplane bases, two fields named Histórico, a military field and a facility whose name says CERRADO (closed), and Fajardo's Aeropuerto Diego Jiménez Torres comes only from OpenStreetMap.

values.transit_stop: Scheduled boarding point that is not a station or terminal. 3,781 records in the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,400 from ATI and 2,381 from municipal feeds.
values.bus_stop: Bus stop mapped in OpenStreetMap that is not within 30 m of a scheduled stop. 459 records in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.bus_station: Bus station or terminal. 91 records in the 2026-10 snapshot: 15 from ATI and 29 from municipal feeds (scheduled stops named Terminal or Estación), and 47 mapped in OpenStreetMap.
values.rail_station: Tren Urbano station: a scheduled stop served by a rail route in the ATI feed. 16 records in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.ferry_terminal: Ferry terminal. 13 records in the 2026-10 snapshot: 6 scheduled stops served by ferry routes in the ATI feed and 7 mapped in OpenStreetMap.
values.airport: Airport. 25 records in the 2026-10 snapshot: 14 from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) list and 11 mapped in OpenStreetMap (more than 2 km from any FAA airport). The mapped ones include seaplane bases, historic and military fields and a closed airfield, so this is not a count of airports with service.
values.taxi: Taxi stand mapped in OpenStreetMap (amenity=taxi). 9 records in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.ev_charging: Electric vehicle charging station mapped in OpenStreetMap. 11 records in the 2026-10 snapshot.

entries.name: Transport point location (latitude and longitude)
entries.plain: Where the point is, as latitude and longitude in decimal degrees.
entries.definition: Latitude (lat, degrees north) and longitude (lng, degrees east, so negative in Puerto Rico) in the World Geodetic System 1984 (WGS 84), the reference system used by satellite navigation. Scheduled stops: the feed's coordinates rounded to 5 decimals (about 1 m). OpenStreetMap (OSM) points: 6 decimals; for areas such as a station building, the centre point. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airports: the position in the FAA layer, 6 decimals. In the 2026-10 snapshot, latitudes run from 17.965554 to 18.507643 and longitudes from -67.931886 to -65.30252.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: Scheduled stops: if a feed gives a positive longitude between 65 and 68 (the minus sign was lost, as in Jayuya's feed in the 2026-10 snapshot), the observatory changes its sign. A stop outside latitude 17.5 to 18.8 and longitude -68 to -65 is dropped.
entries.source_detail: GTFS stops.txt fields stop_lat and stop_lon; OpenStreetMap node position or way centre; FAA Aviation Facilities layer 0 of the National Transportation Atlas Database, point geometry
caveats: Positions are as precise as the source. A scheduled stop can sit some metres from the real pole or shelter.
The sign correction is a rule on the longitude only; it does not test whether the stop is on a road.

entries.name: Transport point name
entries.plain: The name of the stop, station, terminal, airport, stand or charger, as its source gives it. A few names are blank, misspelled or missing letters in the source.
entries.definition: Scheduled stops: the stop_name in the operator's feed, trimmed. OpenStreetMap (OSM) points: the name tag, otherwise the ref tag, otherwise empty text. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airports: the facility name, converted from capitals to title case. Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) names usually describe a position on a street (for example a road and the cross street it is next to) rather than a place name.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: Copied from the source without correction.
entries.source_detail: GTFS stops.txt field stop_name; OpenStreetMap tags name, then ref; FAA Aviation Facilities layer 0 of the National Transportation Atlas Database, field fac_name
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 48 OSM points have no name (the value is empty text).

Some municipal feeds have lost accented letters in the source file itself (in the 2026-10 snapshot, for example, Pblicos for Públicos and Estacin for Estación), and some lose a letter inside a word (for example Funeraria Marn for Marín). The observatory does not repair them.
FAA names have no accents and may be shortened (in the 2026-10 snapshot, for example, Luis Munoz Marin Intl).

entries.name: Transport points: stops, stations, terminals, airports, taxi stands and chargers
entries.plain: Every mapped point that helps people get around: scheduled bus, train and ferry stops, plus stations, terminals, airports, taxi stands and electric vehicle chargers. The 2026-10 snapshot has 4,405 points, and each one says where it came from.
entries.definition: The file transport.json holds one record per point. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 3,847 records are scheduled stops taken from public timetables in GTFS format (General Transit Feed Specification) from ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, the Integrated Transport Authority) and from 24 municipalities; 544 records are points that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap (OSM): bus stops, bus stations, ferry terminals, airports, taxi stands and electric vehicle (EV) chargers; and 14 records are airports from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) list. The field source tells which group a record belongs to. Only scheduled stops carry routes, modes, weekday stop calls (shown on the map as weekday departures), Saturday and Sunday stop calls (calls_sat and calls_sun), the end date of their timetable feed (feed_end) and the operator_name field. OpenStreetMap points can carry operator text that volunteers typed in the operator field.
entries.unit: points (one record per stop, station, terminal, airport, stand or charger)
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: main island, Vieques and Culebra; each point also carries its municipality

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: 1. Scheduled stops: network.py reads every GTFS feed and keeps the boarding points (stops whose location_type is blank or 0) that lie inside Puerto Rico. 2. Mapped points: transport.py asks the Overpass API of OpenStreetMap for bus stops, bus stations, rail and public-transport stations, ferry terminals, taxi stands, bicycle rental, charging stations, aerodromes and helipads inside a box from 17.85 to 18.57 degrees north and 67.97 to 65.20 degrees west. 3. Airports: every airport whose state is PR in the FAA layer of the National Transportation Atlas Database of the Bureau of Transportation Statistics. 4. Duplicates (checked only at a full build, which rebuilds all of the observatory's data): an OSM bus stop, bus station, rail station or ferry terminal within 30 m of a scheduled stop is dropped; an OSM rail station or ferry terminal within 200 m, or bus station within 100 m, of a scheduled or already kept point of the same kind is dropped; an OSM aerodrome within 2 km of an FAA airport is dropped. In the OSM pull of 2026-10-01, 1,804 bus stops, 78 bus stations, 16 rail stations, 13 ferry terminals and 24 aerodromes were mapped; 459, 47, 0, 7 and 11 remain. 5. Each point is given a municipality from its location.
entries.source_detail: ATI GTFS zip (PRITA_GTFS.zip on docs.pr.gov) and the municipal GTFS zips listed in the Transitland Atlas registry of the National Rural Transit Assistance Program (RTAP) portal; OpenStreetMap through the Overpass API; FAA airports from the National Transportation Atlas Database of the Bureau of Transportation Statistics
entries.how_to_read: Look at source first. A point from ati_gtfs or muni_gtfs appears in an operator's published timetable. A point from osm_transport only shows that someone mapped a stop there; it does not show that a vehicle calls there today. A point from faa_airports is an airport record, not a transit stop.
caveats: Stops from expired timetables stay in the file. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 966 of the 3,847 scheduled stops belong to the 7 operators whose feed had ended by the build date (2026-10-02).
Points that volunteers mapped can be missing, out of date or wrong; the observatory does not check them on the ground.
Taxi stands and EV chargers are listed because they help visitors get around. They are not public transit and are not counted as stops.

Licenses differ by source: ATI states its feed is provided without warranty and that an app built on its data must make clear it is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI; the municipal feeds state no license; OpenStreetMap data is under the Open Database License (ODbL); the FAA list is a US Government source. Check each source's terms before reusing the points.
Duplicates between OpenStreetMap points and scheduled stops are removed only at a full build. The nightly refresh replaces the scheduled stops and does not repeat that check.

Scheduled stops are not merged with each other, so a count of points is a count of records, not of distinct places. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 167 pairs of stops of different operators lie within 30 m of each other (the same physical stop can appear once for ATI and once for a municipal system), and 122 positions hold two stops of the same operator.

The airport kind counts mapped aerodromes, not airports with service. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 11 from OpenStreetMap include two seaplane bases, two fields named Histórico, a military field and a facility whose name says CERRADO (closed), and Fajardo's Aeropuerto Diego Jiménez Torres comes only from OpenStreetMap.

entries.plain_es: Cada punto mapeado que ayuda a la gente a moverse: paradas de guaguas, tren y lanchas con horario, además de estaciones, terminales, aeropuertos, paradas de taxis y cargadores de vehículos eléctricos. El corte de datos de 2026-10 tiene 4,405 puntos, y cada uno dice de dónde viene.
entries.name_es: Puntos de transporte: paradas, estaciones, terminales, aeropuertos, paradas de taxis y estaciones de carga
entries.how_to_read_es: Mire primero el campo source. Un punto de ati_gtfs o muni_gtfs aparece en el horario publicado de un operador. Un punto de osm_transport solo muestra que alguien mapeó una parada en ese lugar; no muestra que un vehículo pase por ahí hoy. Un punto de faa_airports es un registro de aeropuerto, no una parada de transporte colectivo.

entries.name: Wheelchair boarding stated for the stop
entries.plain: True means the source says a rider in a wheelchair can board at the stop. False means the source does not say; it does not mean the stop is inaccessible.
entries.definition: Scheduled stops: true when the wheelchair_boarding field of the timetable feed (GTFS, General Transit Feed Specification) is 1. OpenStreetMap (OSM) points: true when the wheelchair tag is yes. Everything else is false. The field is missing on Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) airports.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops: re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and rewritten only when a feed changes. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports: read at each full build, a rebuild of all the observatory's data (the 2026-10 snapshot used OpenStreetMap data of 2026-10-01).

entries.method: network.py compares wheelchair_boarding to 1; transport.py compares the OSM tag to yes.
entries.source_detail: GTFS stops.txt field wheelchair_boarding; OpenStreetMap tag wheelchair
entries.how_to_read: Use true as a positive statement. Do not read false as not accessible.
caveats: In the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed read on 2026-10-02, 1,317 stops have an empty wheelchair_boarding value, 86 have 0 (no information in the GTFS standard) and 34 have 1. In the municipal feeds of the same date, most stops that are not true have an empty value, and Ponce's feed has no such column. The OSM points are true only when tagged yes.
The observatory does not check vehicles, ramps or kerbs.

True is the publisher's own statement, not checked on the ground. In the 2026-10 snapshot, seven municipal feeds mark every stop true (Bayamón, Coamo, Jayuya, Orocovis, Patillas, Utuado and Vieques), while 16 of the 25 feeds have no true stop. Counts or shares of true stops therefore compare how the feeds were filled in, not how accessible each place is. Do not compare across operators or municipalities.

values.true: The source says wheelchair boarding is possible. 458 points in the 2026-10 snapshot (34 ATI, 423 municipal, 1 OSM).
values.false: The source says nothing, says no, or the value is empty. 3,933 points in the 2026-10 snapshot.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Transit stops; Stations, terminals and airports

entries.plain_es: Verdadero significa que la fuente dice que una persona en silla de ruedas puede abordar en la parada. Falso significa que la fuente no lo dice; no significa que la parada sea inaccesible.
entries.name_es: Abordaje en silla de ruedas indicado para la parada
entries.how_to_read_es: Use true como una afirmación positiva. No interprete false como no accesible.

entries.name: Street intersections (TIGER/Line)
entries.plain: How many places in each barrio and municipio three or more streets meet, from the Census Bureau's 2026 street map.
entries.definition: Street intersections: points where three or more street segments of the Census Bureau's TIGER/Line 2026 files meet (secondary roads, local streets, alleys and private roads; limited-access highways, ramps, service drives, trails, walkways and parking lot roads are left out). A dead end or a bend is not an intersection.

coverage.frequency: One snapshot; each dataset in its source's vintage (TRI reporting year 2024; FRS, Green Book and CMS read 2026-10-17; ATTAINS 2024 cycle; LMOP data of 2024-09; HUD CHAS 2016-2020; TIGER/Line 2026). Rebuilt with python conditions.py --refresh.

entries.method: conditions.py reads the TIGER/Line EDGES file of each municipio, keeps the road edges (ROADFLG = Y) once each, counts for every topological node how many street edges end at it (S1200, S1400, S1730, S1740), and keeps the nodes with three or more. Each is placed in the barrio that holds it; density divides by the land area of the 2020 Census (km² / 2.59 = square miles).
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line 2026 EDGES, 78 municipios (MTFCC S1200, S1400, S1730, S1740)

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: street intersections

entries.how_to_read: 116,462 intersections: San Juan 7,599, Bayamón 5,182, Ponce 4,849; Culebra 106.
caveats: The observatory's own road graph (roads.bin) comes from OpenStreetMap; this count uses TIGER/Line, the source the original WCRP index named, so the two networks can differ.
entries.plain_es: En cuántos lugares de cada barrio y municipio se juntan tres calles o más, según el mapa de calles de 2026 del Negociado del Censo.

entries.name: Street intersections per square mile (TIGER/Line)
entries.plain: How many street intersections there are per square mile of land: a finer street grid, usually easier to walk, has more.
entries.definition: Street intersections (three or more street segments of TIGER/Line 2026 meeting at a point; highways, ramps, service drives, trails, walkways and parking lot roads left out) divided by the land area in square miles (2020 Census).

coverage.frequency: One snapshot; each dataset in its source's vintage (TRI reporting year 2024; FRS, Green Book and CMS read 2026-10-17; ATTAINS 2024 cycle; LMOP data of 2024-09; HUD CHAS 2016-2020; TIGER/Line 2026). Rebuilt with python conditions.py --refresh.

entries.method: conditions.py reads the TIGER/Line EDGES file of each municipio, keeps the road edges (ROADFLG = Y) once each, counts for every topological node how many street edges end at it (S1200, S1400, S1730, S1740), and keeps the nodes with three or more. Each is placed in the barrio that holds it; density divides by the land area of the 2020 Census (km² / 2.59 = square miles).
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGER/Line 2026 EDGES; 2020 Census land area

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: intersection density

entries.how_to_read: 34 per square mile for Puerto Rico; San Juan 159, Cataño 131, Bayamón 117; Culebra 9. Town-centre barrios pass 600 (Gurabo pueblo 741); the median barrio has 31.
caveats: Land area includes forests and farms, so a rural barrio with a dense village still reads low.
The original WCRP index gave 124.5 for Puerto Rico with TIGER 2020; it does not say which roads or nodes it counted, so the two are not comparable.
entries.plain_es: Cuántas intersecciones de calles hay por milla cuadrada de tierra: una red de calles más fina, por lo general más fácil de caminar, tiene más.

entries.name: Timetable replay files: weekday, Saturday and Sunday trips
entries.plain: Three files that hold every scheduled trip as its stops and times along its route's line, so the map and the 3D view can show vehicles on their timetable, following the roads. They are not Global Positioning System (GPS) data.
entries.definition: A trip is one scheduled run of a vehicle along a route, as listed in a feed (the set of GTFS files in which an operator publishes its stops, routes, trips and times). In the 2026-10 snapshot, trips.json (weekday, typical Wednesday service) holds 3,297 trips from 25 operators. trips_sa.json (Saturday) holds 1,648 trips from 4 operators: Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), Guaynabo, Juncos and Vega Alta. trips_su.json (Sunday) holds 381 trips from 1 operator, ATI. Each file has five keys: day (a label, which reads 'weekday (typical Wednesday service)' in trips.json, 'Saturday' in trips_sa.json and 'Sunday' in trips_su.json); format (2); paths (one path for each stop pattern, that is each set of trips that stop at the same places in the same order: a list of [longitude, latitude, metres from the start of the path] along the route's line, at 5 decimals); path_kind (for each path, 'line' when it follows the route's line, or 'stops' when no line fits the stops and the path joins them in straight lines); and trips (the list; see Trip record). In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 3,297 weekday trips share 222 stop patterns, 206 of them along their route's line. Only trips with at least two stop times are kept. Trips of the five Patillas routes with an inferred stop order are left out: in the 2026-10 snapshot the operator trips_weekday values in operators.json add up to 3,312, while trips.json holds 3,297 (15 Patillas trips left out). Trips of expired and expiring operators remain in the files: in the 2026-10 snapshot, 372 weekday trips belong to expired operators.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: parse_gtfs in network.py reads each trip's stops and times. trip_paths.py places the stops of each trip on one line of its route (the operator's own shape, or the road network that network.py snaps the route to), in travel order, and keeps the part of the line between the first and the last stop, simplified to about 5 m. Trips with the same stops in the same order share one path. refresh_network.py and build.py save the files. The 2D map loads the file that matches today's day in Puerto Rico; the 3D view loads the weekday file. Between two stops, a vehicle's time is spread along the path in proportion to distance (tripPoints in common.js).
entries.how_to_read: Each trip is one scheduled run, drawn along its route's line. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 3,191 of the 3,297 weekday trips follow their route line; the other 106 (16 stop patterns whose stops do not fit any line of their route) join their stops in straight lines and are marked 'stops' in path_kind. Speeds between stops come from the timetable, so a vehicle keeps its scheduled times but moves at an even speed between two stops. A timetable covers the dates from the operator's feed.start to feed.end in operators.json, not the build date. In the build of 2026-10-02 the earliest start is 2023-01-01 and the latest end is 2029-12-31; Ponce's feed ended 2024-12-31. Cite both the build date and the feed dates.
caveats: The files hold timetables, not observed positions.
The 3D view replays every weekday trip in trips.json, including those of expired timetables; the 2D map leaves expired operators out.

In the 2026-10 snapshot, two weekday trips of Ponce (route Tuque) have one stop time that is far earlier than the stops around it, so the replay would place the vehicle oddly. Ponce's feed ended 2024-12-31, so the 2D map skips these trips; the 3D view does not.

Terms differ by source. The terms of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) say the data are provided as is, without warranty, and that an app built on them must make clear it is not affiliated with or sponsored by ATI. The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it. Parts drawn from OpenStreetMap are under the Open Database License (credit and share-alike). Check each source's terms before reuse.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Vehicles on their timetable now
3D view: Day clock with the replay of weekday transit

entries.plain_es: Tres archivos que guardan cada viaje con horario con sus paradas y horas a lo largo de la línea de su ruta, para que el mapa y la vista 3D puedan mostrar los vehículos según su horario, siguiendo las carreteras. No son datos de GPS (sistema de posicionamiento global).
entries.name_es: Archivos de reproducción de horarios: viajes de lunes a viernes, sábado y domingo
entries.how_to_read_es: Cada viaje es un recorrido programado, trazado a lo largo de la línea de su ruta. En el corte de datos 2026-10, 3,191 de los 3,297 viajes de lunes a viernes siguen la línea de su ruta; los otros 106 (16 patrones de paradas cuyas paradas no encajan en ninguna línea de su ruta) unen sus paradas con líneas rectas y se marcan como 'stops' en path_kind. Las velocidades entre paradas salen del horario, así que un vehículo mantiene sus horas programadas, pero se mueve a velocidad pareja entre dos paradas. Un horario cubre las fechas desde feed.start hasta feed.end del operador en operators.json, no la fecha de compilación. En la compilación del 2026-10-02, el inicio más temprano es 2023-01-01 y el final más tardío es 2029-12-31; la fuente de datos de Ponce terminó el 2024-12-31. Cite tanto la fecha de compilación como las fechas de las fuentes de datos.

entries.name: Trip record: route, mode, operator, stop pattern and stop times
entries.plain: One scheduled trip. It has the route label, the mode, the operator, the path it follows along its route, where its stops are on that path, and the time at each stop.
entries.definition: Each trip (one scheduled run of a vehicle along a route, as listed in a feed) is an object with six keys. r: the route label (the route's short name, or its long name if there is no short name). m: the mode. o: the operator id. k: the trip's path, an index into the file's paths (the stop pattern it shares with every trip that stops at the same places in the same order). s: for each stop time, the index of the point of that path where the stop is. t: the time at each stop, in seconds after midnight, in stop order. A stop time is a line in the feed saying that the trip calls at a stop at a given time; the time is the departure time at the stop, or the arrival time if there is no departure time. Times are local; General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) allows times after 24:00 for trips that run past midnight, but in the 2026-10 snapshot no time in these files is above 86,400 (24:00). In the same snapshot, one Saturday trip and one Sunday trip, both Tren Urbano (TU), end exactly at 86,400; no weekday trip does (the latest weekday time is 86,340, 23:59). The weekday file has 78,414 stop times in that snapshot. A stop sits on its path a median 7 m from the stop's own coordinates (95% within 13 m), because the path follows the road line.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: Built in parse_gtfs (network.py) from the feed's stop_times.txt; trip_paths.py fits the stops to the route line and writes k, s and t. To get the vehicle's position at any time, walk the path between two stops and spread the time between them by distance (tripPoints in site/js/common.js does this).
entries.how_to_read: The value list shows the codes of m. The route label r can be matched with the short or long name of a route of the same operator. The stop times t are the timetable itself: use them, not the path points, to count departures, measure headways or find transfers. Trips that share k are one service pattern of a route, which is the unit to compare supply between routes.
caveats: A route label is only unique within one operator.
A trip with a gap in its stop times only has the stops that carry times, so its path can skip stops.

values.bus: Bus trip. 3,067 weekday trips in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.rail: Tren Urbano trip. 166 weekday trips in the 2026-10 snapshot.
values.ferry: Ferry trip. 64 weekday trips in the 2026-10 snapshot.

entries.plain_es: Un viaje con horario. Tiene la etiqueta de la ruta, el modo, el operador, el trayecto que sigue a lo largo de su ruta, dónde están sus paradas en ese trayecto y la hora en cada parada.
entries.name_es: Registro de viaje: ruta, modo, operador, patrón de paradas y horas en las paradas
entries.how_to_read_es: La lista de valores muestra los códigos de m. La etiqueta de ruta r se puede relacionar con el nombre corto o largo de una ruta del mismo operador. Las horas en las paradas t son el horario mismo: úselas, y no los puntos del trayecto, para contar salidas, medir intervalos de paso o encontrar trasbordos. Los viajes que comparten k son un mismo patrón de servicio de una ruta, que es la unidad para comparar la oferta entre rutas.

entries.name: Typical weekday, Saturday and Sunday service
entries.plain: Weekday trip counts show one reference day, usually Wednesday, so trips that run only on other weekdays are not included. Saturday and Sunday use their own timetables. Holidays are not modelled.
entries.definition: The reference weekday is Wednesday, or the first of Tuesday, Thursday, Monday or Friday that the feed actually serves. A trip counts as weekday service if its service pattern runs on that day, as Saturday service if its pattern runs on Saturday and as Sunday service if it runs on Sunday. A pattern that runs on several day types counts in each. If a trip names a service that the feed does not define, it counts as weekday service. If a feed has no calendar.txt, every service listed in calendar_dates.txt counts as running on every day type.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time and the files are rewritten only when a feed changes. Snapshot built 2026-10-02.

entries.method: parse_gtfs in network.py. The feed's start and end dates for each pattern are not checked, and exceptions in calendar_dates.txt (holidays, added or removed dates) are not applied when the feed has a calendar.txt.
entries.how_to_read: Read weekday counts as the number of trips on a normal Wednesday, not an average of the week.
caveats: The Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed read on 2026-10-02 has a pattern named Holiday_Service_Route_1. Its calendar covers every Monday to Friday from 2026-07-27 to 2027-05-31, but for its Monday and Wednesday pattern the feed's exceptions file removes 87 dates and adds 6. The observatory does not apply exceptions, so the 30 trips of that pattern count as ordinary weekday trips on route 1: 81 in the file, 51 without them.
Service on public holidays, school breaks or special events is not modelled.
A feed whose patterns cover different date ranges is counted as if all ran together.
entries.plain_es: Los conteos de viajes de lunes a viernes muestran un día de referencia, por lo general el miércoles, así que no incluyen los viajes que solo se dan otros días de la semana. El sábado y el domingo usan sus propios horarios. Los días feriados no se modelan.
entries.name_es: Servicio típico de lunes a viernes, sábado y domingo
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea los conteos de lunes a viernes como el número de viajes de un miércoles normal, no como un promedio de la semana.

entries.name: Vehicles on their timetable now
entries.plain: How many trips are in progress right now according to the published timetables. It is a schedule calculation, not GPS (Global Positioning System) tracking. The Transit tab says real-time bus positions are not available to the public (checked 45-10-02).
entries.definition: The number of trips in progress at this moment on the published timetables. The page picks the weekday, Saturday or Sunday timetable file for today's day in Puerto Rico. A trip counts when its first stop time is at or before the current time, its last stop time is at or after it, and its operator's timetable has not expired. Each dot is placed along the trip's route line, between the two timed stops the trip is between, in proportion to distance.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico, operators with a timetable feed

coverage.frequency: Recalculated every 5 seconds in your browser while the layer is on

entries.method: network.js picks trips.json on a weekday, trips_sa.json on Saturday or trips_su.json on Sunday, takes the time of day in Puerto Rico, keeps the trips running at that time, and places each trip along its route line between its stops (tripPoints in common.js). The weekday file holds each feed's typical weekday: Wednesday, or the first of Tuesday, Thursday, Monday or Friday that the feed serves.
entries.source_detail: trips.json, trips_sa.json, trips_su.json (network.py); site/js/network.js (updateNow)
entries.how_to_read: Dots show where vehicles should be if they follow the timetable. The count changes with the hour and the day.
caveats: It is a timetable, not a position. Late or cancelled trips, breakdowns and holidays are not modelled.

Timetables of expired operators are left out: in the data of 2026-10-02, 372 of the 3,297 weekday trips and 48 of the 1,648 Saturday trips. Routes whose feed lists stops out of order are left out of the timetable files. In the data of 2026-10-02, five such routes (15 weekday trips) still show trip counts in their pop-ups and in the Operators list, so a route can show trips but have no moving dots.
The weekday count uses each feed's Wednesday service for every weekday, or, if a feed has no Wednesday service, the first of Tuesday, Thursday, Monday or Friday that it serves.

In the data of 2026-10-02, on Saturday only 4 operators have trips in the timetable files (3 once the expired one is dropped), and on Sunday only ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado). A system with no dots on a weekend may simply publish no weekend timetable.
Times are matched to the clock within one day. A trip that continued past midnight would not carry over into the next day. In the files of 2026-10-02 none does: the latest stop time is 24:00.

Dots follow the route line between stops at an even speed. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 106 of the 3,297 weekday trips have no line that fits their stops; their dots move in a straight line and can sit off the street.
Each timetable trip counts once. The number is not a count of physical vehicles.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Vehicles on their timetable now

entries.name_es: Vehículos según su horario ahora
entries.how_to_read_es: Los puntos muestran dónde deberían estar los vehículos si siguen el horario. El conteo cambia según la hora y el día.

entries.name: Vehicles on their timetable now (timetable replay)
entries.plain: A map layer that shows where each scheduled vehicle should be right now, in Puerto Rico time, according to the published timetable. It is not live Global Positioning System (GPS) tracking and does not show real vehicle positions.
entries.definition: For the current Puerto Rico day, the map picks the Sunday, Saturday or weekday file. A trip counts as in service when the current time is between its first and last stop time. Its position is worked out in a straight line between the two stops that surround the current time, in proportion to the time elapsed. The layer refreshes every 5 seconds and shows the total and the largest operators.

coverage.frequency: Recalculated every 5 seconds in your browser while the layer is on, from timetable files rewritten when a feed changes (last write: 2026-10-02)

entries.method: updateNow in network.js. Trips of operators whose feed is expired on today's date are skipped. Holidays are not modelled.
entries.how_to_read: Read it as where the schedule says vehicles are, not where they are. The number is worked out in your browser every 5 seconds and is not stored in any file. To cite it, give the date, the Puerto Rico clock time shown in the layer note, the build date of the timetables and the feed dates. A timetable covers the dates from the operator's feed.start to feed.end in operators.json, not the build date. In the build of 2026-10-02 the earliest start is 2023-01-01 and the latest end is 2029-12-31; Ponce's feed ended 2024-12-31.
caveats: Real-time bus positions do not exist in the data; see Real-time data.
The position is a straight line between stops, so a vehicle can appear off the road.
A late or cancelled vehicle is shown as on time. On a Monday or Friday the weekday file still shows the reference weekday's timetable, usually Wednesday's.
Only operators with a published timetable appear. Operators with no feed, públicos and OpenStreetMap routes are absent.

Each marker is one scheduled trip in progress, not an identified vehicle: the trip files hold no vehicle ids. In the 2026-10 snapshot, on Saturday only 4 operators, and on Sunday only ATI, have timetable files, so a lower weekend count does not show how much service runs.

view.label: Map, Transit tab: Vehicles on their timetable now

entries.plain_es: Una capa del mapa que muestra dónde debería estar ahora mismo cada vehículo con horario, en hora de Puerto Rico, según el horario publicado. No es un rastreo en vivo por GPS (sistema de posicionamiento global) y no muestra las posiciones reales de los vehículos.
entries.name_es: Vehículos según su horario ahora (reproducción del horario)
entries.how_to_read_es: Léala como dónde dice el horario que están los vehículos, no dónde están. El número se calcula en su navegador cada 5 segundos y no se guarda en ningún archivo. Para citarlo, indique la fecha, la hora de Puerto Rico que aparece en la nota de la capa, la fecha de compilación de los horarios y las fechas de las fuentes de datos. Un horario cubre las fechas desde feed.start hasta feed.end del operador en operators.json, no la fecha de compilación. En la compilación del 2026-10-02, el inicio más temprano es 2023-01-01 y el final más tardío es 2029-12-31; la fuente de datos de Ponce terminó el 2024-12-31.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a municipal stop (count)
entries.plain: How many residents live within 400 m of at least one stop from a municipal transit system's timetable feed. It is a count of people, not a share.
entries.definition: Number of residents (2020 Census) in blocks with at least one stop from any feed other than the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed within 400 m, in a straight line. These are the municipal feeds read by the observatory. Feeds whose timetable has expired are included. It can overlap with pop_served_ati.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: For each populated block the build lists every scheduled stop within 400 m (straight line) and flags the block when one of them belongs to a feed other than ATI. Flagged blocks' populations are added by municipality. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
entries.source_detail: 2020 Census block population; municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops (National RTAP, Rural Transit Assistance Program, portal)
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see how much of a municipality's reach comes from municipal systems. Do not add it to pop_served_ati: people near both are counted twice. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 the observatory reads 24 municipal feeds and the count is non-zero in 35 municipalities.
caveats: Includes residents served only by an expired timetable. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, 53,884 Caguas residents are near a municipal stop, and the Caguas feed ended 2026-01-31.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the count does not describe 2026 residents.
The municipal feeds state no license; ask the municipality before reusing a feed beyond viewing it.
entries.example: In the transit data built 2026-10-02: San Juan 133,352; Guaynabo 63,250; Ponce 77,833.
entries.plain_es: Cuántas personas residentes viven a 400 m o menos de al menos una parada de la fuente de horarios de un sistema municipal de transporte colectivo. Es un conteo de personas, no una proporción.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de una parada municipal (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver qué parte del alcance de un municipio proviene de los sistemas municipales. No lo sume a pop_served_ati: las personas cerca de ambos se cuentan dos veces. En los datos de transporte colectivo compilados el 2026-10-02, el observatorio lee 24 fuentes de horarios municipales y el conteo es distinto de cero en 35 municipios.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (count)
entries.plain: How many residents of the municipality live within 400 m (a quarter mile), in a straight line, of a scheduled transit stop. It uses 2020 Census counts.
entries.definition: Number of residents (2020 Census) who live in a Census block whose internal point (the point inside the block that the Census Bureau stores for it) is less than 401 m in a straight line from the nearest scheduled stop: the build rounds the distance down to whole metres, so a block up to 400.9 m away counts (see municipalities.pop_served_method). Scheduled stops are the boarding points in the timetable feeds of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and the municipal systems (field gtfs_stops), including feeds whose timetable has expired. The stop may lie in another municipality.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: network.py places each of the 36,570 populated 2020 Census blocks at its internal point (fields INTPTLAT and INTPTLON), finds the nearest scheduled stop (nearest by latitude and longitude) and adds the block's population to the municipality's total when the straight-line distance, rounded down to whole metres, is 400 or less. The municipality comes from the county code in the block's ID. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
entries.source_detail: 2020 Census block population and internal points (TIGERweb Census2020 layer 10); ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops
entries.how_to_read: It estimates how many people live a short walk from a stop. It does not say whether a bus comes, how often, or where it goes. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, 925,788 of the island's 3,285,874 residents (28.2%) live within 400 m of a scheduled stop, and the value is 0 in 40 of the 78 municipalities: no scheduled stop lies within 400 m of any populated block.
caveats: Stops of expired timetables count. For stops with a timetable still running, see pop_served_active_pct.
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.

Residents can be near a stop in the next municipality. In the transit data built 2026-10-02, Toa Alta (70), Naranjito (106), Arroyo (72) and Mayagüez (167) show residents served although no scheduled stop lies inside them.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the count does not describe 2026 residents.
entries.example: In the transit data built 2026-10-02: San Juan 276,909 of 342,259 residents; Humacao 2,794 of 50,896.
entries.plain_es: Cuántas personas residentes del municipio viven a 400 m o menos (un cuarto de milla), en línea recta, de una parada de transporte colectivo con horario. Usa los conteos del Censo de 2020.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario (conteo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Estima cuántas personas viven a poca distancia a pie de una parada. No indica si pasa una guagua, con qué frecuencia ni adónde va. En los datos de transporte colectivo compilados el 2026-10-02, 925,788 de los 3,285,874 residentes de la isla (28.2%) viven a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario, y el valor es 0 en 40 de los 78 municipios: ninguna parada con horario está a 400 m o menos de ningún bloque poblado.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop, expired timetables included (%)
entries.plain: Out of every 100 residents of the municipality, how many live within 400 m (a quarter mile), in a straight line, of a scheduled transit stop. It uses the 2020 Census.
entries.definition: pop_served_400m divided by the municipality's residents in the 2020 Census (the sum of its block populations, equal to population_2020 in all 78 municipalities), times 100, rounded to one decimal. Stops of expired timetables count.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: Residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop divided by all residents of the municipality, times 100. See municipalities.pop_served_method.
entries.source_detail: 2020 Census block population (TIGERweb Census2020 layer 10); ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops
entries.how_to_read: A high value means most people live near a stop with a published timetable. It does not measure frequency, hours or destinations. A value of 0.0 means no populated block lies within 400 m of a scheduled stop; it does not mean the municipality has no transit users. The map shades it in five classes (quintiles) and the Municipality tab highlights values under 25%. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 the value ranges from 0.0 to 80.9 (San Juan) and is 28.2% island-wide. In that data 40 of the 78 municipalities have 0.0, so the lowest class holds all 40 and one class is empty; read the legend.
caveats: Stops of expired timetables count, so the share of residents near a stop with a current timetable is lower (see pop_served_active_pct).
Straight-line distance, not a walking route, and every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. See municipalities.pop_served_method.

Share of residents. For tourism places use acc_cur400_pct (a stop with a current timetable) or transit_pct (any mapped stop). The place measures and this one use different stop sets, and transit_pct also counts volunteer-mapped stops and stops of ended timetables, so compare like with like: pop_served_active_pct with acc_cur400_pct. In the transit data built 2026-10-02 Mayagüez shows 0.2% of residents, and 21.5% of tourism places by transit_pct but 4.2% by acc_cur400_pct.
Residents are 2020 Census counts and the stops are those of the transit data built 2026-10-02, so the share does not describe 2026 residents.

entries.plain_es: De cada 100 residentes del municipio, cuántos viven a 400 m o menos (un cuarto de milla), en línea recta, de una parada de transporte colectivo con horario. Usa el Censo de 2020.
entries.name_es: Residentes a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario, incluidos los horarios vencidos (%)
entries.how_to_read_es: Un valor alto significa que la mayoría de la gente vive cerca de una parada con horario publicado. No mide la frecuencia, las horas de servicio ni los destinos. Un valor de 0.0 significa que ningún bloque poblado está a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario; no significa que el municipio no tenga personas usuarias del transporte colectivo. El mapa lo sombrea en cinco clases (quintiles) y la pestaña Municipio resalta los valores menores de 25%. En los datos de transporte colectivo compilados el 2026-10-02, el valor va de 0.0 a 80.9 (San Juan) y es 28.2% en toda la isla. En esos datos, 40 de los 78 municipios tienen 0.0, así que la clase más baja reúne a los 40 y una clase queda vacía; lea la leyenda.

entries.name: Residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable (%)
entries.plain: Out of every 100 residents, how many live within 400 m of a scheduled stop whose operator's timetable has not ended. It is pop_served_pct with the stops of ended timetables left out. The map calls this a stop with a current timetable.
entries.definition: Residents (2020 Census) with at least one scheduled stop within 400 m, in a straight line, from an operator whose feed is active, divided by all residents of the municipality, times 100, rounded to one decimal. Active means the feed's status is not expired on the build date of the transit data: its last service end date is not earlier than that date (2026-10-02 in the current data). Feeds that are current, expiring or of unknown end date are active (see municipalities.feed_status); this includes feeds that expire soon. The observatory calls a stop of an active feed a stop with a current timetable. The tourism-place fields use the same idea (acc_cur400_pct and the other acc_ fields), with one difference: there a feed with no end date does not count. No feed lacks an end date in the 2026-10 snapshot.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes (transit data built 2026-10-02).

entries.method: Same blocks and 400 m rule as pop_served_pct, but stops of operators whose feed status is expired are skipped when looking for a stop within reach. There is no matching count field.
entries.source_detail: 2020 Census block population; GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops of operators whose feed has not expired (ATI, Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, and municipal feeds)

A feed can run out of dates while buses still run, so a low value is not proof that service stopped. entries.name: Residents within a 400 m walk of a scheduled stop (count)
entries.plain: How many residents of the municipality live within a 400 m (quarter mile) walk, along mapped roads, of a scheduled transit stop. It uses 2020 Census counts. It is an estimate: the road map has no footpaths.
entries.definition: Number of residents (2020 Census) who live in a Census block whose internal point is a walk of 400 m or less, along mapped roads, from the nearest scheduled stop (rounded up to whole metres). Scheduled stops are the boarding points in the timetable feeds of ATI and the municipal systems, including feeds whose timetable has expired. It is pop_served_400m measured by walking instead of a straight line. The stop may lie in another municipality.

coverage.frequency: Recomputed in each full build and by the nightly transit refresh when a feed changes, from the road file the site publishes (roads.bin).

entries.method: network.py (coverage) joins each of the 36,570 populated 2020 Census blocks, at its internal point, to the nearest walkable road within 150 m, and searches the walking network of walknet.py (every road of roads.bin except motorways and motorway links, both directions) from every scheduled stop up to 1,000 m. The walk is the connector, the path along the roads and the stop's connector, rounded up to whole metres, and never shorter than the straight line. A block with no walkable road within 150 m keeps its straight-line test: 4,002 of the 36,570 blocks, with 455,383 residents (13.9%), in the 2026-10 snapshot. A stop with no walkable road nearby counts at its straight-line distance.
entries.source_detail: 2020 Census block population and internal points (TIGERweb Census2020 layer 10); ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) and municipal GTFS (General Transit Feed Specification) stops; roads from OpenStreetMap (site/data/roads.bin, ODbL)
entries.how_to_read: It estimates how many people live a short walk from a stop. It does not say whether a bus comes, how often, or where it goes. In the transit data of the 2026-10 snapshot, 510,146 of the island's 3,285,874 residents (15.5%) live within a 400 m walk of a scheduled stop, against 925,788 (28.2%) in a straight line. Stops along main roads, and housing that reaches them only through an entrance or around a block, explain most of the gap.
caveats: Along mapped roads, not every way a person can walk. The road file has no footways, paths, steps, sidewalks or crossings. On 2026-10-16 the same count on the full OpenStreetMap walking network (footways, paths and service roads included) gave 15.5% of residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop, against 15.6% on roads.bin, and municipal shares moved a median 0.0 points (largest 1.7, Carolina).

Each block joins the network at the road nearest its internal point. A large block (a housing complex, a condominium) that fronts an avenue on one side but lies nearer a back street reads a longer walk than its residents may make. Joining each block also to every road within 60 m raises the island share from 15.5% to 17.1% (within 100 m: 19.1%), still far below the straight line (28.2%). Read the share as a careful estimate, with about that range around it.

13.9% of residents (455,383, in 4,002 blocks) live in blocks with no walkable road within 150 m of their internal point. They keep the straight-line test, which can only count them nearer than they are, so for them the walking share is an upper bound.
Stops of expired timetables count. For stops with a timetable still running, see pop_walk_active_pct.
Every resident of a block is placed at the block's internal point. Residents are 2020 Census counts, and the stops are those of the current transit data.
