entries.name_es: Límites de los municipios (78 municipios)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver dónde empieza y dónde termina un municipio en tierra. No lo use para medir superficies ni para decidir si un solar en particular está dentro de un municipio.

entries.name: Municipality code (Census GEOID)
entries.plain: A five-digit Census code that identifies the municipality: 72 for Puerto Rico followed by three digits for the municipality. Barrio codes start with it.
entries.definition: GEOID is the Census Bureau's geographic identifier. For a municipality it is the 2-digit state code 72 plus the 3-digit county code. Codes run from 72001 to 72153. Each barrio's geoid begins with the GEOID of its municipality.

coverage.frequency: Census boundaries as of January 1, 2023

entries.method: Copied from the Census layer. The build matches it to the 2020 Census layer to attach population and housing units, and uses its first five digits to find a barrio's municipality.
entries.source_detail: TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11, field GEOID
entries.how_to_read: Use the code to join Census Bureau tables or other federal data. It stays the same when a name is spelled differently.
caveats: Keep it as text, as the Census Bureau does. If one table holds the code as text and the other as a number, a join will not match.
entries.example: 72127 is San Juan; 72049 is Culebra; 72147 is Vieques
entries.plain_es: Un código censal de cinco dígitos que identifica el municipio: 72 para Puerto Rico, seguido de tres dígitos para el municipio. Los códigos de los barrios empiezan con él.
entries.name_es: Código del municipio (GEOID del Censo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Use el código para unir tablas del Negociado del Censo u otros datos federales. No cambia cuando un nombre se escribe de otra forma.

entries.name: Municipality land area (Census, square meters)
entries.plain: The land area of the municipality in square meters, as the Census Bureau reports it, without water. Divide by 1,000,000 for square kilometers.
entries.definition: AREALAND from the Census Bureau's generalized county layer (a version with simplified edges, made for maps at a scale of 1:500,000), with boundaries as of January 1, 2023: the land area inside the municipality, in square meters, not counting water.

coverage.frequency: Census boundaries as of January 1, 2023

entries.method: Copied from the Census layer without change.
entries.source_detail: TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11, field AREALAND
entries.how_to_read: Use it as the denominator for density when you work with this file. 1 km² equals 1,000,000 m². With boundaries as of January 1, 2023, the 78 values add up to 8,869 km². The smallest is Cataño (12.5 km²) and the largest is Arecibo (326.2 km²).
caveats: municipalities.json holds a second land area (land_km2) taken from the 2020 Census layer. The raw values differ for all 78 municipalities, by at most 0.26 km² in 77 of them and by 1.07 km² in Manatí. After rounding to one decimal, 37 municipalities still differ. Places per km² in municipalities.json uses the 2020 value.
This is the Census Bureau's land area, not the area of the drawn polygon.
entries.example: Cataño: 12515854 m² (12.5 km²), boundaries as of January 1, 2023
entries.plain_es: El área de tierra del municipio en metros cuadrados, según la informa el Negociado del Censo, sin contar el agua. Divida entre 1,000,000 para obtener kilómetros cuadrados.
entries.name_es: Superficie terrestre del municipio (Censo, metros cuadrados)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úsela como denominador de la densidad cuando trabaje con este archivo. 1 km² equivale a 1,000,000 m². Con los límites vigentes al 1 de enero de 2023, los 78 valores suman 8,869 km². El más pequeño es Cataño (12.5 km²) y el más grande es Arecibo (326.2 km²).

entries.name: Municipality name (Census Bureau)
entries.plain: The municipality's name as the Census Bureau writes it. It always ends in the word Municipio.
entries.definition: The NAME field of the Census Bureau's county layer. All 78 values end in the word Municipio.

coverage.frequency: Census boundaries as of January 1, 2023

entries.method: Copied from the Census layer. The build keeps the field so that readers can match the file to Census Bureau tables.
entries.source_detail: TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County layer 11, field NAME
entries.how_to_read: Use it to match Census Bureau tables. For joins inside the observatory, use the observatory spelling (municipality) or the code (GEOID).
caveats: Names are a weaker match than codes: spellings, accents and the word Municipio can differ between sources. To match Census Bureau tables, use the code (see boundaries.municipio_geoid).
entries.example: Las Piedras Municipio
entries.plain_es: El nombre del municipio como lo escribe el Negociado del Censo. Siempre termina con la palabra Municipio.
entries.name_es: Nombre del municipio (Negociado del Censo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para emparejar con las tablas del Negociado del Censo. Para unir datos dentro del observatorio, use la ortografía del observatorio (municipality) o el código (GEOID).

entries.name: Municipality name (observatory spelling)
entries.plain: The municipality's name as the observatory spells it, with accents (for example Mayagüez). Files that list places and municipalities use it to match their rows; the yearly series files use the 5-digit Census code (GEOID) instead.
entries.definition: The Census name with the word Municipio removed, matched without regard to accents or capitals to the observatory's list of 78 municipalities (municipalities.py). The list's spelling is stored. municipalities.json, places.json and barrios.geojson use the same spelling. The yearly series files (economy_series.json, housing_series.json) use the 5-digit GEOID instead.

coverage.frequency: Fixed list of 78 municipalities

entries.method: build.py (MUNI_BY_NORM) lower-cases the Census name, strips accents and looks it up in the observatory's list.
entries.source_detail: Census Bureau name (NAME) matched to the observatory's own list of municipalities
entries.how_to_read: Use this field to match rows between the place and municipality files. The land-use file uses the same spelling for 78 of its 79 municipality values; one water polygon carries the variant Guayanabo (see land.municipio).
caveats: Names are text with accents. Joins that strip accents on one side only will fail.
entries.example: Mayagüez
entries.plain_es: El nombre del municipio como lo escribe el observatorio, con acentos (por ejemplo, Mayagüez). Los archivos que listan lugares y municipios lo usan para emparejar sus filas; los archivos de series anuales usan en su lugar el código censal de 5 dígitos (GEOID).
entries.name_es: Nombre del municipio (ortografía del observatorio)
entries.how_to_read_es: Use este campo para emparejar filas entre los archivos de lugares y de municipios. El archivo de uso de terrenos usa la misma ortografía en 78 de sus 79 valores de municipio; un polígono de agua lleva la variante Guayanabo (vea land.municipio).

entries.name: Population, 2020 Census (boundary file)
entries.plain: The number of people the 2020 Census counted in the municipality on Census Day, April 1, 2020. The same count is stored in municipalities.json (see municipalities.population_2020).
entries.definition: POP100 is the total resident population of the municipality in the 2020 Census, as published in the Census Bureau's TIGERweb county layer for 2020.

coverage.frequency: Every 10 years; the observatory holds the 2020 count

entries.method: Read from the 2020 Census county layer (not the generalized layer) and joined to the shoreline-clipped shapes by GEOID.
entries.source_detail: TIGERweb tigerWMS_Census2020 MapServer layer 82, field POP100
entries.how_to_read: It describes April 2020, not today. In the 2020 Census the 78 values add up to 3,285,874, the Census count for Puerto Rico. The smallest is Culebra (1,792) and the largest is San Juan (342,259). For yearly estimates, see the resident population series.
caveats: The Census Bureau applied disclosure avoidance (a method that protects privacy) to 2020 counts. See its 2020 disclosure avoidance documentation for how this affects small areas.

The Housing page's 2020 population is not this count. It is the Census Bureau's updated April 2020 base for its estimates, which includes post-census count corrections. In the 2026-10 snapshot it differs from this count by 1 to 31 people in 68 of the 78 municipalities; the island total is the same, 3,285,874. See housing.population and methods.population_vintage_break.
People are counted where they usually live, including people in group quarters such as nursing homes.
Estimates after 2020 come from a different Census program and can differ from this count.
entries.plain_es: La cantidad de personas que el Censo de 2020 contó en el municipio el Día del Censo, 1 de abril de 2020. El mismo conteo está en municipalities.json (vea municipalities.population_2020).
entries.name_es: Población, Censo 2020 (archivo de límites)
entries.how_to_read_es: Describe abril de 2020, no el presente. En el Censo 2020, los 78 valores suman 3,285,874, el conteo del Censo para Puerto Rico. El más pequeño es Culebra (1,792) y el más grande es San Juan (342,259). Para estimados anuales, vea la serie de población residente.

entries.name: Tourism region in the boundary file (Puerto Rico Tourism Company)
entries.plain: The tourism region the municipality belongs to, one of the seven Porta regions of the Puerto Rico Tourism Company. A tourism region is not a Census, planning or political unit.
entries.definition: The tourism region of each municipality, the same assignment as municipalities.region (see there for the seven regions and their members). Here it is the field region of municipios.geojson.

coverage.frequency: Fixed list; updated by hand if the Tourism Company changes its regions

entries.method: Looked up by municipality name in municipalities.py and written to municipios.geojson and municipalities.json.
entries.source_detail: Region assignment: Puerto Rico Tourism Company, https://tourism.pr.gov/regions/ (as coded in municipalities.py). The Census layer supplies only the list of 78 municipalities; the Census Bureau is not the source of the grouping.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to group municipalities the way the Tourism Company does. The observatory stores no regional totals: add up the municipality rows if you need them. The observatory's counts are Overture listings, not Tourism Company statistics.
caveats: Regions are tourism groupings, not compact areas: Porta del Mar runs from Loíza to Maunabo and Yabucoa and includes Culebra and Vieques, and Porta Capital runs from San Juan and Bayamón to Cayey.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab: Boundaries

entries.plain_es: La región turística a la que pertenece el municipio, una de las siete regiones Porta de la Compañía de Turismo de Puerto Rico. Una región turística no es una unidad censal, de planificación ni política.
entries.name_es: Región turística en el archivo de límites (Compañía de Turismo de Puerto Rico)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úsela para agrupar los municipios como lo hace la Compañía de Turismo. El observatorio no guarda totales regionales: si los necesita, sume las filas de los municipios. Los conteos del observatorio son listados de Overture, no estadísticas de la Compañía de Turismo.

entries.name: Barrio count in the build file
entries.plain: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the build published 901 barrio polygons.
entries.definition: barrios.barrios is the number of barrio (county subdivision) polygons written to the barrios file, from the Census Bureau's county subdivisions (TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023, layer 7).

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: landuse.py (build_barrios) counts the polygons it writes.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD MapServer layer 7 (County Subdivisions 500K); landuse.py (BARRIOS_URL, build_barrios)
entries.how_to_read: Barrios are divisions of a municipality. The count is the number of polygons, not of neighbourhoods.
caveats: Barrio boundaries are the Census Bureau's. Some barrios are named the same in different municipalities.
entries.plain_es: En el corte de datos de 2026-10, la compilación publicó 901 polígonos de barrios.
entries.name_es: Conteo de barrios en el archivo de compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: Los barrios son divisiones de un municipio. El conteo es el número de polígonos, no de vecindarios.

entries.name: Build date and time
entries.plain: When the full build wrote the data, as a date and time in UTC. In the 2026-10 snapshot it is 2026-10-02 02:31 UTC, which is 2026-10-01 at 10:31 pm in Puerto Rico.
entries.definition: The moment the full build finished collecting data and wrote meta.json, in ISO 8601 form with a +00:00 offset, which means UTC, Coordinated Universal Time. Puerto Rico is 4 hours behind UTC all year.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: build.py writes the current UTC time as a text with second precision.
entries.source_detail: build.py (meta['generated_at']); written by the observatory's own build step, not an external source
entries.how_to_read: The 2026-10 snapshot's value is 2026-10-02T02:31:31+00:00. The map shows only the first ten characters, the UTC date: as hover text on the snapshot label and in the About tab. That date can be one day later than the date in Puerto Rico.
caveats: The value is the time of the last full build. The nightly transit refresh does not change it; the 'network' part has its own date.
Source data can be older than this time, because the build can reuse source files downloaded earlier. Overture places and OpenStreetMap roads have their own extract dates, shown in their entries.
entries.plain_es: Cuándo la compilación completa escribió los datos, como fecha y hora en UTC. En el corte de datos de 2026-10 es 2026-10-02 02:31 UTC, que en Puerto Rico es 2026-10-01 a las 10:31 p. m.
entries.name_es: Fecha y hora de la compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: El valor del corte de datos 2026-10 es 2026-10-02T02:31:31+00:00. El mapa muestra solo los primeros diez caracteres, la fecha UTC: como texto emergente en la etiqueta del corte y en la pestaña Info. Esa fecha puede ser un día posterior a la fecha en Puerto Rico.

entries.name: Build information file (meta.json)
entries.plain: A small file that says when the data snapshot was built, which area it covers, how many records each step kept, and which sources were used. Cite its snapshot label and date.
entries.definition: meta.json has 13 parts: label, generated_at, bbox, counts, sources, housing, landuse, barrios, transport, network, time, taxonomy_dropped_top and access. The full build (build.py) writes all of them. The nightly transit refresh (refresh_network.py) rewrites the 'network' part on nights when it finds a changed feed. Through access.py it also rewrites the 'access' part, and the count places_near_transit inside 'transport', when a value changes.
entries.unit: Mixed: text, dates, coordinates and counts

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: build.py collects the sources, classifies and filters the data, writes every data file and then writes meta.json with the label, the time, the settings and the counts of what each step kept.
entries.source_detail: build.py (main) and the SOURCES, meta and counts of transport.py, network.py, housing.py, landuse.py and timeseries.py
entries.how_to_read: Use the label and the build date to say which snapshot a figure comes from. The counts describe what the build kept; the data entries describe each dataset.
caveats: Parts of the file can be from different dates. 'network' is rewritten by the nightly transit refresh when it finds a changed feed, and 'access' (with the count places_near_transit in 'transport') when an access value changes; every other part keeps the values of the last full build.
Some counts (for example time.trips) were not refreshed with 'network', so they can differ from the matching count in 'network'.
The license field of each source is named 'license' in this file; the source records of this dictionary name it 'licence'.

values.label: Name of the snapshot, for example 'Snapshot 2026-10'.
values.generated_at: Date and time of the full build, in UTC.
values.bbox: Map box [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees.
values.counts: Eleven values: ten counts of what the build read or kept (Overture place records, tourism places with and without the confidence cut-off, listings, duplicates folded, places of worship, flood polygons, protected-area records, municipalities and residents) and the confidence cut-off, 0.5.
values.sources: In the file of 2026-10-02, credit records for 30 sources: name, link and license for each, and a credit line for 25 of them. The keys are older source ids.
values.housing: Settings of the housing step: the two American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year vintages, the number of municipalities covered and the affordability method.
values.landuse: Land-use plan facts: number of polygons, plan version, land-class groups, zoning-layer status and places on protected land.
values.transport: Counts of transit features, kinds, walking distance, places near any mapped stop and the ride-hailing listing. The nightly refresh keeps the count places_near_transit in step with places.json.
values.network: Transit network facts: operators, status counts, routes, scheduled stops, weekday trips and residents near a stop. Rewritten by the nightly refresh on nights when a transit feed changed.
values.time: Facts for the time views: weekday trips and storms near Puerto Rico.
values.taxonomy_dropped_top: The 25 most common Overture categories that the build dropped as not tourism-related, with counts.
values.access: The island-wide access figures: shares of tourism places near a stop with a current timetable, near a frequent stop and near any mapped stop, the stop counts by timetable state, and the number of current and expired feeds, as of one date. Rewritten by the nightly refresh when a value changes.

view.label: Map header: the snapshot label (hover for the build date)

entries.plain_es: Un archivo pequeño que dice cuándo se generó el corte de datos, qué área cubre, cuántos registros conservó cada paso y qué fuentes se usaron. Cite su etiqueta de corte y su fecha.
entries.name_es: Archivo de información de la compilación (meta.json)
entries.how_to_read_es: Use la etiqueta y la fecha de compilación para indicar de qué corte de datos proviene una cifra. Los conteos describen lo que conservó la compilación; las fichas de datos describen cada conjunto de datos.

entries.name: Housing settings in the build file
entries.plain: In the 2026-10 snapshot, meta.json records four housing settings: the latest survey window (2020-2024), the earlier window used for change (2008-2012), the number of municipalities with data (78) and the name of the affordability method.
entries.definition: acs_latest is the last year of the American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates used for the latest figures. acs_base is the last year of the earlier 5-year estimates, used for change over time. municipalities_with_acs counts the municipalities with ACS data in the latest vintage. method is the build's text naming the affordability method of the State of Housing study (2023) by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR).

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC. Survey periods: ACS 2008-2012 and 2020-2024

entries.method: housing.py sets the two vintages (LATEST and BASE), counts the municipalities for which the latest ACS tables returned data, and records the method text.
entries.source_detail: housing.py (LATEST, BASE, build_housing); ACS is the US Census Bureau American Community Survey
entries.how_to_read: ACS 5-year figures are averages over five years of survey responses, not a single year.
caveats: The 2020-2024 estimates have margins of error, which are larger for small municipalities.
The method text is a build setting. The housing entries explain each measure.
The method text in the file calls the affordability table Table 6, the number this dictionary and the Housing page use. The study PDF prints that table as Table 8.

The 5% rate is the one the study states in its endnotes for the maximum mortgage. The study's printed maximum loans work out at a rate of 4.994%, so using exactly 5% leaves the observatory's figures $19 to $65 below them. It is a modelling assumption, not a mortgage rate in force in any year, and the result is an indicator, not a loan limit and not advice on buying a home.

values.acs_latest: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2024, the ACS 2020-2024 5-year estimates.
values.acs_base: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2012, the ACS 2008-2012 5-year estimates, used as the earlier point for change.
values.municipalities_with_acs: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 78 municipalities with ACS data in the latest vintage.
values.method: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 'FPR State of Housing 2023, Table 6 affordability method (30% of income, 78% to principal and interest, 30-year loan at 5%)'.

entries.plain_es: En el corte de datos de 2026-10, meta.json guarda cuatro ajustes de vivienda: el periodo de encuesta más reciente (2020-2024), el periodo anterior que se usa para medir el cambio (2008-2012), el número de municipios con datos (78) y el nombre del método de asequibilidad.
entries.name_es: Ajustes de vivienda en el archivo de compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: Las cifras de 5 años de la ACS (Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense) son promedios de cinco años de respuestas a la encuesta, no de un solo año.

entries.name: Land-use facts in the build file
entries.plain: Facts about the land-use layer: how many polygons it has, which plan it comes from, and its land classes. It also records whether the zoning service answered (it did not in the 2026-10 snapshot) and how many listings sit on protected rural land.
entries.definition: put_polygons counts the polygons of the published land-use file. put_version names the plan version. groups maps 12 land-class codes to their Spanish names. The plan uses 17 class codes; the build file names 12 of them. The five less common subtypes of specially protected rural land (SREP-AE, SREP-EA, SREP-AP, SREP-EP, SREP-P) are not in this list. calificacion records whether the zoning (Calificación de suelos) service answered at build time. places_on_protected_land counts listings whose point lies in a protected rural land class.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC. Reference date: plan version of 30 November 2015

entries.method: landuse.py reads the Junta de Planificación land-use plan, simplifies the polygons for display, tests whether each listing falls inside a polygon, and tries to reach the zoning service.
entries.source_detail: landuse.py (build_landuse, try_fetch_calificacion); Junta de Planificación Plan de Uso de Terrenos (PUT), version of 30 November 2015
entries.how_to_read: The plan describes how land is meant to be used under the 2015 plan, not what is built there today.
caveats: places_on_protected_land counts all listings, including places of worship and listings below the 0.5 confidence cut-off, not only the tourism places in the statistics.

'Protected land' here means the Junta's SREP land classes (specially protected rural land). It is not the same as the USGS protected areas (PAD-US). In the places file of the 2026-10 snapshot, 2,151 listings are in SREP classes and 1,013 listings carry a PAD-US area; do not compare the two counts.
In the 2026-10 snapshot the zoning layer was not reachable at build time (calificacion.available is false, reason HTTPError), so the observatory has no zoning layer.
The published polygons are simplified by about 110 m (0.001 degree) for display. Counts of listings use the full-detail polygons.
The Junta states no data license (its site footer reads 'Todos los derechos reservados'). See the source record before reusing the polygons.

values.put_polygons: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 996 polygons in the published land-use file (display copy).
values.put_version: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 'PUT-2014, 30-NOV-2015', the Plan de Uso de Terrenos version used.
values.groups: SU Suelo Urbano (urban land); SURP Suelo Urbanizable Programado (programmed developable land); SURNP Suelo Urbanizable No Programado (non-programmed developable land); SRC Suelo Rústico Común (common rural land); SREP Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido (specially protected rural land); SREP-E ecological; SREP-A agricultural; SREP-H water resources (hídrico); SREP-EH ecological and water; SREP-AH agricultural and water; AGUA water; VIAL road.
values.calificacion: In the 2026-10 snapshot: {available: false, reason: 'HTTPError'}; the zoning service did not answer at build time.
values.places_on_protected_land: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2,151 listings in the SREP classes.

entries.plain_es: Datos sobre la capa de uso de terrenos: cuántos polígonos tiene, de qué plan viene y sus clases de terreno. También dice si el servicio de calificación respondió (no respondió en el corte de datos de 2026-10) y cuántos listados están en suelo rústico protegido.
entries.name_es: Datos de uso de terrenos en el archivo de compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: El plan describe cómo se pretende usar el terreno según el plan de 2015, no lo que hay construido hoy.

entries.name: Map box (bounding box)
entries.plain: The rectangle the build asked Overture and OpenStreetMap about: west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.2, north 18.57. It covers Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra and Mona.
entries.definition: Four numbers [west, south, east, north] in decimal degrees: -67.97, 17.85, -65.2, 18.57. The build requests Overture Maps places and OpenStreetMap transit stops, stations and terminals inside this box.
entries.unit: Decimal degrees (longitude from west to east, latitude from south to north)
entries.geography: The map box: west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.2, north 18.57 (Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra, Mona and the sea around them)

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: Set by hand in build.py (and repeated in transport.py) as a rectangle around the island group. It is not computed from the data.
entries.source_detail: build.py (BBOX) and transport.py (BBOX)
entries.how_to_read: Places and stops outside the rectangle are not requested. A rectangle also takes in open sea, so it is larger than the land.
caveats: The box limits only the Overture and the OpenStreetMap transit-stop requests. Flood zones, protected areas and Census boundaries are requested by Puerto Rico's own codes. Roads and place names come from the Puerto Rico extract of OpenStreetMap.
entries.plain_es: El rectángulo por el que la compilación les preguntó a Overture y a OpenStreetMap: oeste -67.97, sur 17.85, este -65.2, norte 18.57. Cubre Puerto Rico, Vieques, Culebra y Mona.
entries.name_es: Recuadro del mapa (rectángulo envolvente)
entries.how_to_read_es: Los lugares y las paradas fuera del rectángulo no se solicitan. Un rectángulo también incluye mar abierto, así que es más grande que la tierra.

entries.name: Overture categories dropped by the build
entries.plain: The 25 most common Overture categories the build left out as not tourism-related, with record counts. Beauty salons, grocery stores and doctors' offices are examples.
entries.definition: A list of 25 pairs [category, count], largest first. The count is the number of Overture place records with that primary category that the observatory's rules did not place in a tourism category. The pair '(none)' counts records with no category.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico (the map box, see the entry on the map box)

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: build.py counts the primary Overture category of every record that classify() could not assign, before duplicate folding, and keeps the 25 largest groups.
entries.source_detail: build.py (parse_places, classify); Overture Maps Places, release 2026-09-23.1
entries.how_to_read: Use it to check what the observatory treats as outside tourism, for example whether a category you care about was dropped. In the 2026-10 snapshot, '(none)' is 3,388, and the 25 pairs add up to 28,986 of the 63,117 dropped records.
caveats: Dropped means not classified as tourism by the observatory's rules. It does not mean the places are unimportant.
Only the top 25 are stored. In the 2026-10 snapshot, about 34,100 dropped records are in smaller categories.
entries.plain_es: Las 25 categorías de Overture más comunes que la compilación dejó fuera por no estar relacionadas con el turismo, con su número de registros. Algunos ejemplos son los salones de belleza, los supermercados y las oficinas médicas.
entries.name_es: Categorías de Overture que la compilación descartó
entries.how_to_read_es: Úsela para ver qué considera el observatorio fuera del turismo; por ejemplo, si se descartó una categoría que le interesa. En el corte de datos 2026-10, '(none)' tiene 3,388, y los 25 pares suman 28,986 de los 63,117 registros descartados.

entries.name: Snapshot label
entries.plain: The name of the data snapshot, for example 'Snapshot 2026-10'. Cite it so readers know which build you used.
entries.definition: Text set at build time. It is the --label option when one is given. Otherwise it is the word 'Snapshot' followed by the year and month of the build, in UTC.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: build.py writes args.label or 'Snapshot' plus the build date formatted as year-month.
entries.source_detail: build.py (meta['label']); written by the observatory's own build step, not an external source
entries.how_to_read: The label names the full build. It appears next to the check mark in the header of the map, 3D, housing and dictionary pages. It does not change when the nightly transit refresh runs.
caveats: The label dates the build, not the data in it. Each dataset keeps its own reference date, for example April 2020 for census counts and 2015 for the land-use plan.
A month label does not say the day. The build date is in the build date and time entry.
The label is not a version number. Two builds in one month can have the same label.
entries.plain_es: El nombre del corte de datos, por ejemplo "Corte 2026-10". Cítelo para que se sepa qué versión de los datos se usó.
entries.name_es: Etiqueta del corte de datos
entries.how_to_read_es: La etiqueta nombra la compilación completa. Aparece junto a la marca de verificación en el encabezado de las páginas del mapa, 3D, vivienda y diccionario. No cambia cuando corre la actualización nocturna del transporte colectivo.

entries.name: Source credit records in the build file
entries.plain: A list in meta.json with a record for each of 30 source keys (file of 2026-10-02): name, link and license, and for 25 of them the credit line to print. The Sources section of this dictionary gives the same facts with canonical ids.
entries.definition: An object whose keys are source ids (older ones, such as 'census' or 'osm_roads') and whose values have the text fields name, url and license. Most values also have credit; fpr_housing_2023 adds home and program. Each module adds its own sources when it builds.
entries.unit: Text (30 records in the file of 2026-10-02)

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: build.py merges the SOURCES dictionaries of build.py, transport.py, network.py, timeseries.py, housing.py, housing_series.py, economy_series.py and landuse.py.
entries.source_detail: meta.json 'sources': keys overture, fema, padus, census, census_shore, noaa_slr, osm, ati_gtfs, osm_transport, faa_airports, uber, muni_gtfs, ntd, osm_routes, census_blocks, hurdat2, census2010, acs_latest, acs_2012, fpr_housing_2023, nalcab, census_barrios, put2015, calificacion, osm_roads, housing_pep, housing_census, housing_acs, housing_fema, housing_derived
entries.how_to_read: Use the 'credit' text when you print a map or a chart. For a record with no credit text, use the credit line in the Sources section. For license terms, follow the link and read the source's own terms. In the file of 2026-10-02, 25 of the 30 values have credit; housing_pep, housing_census, housing_acs, housing_fema and housing_derived have none.
caveats: The same source can appear under several keys (for example 'osm', 'osm_transport', 'osm_routes' and 'osm_roads' are all OpenStreetMap).

The meta.json written on 2026-10-02 has no records for the economy series (economy_qcew, economy_laus, economy_acs, economy_usaspending, economy_openfema, economy_pep, economy_cpi and economy_overture). Their credit lines are in economy_series.json (sources) and in the Sources section of this dictionary.
License text is what the source states. It is not legal advice. Check the source's terms before reuse.

The license text in meta.json is the build's short summary. The Sources section of this dictionary is the maintained list. Where they differ (for example for the Junta de Planificación land-use plan and zoning service, and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) sea level rise layers), use the Sources section.
Not every source is open data. Each source record states its license or says that none is stated.
entries.plain_es: Una lista en meta.json con un registro para cada una de 30 claves de fuente (archivo del 2026-10-02): nombre, enlace y licencia, y para 25 de ellas la línea de crédito que se debe imprimir. La sección "Fuentes" de este diccionario da los mismos datos con los identificadores oficiales.
entries.name_es: Registros de crédito de las fuentes en el archivo de compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: Use el texto 'credit' cuando imprima un mapa o una gráfica. Para un registro sin texto de crédito, use el crédito de la sección Fuentes. Para los términos de la licencia, siga el enlace y lea los términos de la propia fuente. En el archivo del 2026-10-02, 25 de los 30 valores tienen crédito; housing_pep, housing_census, housing_acs, housing_fema y housing_derived no tienen.

entries.name: Time-view facts in the build file
entries.plain: Facts for the time views: the number of weekday trips, which weekday the timetable stands for, and how many Atlantic storms passed near Puerto Rico (from 1851 through 2025 in the 2026-10 snapshot).
entries.definition: trips is the weekday trip count at the last full build. trips_day is the label of the timetable day used. The weekday timetable uses each feed's Wednesday service or, if a feed has none, the first of Tuesday, Thursday, Monday or Friday that it serves. storms_near_pr counts Atlantic tropical cyclones whose track came within 250 km of a point at the centre of the island (18.22, -66.45). major_hurricanes_near_pr counts those whose strongest wind near Puerto Rico was category 3 or higher on the Saffir-Simpson scale. storm_years gives the first and last year in the list.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico and its surrounding waters

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC. In the 2026-10 snapshot the storms run from 1851 to 2025

entries.method: build.py counts the weekday trips it writes. timeseries.py reads the HURDAT2 best-track database of NOAA (the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration), keeps storms within 250 km of the island's centre and assigns a category from the peak wind (in knots) within that distance: 64 or more category 1, 83 category 2, 96 category 3, 113 category 4, 137 category 5.
entries.source_detail: build.py (meta['time']); timeseries.py (load_hurricanes); HURDAT2 is the National Hurricane Center's Atlantic hurricane database
entries.how_to_read: The storm counts are storms that came near the island, not storms that struck it.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, trips (3,312) is the weekday trip count written by the last full build. It includes 15 trips on five routes whose stop order is unreliable. A later nightly refresh leaves those routes out, which gives 3,297, the count in the network part of meta.json and in trips.json. Use 3,297 for the timetable replay.
The category is from the wind near Puerto Rico, not the storm's peak anywhere on its track.

Distance and category come from the recorded track points (about every six hours), not from the line between them. A storm whose recorded points were all farther than 250 km is left out even if its path crossed the circle.
250 km is measured from one point at the centre of the island, so a storm can pass nearer the east or west end than the centre and still be left out.

Observation methods changed a great deal between 1851 and 2025. Older tracks and winds are less certain, and the National Hurricane Center (NHC) revises past seasons from time to time, so do not read the counts as a trend by decade.

values.trips: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 3,312 weekday trips at the last full build, including 15 trips on five routes whose stop order is unreliable. The timetable file has 3,297.
values.trips_day: 'weekday (typical Wednesday service)': the label of the timetable used for Monday to Friday. It uses each feed's Wednesday service or, if a feed has none, the first of Tuesday, Thursday, Monday or Friday that it serves.
values.storms_near_pr: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 157 Atlantic storms within 250 km of (18.22, -66.45), 1851 to 2025.
values.major_hurricanes_near_pr: In the 2026-10 snapshot: 29 of those storms were category 3 or higher near Puerto Rico.
values.storm_years: In the 2026-10 snapshot: [1851, 2025], the first and last year in the list of storms.

entries.plain_es: Datos para las vistas de tiempo: el número de viajes de lunes a viernes, qué día de la semana representa el horario y cuántas tormentas del Atlántico pasaron cerca de Puerto Rico (desde 1851 hasta 2025 en el corte de datos de 2026-10).
entries.name_es: Datos de las vistas de tiempo en el archivo de compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: Los conteos de tormentas son tormentas que pasaron cerca de la isla, no tormentas que la azotaron.

entries.name: Transit access facts in the build file
entries.plain: The island-wide access figures: the share of tourism places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable, of a frequent stop and of any mapped stop, the stop counts by timetable state and the feeds that are current or expired, as of one date.
entries.definition: as_of is the date against which the observatory judged whether each timetable had ended. basis says which places are counted and places counts them. near_m, far_m and frequent_calls are the two distances and the number of weekday calls that the figures use. The shares are percentages of the counted places: any400_pct (any mapped stop within 400 m), cur400_pct and cur800_pct (a stop with a current timetable within 400 m or 800 m), freq400_pct (with 20 or more weekday calls), sat400_pct and sun400_pct (with Saturday or Sunday service), hub400_pct (a rail station or ferry terminal within 400 m, any source) and paper_pct (within 400 m of a mapped stop but of no stop with a current timetable). stops counts the stops, stations and terminals by timetable state: current, expired and osm. feeds counts the operators whose timetable feed has an end date, as current (not ended on the as-of date) or expired.
entries.unit: A date, text, counts and % of tourism places

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py) and by the nightly transit refresh when a value changes (access.py). In the 2026-10 snapshot the figures are as of 2026-10-06 and the stops were read on 2026-10-02.

entries.method: access.py (island_summary) computes the figures from places.json, transport.json and operators.json, with the same rules as the municipal fields (see methods.access_profile). build.py writes the block into meta.json and refresh_network.py rewrites it through access.py.
entries.source_detail: access.py (island_summary, run by build.py and refresh_network.py); the places, stops and feed dates it reads are those of places.json, transport.json and operators.json
entries.how_to_read: Use these as the island totals behind the municipal fields. Each share is the number of places divided by all the places counted, not an average of municipal shares. In the 2026-10 snapshot, as of 2026-10-06: 47.5% of the 24,209 counted places are within 400 m of any mapped stop, 32.2% of a stop with a current timetable, 21.3% of a frequent stop, 22.4% of a stop with Saturday service and 6.4% with Sunday service; 15.4% are near only an expired or unscheduled stop.
caveats: The figures describe timetables on the as-of date. They change on the day a feed ends: 9 of the 18 current feeds end between 2026-10-31 and 2027-01-31 (see methods.access_profile).
The nightly refresh rewrites this part only when a value changes, so as_of can be older than the last run.
The limits of the municipal fields apply: straight-line distance, schedule-based figures with no real-time data, and públicos, taxis, ride-hailing and rental cars in no timetable.

entries.plain_es: Las cifras de acceso de toda la isla: la proporción de lugares turísticos a 400 m o menos de una parada con horario vigente, de una parada frecuente y de cualquier parada mapeada; el número de paradas según el estado de su horario, y las fuentes de horarios vigentes o vencidas, a una fecha dada.

entries.how_to_read_es: Úselas como los totales de la isla detrás de los campos municipales. Cada proporción es el número de lugares dividido por todos los lugares contados, no un promedio de las proporciones municipales. En el corte de datos 2026-10, al 2026-10-06: el 47.5% de los 24,209 lugares contados está a 400 m o menos de cualquier parada mapeada, el 32.2% de una parada con horario vigente, el 21.3% de una parada frecuente, el 22.4% de una parada con servicio los sábados y el 6.4% de una con servicio los domingos; el 15.4% está cerca solo de una parada con horario vencido o sin horario.

entries.name: Transit network facts in the build file
entries.plain: The latest facts about the transit network: operators and the state of their data, routes, stops, weekday trips, and residents within 400 m of a stop. It is rewritten when a nightly check finds a changed feed.
entries.definition: built is the date of the last full build or nightly refresh that wrote changes. operators counts the operators listed. by_status counts them by the state of their schedule data. routes counts the routes on the map. scheduled_stops counts stops in timetable feeds. weekday_trips counts trips in the typical-weekday timetable. residents is the 2020 population in census blocks. residents_within_400m counts residents in blocks whose nearest scheduled stop is 400 m or less away.
entries.unit: A date and counts (operators, routes, stops, trips, people)

coverage.frequency: Rewritten by each full build and by a nightly transit refresh that finds a changed feed (last write: 2026-10-02)

entries.method: network.py reads every operator's timetable feed and the 2020 Census block counts and measures the distance from each block to its nearest scheduled stop; refresh_network.py rewrites this part of meta.json when it finds a changed feed.
entries.source_detail: network.py (build_network, coverage); refresh_network.py; the operator checklist is from the National Transit Database of the Federal Transit Administration (FTA)
entries.how_to_read: The Transit tab shows these figures. In the file written on 2026-10-02, 925,788 of 3,285,874 residents (28.2%) live within 400 m of a scheduled stop.
caveats: In the file written on 2026-10-02, routes (165) includes 16 volunteer-mapped routes in OpenStreetMap; the other 149 come from timetable feeds.

scheduled_stops includes stops of operators whose timetables have expired, so residents_within_400m is higher than the count that uses only unexpired timetables (729,507 in the file written on 2026-10-02).
by_status is as of the build or refresh date. The browser works out each status again from the feed end date when the page opens.

entries.name: Transit settings and counts in the build file
entries.plain: Counts of transit features, the 400 m walking distance, and how many tourism places are near any mapped stop. It also records the date of the ride-hailing listing check.
entries.definition: gtfs counts operators with a feed, routes and scheduled stops. osm_features and faa_airports count the other features. features is the total number of rows in the transit features file. kinds counts the rows by kind. walk_access_m is the walking distance used for access to a stop: 400 m. places_near_transit counts tourism places within that distance of any mapped stop, station or terminal, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. uber_listed_municipalities and uber_checked record the ride-hailing listing. sources holds the credit records of the four sources.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: transport.py counts the features it assembles from the timetable feeds, OpenStreetMap and the FAA airport list, and the tourism places within 400 m of the nearest stop, station or terminal of any mode (not taxi, EV charging or airport).
entries.source_detail: transport.py (build_transport, meta); GTFS means General Transit Feed Specification, the standard format of public timetable feeds; FAA is the Federal Aviation Administration
entries.how_to_read: The numbers describe the last full build, except places_near_transit, which the nightly refresh recomputes through access.py. The nightly refresh also updates scheduled stops in the transit file, but not the other counts. The counts in the table of codes are from the 2026-10 snapshot. For the places near a stop with a current timetable, see the access part of this file.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot, gtfs.routes (165) counts every route on the map, including 16 routes mapped by volunteers in OpenStreetMap that have no timetable. The routes with a timetable feed number 149.

places_near_transit counts the nearest stop, station or terminal of any of those kinds, including the 459 OpenStreetMap bus stops that have no timetable (2026-10 snapshot). It is not on the same basis as the 'scheduled stop' figures in the Transit tab.

places_near_transit counts straight-line distance to the nearest stop; the places file stores the distance as a whole number of metres, cut and not rounded, so in the 2026-10 snapshot 14 listings just over 400 m (11 of them counted tourism places; 3 are places of worship) show a value of 400 there.
The ride-hailing figure is a listing on Uber's public cities page (57 municipalities, checked 45-10-01). It is not measured coverage.
'Not listed' on Uber's page does not mean Uber does not operate there.

entries.name_es: Ajustes y conteos de transporte colectivo en el archivo de compilación

La actualización nocturna también actualiza las paradas con horario en el archivo de transporte colectivo, pero no los demás conteos.
