entries.plain: The cut-off the observatory uses on Overture's confidence score: 0.5. Listings below it are hidden on the map by default and left out of the tourism statistics.
entries.definition: A number between 0 and 1. Overture gives each place record a confidence score. The observatory keeps a listing in its tourism statistics only when the score is at least this value.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.method: Set by hand in build.py (MIN_CONF). The map's confidence filter starts at the same value.
entries.source_detail: build.py (MIN_CONF); Overture Maps Places 'confidence' field
entries.how_to_read: A higher cut-off keeps fewer listings, those that Overture scores as more confident. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 0.5 cut-off keeps 24,209 tourism places; with no cut-off it would keep 27,509.
caveats: The score is Overture's estimate, not a check by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR).
The cut-off is a choice. A different one gives different counts.

Some fields do not use the cut-off. The municipality counts assets_all_confidence and listings_all, and the three land-use place fields (places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct), include listings of any confidence.
entries.plain_es: El límite que el observatorio usa en la puntuación de confianza de Overture: 0.5. Los listados por debajo se esconden en el mapa de forma predeterminada y quedan fuera de las estadísticas de turismo.
entries.name_es: Confianza mínima usada
entries.how_to_read_es: Un umbral más alto conserva menos listados, los que Overture califica con más confianza. En el corte de datos 2026-10, el umbral de 0.5 conserva 24,209 lugares turísticos; sin umbral conservaría 27,509.

entries.name: Municipalities in the build
entries.plain: The build covers 78 municipalities. That is every municipio of Puerto Rico.
entries.definition: The number of municipalities for which the build computed statistics. It is the number of municipalities in the build's list (municipalities.py).
entries.method: build.py counts the municipalities in its statistics table.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census county equivalents (municipios) of Puerto Rico
entries.how_to_read: Every municipality-level figure in the observatory has one value for each of these 78.
caveats: Culebra and Vieques are municipalities of their own and are included.

entries.plain_es: La compilación cubre 78 municipios. Son todos los municipios de Puerto Rico.
entries.name_es: Municipios en la compilación
entries.how_to_read_es: Cada cifra a nivel de municipio del observatorio tiene un valor para cada uno de estos 78.

entries.name: Overture place records in the map box
entries.plain: In the 2026-10 snapshot, Overture Maps held 99,323 place records inside the observatory's map box, in every category. The observatory keeps only the tourism-related ones.
entries.definition: Number of place records in the Overture Maps Places theme, in the release the snapshot uses, with a point inside the map box. Every category is counted: shops, offices and clinics as well as tourism places.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico (the map box, see the entry on the map box)
entries.method: build.py downloads the records with the overturemaps command and counts them. It then classifies each record into the observatory's tourism taxonomy, drops the records with no tourism category and folds duplicates.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Foundation, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 2026-10-01. meta.json does not store the release name.
entries.how_to_read: This is the raw size of the source, not the number of tourism places. For tourism places use the entry 'Tourism places counted in the statistics'. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 63,117 records were dropped as not tourism-related (3,388 of them have no category at all) and 1,088 more were folded as duplicates, which leaves 35,118 listings; 2,577 of them are not tourism (homes, housing and care services) and are left out, which leaves 32,541 (since 2026-10-18).
caveats: Listings are third-party records that the observatory has not checked on the ground, so a listing can be of a business that has closed or moved. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory folded 1,088 duplicates that it found.
In the 2026-10 snapshot, the 63,117 dropped records are the difference between this count and the 36,206 classified records; meta.json does not store that number.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.plain_es: En el corte de datos de 2026-10, Overture Maps tenía 99,323 registros de lugares dentro del recuadro del mapa del observatorio, de todas las categorías. El observatorio se queda solo con los relacionados con el turismo.
entries.name_es: Registros de lugares de Overture en el recuadro del mapa
entries.how_to_read_es: Este es el tamaño bruto de la fuente, no el número de lugares turísticos. Para los lugares turísticos, use la ficha 'Lugares turísticos contados en las estadísticas'. En el corte de datos 2026-10 se descartaron 63,117 registros por no estar relacionados con el turismo (3,388 de ellos no tienen ninguna categoría) y se fusionaron otros 1,088 como duplicados, lo que deja 35,118 listados; 2,577 de ellos no son turísticos (viviendas, servicios de vivienda y de cuidado) y se excluyen, lo que deja 32,541 (desde el 2026-10-18).

entries.name: Places of worship in the places file
entries.plain: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 5,032 listings are places of worship, such as churches. The places file keeps them and the map hides them by default. The tourism statistics leave them out. Only the all-listings count and the three land-use place fields count them.
entries.definition: Listings whose observatory type is 'Places of Worship' (religious categories in Overture, matched by build.py), after duplicate folding.
entries.geography: Puerto Rico (the map box, see the entry on the map box)
entries.method: build.py assigns the type 'Places of Worship' to categories that match place of worship, church, cathedral, chapel, synagogue, mosque, temple or religious, then counts them.
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Places, release 2026-09-23.1, classified by build.py (RULES)
entries.how_to_read: They are left out of tourism statistics, the route planner's tourism count and the transit-access shares. The all-listings count of each municipality (listings_all) and the three land-use place fields (places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct and places_urban_pct) are the exceptions: they count them.
caveats: This count includes worship places at any confidence.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.plain_es: En el corte de datos de 2026-10, 5,032 listados son lugares de culto, como iglesias. El archivo de lugares los conserva y el mapa los esconde de forma predeterminada. Las estadísticas de turismo los dejan fuera. Solo los cuentan el conteo de todos los listados y los tres campos de lugares del uso de terrenos.
entries.name_es: Lugares de culto en el archivo de lugares
entries.how_to_read_es: Se excluyen de las estadísticas de turismo, del conteo de turismo del planificador de rutas y de las proporciones de acceso al transporte colectivo. El conteo de todos los listados de cada municipio (listings_all) y los tres campos de lugares por uso de terrenos (places_on_protected_land, places_on_protected_land_pct y places_urban_pct) son las excepciones: sí los cuentan.

entries.name: Protected-area records
entries.plain: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory held 665 protected-area records for Puerto Rico from the USGS Protected Areas Database. They carry 640 different area names.
entries.definition: The number of polygon records of the Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US 4.1), kept by the USGS (United States Geological Survey), with state PR. The count is of records, not of areas: several records can carry one unit name. Records with designation PROC are proclamation boundaries.
entries.method: build.py requests every record of the PAD-US service where State_Nm is PR, and counts them.
entries.source_detail: USGS PAD-US 4.1, Protection Mechanism Category service, State_Nm = 'PR'
entries.how_to_read: A protected area is not always a closed area. Protected status describes how land is managed. The Pub_Access field of the published file says whether the public may enter. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 665 records carry 640 different unit names. Seven records are proclamation boundaries (designation PROC): five National Wildlife Refuges (Cabo Rojo, Culebra, Desecheo, Laguna Cartagena and Vieques), El Yunque National Forest and San Juan National Historic Site.
caveats: The tourism places statistics do not count the proclamation boundaries (seven in the 2026-10 snapshot) as 'in a protected area'. The route planner's protected-area share does.
Several records can belong to one unit.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC

entries.plain_es: En el corte de datos de 2026-10, el observatorio tenía 665 registros de áreas protegidas de Puerto Rico de la base de datos de áreas protegidas del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). Tienen 640 nombres de área distintos.
entries.name_es: Registros de áreas protegidas
entries.how_to_read_es: Un área protegida no siempre es un área cerrada. La condición de protección describe cómo se maneja el terreno. El campo Pub_Access del archivo publicado indica si el público puede entrar. En el corte de datos 2026-10, 665 registros llevan 640 nombres de unidad distintos. Siete registros son límites de proclamación (designación PROC): cinco refugios nacionales de vida silvestre (Cabo Rojo, Culebra, Desecheo, Laguna Cartagena y Vieques), el Bosque Nacional El Yunque y el Sitio Histórico Nacional de San Juan.

entries.name: Residents counted in the 2020 Census
entries.plain: The 2020 Census counted 3,285,874 residents in Puerto Rico's 78 municipalities.
entries.definition: The sum of the 2020 Census resident counts (field POP100) of the 78 municipios, as given by the Census Bureau's TIGERweb service. Residents on Census Day, 1 April 2020.
entries.method: build.py adds the POP100 values of the 78 municipio records.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau TIGERweb, 2020 Census, layer 82, field POP100
entries.how_to_read: It is the 2020 count, not the present population. Later estimates are in the population series.
caveats: The count is a point in time (April 2020) and has not been updated for later years.
The Census Bureau's resident count (POP100) includes people in group quarters such as dormitories and care homes, as the Census Bureau defines it. The observatory does not separate them.

coverage.frequency: Rewritten at each full build (build.py); the last full build is dated 2026-10-02 UTC. The count is as of 1 April 2020

entries.plain_es: El Censo de 2020 contó 3,285,874 residentes en los 78 municipios de Puerto Rico.
entries.name_es: Residentes contados en el Censo 2020
entries.how_to_read_es: Es el conteo de 2020, no la población actual. Los estimados posteriores están en la serie de población.

entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Places, release 2026-09-23.1, classified by build.py (RULES)

caveats: Overture gives these listings a confidence score below 0.5. The score is Overture's own estimate and the observatory has not checked the listings.

entries.name_es: Lugares turísticos con cualquier nivel de confianza
entries.how_to_read_es: Ponga el filtro de confianza del mapa en 0 para ver este conjunto más amplio. Las estadísticas predeterminadas no lo usan. En el corte de datos 2026-10, 27,509 menos 24,209 deja 3,300 listados por debajo de 0.5.

entries.name: Tourism places counted in the statistics
entries.plain: In the 2026-10 snapshot, the map and the tourism statistics count 24,209 tourism places in four groups: Attractions, Gastronomy (restaurants, bars and cafes), Accommodations and Visitor services. Places of worship and low-confidence listings are left out.
entries.definition: Listings after duplicate folding that are tourism supply (not homes, housing or care services), are not places of worship and have an Overture confidence of at least 0.5. The map's default filter and the tourism statistics use this basis. It equals the sum of the municipality counts of tourism places.
entries.method: build.py counts listings whose type is not 'Places of Worship' and whose confidence is at least 0.5 (MIN_CONF), after leaving out the listings that are not tourism (places_privacy.not_tourism).
entries.source_detail: Overture Maps Places, release 2026-09-23.1, classified by build.py (RULES)
entries.how_to_read: Use it as 'listings in the observatory's tourism data', not as the number of businesses open today.
caveats: The categories are the observatory's own rules (build.py), not Overture's categories.
A count of listings, not of businesses. Listings can be closed, moved or missing.
The separate phone, email and social-media fields are not published; name, address and website are copied as the source wrote them (see the entry on fields the observatory does not publish).

What the count includes changed on 2026-10-18 (HANDOFF decision 47). Meta users file homes, condominiums, public housing estates, subdivisions and care homes under tourism categories, mostly lodging and historic site. Those listings are not tourism supply, so they are no longer counted: 2,370 of the 26,579 places counted before were left out, which gives 24,209. Holiday rentals stay counted (they are tourism supply), although the map does not draw them. Every published figure built on this count was rebuilt the same day.

Quedan fuera los lugares de culto y los listados de baja confianza.

entries.name: Census tables and cells behind each housing and household field
entries.plain: Use this list to find the Census Bureau table and cell behind each housing and household field. It helps you cite the original numbers. The 'Code' column lists field names in municipalities.json, not coded values.
entries.definition: For each field, the American Community Survey (ACS) table number, the cell numbers used and the calculation. Table numbers are the Census Bureau's own (for example B25077). 'Cell 001' is the first line of the table. In the 2026-10 snapshot the latest window is 2020-2024. The baseline window for the change fields is 2008-2012. In the table-based files the estimate for cell 001 is the column B25077_E001 and its margin of error is B25077_M001.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. The Census Bureau publishes a new 5-year window each year.

entries.method: Latest window (2020-2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot): the Census Bureau's table-based summary files, one file per table (acsdt5y2024-<table>.dat), filtered to the rows for Puerto Rico's municipalities (the Census Bureau calls them municipios; geographic codes starting 0500000US72). Baseline window: the 2012 ACS 5-year Puerto Rico sequence files (PuertoRico_All_Geographies_Not_Tracts_Block_Groups.zip), with cells located through the Census Bureau's sequence-and-table lookup file. Tables read for the latest window: B25077, B25064, B19013, B25002, B25004, B25003, B15003, B25070, B25091, B01003, B17001, B01002, B23025. Tables read for the baseline: B25077, B25064, B19013, B15002, B01003.

values.acs_year: Not an ACS cell. The last year of the latest window, set when the observatory is rebuilt (2024 in the 2026-10 snapshot).
values.median_home_value: B25077 cell 001 (median value, owner-occupied housing units). Baseline: same cell, 2008-2012.
values.median_gross_rent: B25064 cell 001 (median gross rent, renter-occupied units paying cash rent). Baseline: same cell, 2008-2012.
values.median_hh_income: B19013 cell 001 (median household income in the past 12 months, households). Baseline: same cell, 2008-2012.
values.seasonal_units: B25004 cell 006 (vacant: for seasonal, recreational, or occasional use).
values.seasonal_pct: B25004 cell 006 divided by B25002 cell 001.
values.owner_occupied_pct: B25003 cell 002 (owner occupied) divided by cell 001 (occupied housing units).
values.renter_cost_burden_pct: B25070 cells 007 to 010 (30.0 percent or more) divided by cell 001 minus cell 011 (not computed).
values.owner_cost_burden_pct: B25091 cells 008 to 011 (30.0 percent or more, with a mortgage) divided by cell 002 minus cell 012 (not computed).
values.poverty_pct: B17001 cell 002 (below the poverty level) divided by cell 001 (population for whom poverty status is determined).
values.employment_rate_pct: B23025 cell 004 (employed civilians) divided by cell 001 (population 16 and over).
values.bachelors_pct: B15003 cells 022 to 025 (bachelor's, master's, professional, doctorate) divided by cell 001 (population 25 and over). Baseline for the change: B15002 cells 015-018 and 032-035 over cell 001.
values.max_affordable_loan: Calculated from B19013 cell 001 with the Table 6 method (see methods.affordability_method).
values.affordability_ratio: Calculated: B25077 cell 001 divided by max_affordable_loan.
values.bachelors_change_pts: Share from B15003 (latest window) minus share from B15002 (2008-2012).
values.population_change_2012_pct: B01003 cell 001 (total population), latest window against 2008-2012.
values.residents_per_unit: Not ACS. 2020 census population (POP100) divided by 2020 census housing units (HU100), Census Bureau TIGERweb.

entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, ACS 5-year summary files. Latest window: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2024/table-based-SF/data/5YRData/acsdt5y2024-<table>.dat, one file per table (for example acsdt5y2024-b25077.dat). 2008-2012 baseline: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2012/data/5_year_by_state/PuertoRico_All_Geographies_Not_Tracts_Block_Groups.zip, with cells located through https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/2012/documentation/5_year/user_tools/Sequence_Number_and_Table_Number_Lookup.txt
entries.how_to_read: To cite a number, give the table, the window and the geography, for example 'US Census Bureau, ACS 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table B25077, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico'. For a change field cite both windows ('2020-2024 compared with 2008-2012') and both tables. For a calculated field cite the input tables and say who calculated it. If you took the number from the observatory's files rather than from the Census Bureau, cite the observatory as well (Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory).
caveats: The keys of the list are field names in municipalities.json, not codes found in the data.
The observatory reads the Census Bureau's summary files directly and needs no data API key.
Census codes for values that are not available (-666666666 and below) become empty fields. In the 2026-10 snapshot, no estimate in the 2020-2024 files used for the 78 municipalities is negative.
entries.plain_es: Use esta lista para encontrar la tabla y la celda del Negociado del Censo detrás de cada campo de vivienda y hogares. Sirve para citar los números originales. La columna "Código" presenta nombres de campos de municipalities.json, no valores codificados.
entries.name_es: Tablas y celdas del Censo detrás de cada campo de vivienda y hogar
entries.how_to_read_es: Para citar una cifra, indique la tabla, la ventana y la geografía, por ejemplo 'Negociado del Censo de EE. UU., estimados de 5 años de la ACS 2020-2024, tabla B25077, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico'. Para un campo de cambio, cite ambas ventanas ('2020-2024 comparado con 2008-2012') y ambas tablas. Para un campo calculado, cite las tablas de origen y diga quién hizo el cálculo. Si tomó la cifra de los archivos del observatorio y no del Negociado del Censo, cite también el observatorio (Foundation for Puerto Rico, Observatorio de Datos de PR).

entries.name: Census tables behind the income, worker, commuting and internet figures
entries.plain: Use this list to find the Census Bureau table and cells behind each income, worker, commuting, vehicle and internet figure on the Analysis tab. It helps you cite the original numbers. The 'Code' column lists variable ids, not coded values.
entries.definition: In Puerto Rico the American Community Survey (ACS) is called the Puerto Rico Community Survey (PRCS). The Codes list gives, for each variable on the Analysis tab, the ACS table, who is counted and the cells used. 'Cell 1' is the first line of the table, and table numbers and titles are the Census Bureau's own.

coverage.frequency: Five-year windows, labeled by their last year (the Years line shows each window's last year). In the 2026-10 snapshot they run from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024. Table B28002 starts with 2013-2017, labeled 2017.

entries.method: The observatory lists the tables and the number of cells each must have (B19083: 1, B19001: 17, B08301: 21, B08303: 13, B25044: 15, B28002: 13, B24080: 21). Before it publishes, the observatory checks that each table has the expected number of cells, and a mismatch stops the update. The one exception is table B28002 (internet): a vintage that lacks it or lays it out differently is left out without stopping the update. The observatory reads the Census Bureau's per-sequence summary files for windows ending 2010 to 2020 and its table-based summary files for windows ending 2021 and later, for the 78 municipio rows and the Puerto Rico row. Table B28002 is not in the Puerto Rico summary files for windows ending 2010 to 2016, so the internet figures start with 2013-2017. Shares are calculated by the observatory; their margins of error follow the Census Bureau's formulas (margins of summed cells are combined as the square root of the sum of their squares; a share whose numerator is part of its denominator uses the proportion formula).
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, ACS 5-year summary files: https://www2.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/summary_file/. To find a table by its number: https://data.census.gov/
entries.how_to_read: To cite a number from the Census Bureau, give the table, the window and the geography, for example 'US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates 2020-2024, table B25044, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico'. The percentage shares are not printed in the Census Bureau's tables: the observatory calculates them, so cite the observatory for a share and the cells for the Census Bureau's own counts. On the Analysis tab, the info (i) button beside a dataset opens its definition and sources, links to its entry in this dictionary and offers a CSV of every year, with the margins of error. In the downloaded CSV, the column headed 2024 is the 2020-2024 window and the column '2024 margin of error' holds its margin. In economy_series.json, find the variable under 'vars' by its key; 'years' and 'moe' hold one list per window, in the order of 'geo.names' (Puerto Rico is last). The trend line and the trend chart plot one point per window, labeled by its last year. Under each trend line in the inspector, the caption gives the length of the trend and the first and last label; for these survey series it counts windows, not separate years of data (in the 2026-10 snapshot, '15 yrs · 2010–24'). Neighboring points share four of their five survey years, so they are not independent yearly values.
caveats: Income bands in B19001 are in the dollars of the window's last year: the Census Bureau states the table in inflation-adjusted dollars of that year. The observatory does not convert one window's dollars to another's.

The means-of-transportation shares use all workers as the base, including those who worked from home. The travel-time share uses workers who did not work from home. Neither base is the same count as the civilian employed residents in the class-of-worker table.
Margins of error are published at the 90% confidence level and cover sampling error only.

Windows that include 2017 or 2020 carry survey disruption. The Census Bureau says it halted Puerto Rico Community Survey data collection from October to December 2017 after Hurricane María (https://www.census.gov/library/stories/2020/08/estimating-puerto-rico-population-after-hurricane-maria.html). It also says margins of error for 5-year estimates that include 2020 data rose because fewer interviews were completed in 2020 (https://www.census.gov/programs-surveys/acs/technical-documentation/user-notes/2022-04.html). The windows ending 2017 to 2021 include 2017 and the windows ending 2020 to 2024 include 2020. The observatory makes no adjustment.
Neighboring windows share four of their five years of survey responses, so the change from one window to the next mostly reflects one year of new responses.

values.gini: Table B19083, Gini Index of Income Inequality. Households. Cell 1.
values.hh_income_under_25k_pct: Table B19001, Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in inflation-adjusted dollars of the window's last year). Households. Cells 2 to 5 divided by cell 1.
values.hh_income_75k_plus_pct: Table B19001, Household Income in the Past 12 Months (in inflation-adjusted dollars of the window's last year). Households. Cells 13 to 17 divided by cell 1.
values.workers_16plus: Table B24080, Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over. Civilian employed residents 16 and over. Cell 1.
values.gov_worker_pct: Table B24080, Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over. Civilian employed residents 16 and over. Cells 7, 8, 9, 17, 18 and 19 divided by cell 1.
values.self_employed_pct: Table B24080, Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over. Civilian employed residents 16 and over. Cells 5, 10, 15 and 20 divided by cell 1.
values.nonprofit_worker_pct: Table B24080, Sex by Class of Worker for the Civilian Employed Population 16 Years and Over. Civilian employed residents 16 and over. Cells 6 and 16 divided by cell 1.
values.commute_drive_alone_pct: Table B08301, Means of Transportation to Work. Workers 16 and over, including those who worked from home. Cell 3 divided by cell 1.
values.commute_transit_pct: Table B08301, Means of Transportation to Work. Workers 16 and over, including those who worked from home. Cell 10 divided by cell 1.
values.commute_walk_pct: Table B08301, Means of Transportation to Work. Workers 16 and over, including those who worked from home. Cell 19 divided by cell 1.
values.work_from_home_pct: Table B08301, Means of Transportation to Work. Workers 16 and over, including those who worked from home. Cell 21 divided by cell 1.
values.commute_45plus_pct: Table B08303, Travel Time to Work. Workers 16 and over who did not work from home. Cells 11 to 13 divided by cell 1.
