values.no_internet_pct: Table B28002, Presence and Types of Internet Subscriptions in Household. Households. Cell 13 divided by cell 1. First window: 2013-2017.

entries.plain_es: Use esta lista para encontrar la tabla y las celdas del Negociado del Censo que hay detrás de cada cifra de ingreso, personas trabajadoras, viaje al trabajo, vehículos e internet de la pestaña Análisis. Ayuda a citar los números originales. La columna "Código" enumera identificadores de variables, no valores codificados.
entries.name_es: Tablas del Censo detrás de las cifras de ingreso, trabajo, viaje al trabajo e internet
entries.how_to_read_es: Para citar un número del Negociado del Censo, indique la tabla, la ventana y la geografía, por ejemplo: 'Negociado del Censo de EE. UU., Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS), estimados de 5 años 2020-2024, tabla B25044, Ponce Municipio, Puerto Rico'. Las proporciones en porcentaje no aparecen en las tablas del Negociado del Censo: el observatorio las calcula, así que cite el observatorio para una proporción y las celdas para los conteos propios del Negociado del Censo. En la pestaña Análisis, el botón de información (i) junto a un conjunto de datos abre su definición y sus fuentes, enlaza a su entrada en este diccionario y ofrece un CSV con todos los años, con los márgenes de error. En el CSV descargado, la columna con el encabezado 2024 es la ventana 2020-2024 y la columna '2024 margen de error' contiene su margen. En economy_series.json, busque la variable bajo 'vars' por su clave; 'years' y 'moe' contienen una lista por ventana, en el orden de 'geo.names' (Puerto Rico va al final). La línea de tendencia y la gráfica de tendencia trazan un punto por ventana, identificado por su último año. Debajo de cada línea de tendencia en el inspector, la leyenda indica la duración de la tendencia y la primera y la última etiqueta; en estas series de encuesta cuenta ventanas, no años de datos distintos (en el corte de datos 2026-10, '15 años · 2010–24'). Los puntos vecinos comparten cuatro de sus cinco años de encuesta, así que no son valores anuales independientes.

entries.name: How reliable the survey-based housing and household fields are
entries.plain: Survey figures are estimates with a margin of error. The municipality file does not show the margins. Take extra care in small municipalities and with small differences.
entries.definition: The American Community Survey (ACS) interviews a sample of households, so every estimate has a margin of error. The Census Bureau publishes it at the 90% confidence level: it is 90% confident that the true value lies within the estimate plus or minus the margin. The municipality file carries estimates only. Margins for most fields are in the Housing page series (housing_series.json, 'moe' values, by window).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. The Census Bureau publishes a new 5-year window each year.

entries.method: Margins are read from the Census Bureau's own margin columns. For shares and sums the observatory computes margins with the Census Bureau's formulas.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau ACS 5-year margins of error; Housing page series (housing_series.json)
entries.how_to_read: Check the margin before ranking or comparing. Add and subtract the margin to get a range for each municipality. If the two ranges overlap, the survey may not be able to tell the municipalities apart. For a formal test, use the Census Bureau's formula for the margin of a difference. In the 2026-10 snapshot, margins are widest in the smallest municipalities, such as Culebra, Vieques, Florida and Maricao.
caveats: In the 2026-10 snapshot (2020-2024 window), margins of error in the Housing page series run across the 78 municipalities as follows: median home value ±$1,926 (Carolina) to ±$44,042 (Vieques); median gross rent ±$16 (San Juan) to ±$240 (Culebra); median household income ±$805 (Mayagüez) to ±$7,604 (Culebra); people below poverty ±1.1 points (San Juan) to ±9.5 points (Culebra); employment rate ±0.7 points (San Juan) to ±5.9 points (Culebra and Vieques); cost-burdened renters ±0.7 points (Gurabo) to ±67.9 points (Florida).
The maximum affordable loan, the affordability ratio and the change fields have no margin of error. Their inputs do.

For total population and for the adult population aged 25 and over the Census Bureau sets the survey totals to its own estimates and often publishes no margin. In the 2026-10 snapshot (2020-2024 window) that holds for total population in 76 of 78 municipalities and for the adult population in 73 of 78. The observatory does not calculate a share's margin when the Census Bureau publishes none for the total the share is built on, so shares built on those totals show no margin in the Housing page series (for example 'Adults 25+ with a bachelor's degree or higher (%)'). The Population series and the files below the municipality give such a total a margin of zero instead, so their shares keep the margin of the numerator (methods.small_area_estimates). A missing margin does not mean the figure is exact.
Windows that end one year apart share four of five survey years. A difference between neighboring windows mostly reflects one year of new responses. The 2008-2012 and 2020-2024 windows share none.
A margin covers sampling error only. It does not cover mistakes in answers, such as owners' estimates of home value.
entries.plain_es: Las cifras de encuesta son estimados con un margen de error. El archivo de municipios no muestra los márgenes. Tenga cuidado especial con los municipios pequeños y con las diferencias pequeñas.
entries.name_es: Qué tan confiables son los campos de vivienda y hogar basados en la encuesta
entries.how_to_read_es: Revise el margen antes de ordenar o comparar. Sume y reste el margen para obtener un intervalo para cada municipio. Si los dos intervalos se solapan, es posible que la encuesta no pueda distinguir entre los municipios. Para una prueba formal, use la fórmula del Negociado del Censo para el margen de una diferencia. En el corte de datos 2026-10, los márgenes son más amplios en los municipios más pequeños, como Culebra, Vieques, Florida y Maricao.

entries.name: American Community Survey 5-year windows and how the observatory labels them
entries.plain: Survey figures come from five years of responses pooled together. The observatory labels each window by its last year, so '2024' means the 2020-2024 window. They are averages over a window, not figures for one year.
entries.definition: The American Community Survey (ACS) 5-year estimates pool the responses collected over 60 months. In Puerto Rico the Census Bureau runs the survey as the Puerto Rico Community Survey (PRCS); its 5-year estimates are published with the ACS tables that the observatory reads. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory reads every window from 2006-2010 to 2020-2024 (15 windows) and labels each one by its last year: 2010 is 2006-2010 and 2024 is 2020-2024. Windows one year apart share four of their five years. The Census Bureau's documentation of the 2013-2017 PRCS 5-year estimates says money values are adjusted to the dollars of the final year of the period, using the national Consumer Price Index. Check the Bureau's documentation for the window you cite before you compare dollar figures across windows. A window is a reading of a typical year in that period, not of its last year.
entries.unit: year label (last year of the window)

coverage.frequency: A new window is added when the Census Bureau publishes it

entries.method: housing_series.py reads the per-sequence summary files for the windows labelled 2010-2020 and the table-based files for 2021 onward, and finds the next window by itself. economy_series.py reads further tables from the same windows. The Housing page spells out the window ('ACS 2020-2024'), and so does the Analysis tab's year chip ('2020–2024'): a series made only from ACS tables is a window in Core.adapters and Core.time, and a series that mixes a yearly count into a survey (jobs per employed resident) is not. A table the survey did not yet have is skipped for early windows: the internet questions start with the 2013-2017 window, labelled 2017.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, summary files 2006-2010 through 2020-2024; US Census Bureau, Puerto Rico Community Survey, Multiyear Accuracy of the Data (5-year 2013-2017), for the dollar adjustment.
entries.how_to_read: Read a figure labelled 2024 as 'the typical value over 2020-2024'. To judge real change, compare windows that do not overlap, for example 2014, 2019 and 2024.
caveats: Because windows overlap, a change between neighbouring labels mostly reflects one year of new responses and understates real change.
A window pools years before and after an event, so it smooths sudden changes. The 2020-2024 window mixes the pandemic years with later years.

Windows that include 2017 or 2020 carry survey disruption. The Census Bureau halted Puerto Rico Community Survey data collection from October to December 2017 after Hurricane María. It also says margins of error for 5-year estimates that include 2020 data rose because fewer interviews were completed in 2020. The windows ending 2017 to 2021 include 2017, and the windows ending 2020 to 2024 include 2020. The observatory makes no adjustment. See 'Census tables behind the income, worker, commuting and internet figures' (economy.acs_work_income_tables) for the Census sources.
Small municipalities have small samples, so figures are noisy. Margins of error are published (90% confidence) and shown where they exist.
For rescaling by population, the observatory uses the population of the last year of the window, not an average.
entries.plain_es: Las cifras de la encuesta combinan cinco años de respuestas. El observatorio identifica cada ventana por su último año, así que "2024" significa la ventana 2020-2024. Son promedios de una ventana, no cifras de un solo año.
entries.name_es: Ventanas de 5 años de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS) y cómo las rotula el observatorio
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea una cifra rotulada 2024 como 'el valor típico de 2020-2024'. Para juzgar un cambio real, compare ventanas que no se solapen, por ejemplo 2014, 2019 y 2024.

entries.name: Nearest-year rule (latest value at or before the chosen year)
entries.plain: One year control sets every layer. A layer that has no value for that year shows its latest earlier year, and a small note beside the layer (the year chip) says which year it used.
entries.definition: For the year chosen on the year bar, each layer shows its own data year: the latest year in its series that is not later than the chosen year. If every year in the series is later, it shows its first year and the year chip says 'first data'. A one-time snapshot layer always shows its snapshot year. With 'Latest' chosen, each layer shows its own last year. The same rule picks the denominators for per-1,000, per-resident, share-of-jobs and location-quotient views.

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser each time the map redraws

entries.method: The function resolve of Core.time (site/js/core/time.js), used by the layer engine (the Analysis tab) and by the Housing page. The year chip comes from E.chip: '2019 (latest at or before 2020)', 'first data 2014', 'snapshot 2026' or, for a survey window, '2016–2020'. The year bar lists the years from 2010 on. Population, jobs and housing units for rescaling come from E.pop, E.jobs and E.hu, which apply the same rule.
entries.source_detail: Every dataset in the Analysis tab.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot: choose 2020, and unemployment from the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) shows 2019, because the observatory's unemployment series has no 2020 value, while poverty shows the survey window that ends in 2020. Choose 2012, and jobs show 2014 as 'first data 2014', because the jobs series starts in 2014. Choose 2015, and Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Public Assistance shows 2011, the latest declaration year in the data before 2015. Choose 2025, and survey series show the 2020-2024 window.
caveats: A layer can be older than the year you chose. Read the year chip beside each layer in the legend.

FEMA series have values only for years with a disaster declaration. A year with none shows the last earlier declaration year, not zero, and the dollars are those of that earlier disaster. In the 2026-10 snapshot, choosing 2019 shows 2017 for Public Assistance.
Two layers can describe different years. The table, the scatter plot and the correlation use each layer's own data year.
In the Analysis tab the year chip for a survey series names the whole five-year window, for example 2020–2024, while the year bar counts it by its last year (2024).
The year bar in a shared link stores your choice. Without it the link opens at 'Latest'.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: unemployment rate with the year set to 2020

entries.plain_es: Un solo control de año rige todas las capas. Una capa que no tiene valor para ese año muestra su año anterior más reciente, y una nota pequeña junto a la capa (la etiqueta del año) indica qué año usó.
entries.name_es: Regla del año más cercano (el último valor en el año elegido o antes)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10: si elige 2020, el desempleo del Negociado de Estadísticas Laborales (BLS) muestra 2019, porque la serie de desempleo del observatorio no tiene valor para 2020, mientras que la pobreza muestra la ventana de la encuesta que termina en 2020. Si elige 2012, los empleos muestran 2014 como 'datos desde 2014', porque la serie de empleos empieza en 2014. Si elige 2015, la Asistencia Pública de la Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias (FEMA) muestra 2011, el último año de declaración en los datos antes de 2015. Si elige 2025, las series de encuesta muestran la ventana 2020-2024.

entries.name: Snapshot labels and rebuilds
entries.plain: The observatory's data are rebuilt as a snapshot with a label such as 'Snapshot 2026-10'. The label names the full build, not every file. Transit files refresh nightly and some series files carry their own build dates.
entries.definition: A full build (python build.py) downloads or reuses every source, writes every data file and then meta.json, whose 'label' is the --label text or, by default, 'Snapshot' plus the year and month of the build in Coordinated Universal Time (UTC). meta.json also holds 'generated_at'. The time-series builders write their own 'built' dates, and a nightly job refreshes only the transit data: the transit files and the transit and access fields of places.json, municipalities.json and meta.json. The label is shown on the map pages, appears in the file name of the municipality table download (for example pr_digital_twin_municipalities_Snapshot_2026-10.csv) and in every citation the data dictionary offers.

coverage.frequency: Full build on demand; transit refresh nightly

entries.method: build.py (label, generated_at); refresh_network.py (nightly, writes only when a feed or an access value changed, leaves the label as it is); housing_series.build and economy_series.build (their own 'built' dates); registry.main and dictionary.build run at the end of a full build. Downloads are kept between builds, so a rebuild reuses them unless a refresh is requested.
entries.source_detail: Sources captured at the snapshot: Overture places, Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) flood zones, Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US), Census boundaries; transit feeds refreshed nightly.
entries.how_to_read: Quote the snapshot label, the year or window of the figure and the date you retrieved it (the Cite button adds the retrieval date). As of 2026-10-04, the full build of the 2026-10 snapshot is dated 2026-10-02 (UTC), the transit files 2026-10-02, the housing series 2026-10-03 and the economy series 2026-10-04. The access fields of the tourism places (place_access.json and the acc_ fields) are as of 2026-10-06. The build date is on the map page: hover over the snapshot label at the top or open the About section. The dictionary entry for each dataset says how old its source data are.
caveats: A month label does not give the day, and two builds in one month can share a label.
Parts of one snapshot can have different dates: the label names the full build only.
Source data can be older than the build, because the build reuses cached downloads. Each source's own release date applies.
Rebuilding can change numbers: new releases, revised estimates and changed source records all flow in.
entries.plain_es: Los datos del observatorio se reconstruyen como un corte de datos con una etiqueta como "Corte 2026-10". La etiqueta nombra la construcción completa, no cada archivo. Los archivos de transporte colectivo se actualizan cada noche y algunos archivos de series tienen sus propias fechas de construcción.
entries.name_es: Etiquetas de los cortes de datos y reconstrucciones
entries.how_to_read_es: Cite la etiqueta del corte de datos, el año o la ventana de la cifra y la fecha en que la obtuvo (el botón Citar agrega la fecha de consulta). Al 2026-10-04, la compilación completa del corte de datos 2026-10 tiene fecha 2026-10-02 (UTC), los archivos de transporte colectivo 2026-10-02, las series de vivienda 2026-10-03 y las series de economía 2026-10-04. Los campos de acceso de los lugares turísticos (place_access.json y los campos acc_) son al 2026-10-06. La fecha de compilación está en la página del mapa: pase el cursor sobre la etiqueta del corte de datos en la parte superior o abra la sección Info. La ficha del diccionario de cada conjunto de datos indica qué tan antiguos son los datos de su fuente.

entries.name: The 2020 break in the population series
entries.plain: Population estimates for 2011-2019 were built on the 2010 census and never revised after the 2020 census. The series therefore steps up in 2020. Do not read that step as one year of growth.
entries.definition: A vintage is one annual release of Census Bureau population estimates. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the observatory uses Vintage 2020 for 2011-2019 (built on the 2010 census) and Vintage 2025 for 2020-2025 (built on the 2020 census). The 2010 and 2020 values are April 1 values; the other years are July 1 estimates.

coverage.frequency: A new vintage is read when the Census Bureau releases it

entries.method: In the 2026-10 snapshot, population() in housing_series.py reads PRM-EST2020.csv (2010 and 2011-2019) and the cc-est2025-agesex-72 file (2020 and 2021-2025) and records each year's basis in the series ('basis'). The notes of housing_series.json say: 'Estimates for 2011-2019 were made before the 2020 census and were not revised to match it; 2020 and later are on the 2020 census base.' The 2020 value is the April 2020 base of the latest estimates. It includes the Census Bureau's post-census count corrections, so a few municipalities differ from the census count in municipalities.json:population_2020.
entries.source_detail: US Census Bureau Population Estimates, municipios of Puerto Rico (Vintage 2020 and Vintage 2025); 2010 and 2020 census counts.
entries.how_to_read: Compare years inside one base (2011-2019, or 2020-2025), or compare the two census counts (2010 and 2020). Do not compare 2019 with 2020 as if both rested on the same count. In the 2026-10 snapshot, the island-wide July 2019 estimate is 3,193,553 and the 2020 value is 3,285,874, a rise of 2.9%; the 2021 estimate is 3,262,731, a fall of 0.7%.
caveats: Everything divided by population is affected: per-1,000 and per-resident values step in 2020 as well.
'Population change since 2010' compares each year with the 2010 census count. The 2011-2019 values rest on the 2010 base and the 2020-2025 values on the 2020 base, so that series also steps at 2020.
These are estimates, not head counts, and the Census Bureau publishes no margin of error for them.
The American Community Survey also estimates population. The observatory's population series does not use it, so the two can differ.

The series labels the 2020 value '2020 census count', but it is the April 2020 base of the latest estimates, which includes the Census Bureau's post-census count corrections. In the 2026-10 snapshot it matches the census count for the island (3,285,874) but differs from municipalities.json:population_2020 in 68 of 78 municipalities, by 1 to 31 people.
entries.plain_es: Los estimados de población de 2011-2019 se basaron en el Censo de 2010 y nunca se revisaron después del Censo de 2020. Por eso la serie da un salto hacia arriba en 2020. Ese salto no debe leerse como un año de crecimiento.
entries.name_es: El salto de 2020 en la serie de población
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare años dentro de una misma base (2011-2019, o 2020-2025), o compare los dos conteos del censo (2010 y 2020). No compare 2019 con 2020 como si ambos se basaran en el mismo conteo. En el corte de datos 2026-10, el estimado de toda la isla para julio de 2019 es 3,193,553 y el valor de 2020 es 3,285,874, un aumento de 2.9%; el estimado de 2021 es 3,262,731, una disminución de 0.7%.

entries.name: Trend line in the inspector and the Trend chart
entries.plain: The small line beside each value in the workbench's Inspector, and the Trend view of the workbench, show how a layer's value moved across the years. A caption under each small line says how many years it covers. The Housing page profile has similar lines.
entries.definition: The Trend column of the workbench's Inspector view shows the layer's calculated values (with the same rescaling, inflation and base-year settings) for each data year from 2010 on, as one small line per layer for the place you selected. The column header reads 'Trend' with 'years shown; dot = chosen year' under it. Under each line a caption gives the number of years from the first to the last (counting years with no data), then the span, in the form 'N yrs · 2014–25'. When some years have no value it adds the number of values, in the form 'N yrs, M values · 2010–25'. A dot marks the data year on the map. The line needs at least two values and is not drawn for one-time snapshots. The Housing page profile has lines of the same kind, drawn from every year the series has, with a caption of the number of years only ('N yrs'). The Trend view charts the places you click or add, with the layer's settings. It uses years from 2010 on, and from the first year for the three Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) datasets. It draws at most eight lines.

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser each time the map redraws

entries.method: Functions ecSpark and ecBenchTrend in site/js/economy.js and spark in site/js/housing.js. Each line in the Trend column (and on the Housing page profile) is scaled between that place's own lowest and highest value. The chart joins points across years with no value (spanGaps).
entries.source_detail: Any dataset with more than one year in the Analysis tab; the Trend tab chart is drawn with Chart.js.
entries.how_to_read: Use the line for direction and timing, then read the numbers in the table. The caption tells you whether the line covers a full run of years or has gaps. In the 2026-10 snapshot, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) jobs read '12 yrs · 2014–25'. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) unemployment rate reads '16 yrs, 15 values · 2010–25' because it has no 2020 value. On the Housing page the resident population reads '16 yrs'.
caveats: Each small line is scaled to its own minimum and maximum, so the steepness of two lines cannot be compared between rows or between municipalities.

Where years have no value the chart draws a straight line across the gap, which suggests steady change. FEMA series have values only for years with a disaster declaration. The observatory's unemployment series has no 2020 value.
For survey series each year on the line is a five-year window, so '15 yrs' means 15 overlapping windows, not 15 separate years of responses.
The population series changes base in 2020 and survey windows overlap, which can bend or smooth a line (see the entries on both).
For a 'Change since the base year' layer the line starts after the base year.

The Trend view draws at most eight lines. Puerto Rico always comes first when it is chosen, then the municipalities in list order, so with more than seven municipalities chosen the last ones in the list are left out and Puerto Rico stays.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: poverty rate (click a municipality, choose 'Open in the workbench', then read the Trend column)
Housing page: the small lines beside each value in a municipality profile

entries.plain_es: La línea pequeña junto a cada valor en el Inspector de la mesa de trabajo, y la vista Tendencia de la mesa de trabajo, muestran cómo cambió el valor de una capa a lo largo de los años. Una leyenda debajo de cada línea pequeña indica cuántos años abarca. El perfil de la página de Vivienda tiene líneas parecidas.
entries.name_es: Línea de tendencia en el Inspector y en la gráfica Tendencia
entries.how_to_read_es: Use la línea para ver la dirección y el momento de los cambios, y luego lea los números en la tabla. La leyenda indica si la línea abarca una serie completa de años o si tiene huecos. En el corte de datos 2026-10, los empleos del Censo Trimestral de Empleo y Salarios (QCEW) dicen '12 años · 2014–25'. La tasa de desempleo del Negociado de Estadísticas Laborales (BLS) dice '16 años, 15 valores · 2010–25' porque no tiene valor para 2020. En la página Vivienda, la población residente dice '16 años'.

entries.name: What 'latest' means
entries.plain: 'Latest' means the newest year each dataset has, and datasets do not all end in the same year. The build looks for the newest release itself, so 'latest' moves when the data are rebuilt.
entries.definition: On the year bar, 'Latest' makes every layer show its own last year. The table of codes below gives those years for the 2026-10 snapshot.

coverage.frequency: Moves each time the data are rebuilt

entries.method: Each series script finds its last year when it runs. housing_series.py asks the Census Bureau's server whether the next American Community Survey (ACS) window and the next population vintage exist, starting from 2024 and 2025. economy_series.py asks the BLS server whether the next QCEW year exists, starting from 2024, reads unemployment and CPI through the last full calendar year, and reads federal awards through the last fiscal year, counted as final from 15 November. The page then shows 'Latest' by taking the last year of each series (ecResolve in site/js/economy.js, resolve in site/js/housing.js).
entries.source_detail: The release calendars of each source decide the last year available at build time.
entries.how_to_read: Check the year chip beside each layer before comparing two layers on 'Latest': they may describe different years. For a fixed comparison, choose a year on the year bar.
caveats: The newest year of some sources can be revised. The Analysis tab's description of the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) unemployment series calls its latest year preliminary. USAspending.gov says new or updated data appear the day after an agency submits them, so a recent fiscal year can change. Check the QCEW release notes for its newest year.
The newest values can be thinner than earlier ones: fewer sector figures are published, and small municipalities swing more.
A shared link opens at 'Latest' unless it stores a year, so the same link can show later data after a rebuild.

The observatory has no 2020 value for its four unemployment series (rate, labor force, employed and unemployed). The annual average for 2020 is empty in the BLS data the observatory downloaded, so the series skip 2020.

values.Jobs, work sites and pay (Quarterly Cens: 2025. Mining jobs (industry code 21 in the North American Industry Classification System, NAICS) and jobs per employed resident end in 2024.
values.Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEM: 2024, the latest declaration year with funded projects in the OpenFEMA file at build time
values.FEMA Individual Assistance (OpenFEMA): 2022, the latest declaration year with approved housing assistance in the OpenFEMA file at build time
values.Consumer Price Index: 2025, the reference year for inflation adjustment

entries.plain_es: "Último" significa el año más reciente que tiene cada conjunto de datos, y no todos terminan en el mismo año. La compilación busca por sí mismo la publicación más reciente, así que "Último" cambia cuando se reconstruyen los datos.
entries.name_es: Qué significa 'Último'
entries.how_to_read_es: Revise la etiqueta del año junto a cada capa antes de comparar dos capas en 'Último': pueden describir años distintos. Para una comparación fija, elija un año en la barra de años.

entries.name: Less reliable values: hatching, dashed outlines and italics
entries.plain: A value is marked less reliable when it is a survey estimate whose margin of error is large next to the estimate, or a rate or share built on fewer than ten counted. On a shaded map the municipality is hatched, a symbol gets a dashed outline, and the value in a pop-up or table is in italics. The mark says how much to trust a number, not whether it is right.
entries.definition: Two rules, applied to the values a layer shows. (1) Margin of error: the published margin of error (90% confidence) is more than 30% of the estimate; an estimate of zero with any margin counts, because the margin cannot be small next to nothing. For a change since a base year, either of the two years counts. (2) Few counted: a rate or share of a count (per 1,000 residents, per 1,000 housing units, % of the municipality's jobs, % of the area's residents or housing units, location quotient; or a share whose dataset names the count it rests on) where the count is above zero and below 10. A figure that the source withholds is not flagged: the municipality has no value and the legend says why (see methods.qcew_suppression). A municipality with no published margin is never flagged by rule 1.
entries.unit: flag for each municipality (yes or no)

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser each time the map redraws

entries.method: Core.reliability (site/js/core/reliability.js). isUnreliable(value, moe) is true when moe is above zero and either the value is zero or moe ÷ |value| is above 0.3. assess() applies it to the published estimates of the year shown and the small-count rule to the layer's counts, and the layer engine keeps the result (E.reliability). The 2D map draws the hatch as a pattern over the municipality (a dark line beside a white one, so it shows on pale and dark colours and in print), the legend lists each flag in words with the number of municipalities, and the pop-up, the workbench table and the hover card set the value in italics with a sentence below. The Housing page uses the same rule and the same sentence.
entries.source_detail: Margins of error: American Community Survey 5-year estimates, published by the Census Bureau or computed by Foundation for Puerto Rico with the Bureau's formulas (see measures.margin_of_error). The thresholds, 30% and 10 counted, are display conventions chosen by FPR, not statistical tests.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, 74 of the 78 municipalities are hatched for workers who walk to work (2020-2024) and 66 for nonprofit workers, because few residents in a small municipality give such an answer; none is hatched for median household income. For rule 2, 10 municipalities have fewer than 10 housing units inside the area flooded by 3 feet of sea level rise, so their share of housing units is hatched.
caveats: A flag is a caution, not a verdict: a flagged value can be close to the truth, and an unflagged one can be off.
The thresholds are conventions. 30% is the rule the Housing page has always used; fewer than 10 is a common point below which a count is treated as small.

Margins of error are not carried through a rescaling (per 1,000 residents, index, difference, change, percentile). The flag describes the published estimate, and the legend says so when a view other than 'As published' is flagged.
A value with no margin published (for example a figure that is not from a survey) is never flagged by the margin rule.
Housing page tables set zero estimates that carry a margin in italics, as the Analysis tab does; before 2026-10 they were left as ordinary figures.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: workers who walk to work (74 of 78 municipalities hatched)
Housing page: full data for seasonal units, with margins and italic values

entries.plain_es: Un valor se marca como menos confiable cuando es un estimado de encuesta con un margen de error grande en comparación con el estimado, o una tasa o proporción basada en menos de diez casos contados. En un mapa sombreado el municipio aparece rayado, un símbolo lleva un contorno de línea discontinua y el valor en una ventana emergente o una tabla aparece en cursiva. La marca indica cuánto confiar en una cifra, no si es correcta.
entries.name_es: Valores menos confiables: rayado, contornos discontinuos y cursiva
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, 74 de los 78 municipios aparecen rayados en personas que caminan al trabajo (2020-2024) y 66 en residentes que trabajan para organizaciones sin fines de lucro, porque pocas personas residentes de un municipio pequeño dan esa respuesta; ninguno aparece rayado en ingreso mediano del hogar. Por la regla 2, 10 municipios tienen menos de 10 unidades de vivienda dentro del área inundada con 3 pies de aumento del nivel del mar, así que su proporción de unidades de vivienda aparece rayada.

entries.name: Margin of error (survey figures, 90% confidence)
entries.plain: Figures from the American Community Survey are estimates from a sample, so they carry a margin of error. A figure of 38.8% ± 1.1 percentage points means the Census Bureau is 90% confident that the true value lies between 37.7% and 39.9%.
entries.definition: The margin of error (written ±) is the Census Bureau's published margin at the 90% confidence level: the Bureau is 90% confident that the true value lies within the estimate plus or minus the margin. The observatory carries the Bureau's margins for single cells such as medians. For sums and shares it computes the margin with the Bureau's formulas: the margin of a sum is the square root of the sum of the squared margins, and shares use the Bureau's proportion formula. If that formula would take the square root of a negative number, it uses the ratio formula. Margins are in the same unit as the estimate: percentage points for percent figures, dollars for dollar figures. On the Analysis tab the margin of a rate prints in percentage points with one decimal (for example '±1.1 pts').
entries.geography: 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico; for the variables of the Census small-area files also 901 barrios, 981 census tracts and 2,555 block groups

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser each time the map redraws

entries.method: Functions derive, pct and Cells in housing_series.py, derive_econ in economy_series.py and derive_pop in small_area.py compute and store the margins (the 'moe' values of housing_series.json, economy_series.json, population_series.json and, for the levels below the municipality, acs_barrio.json, acs_tract.json and acs_blockgroup.json; see methods.small_area_estimates). The Analysis tab shows '±' in the inspector and the popup when a layer is shown as published (a rate in percentage points, for example '±1.1 pts', and a dollar figure in dollars); with 'Inflation-adjusted' ticked the margin is multiplied by the same factor. The Housing page shows ± in its readouts and profile. Downloads of a series (comma-separated values, CSV, files) add a margin column per year. A value whose margin is above 30% of the estimate is marked less reliable (hatching, a dashed outline, italics) by Core.reliability; see measures.less_reliable_values.
entries.source_detail: American Community Survey 5-year estimates; margins as published by the Census Bureau or computed by Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) with the Bureau's formulas.
entries.how_to_read: In the 2026-10 snapshot, San Juan's poverty rate in the 2020-2024 window is 38.84% ± 1.08 points. Culebra's is 25.74% ± 9.48 points and Maricao's 52.89% ± 7.73 points. San Juan's median household income is $27,992 ± $1,036. In that snapshot 94 of the 549 Analysis tab datasets have margins of error. Census Bureau guidance: a difference between two estimates is statistically significant at the same confidence level when it is larger than the square root of the sum of the two squared margins. Use this rule for two estimates from different places in the same window. It does not apply to two overlapping windows. A municipality compared with Puerto Rico is not an independent comparison, because the island figure includes the municipality, so treat that result as approximate.
caveats: Margins are wide for small municipalities and narrow for large ones.

Rescaled views (per 1,000, index, difference, change, percentile) hide the margin. No margin is calculated for a difference, an index, a change or the affordability figures. A value whose published margin is wide is still marked less reliable in those views (see measures.less_reliable_values).
On the Analysis tab the margin of median age prints as '± … pts' although median age is in years.
A margin covers sampling error only. It does not cover mistakes in answers, such as an owner's estimate of home value.

Datasets from sources that are not surveys have no margin: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW) jobs, the Population Estimates, USAspending and OpenFEMA. The Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) unemployment series is a model estimate and has none in the observatory.

A share shows no margin when the observatory cannot calculate one from the margins published for its cells. In the 2026-10 snapshot, for adults with a bachelor's degree, 68 to 73 of the 78 municipalities have no margin in the 2021 to 2024 windows, while all 78 have one in 2010 to 2020. The Population series and the files below the municipality give such a total a margin of zero instead (the Census Bureau says it may be treated as zero), so their shares keep the margin of the numerator; see methods.small_area_estimates.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: click a municipality to see the ± beside the poverty rate
Data dictionary: entries that have margins of error

entries.plain_es: Las cifras de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad (ACS) son estimados basados en una muestra, así que tienen un margen de error. Una cifra de 38.8% ± 1.1 puntos porcentuales significa que el Negociado del Censo tiene un 90% de confianza de que el valor real está entre 37.7% y 39.9%.
entries.name_es: Margen de error (cifras de encuesta, 90% de confianza)
entries.how_to_read_es: En el corte de datos 2026-10, la tasa de pobreza de San Juan en la ventana 2020-2024 es 38.84% ± 1.08 puntos. La de Culebra es 25.74% ± 9.48 puntos y la de Maricao, 52.89% ± 7.73 puntos. El ingreso mediano del hogar de San Juan es $27,992 ± $1,036. En ese corte, 94 de los 549 conjuntos de datos de la pestaña Análisis tienen márgenes de error. Guía del Negociado del Censo: una diferencia entre dos estimados es estadísticamente significativa, con el mismo nivel de confianza, cuando es mayor que la raíz cuadrada de la suma de los cuadrados de los dos márgenes. Use esta regla para dos estimados de lugares distintos en la misma ventana. No se aplica a dos ventanas que se solapan. Un municipio comparado con Puerto Rico no es una comparación independiente, porque la cifra de la isla incluye al municipio, así que trate ese resultado como aproximado.

entries.name: How a shared link stores a view
entries.plain: A link from the map or the housing page stores your view settings in the web address: where the map is looking, which layers are on and the year. It holds no table of data and no name or account. If you plan a route, the link also holds the route's map coordinates, so check it before you share it.
entries.definition: The 2D map writes #Municipality&c=lat,lng,zoom&l=layers&s=shading&r=route&e=economy layers&ey=year&eb=base year&slr=feet into the address as you work. The 'e' part lists each Economy layer as ten values joined by dots: dataset key, mode (shaded or symbols), rescaling, colour ramp, class method, visible, same classes in every year, inflation-adjusted, opacity and symbol colour. 'ey' is written only when you choose a year ('Latest' has none) and 'eb' only when the base year is not 2014. The 3D view writes #c=lat,lng,zoom and r. The housing page writes ?m=municipality, then y=year only when you choose a year ('Latest' has none) and c=base year only when it is not 2012 (and ?d=dataset for an open dataset). The dictionary writes #entry and its filters as ?q=, domain, source, kind, time, file and moe.

coverage.frequency: Applies to every page

entries.method: Functions writeHash, parseHash and applyHash in site/js/app.js, ecEncode and ecRestore in site/js/economy.js, writeUrl in site/js/housing.js and the 3D page's address writer. The page updates the address in the browser (history.replaceState); nothing is sent to a server. A dataset key that no longer exists is skipped when a link is opened, and a rescaling that does not suit the dataset falls back to 'As published'.
entries.source_detail: Map position and zoom come from the Leaflet (2D) and MapLibre (3D) maps.
entries.how_to_read: A shared link shares a view, not a table of numbers. If the data were rebuilt after you made the link, the same view can show different numbers. To fix numbers in a report, cite the snapshot label and the date and keep the downloaded data file.
caveats: Route points are saved as coordinates with four decimals (about 11 metres). A route that starts at a home would put that location in the link. The link also holds the map centre (four decimals) and the municipality you selected. Check a link before sharing it.
A link without a year opens at 'Latest', which moves when the data are rebuilt.
Not everything is stored: an open workbench tab, the Ask the observatory chat and the selected municipality in the Analysis tab are not in the link.
entries.plain_es: Un enlace del mapa o de la página de Vivienda guarda la configuración de la vista en la dirección web: hacia dónde mira el mapa, qué capas están activas y el año. No contiene tablas de datos, nombres ni cuentas. Si se planifica una ruta, el enlace también guarda las coordenadas de la ruta en el mapa, así que revíselo antes de compartirlo.
entries.name_es: Cómo guarda una vista un enlace compartido
entries.how_to_read_es: Un enlace compartido comparte una vista, no una tabla de números. Si los datos se reconstruyeron después de crear el enlace, la misma vista puede mostrar números distintos. Para fijar los números en un informe, cite la etiqueta del corte de datos y la fecha, y guarde el archivo de datos descargado.

entries.name: How the Overview works out the headline figure of each field
entries.plain: Each field on the Topics tab shows one figure for the whole of Puerto Rico. It is either the Puerto Rico value of a yearly series, for example the median rent, or a total or share worked out from the 78 municipal values by a rule written next to the field in the registry. It is a figure to start from, not a score.
entries.definition: The registry (dictionary_src/domains.json) names one dictionary entry as the headline of a field, with a short label in Spanish and English. For a yearly series (the housing and economy series files) the figure is the Puerto Rico value of the latest year and the trend is the Puerto Rico value of every year. For a measure held for each municipality (a field of municipalities.json) the registry also gives an 'island' rule: a sum of one field, a ratio of the sums of two fields times a scale, or an average of one field weighted by another. The result is rounded to the decimals the registry gives. The period on the card says what the figure covers: a five-year estimate, a calendar year, a year of declaration, or the snapshot.
entries.unit: Depends on the figure (dollars, a percentage or a count)

coverage.frequency: Recomputed whenever catalog.py runs (each full build). In the 2026-10 snapshot the series figures are the latest years in the files (2024 for the American Community Survey windows, 2025 for jobs and population).

entries.method: catalog.py headline() reads the last element of each year's array in the series file (the Puerto Rico row) and keeps the years that have a value. island_value() applies the registry's rule to the municipal values. In the 2026-10 snapshot the rules are: tourism places listed is the sum of the municipal counts; tourism places in a flood hazard area is the sum of places in a flood hazard area divided by the sum of places, times 100; tourism places inside protected areas is the sum of the municipal counts; residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable is the average of the municipal shares weighted by the 2020 residents, which equals the island share apart from rounding.
entries.source_detail: catalog.py (headline, island_value, period_of); dictionary_src/domains.json (headline.label, headline.island)
entries.how_to_read: Read each figure with its period and its name: they say what it counts. A headline is chosen to start a conversation about a field. It does not say which field matters most, and a different headline for the same field would tell a different story.
caveats: Several headlines count tourism places (Overture Maps listings), not businesses, visitors or hazards in general. That is what the data hold today; fuller hazard and land figures for residents and homes are planned.
A five-year estimate (the American Community Survey) has a margin of error that the card does not show. The Housing page and the dictionary entry do.
A series of events (FEMA Public Assistance) shows the latest year that has a value, which can be small next to the years of large disasters. Read it with its trend line.
The share of residents near a stop with a current timetable depends on the date: it is computed as of the build date, and a feed that ends changes it (see methods.access_profile).
Where a field has no headline yet, or no data, the card says so instead of leaving the field out.

view.label: Map, Topics tab

entries.plain_es: Cada campo de la pestaña Temas muestra una cifra para todo Puerto Rico. Es el valor de Puerto Rico de una serie anual, por ejemplo la mediana del alquiler, o un total o una proporción que se calcula con los 78 valores municipales según una regla escrita junto al campo en el registro. Es una cifra de partida, no una puntuación.
entries.name_es: Cómo calcula el Resumen la cifra principal de cada campo
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea cada cifra con su período y su nombre: indican lo que cuenta. Una cifra principal se escoge para iniciar una conversación sobre un campo. No indica qué campo importa más, y otra cifra principal para el mismo campo contaría una historia distinta.

entries.name: How to cite the observatory and its sources
entries.plain: Cite the original source for the data and the observatory for how the data were put together. The Cite button on each dictionary entry gives a ready credit line and APA, Chicago and BibTeX versions.
entries.definition: Each dictionary entry has a Cite button with four formats. The credit line joins the credit lines of the entry's sources and adds 'Processed by Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory (snapshot label)'. APA 7 and BibTeX give Foundation for Puerto Rico as author and the entry name and its years as the title. Chicago gives the entry name only. All three add the snapshot label, the address of the entry, the original sources and the date you retrieved it. The year is the year of the snapshot build. The dictionary page also has a citation for the whole site. It uses the address of the page you are on, or https://observatory.foundationpr.org/ when the page runs on a local address.

coverage.frequency: Applies to every entry

entries.method: Functions citeTexts and citePanel in site/js/dictionary.js. The credit line of each source is stored in the dictionary's source list. When the page runs on a local address, the public address is used in the citation.
entries.source_detail: Not a data entry. The sources listed are examples of those that figures from the observatory credit. When you cite this entry, credit the observatory only.
entries.how_to_read: Say what the figure is, the year or window, the snapshot label and the retrieval date. For survey figures, add the window ('2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-year estimates'). For figures the observatory calculates, such as rates per 1,000 residents or the affordability ratio, say that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) calculated them from the named sources. Example, calculated figure: 'In 2025 there were about 770 jobs located in San Juan for every 1,000 residents (FPR calculation from US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, 2025 annual average, and US Census Bureau Population Estimates, Vintage 2025; PR Data Observatory, Snapshot 2026-10, retrieved [date]).' Example, survey figure: 'San Juan's poverty rate was 38.8% ± 1.1 percentage points (90% confidence), 2020-2024 American Community Survey 5-year estimates (PR Data Observatory, Snapshot 2026-10, retrieved [date]).' Measure and method entries are not data sets. In the APA citation of one of them, delete '[Data set]'. In the APA and BibTeX citations, delete a title ending '(Not tied to a year)'. Every dataset dialog on the Analysis tab and the Housing page links to its dictionary entry, where the Cite button is.
caveats: The observatory's citation does not replace the source's own terms. Check the license or terms of the source, which are in the Sources section, before reuse.

Terms differ by source. Examples: OpenStreetMap data need credit and share-alike under the Open Database License (ODbL); municipal transit feeds state no license; Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) data are provided as is; OpenFEMA asks for a statement that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) does not endorse the product. Check each source's terms in the Sources section. This is not legal advice.
Credit lines are recorded in the source list. Check each source's own terms for the wording it requires; the observatory does not give legal advice.
Numbers can change when the data are rebuilt, so always give the snapshot label.
entries.plain_es: Cite la fuente original por los datos y el observatorio por la forma en que se reunieron los datos. El botón "Citar" de cada entrada del diccionario da una línea de crédito lista y versiones en APA, Chicago y BibTeX.
entries.name_es: Cómo citar el observatorio y sus fuentes
entries.how_to_read_es: Indique qué es la cifra, el año o la ventana, la etiqueta del corte de datos y la fecha de consulta. Para las cifras de encuesta, agregue la ventana ('estimados de 5 años de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense 2020-2024'). Para las cifras que calcula el observatorio, como las tasas por cada 1,000 residentes o la razón de asequibilidad, indique que Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) las calculó a partir de las fuentes nombradas. Ejemplo de cifra calculada: 'En 2025 había unos 770 empleos ubicados en San Juan por cada 1,000 residentes (cálculo de FPR a partir de US Bureau of Labor Statistics, Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, promedio anual de 2025, y US Census Bureau Population Estimates, Vintage 2025; Observatorio de Datos de PR, Corte 2026-10, recuperado el [fecha]).' Ejemplo de cifra de encuesta: 'La tasa de pobreza de San Juan era 38.8% ± 1.1 puntos porcentuales (90% de confianza), estimados de 5 años de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense 2020-2024 (Observatorio de Datos de PR, Corte 2026-10, recuperado el [fecha]).' Las fichas de medidas y métodos no son conjuntos de datos. En la cita APA de una de ellas, borre '[Conjunto de datos]'. En las citas APA y BibTeX, borre un título que termine en '(No ligado a un año)'. Cada cuadro de diálogo de un conjunto de datos en la pestaña Análisis y en la página Vivienda enlaza a su ficha del diccionario, donde está el botón Citar.

entries.name: Rounding and how numbers are displayed
entries.plain: The observatory keeps more decimals than it shows. Maps, legends and tables round numbers for reading. Downloads and data files keep the stored precision. Cite the stored value with its unit and year.
entries.definition: Display: numbers use US format (commas for thousands, points for decimals). A missing value shows as a dash on the page, 'No data' in grey on the map, and an empty cell in downloads. Legend and axis labels, negative dollar amounts, the Ask the observatory chat's changes and the Housing page's signed changes use a true minus sign (−). Other negative figures, such as those in the Analysis tab inspector and table, use a plain hyphen (-). The Analysis tab gives each dataset its own number of decimals (counts none, most percentages one, the Gini index three). A rescaling overrides it: per 1,000 one decimal; per km² one decimal (none for dollars); dollars per resident none; difference from Puerto Rico the dataset's own decimals (none for dollars); share of Puerto Rico two; share of jobs one; location quotient two; index none; percentile none; change one (two for ratios). Margins of error (±) print with one decimal for rates, in percentage points. Legend and axis labels are shortened (255K, 1.5K, 12M). Median year built shows as a whole year. The Housing page shows dollars to the whole dollar. Stored precision: place coordinates six decimals, confidence three, tourism places per 1,000 residents and per km² two, flood share one, land area one, survey shares two, Gini three.

coverage.frequency: Applies to every page

entries.method: Functions ecFmt, ecCompact and ecOut in site/js/economy.js; fmt in site/js/common.js; the rounding in build.py, housing_series.py and economy_series.py. Downloads are comma-separated values (CSV) files. The table download from the Analysis tab writes the calculated values (per-1,000 values already rounded to three decimals), a series download writes the stored values, and the municipality download on the Rankings tab writes municipalities.json as stored.
entries.source_detail: Applies to every dataset in the observatory.
entries.how_to_read: Round only in your own text, and say the year and the unit. If two numbers look equal on screen, check the stored values in a download.
caveats: Rounded shares may not add up to 100%.
Ranks and colour classes use unrounded values. Two municipalities that show the same rounded number can have different ranks or colours.
Per-1,000 values are calculated to three decimals and shown with one.
The legend limits are rounded labels. A value shown as 41.3 may sit on either side of a limit labelled 41.3.
entries.plain_es: El observatorio guarda más decimales de los que muestra. Los mapas, las leyendas y las tablas redondean los números para facilitar la lectura. Las descargas y los archivos de datos mantienen la precisión guardada. Cite el valor guardado con su unidad y su año.
entries.name_es: El redondeo y cómo se muestran los números
entries.how_to_read_es: Redondee solo en su propio texto e indique el año y la unidad. Si dos números se ven iguales en pantalla, revise los valores guardados en una descarga.

entries.name: Analysis tab
entries.plain: The Analysis tab puts yearly datasets on the map: jobs, pay, unemployment, income, poverty, commuting, federal money, housing and reported crime. Shade a rate, size a count, move the year, and click the map to see every layer at that place.
entries.definition: In Snapshot 2026-10 the tab lists 549 datasets: 275 yearly series for the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico, and 274 counts and shares for a single year (tourism places, places in a flood hazard area or a protected area, the tourism places near transit, transit stops and the residents near them, whether Uber lists the municipality, the change in median gross rent since 2008-2012, land by plan class, and the residents and housing units inside a hazard, inside protected land or near a stop, the health center sites and shortage areas of each municipality, its hospitals and other care facilities, the distance from where residents live to the nearest health center, its drinking water systems (and those outside PRASA, with the residents they serve) and power plants, its expected yearly loss from natural hazards, the landslides mapped after Hurricane María, its wetlands and mangroves, its public housing developments and units, its tax credit housing projects and units, fire, EMS and police stations and public libraries, its tax-exempt organizations by field, its places on the National Register of Historic Places, its substance use and mental health treatment facilities by type, and its EPA-regulated sites, impaired waters and air quality non-attainment areas, households with severe housing problems, street intersections and drive time to a general hospital, which also have barrio values; and the WCRP vulnerability indices, which have values for barrios only). Of the 275 series, 104 are listed in the economy file (some take their values from the Housing page's series, such as poverty and median income) and 171 more come from the Housing page's series (33), from the Population series of the survey (30), from the daytime population series (3), from the survey's series of labor force participation by sex (7), from the education series of public schools and colleges (7), from the Medicare series (3), from the bridges series (3), from the series of community resilience and earthquakes (5), from the airport and ferry series (4), from the night-time lights series (2), from the satellite fire detections series (3), from the fixed broadband series (6), from the road traffic series (6), from the road deaths series (6), from the bank offices and home loans series (6), from the drought series (3), from the storm recovery series (2), from the essentials series (7), from the degrees series (11), from the school conditions series (4), from the test results series (2), from the health providers series (7) and from the cut-off series (5). Any dataset can be added to the map as a shaded layer or as sized symbols. Up to two shaded layers and any number of symbol layers can be on at once. The tab holds a year control, six ready-made views and the list of layers on the map with their settings. It also has buttons for the workbench, for clearing the layers and for copying a link, switches for other map layers, the dataset list with a search box, four reading notes and a list of sources with their licenses. The tab loads its data the first time you open it. While the tab is open and a layer is visible, a click on the map opens the economy popup, not the municipality profile.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js reads data/economy_series.json (built by economy_series.py) and data/housing_series.json (built by housing_series.py). A housing series that the economy file does not list is added under a 'Housing ·' group. The five tourism counts are built in the browser from municipalities.json.
entries.how_to_read: Start from a ready-made view, then change one thing at a time. Each layer says which year it shows.
caveats: Jobs, pay and establishments count the workplace (Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, QCEW). Income, poverty and commuting describe residents (American Community Survey, ACS). In the 2024 data of Snapshot 2026-10, 9 of the 78 municipalities have more jobs than employed residents; San Juan (1.9 jobs per employed resident) and Mayagüez (1.5) have the most. This fits commuting into job centres, but the ratio does not measure commuting.

Survey figures (ACS, Local Area Unemployment Statistics, LAUS) are noisy for small municipalities. Margins of error are shown where the source publishes them. The jobs data hide cells that would identify one employer, so some sectors are blank in small municipalities.
The informal economy is not in the jobs data. The share of self-employed residents points to some work the jobs data miss, but it is not a measure of the informal economy.

Federal awards are placed where the work is done, as the awarding agency reports it. The awarding agency often records awards for statewide programs under the capital, so San Juan's total can include money that serves other places. See the entry on federal awards, all types.

In Snapshot 2026-10 the latest year (2025) of the jobs and unemployment series is preliminary and can be revised. The unemployment rate has no 2020 value. Some series are not yearly: four census series hold only 2010 and 2020, and the recovery series of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) are by declaration year (12 years from 2001 to 2024 for Public Assistance).
Federal award and recovery amounts (federal awards, FEMA Public Assistance and FEMA Individual Assistance) are amounts obligated (committed) or approved. They are not money spent, damage or need.
Values per resident step in 2020, because the Census Bureau's population estimates change base that year (see the entry on the 2020 break in the population series).

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Análisis pone en el mapa conjuntos de datos anuales: empleos, paga, desempleo, ingreso, pobreza, viaje al trabajo, fondos federales, vivienda y delitos informados. Sombree una tasa, muestre un conteo con símbolos, cambie el año y haga clic en el mapa para ver todas las capas en ese lugar.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis
entries.how_to_read_es: Empiece con una vista preparada y luego cambie una cosa a la vez. Cada capa indica qué año muestra.

entries.name: Analysis tab: 'Also show on the map'
entries.plain: 'Also show on the map' repeats eight switches of the Map layers tab, in the order of that tab and with its names, so you can add context to an economy view without leaving the tab.
entries.definition: The eight switches are Tourism places, Transit routes, Transit stops, Barrios, Flood hazard zones, Protected areas, Land use (PUT 2015, the Plan de Uso de Terrenos) and Municipality boundaries. Each one is the same switch as on the Map layers tab. A change in one place shows in the other.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: economy.js (ecRenderContext, ecContextSync) sets the Layers-tab checkbox and sends it a change event.
entries.how_to_read: Add one context layer at a time. Several overlays together make the economy colours hard to read.
caveats: The sea level and transit planning layers are not in this list. Use the Layers and Transit tabs for them.

entries.plain_es: "Mostrar también en el mapa" repite ocho interruptores de la pestaña Capas del mapa, en el orden de esa pestaña y con sus nombres, para agregar contexto a una vista económica sin salir de la pestaña.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: 'Mostrar también en el mapa'
entries.how_to_read_es: Agregue una capa de contexto a la vez. Varias capas superpuestas juntas hacen difícil leer los colores de la economía.

entries.name: Analysis tab: click, hover and the municipality card
entries.plain: Click a municipality while the Analysis tab is open. A card shows the value of each visible layer for that place and its rank among the 78. It also shows the margin of error where the source publishes one.
entries.definition: A click outlines the municipality in black and opens a card. The card has a table with one row for each visible layer. A row gives the name (press it to open the dataset's information), how the layer is shown and for which year, and the value. It adds the margin of error (±) when the source publishes one and the layer is shown 'as published'. For a rate the margin is in percentage points (for example ±1.2 pts). For other datasets it is in the dataset's own unit. It ends with the rank ('#n of N', where 1 is the highest value). A link opens the workbench. On a computer, pointing at the map also shows a small box at the bottom right with each layer's value for the municipality under the pointer. That box is not shown on phones. In the workbench's Inspector tab the same table adds a column for Puerto Rico and a column headed 'Trend' with a trend line for each layer. A caption under each line gives its length, for example '12 yrs · 2014–25' (see the entry on trend lines). The map popup has no trend column. When the jobs data are available, a line names the industry sector, or government, that has the most jobs in the municipality, with its share of the municipality's jobs, for the year the jobs dataset shows.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecInspect, ecValue, ecRank, ecHover, ecSelect).
entries.how_to_read: Use the rank to place the municipality, and the margin of error to judge whether a small difference means anything.
caveats: Margins of error are 90% confidence margins from the Census Bureau's survey. Many datasets are counts or administrative figures with no margin.
The rank counts the municipalities that have a value. Tied values share the first of their places.
The 'largest sector' line counts private industry sectors and government. Hidden cells can change it in small municipalities.
Rank 1 is the highest value, which for unemployment or poverty is the worst result. Compare ranks only within the same layer and year.

entries.plain_es: Haga clic en un municipio con la pestaña Análisis abierta. Una tarjeta muestra el valor de cada capa visible en ese lugar y su posición entre los 78. También muestra el margen de error cuando la fuente lo publica.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: clic, cursor y tarjeta del municipio
entries.how_to_read_es: Use la posición para situar el municipio y el margen de error para juzgar si una diferencia pequeña significa algo.

entries.name: Analysis tab: dataset information window
entries.plain: The info button beside a dataset opens a window with its definition, years, sources and licenses. It also links to the dataset's dictionary entry and lets you download all its years as a comma-separated values (CSV) file.
entries.definition: The window shows the dataset's group and type (count, dollar total, dollar level, rate or ratio) and a definition. Jobs (qcew_jobs) and the unemployment rate (laus_unemp_rate) have an extra note. Next come the source reference and the years the dataset covers (for example '2014–2025 (12 years)', with 'margins of error at 90% confidence are published' when they are). Then come the geography, the build date and a note on dollars where they apply. A line 'Full entry' links to the dataset's entry in the data dictionary, where you find its meaning, method, cautions and how to cite it. For Public Assistance of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) the window also gives the share of money recorded as statewide for each declaration year. For the federal award datasets it gives the share of awards that name no municipality, by fiscal year. Below are the sources with their license text and links. Buttons add the dataset to the map as a shaded layer or as symbols. 'Download all years (CSV)' saves pr_economy_<dataset>.csv with the columns GEOID (the geographic identifier code), Municipality and one column for each year, plus a margin-of-error column for each year when the source publishes one. Values are as published. Nothing is normalised or inflation-adjusted.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecInfo), which fills an HTML dialog element. The dictionary link opens dictionary.html#economy.<dataset>, or #housing.<dataset> for series that come from the Housing page.
entries.how_to_read: Read the definition and the source before you cite a number. The dictionary entry gives the full method and a citation.
caveats: The license text is what the source states. Check the source's own terms before you reuse the data.
The CSV can start earlier than 2010 because it holds every year of the dataset.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab, dataset list

entries.plain_es: El botón de información junto a un conjunto de datos abre una ventana con su definición, años, fuentes y licencias. También enlaza a su ficha en el diccionario y permite descargar todos sus años como archivo CSV (valores separados por comas).
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: ventana de información del conjunto de datos
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea la definición y la fuente antes de citar una cifra. La ficha del diccionario da el método completo y una cita.

entries.name: Analysis tab: dataset list and search
entries.plain: The dataset list on the Analysis tab shows every dataset in groups. Type in the search box to find one, then press 'Shade' or 'Symbols' to put it on the map, or the info button to read its definition and sources.
entries.definition: In Snapshot 2026-10 the list has 101 groups, shown below with the number of datasets in each. The search box looks for the text you type, as one phrase (not word by word), ignoring accents and capitals, in each dataset's name, group, source reference and definition. A search opens every group that has a match. Without a search only the first group is open. The count beside 'Datasets' shows how many are listed. Each row gives the name and the years it covers (for example 2014–2025, or 'snapshot 2026'), with '± margins' when the source publishes margins of error. 'Shade' adds the dataset as a shaded layer. For a count it is shown per 1,000 residents, and for a dollar total per resident, because a shaded map of a raw count mostly shows how big the municipality is. 'Symbols' adds it as sized circles with the value as published. The info button opens the dataset dialog.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecLoad, ecRenderBrowse). Groups appear in the order of sortGroups in core/datasets.js, the themes of the layer menu (docs/layers.md): population, the economy, hazards and environment, land and housing, infrastructure and mobility, community services, communities, and the visitor economy (Tourism supply) last.
entries.how_to_read: The group is the tab's own grouping. It is not the dictionary's grouping.
caveats: A dataset can appear under a different group here than in the dictionary. For example, poverty, median income and population are listed under groups of the economy file, and housing series appear under 'Housing ·' groups.

values.Population · People and age: 20 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the survey's estimate of the population, the share of women and girls, and the count and share of eight age groups (under 3, 3 and 4, 5 to 17, under 18, 18 to 24, 25 to 44, 45 to 64 and 65 and older) and of the broader group 18 to 44.
values.Population · Household types: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the shares of family households and of one-person households.
values.Population · Disability and veterans: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the share of veterans among civilians 18 and older, and the share of people with a disability among people outside institutions.
values.Population · Health insurance: 1 dataset in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the share of people outside institutions without health insurance.
values.Population · Education level: 1 dataset in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the share of adults 25 and older without a high school diploma.
values.Population · Language: 1 dataset in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the share of people 5 and older who speak English less than "very well".
values.Population · Poverty and assistance: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (5-year windows 2017-2021 to 2020-2024): the share of households that received nutrition assistance (PAN), and the shares of children under 18 and of people 65 and older below the poverty level.
values.Population · Daytime population: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, calculated from the Census Bureau's commuting flows of 2016-2020 and the 2020 Census: the daytime population, the daytime change as a percent of residents, and the share of resident workers who work in another municipio.
values.Vulnerability (CDC/ATSDR SVI): 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2022): CDC's Social Vulnerability Index rank among the 78 municipios, overall and for three themes (socioeconomic status, household characteristics, housing type and transportation).
values.Hazards · Facilities and roads in hazard: 17 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the public facilities, the public schools and their students, and the kilometres of main road inside FEMA's 1% flood area, NOAA's 3 ft sea level rise area and the USGS high landslide susceptibility classes, as counts and as shares.
values.Hazards · Drought (US Drought Monitor): 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, yearly 2000-2026, from the weekly US Drought Monitor: the average share of the area in drought, and the weeks with drought, and with severe drought, over half the area.
values.Hazards · Storm recovery (night-time lig: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, for Hurricanes María (2017) and Fiona (2022), calculated from the monthly night-time light: the months until light came back and the darkest month after each storm.
values.Hazards · Cut off from hospitals (estima: 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, estimates for the current year: the share of residents with no open road to a hospital when the roads in FEMA's 1% flood area close (and of them, those on a dry street), when the bridges in poor condition close, and both, and the residents cut off by floods.
values.Communities · Road distance to essential: 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, estimates for the current year: road distance from where residents live to a supermarket, any food store, a pharmacy, a bank or cooperativa, a library and a fire or EMS station, and the share of residents more than 5 km from a supermarket.
values.Education · Degrees awarded (IPEDS): 11 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, academic years ending 2015 to 2024: degrees and certificates awarded by colleges, by level (associate, bachelor's, master's and doctor's) and by broad field, counted where the campus is.
values.Education · School conditions (Civil Rig: 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, school years 2017-18 and 2021-22: chronic absence, students per counselor, schools with a nurse and schools with no counselor in public schools.
values.Education · Test results (META-PR, 2014-: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, school years 2014-15 to 2018-19: public school students proficient in reading (Spanish) and math on Puerto Rico's test (META-PR).
values.Health · Health care providers (NPPES re: 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, for the current year: health care providers registered with a practice address in each municipio, by type (NPPES registry; a municipio with 1 to 9 is empty).
values.Labor force by sex: 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the American Community Survey (three 5-year windows that share no year: 2010-2014, 2015-2019 and 2020-2024), with margins: the labor force participation rate of women 16 and over, of men 16 and over and of women 25 to 54, the gap between men and women in percentage points, the unemployment rate of women, the women 16 and over and the women in the labor force.
values.Economy · Nonprofit organizations: 12 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot (the IRS file of 2026-10-13): tax-exempt organizations, 501(c)(3) charities and the ten NTEE major groups (IRS Exempt Organizations Business Master File).
values.Economy · Night-time lights (NASA Black: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, yearly 2012-2025, from NASA Black Marble VNP46A3: the mean night-time radiance and the share of pixels of poor quality or gap-filled, with barrio values.
values.Economy · Banks and deposits (FDIC): 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, yearly 2000-2026 (June 30), from the FDIC Summary of Deposits: the offices of FDIC-insured banks and the deposits booked at them. Cooperativas are not in it.
values.Housing · Home loans (HMDA): 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, yearly 2018-2025, from the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act data: home loans made, home purchase loans, their amount and the share of decided applications denied.
values.Residents · Flood hazard · FEMA: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): residents inside a Special Flood Hazard Area (1% annual chance) and inside any flood hazard area (1% or 0.2% annual chance).
values.Housing units · Flood hazard · FEMA: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): housing units inside a Special Flood Hazard Area (1% annual chance) and inside any flood hazard area (1% or 0.2% annual chance).
values.Residents · Sea level rise · NOAA (conne: 10 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): residents on land inundated by 1 to 10 feet of sea level rise, one dataset for each height.
values.Residents · Sea level rise · NOAA (low-l: 10 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): residents in low-lying areas that may flood at 1 to 10 feet of sea level rise but are not connected to the ocean, one dataset for each height.
values.Residents · Storm surge · NOAA NHC (near: 10 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): residents where NOAA's storm surge maps show water in a category 1 to 5 hurricane, at any depth and under 3 feet or more, one dataset for each category and depth.
values.Housing units · Sea level rise · NOAA (c: 10 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): housing units on land inundated by 1 to 10 feet of sea level rise, one dataset for each height.
values.Housing units · Sea level rise · NOAA (l: 10 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): housing units in low-lying areas that may flood at 1 to 10 feet of sea level rise but are not connected to the ocean, one dataset for each height.
values.Housing units · Storm surge · NOAA NHC (: 10 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): housing units where NOAA's storm surge maps show water in a category 1 to 5 hurricane, at any depth and under 3 feet or more, one dataset for each category and depth.
values.Residents · Protected areas · USGS PAD-U: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): residents inside a protected area and inside a strictly protected area (GAP status 1 or 2).
values.Housing units · Protected areas · USGS P: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): housing units inside a protected area and inside a strictly protected area (GAP status 1 or 2).
values.Environment · Natural hazard risk: 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: FEMA's expected annual loss from natural hazards in all and from hurricane wind, earthquake, inland flooding, landslide, coastal flooding and tsunami (National Risk Index, December 2025).
