values.Environment · Landslides: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, for 2017: landslides mapped after Hurricane María, in all and per km² of land (USGS).
values.Environment · Landslide susceptibility (: 9 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the USGS map of susceptibility to landslides triggered by intense rainfall (2020): the share of the land in the high-or-above and very-high-or-above classes and in each of the five classes, and the 2020 residents living in the high-or-above classes (an estimate), with barrio values.
values.Environment · Surface heat (Landsat): 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from Landsat 8 and 9 land surface temperature on clear summer mornings (June to September 2024-2026): the median and the hottest tenth of the land's temperature, the share of land among Puerto Rico's hottest tenth and the 2020 residents living there (an estimate), with barrio values.
values.Environment · Vegetation (Sentinel-2): 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from Sentinel-2 vegetation greenness (NDVI) on clear summer days (June to September 2024-2026, the window of surface heat): the median NDVI, the share of land with dense vegetation and with little or none, and the 2020 residents living on land with little or none (an estimate), with barrio values.
values.Environment · Night surface heat (ECOSTR: 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from NASA ECOSTRESS land surface temperature on clear summer nights (21:00 to 06:00, June to September 2024-2026): the median and the warmest tenth of the land's night temperature, the share of land among Puerto Rico's warmest tenth at night and the 2020 residents living there (an estimate), with barrio values.
values.Environment · Slope of the land (USGS 3D: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10: the share of the land steeper than 15% and than 30%, and the mean slope, from the slope of every 10 m cell of the USGS 3DEP elevation model (Horn's method), with barrio values.
values.Infrastructure · Climb on the walk to a: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, for the residents within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable: the median round-trip climb of their walk, and the residents (share and count) whose walk has a stretch steeper than a ramp may be under the 2010 ADA Standards, from USGS 3DEP heights, with barrio values.
values.Environment · Wetlands: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: wetland area, wetland share of land and mangrove area (National Wetlands Inventory, almost all mapped from photographs of 1983).
values.Environment · Community resilience: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value a year from 2019 (no 2020): residents with no, one or two, and three or more disaster risk factors, with margins (Census Community Resilience Estimates).
values.Environment · Earthquakes: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value a year from 2000: earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more and 4.0 or more in or just off each municipio (USGS ComCat).
values.Environment · Regulated sites (EPA): 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot each in its source's vintage: Toxics Release Inventory facilities (reporting year 2024), active Risk Management Plan facilities and Superfund National Priorities List sites (EPA Facility Registry Service), and municipal solid waste landfills, all and still open (EPA LMOP, data of 2024). Also by barrio.
values.Environment · Water and air quality (EPA: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10: the share of the area draining to or in a 303(d)-listed impaired water (EPA ATTAINS, 2024 cycle) and inside a sulfur dioxide or a lead non-attainment area (EPA Green Book). Also by barrio.
values.Land use (PUT 2015): 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the share of each municipality's land that the 2015 land use plan classifies as urban land and as specially protected rural land.
values.Housing · Prices and incomes: 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10: four yearly series and the change in median gross rent since 2008-2012, for a single year.
values.Housing · Public housing: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot (HUD's layer of 2026-06): public housing developments and their units (HUD).
values.Housing · Tax credit housing: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot (HUD's LIHTC database, release of 2026-04-30): Low-Income Housing Tax Credit projects, their housing units and their low-income units (HUD).
values.Environment · Fires (NASA FIRMS): 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from NASA FIRMS active fire detections (VIIRS 375 m on NOAA-20): vegetation fire detections each year since 2019 and per 100 km² of land, and in the last 12 months, by municipio.
values.Housing · Buildings (Overture): 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from Overture's buildings theme (release 2026-10-21.0; OpenStreetMap, Google and Microsoft footprints): the number of buildings, buildings per km², land under roofs, the median footprint, buildings in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area (count and share) and the share traced by machine learning, with barrio values.
values.Housing · Severe housing problems: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10 (HUD CHAS 2016-2020): households with one or more severe housing problems and their share. Also by barrio, as estimates spread from census tracts.
values.Transit access: 6 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the number of transit stops and stations, and the shares of residents within 400 m in a straight line, and within a 400 m walk along mapped roads, of a stop with a timetable on file and of a stop with a current timetable, and whether Uber lists the municipality (1 or 0).
values.Residents · Transit stops within 400 m: 8 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): residents within 400 m of any mapped stop, of a stop with a timetable on file, of a stop with a current timetable, of a frequent stop (20 or more weekday departures) and of a stop with Saturday or Sunday service, and within a 400 m walk along mapped roads of a stop with a current timetable and of a frequent stop.
values.Housing units · Transit stops within 400: 8 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): housing units within 400 m of any mapped stop, of a stop with a timetable on file, of a stop with a current timetable, of a frequent stop (20 or more weekday departures) and of a stop with Saturday or Sunday service, and within a 400 m walk along mapped roads of a stop with a current timetable and of a frequent stop.
values.Infrastructure · Wastewater: 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: the facilities with their own federal permit to discharge wastewater in each municipality, the public sewage treatment plants and the major dischargers among them, and those with a violation on record (EPA ECHO).
values.Infrastructure · Air pollution sources: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: the facilities the Clean Air Act regulates for air pollution in each municipality, and the major sources among them (EPA ECHO).
values.Infrastructure · Hazardous waste: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: the handlers of hazardous waste in each municipality, and the large quantity generators among them (EPA ECHO).
values.Infrastructure · Environmental enforceme: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: the regulated facilities of each municipality that were inspected, and those that received a formal enforcement action, in the last five years (EPA ECHO).
values.Infrastructure · Toxic chemical releases: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: the pounds of listed toxic chemicals released by the facilities of each municipality that report to the Toxics Release Inventory, in total and to the air (EPA).
values.Infrastructure · Drinking water: 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: community water systems serving each municipality, those with a health-based violation, those that are an enforcement priority, those outside PRASA (non-PRASA) and the residents those serve (EPA ECHO).
values.Infrastructure · Power plants: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year: operating power plants, generating capacity and renewable generating capacity of each municipality (EIA-860M).
values.Infrastructure · Bridges: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value a year from 2016: highway bridges, bridges in poor condition and their share (FHWA National Bridge Inventory).
values.Infrastructure · Airports and ferries: 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value a year: air passengers boarding and commercial flights departing from 2014 (BTS T-100), air passengers boarding by FAA's count from 2023, and ferry passengers boarding in 2019, 2022 and 2024 (BTS ferry census).
values.Infrastructure · Street connectivity: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10 (Census TIGER/Line 2026): street intersections and intersections per square mile of land. Also by barrio.
values.Public safety: 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10: Type I crimes reported to the Police, violent crimes, property crimes and murders, by calendar year from 2017.
values.Infrastructure · Emergency services: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot each: fire and EMS stations (USGS National Structures Dataset) and police stations (OpenStreetMap).
values.Infrastructure · Broadband (FCC): 6 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from the FCC Broadband Data Collection (the release as of June 30 of each year 2023-2026): broadband serviceable locations, the shares served at 100/20 Mbps or more, underserved and unserved in NTIA's BEAD terms, the locations below 100/20, and the share where fiber is available; also by barrio.
values.Health care · Health centers: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the permanent sites and the mobile vans of the health centers that hold a federal grant or a look-alike status, as HRSA lists them.
values.Health care · Primary care shortage area: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the primary care physicians still needed (full-time equivalents), the share of that need met and HRSA's priority score, for each municipality with an area shortage designation.
values.Health care · Dental shortage areas: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the dentists still needed (full-time equivalents), the share of that need met and HRSA's priority score, for each municipality with an area shortage designation.
values.Health care · Mental health shortage are: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): the psychiatrists still needed (full-time equivalents), the share of that need met and HRSA's priority score, for each municipality with an area shortage designation.
values.Health care · Hospitals and care facilit: 6 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): Medicare-certified hospitals, hospitals with an emergency department, dialysis facilities, nursing homes, home health agencies and hospice providers in each municipality (CMS Provider Data Catalog).
values.Health care · Distance to a health cente: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026), estimated by the observatory: the average road distance and drive time from where residents live to the nearest health center site, and the share of residents within 10 km by road.
values.Health care · Medicare: 3 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value a year from 2013 (CMS Medicare Monthly Enrollment): people enrolled in Medicare, the share in Medicare Advantage and the share entitled by disability.
values.Health · Treatment facilities (SAMHSA): 4 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, for 2024 (SAMHSA's 2025 National Directories): substance use and mental health treatment facilities in all and by type of care, counts only.
values.Health care · Distance to a general hosp: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10: the observatory's estimate of the drive time and road distance from where people live to the nearest general hospital with an emergency department (CMS list, OpenStreetMap roads). Also by barrio.
values.Education · Public schools: 5 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value for each school year from 2010-11 (NCES Common Core of Data, through the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal): public schools open, their students, their teachers (full-time equivalents), students per teacher and schools closed since the year before.
values.Education · Colleges and universities: 2 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, one value for each year from 2010 (NCES IPEDS, through the Urban Institute's Education Data Portal): colleges, universities and other postsecondary institutions, and their students in the fall.
values.Education · Libraries: 1 dataset in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot: public libraries registered in the E-Rate program (USAC).
values.Education · Historic places: 1 dataset in Snapshot 2026-10, one snapshot (NPS edits up to 2026-08-07): places on the National Register of Historic Places (National Park Service).
values.Vulnerability (WCRP) · Original 2022 (AC: 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single period and for barrios only (no municipio has a value): the overall index and the six area indices of the WCRP Risk and Vulnerability Indicators as published in 2022 by Hunter College for FPR. In review.
values.Vulnerability (WCRP) · Updated 2020–2024: 7 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single period and for barrios only (no municipio has a value): the same indices updated by the observatory with the WCRP method on ACS 2020–2024 and current local conditions (Updated 2020–2024). In review.
values.Tourism supply: 18 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, each for a single year (2026): five counts of tourism places by kind, then the places in a flood hazard area (as a count and as a share), the places inside a protected area, the places with a website, and nine shares of the places near transit: within 400 m of any mapped stop, of a stop with a current timetable, of a frequent stop and of a stop with Saturday or Sunday service, within a 400 m or 800 m walk, and near only an expired or unscheduled stop.
values.Infrastructure · Traffic (FHWA HPMS): 6 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, data year 2025 of FHWA's Highway Performance Monitoring System: daily vehicle-kilometres, per resident, km of arterials and major collectors, the busiest count, trucks and main roads with rough pavement.
values.Infrastructure · Road safety (NHTSA FARS: 6 datasets in Snapshot 2026-10, from NHTSA's Fatality Analysis Reporting System: people killed, fatal crashes, pedestrians and bicyclists killed and motorcyclists killed each year from 2020, and deaths per 100,000 residents and per 100 million vehicle-km over five years. Counts only.
values.Infrastructure · Energy (LUMA): 4 datasets: home and business batteries, their storage in MWh, electricity sales and the share of customers with smart meters, by municipio (LUMA's monthly metrics filed with the Energy Bureau).
values.Infrastructure · Energy (ACS): 2 datasets: the households paying $250 or more a month for electricity, as a share and a count, by municipio and barrio (ACS 5-year B25132, with margins of error).

entries.plain_es: La lista de conjuntos de datos de la pestaña Análisis muestra todos los conjuntos por grupos. Escriba en el buscador para encontrar uno y oprima "Sombrear" o "Símbolos" para ponerlo en el mapa, o el botón de información para leer su definición y sus fuentes.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: lista y búsqueda de conjuntos de datos
entries.how_to_read_es: El grupo es la agrupación propia de la pestaña. No es la agrupación del diccionario.

entries.name: Analysis tab: inflation-adjusted dollars
entries.plain: The 'Inflation-adjusted' box on a dollar layer restates every year's dollars in the dollars of the latest index year (2025 in Snapshot 2026-10), so years can be compared. It uses the US consumer price index, because the observatory holds no price index for Puerto Rico.
entries.definition: The box appears on layers whose unit is dollars. It multiplies each year's value by the index of the latest index year (2025) divided by the index of that year. The index is the annual average of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), US city average (1982-84 = 100), which runs from 172.2 in 2000 to 321.943 in 2025 in Snapshot 2026-10. Years before 2010, such as the 2001 to 2009 declaration years of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) datasets, use the index of their own year. For a year outside 2000–2025 the nearest year is used. The legend and the layer title then say '2025 dollars'. The margin of error shown in the inspector is multiplied the same way. With 'Change since the base year', both ends are adjusted. 'Show as' options that divide dollars, such as per resident, work on the adjusted numbers.

coverage.frequency: One index value per year. The latest year of the index sets the reference year.

entries.method: economy.js (cpiFactor, ecCalc). The index values come from the deflator list in the economy file.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to compare a dollar amount across years. It does not change a single year's map. Example: $1,000 in 2015 becomes about $1,358 in 2025 dollars, because 321.943 divided by 237.017 is 1.358. For another worked example see the entry on the inflation adjustment.
caveats: The US index only approximates the prices Puerto Rico residents pay. The page says so.
The tab's note says American Community Survey (ACS) dollars are already in the final year of each five-year window. The adjustment treats that final year as the year of the value.
Dollar amounts as published (not adjusted) are in the dollars of their own year.

view.label: 2D map: average pay, 2015, in 2025 dollars

entries.source_detail: economy_series.json, deflator list (CPI-U annual averages 2000 to 2025). The map draws no credit line for this layer.
entries.plain_es: La casilla "Ajustado por inflación" de una capa en dólares expresa los dólares de cada año en dólares del año índice más reciente (2025 en el corte de datos de 2026-10), para poder comparar los años. Usa el índice de precios al consumidor de Estados Unidos, porque el observatorio no tiene un índice de precios para Puerto Rico.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: dólares ajustados por inflación
entries.how_to_read_es: Úsela para comparar un monto en dólares entre años. No cambia el mapa de un solo año. Ejemplo: $1,000 de 2015 equivalen a unos $1,358 en dólares de 2025, porque 321.943 dividido entre 237.017 es 1.358. Para otro ejemplo resuelto, vea la ficha sobre el ajuste por inflación.

entries.name: Analysis tab: ready-made views
entries.plain: 'Start from a view' offers six ready-made combinations of layers. One click replaces the layers on the map with that set and shows a short message.
entries.definition: The six views are listed below with the layers each sets. A view replaces all economy layers with its own, each at its start settings (classes of equal counts, 'Same classes in every year' on). It also sets the other map layers, so that the view is not buried under pins. It keeps on only the layer it names (tourism places or transit routes). It turns off tourism places, transit routes, transit stops, barrios, flood zones, protected areas and land use otherwise. The municipality outlines stay as they are. The year and the base year do not change.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecRenderPresets, ecSetContext).
entries.how_to_read: Use a view as a starting point, then open each layer's settings to adjust it.
caveats: A view is a combination of layers. It is not a finding.
The Public money view shows federal amounts obligated (committed). They are not money paid, damage or need. See the codes below.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab, 'Poverty and unemployment' set by hand

values.Jobs and pay: Shaded: average pay (qcew_avg_pay). Symbols: jobs (qcew_jobs). No extra layers.
values.Poverty and unemployment: Two shaded layers, so a bivariate map: poverty rate (poverty_pct) and unemployment rate (laus_unemp_rate). Symbols: unemployed residents (laus_unemployed).
values.Job centres and commuting: Two shaded layers, so a bivariate map: jobs per employed resident (jobs_per_employed_resident) and commuters with 45 minutes or more (commute_45plus_pct). Symbols: jobs (qcew_jobs). Also shows transit routes.
values.Public money: Shaded: federal awards per resident (fed_awards_total, 'perCapita'). Symbols: Public Assistance of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), amounts obligated (fema_pa_obligated). These are federal amounts obligated (committed). They are not money paid, not damage and not need. In the 2026-10 snapshot, over all years combined, 77.9% of FEMA Public Assistance money is recorded as statewide and is not in the municipality values (80.9% for the 2017 declarations, 13.1% for 2024, the year this view shows on Latest). Awards that serve the whole island are often booked to the capital.
values.Government and self-employment: Two shaded layers, so a bivariate map: government jobs as a share of all jobs (gov_job_share_pct) and self-employed workers (self_employed_pct).
values.Tourism economy: Shaded: tourism jobs as a share of the municipality's jobs (tourism_jobs, 'shareJobs'). Symbols: accommodation jobs (accommodation_jobs). Also shows the tourism places pins.

entries.plain_es: "Empezar con una vista" ofrece seis combinaciones de capas ya preparadas. Un clic reemplaza las capas del mapa por ese conjunto y muestra un mensaje breve.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: vistas preparadas
entries.how_to_read_es: Use una vista como punto de partida y luego abra los ajustes de cada capa para modificarla.

entries.name: Analysis tab: shaded layers
entries.plain: A shaded layer colours each municipality by one dataset. The Analysis tab allows two shaded layers at a time. Colours run from light to dark in five groups.
entries.definition: A third shaded layer is refused with a message that says to remove one or to show the new dataset as symbols. Open 'Settings' on a layer's card to change its options. The class limits are set from the values of the 78 municipalities, not from the Puerto Rico figure. With 'Same classes in every year' on, which is the start setting, the limits use the values of all years together, so one colour means the same number in every year. Turn it off to use only the year on screen. The legend lists the range of each class and how many municipalities fall in it. A municipality with no value is grey (#EDEDED), and the legend counts it as 'No data'. The settings are listed below.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecAdd, ecBreaks, ecClass, ecRenderMap, ecRenderLegend). Natural breaks use the Jenks method, which groups values to keep each class as uniform as possible. When more than 1,500 values are pooled, every n-th value is used. The sheet is a copy of the municipality outlines in its own map pane.
entries.how_to_read: With 'Same classes in every year' on (the start setting) a colour is a class among all municipalities in all years pooled, so one year can have uneven group sizes. Read the legend counts for the numbers. On the diverging scale red means below the centre (below Puerto Rico, or below zero change) and blue means above. Neither means better or worse: a red unemployment rate is a lower rate.
caveats: With 'Same classes in every year' on, some colours may not appear in a year whose values cover a narrower range.
Equal intervals can put most municipalities in one class when one or two are very large.
Shading rates and levels suits comparison between places. Shading a raw count mostly shows how big the municipality is.

view.label: 2D map: shaded poverty rate, 2022

values.Show as: Described in the entry on the 'Show as' options.
values.Classes: Quantiles with equal counts, Equal intervals or Natural breaks.
values.Colours: Blue, Green, Gold, Red or Gray. Each ramp has five colours.
values.Opacity: From 20% to 100%. It starts at 85%. The opacity of the first shaded layer sets the opacity of the sheet.
values.Same classes in every year: A checkbox, on at the start.
values.Diverging scale: Options that compare with a centre (index, difference, location quotient and change) use a diverging scale of five classes: dark red, light red, pale grey, light blue and dark blue. The limits are set as shares of the largest distance from the centre: below −50%, −50% to −10%, within ±10%, +10% to +50% and above +50%. Red means below the centre and blue means above. Neither means worse or better.
values.Layer card buttons: Hide, move up or down, open information and remove the layer.

entries.source_detail: economy_series.json and housing_series.json. Each dataset's source reference is in its information window. The map draws no credit line for this layer.
entries.plain_es: Una capa sombreada colorea cada municipio según un conjunto de datos. La pestaña Análisis permite dos capas sombreadas a la vez. Los colores van de claro a oscuro en cinco grupos.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: capas sombreadas
entries.how_to_read_es: Con 'Mismas clases en todos los años' activado (el ajuste inicial), un color es una clase calculada con todos los municipios de todos los años juntos, así que en un año los grupos pueden tener tamaños desiguales. Lea los conteos de la leyenda para ver las cifras. En la escala divergente, el rojo significa por debajo del centro (por debajo de Puerto Rico o por debajo de un cambio de cero) y el azul significa por encima. Ninguno de los dos significa mejor o peor: una tasa de desempleo en rojo es una tasa más baja.

entries.name: Analysis tab: sized symbols
entries.plain: A symbol layer draws a circle on each municipality. The circle's area shows the value, so big circles are big amounts. Symbols suit counts and totals such as jobs or dollars.
entries.definition: Each circle is centred on the municipality's centre. The circle for the largest value has a radius of 30 pixels (20 on a phone). Other radii shrink with the square root of the value, so the area is proportional to the value, down to a minimum of 2.5 pixels. Larger circles are drawn first so small ones stay visible. The largest value is taken over all years when 'Same classes in every year' is on, and over the year on screen otherwise. Colours: Red, Blue, Gold, Green or Charcoal. If a dataset can be negative, for example a change since the base year, increases are blue and decreases red. The legend shows three circles at the largest value, at half of it and at a tenth of it. No circle is drawn for Puerto Rico as a whole or for a municipality with no value. The centre is the area-weighted centre of the municipality's largest part, so islands do not pull the point into the sea.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecRenderMap, ecRenderLegend). Circles are Leaflet circle markers in their own map pane. They do not take clicks.
entries.how_to_read: Compare circle sizes between municipalities in the same layer. Do not compare sizes between two different layers.
caveats: The centre of a long or crescent-shaped municipality can fall away from its towns.
Circles overlap in the San Juan area and may hide each other.

view.label: 2D map: jobs as symbols, 2024

entries.source_detail: economy_series.json and housing_series.json. Each dataset's source reference is in its information window. The map draws no credit line for this layer.
entries.plain_es: Una capa de símbolos dibuja un círculo en cada municipio. El área del círculo muestra el valor, así que los círculos grandes son cantidades grandes. Los símbolos sirven para conteos y totales, como empleos o dólares.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: símbolos de tamaño variable
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare el tamaño de los círculos entre municipios de una misma capa. No compare tamaños entre dos capas distintas.

entries.name: Analysis tab: the 'Show as' options
entries.plain: Each layer has a 'Show as' menu. It changes the number behind the colour or circle. Choices include as published, per resident, per km², share, index, change and percentile.
entries.definition: The options depend on the kind of dataset. Counts (people, jobs, places) can be shown as published, per 1,000 residents, per km² and as a share of the Puerto Rico total. The jobs datasets (25 in Snapshot 2026-10) can also be shown as a share of the municipality's jobs and as a location quotient. Dollar totals (wages, federal money, recovery money of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, FEMA) can be shown as published, per resident, per km² and, except for federal loans, as a share of the Puerto Rico total. Everything else (rates, ratios and dollar levels such as median income) can be shown as published, as an index or as a difference from Puerto Rico. Every dataset with more than one year also offers 'change since the base year', and every dataset offers 'percentile among municipalities'. The codes below are the ones written in a shared link.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecNormOptions, ecOut, ecCalc). Land area is the land_km2 field of municipalities.json. Population is the population series. Jobs are the jobs series of the Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages (QCEW).
entries.how_to_read: Choose the option that answers your question. 'Per 1,000 residents' compares places of different size. 'Index' and 'difference' compare with the island.
caveats: 'Per 1,000 residents' divides by residents, not by workers. Jobs are counted at the workplace, so places that draw commuters show high values.
A location quotient above 1 says an industry is concentrated. It does not say the industry is large.

For the five tourism-place counts the Analysis tab divides by the latest population estimate (2025 in Snapshot 2026-10), but the Map layers tab, the Rankings tab and the municipality table divide by the 2020 Census count. The two views can differ (San Juan: 10.4 and 10.0 places per 1,000 residents in Snapshot 2026-10).

view.label: 2D map: tourism jobs as a share of all jobs, 2024

values.value: As published. The dataset's own number in its own unit. Offered for every dataset. The start choice for symbols and for rates, ratios and dollar levels.
values.per1000: Per 1,000 residents. The count divided by the municipality's population, times 1,000, rounded to three decimals. Counts only. The start choice when a count is shaded. Population is the value of the population series for the year shown, or for the latest earlier year, or for its first year when the year shown is earlier. The population series changes basis in 2020 (the 2011-2019 estimates were not revised to the 2020 Census), so in Snapshot 2026-10 the island's population steps up 2.9% from 2019 to 2020 (3.1% for the median municipality), and per-resident values drop by about 3% for that reason alone. Changes that cross 2019 to 2020 include the same jump.
values.perkm2: Per km². The value divided by the municipality's land area in square kilometres. Counts and dollar totals.
values.sharePR: % of the Puerto Rico total. The value divided by the dataset's Puerto Rico figure, times 100. Counts and dollar totals. It is not offered for federal loans. Shares can add up to less than 100% when the island figure holds amounts that belong to no municipality, for example FEMA Public Assistance recorded as statewide, federal awards that name no municipality, or jobs hidden in withheld cells.
values.shareJobs: % of the municipality's jobs. Jobs in an industry divided by all jobs in the same municipality (QCEW), times 100. Only the jobs datasets (25 in Snapshot 2026-10), from 2014.
values.lq: Location quotient (Puerto Rico = 1). The industry's share of the municipality's jobs divided by its share of Puerto Rico's jobs. Above 1 means the industry is more concentrated here than on the island as a whole. Only the jobs datasets. Diverging scale centred on 1.
values.perCapita: $ per resident. The dollar total divided by the municipality's population. Dollar totals only. The start choice when a dollar total is shaded. The same break in the population series in 2020 applies. For FEMA Public Assistance and for federal awards the Puerto Rico per-resident value includes money recorded as statewide or naming no municipality, so it is not comparable with a municipality's value.
values.index: Index (Puerto Rico = 100). The value divided by the Puerto Rico value, times 100. Rates, ratios and dollar levels. Diverging scale centred on 100.
values.diff: Difference from Puerto Rico. The value minus the Puerto Rico value, in the dataset's unit (percentage points for percentages). Rates, ratios and dollar levels. Diverging scale centred on 0.
values.change: Change since the base year. For rates and ratios, the value minus the value in the base year (points for percentages). For counts and dollars, the percent change from the base year, blank where the base value is 0. The base year is chosen in 'Change measured from' (2014 at the start). The dataset's latest year at or before it is used. Blank for years up to the base year. Not offered for the five tourism snapshots. Diverging scale centred on 0. Windows of the American Community Survey (ACS) that overlap share most of their sample, so choose a base year at least five years before the year shown.
values.pctile: Percentile among municipalities. The place of the municipality among the 78 when they are sorted from the lowest value (0) to the highest (100). Municipalities with equal values share the lowest of their places. Puerto Rico as a whole has none.

entries.source_detail: economy_series.json and housing_series.json for the datasets, with land area and the tourism counts from municipalities.json. The map draws no credit line for this layer.
entries.plain_es: Cada capa tiene un menú "Mostrar como". Cambia el número que hay detrás del color o del círculo. Las opciones incluyen tal como se publicó, por residente, por km², proporción, índice, cambio y percentil.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: las opciones de 'Mostrar como'
entries.how_to_read_es: Elija la opción que responde a su pregunta. 'Por cada 1,000 residentes' compara lugares de distinto tamaño. 'Índice' y 'diferencia' comparan con la isla.

entries.name: Analysis tab: two shaded layers together (bivariate map)
entries.plain: When two shaded layers are on, the map shows both at once with nine colours. Each layer is cut into three classes: low, middle and high.
entries.definition: The first visible shaded layer in the list is the horizontal axis of the legend, which increases to the right. The second is the vertical axis, which increases upward. Each layer is cut into three classes, using the class method set on its card: equal counts (terciles), equal intervals or natural breaks. The nine colours run from light grey (low on both), through teal (high on the first only) and magenta (high on the second only), to dark blue (high on both). The legend shows the three-by-three grid and, for each axis, the layer, its year, and the limits of 'low' and 'high'. The legend title says 'terciles of each' only when both layers use equal-count classes. Otherwise it says 'three classes of each'. A municipality with no value in either layer is grey (#EDEDED). In this mode the diverging scale is not used: every layer is cut into three classes.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecRenderMap, ecRenderLegend, EC_BIV). The colour table is indexed by the class of the second layer and then by the class of the first.
entries.how_to_read: Find the dark cells (both high) and the pale ones (both low). Colours that mix show where the two layers disagree.
caveats: The map shows where two things are high or low together. It does not show that one causes the other.
The three classes are relative to the 78 municipalities (all years pooled when 'Same classes in every year' is on). They are not thresholds of any standard.
The two layers may show different years. The legend names each layer's year, so read it before you compare.

view.label: 2D map: poverty rate and unemployment rate together, 2022

entries.source_detail: economy_series.json and housing_series.json. Each dataset's source reference is in its information window. The map draws no credit line for this layer.
entries.plain_es: Cuando hay dos capas sombreadas activadas, el mapa muestra ambas a la vez con nueve colores. Cada capa se divide en tres clases: baja, media y alta.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: dos capas sombreadas juntas (mapa bivariado)
entries.how_to_read_es: Busque las celdas oscuras (ambas altas) y las pálidas (ambas bajas). Los colores mezclados muestran dónde las dos capas no coinciden.

entries.name: Analysis tab: year control, Play and base year
entries.plain: One year control moves every layer on the Analysis tab. Choose 'Latest' or a year (2010 to 2025 in Snapshot 2026-10), step with the arrows, drag the slider or press Play to watch the years go by.
entries.definition: In Snapshot 2026-10 the year list has 'Latest' and then 2025 down to 2010. 'Latest' shows each dataset's own last year. A chosen year is used by every layer. A dataset with no value for that year shows its latest earlier year, and the layer says '2022 (latest at or before 2023)'. If the year is earlier than the dataset starts, the layer shows its first year and says 'first data 2014'. Snapshot datasets always say 'snapshot 2026'. Play starts at 2010 (or at the chosen year) and moves one year every 1.4 seconds up to the last year (2025), then stops. Choosing a year by hand stops Play. 'Change measured from' lists every year before the last one (2010 to 2024 in Snapshot 2026-10) and starts at 2014. It sets the base of the 'change since the base year' option only. The year and the base are kept in a shared link (ey and eb).

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecInitYear, ecResolve, ecChip). The years offered are all years from 2010 on that any yearly dataset holds.
entries.how_to_read: Check each layer's year chip before comparing two layers. Layers can show different years under one control.
caveats: In Snapshot 2026-10, 'Latest' and '2025' are not the same: survey datasets end in 2024, so choosing 2025 shows their 2024 value with a note.
American Community Survey (ACS) years are five-year windows labelled by their last year, so neighbouring years share most of their sample. Compare windows that do not overlap for real change.

On Latest, a pair of layers can come from different years (in Snapshot 2026-10, jobs 2025 and ACS 2024). Check each year chip before you compare two layers, read them as a pair or correlate them. In Snapshot 2026-10 the unemployment rate has no 2020 value, so choosing 2020 shows 2019.

view.label: 2D map: unemployment rate in 2020

entries.plain_es: Un solo control de año mueve todas las capas de la pestaña Análisis. Elija "Último" o un año (de 2010 a 2025 en el corte de datos de 2026-10), avance con las flechas, arrastre el control deslizante u oprima "Reproducir" para ver pasar los años.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Análisis: control del año, Reproducir y año base
entries.how_to_read_es: Revise la etiqueta del año de cada capa antes de comparar dos capas. Las capas pueden mostrar años distintos bajo un mismo control.

entries.name: Economy workbench: panel and Inspector tab
entries.plain: The Workbench is a panel at the bottom of the screen that opens from the Analysis tab. It has ten tabs: Inspector, Table, Scatter, Trend, Correlations, Small multiples, Compare two maps, Composite, Scenarios and Study areas. All of them follow the layers, the year and the settings on the map.
entries.definition: The 'Workbench' button opens the panel beside the side panel, and the button or the × closes it. The panel's header shows the year, or 'Latest year'. Inspector tab: pick a place from the menu, Puerto Rico as a whole included, or click the map. The table gives each visible layer's value for the place, the Puerto Rico value and a trend line with its length under it (see the entry on trend lines). The other tabs are described in their own entries. It also opens from the link 'Open in the workbench' on a municipality card, from 'View the map as a table' at the foot of the map's legend (the Table tab, so every map can be read as a table) and from buttons in the chat.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchOpen, ecRenderBench, ecBenchInspect; the views of plan item 12: ecBenchMatrix, ecBenchMultiples, ecBenchSwipe, ecBenchComposite; docs/workbench.md).
entries.how_to_read: Use the Inspector to answer 'what do all my layers say about this place?'.
caveats: A layer that is hidden (eye closed) does not appear in the workbench.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench)

entries.plain_es: La "Mesa de trabajo" es un panel en la parte inferior de la pantalla que se abre desde la pestaña Análisis. Tiene diez pestañas: "Inspector", "Tabla", "Dispersión", "Tendencia", "Correlaciones", "Mapas pequeños", "Comparar dos mapas", "Índice compuesto", "Escenarios" y "Áreas de estudio". Todas siguen las capas, el año y los ajustes del mapa.
entries.name_es: Mesa de trabajo de Economía: panel y pestaña Inspector
entries.how_to_read_es: Use el Inspector para responder '¿qué dicen todas mis capas sobre este lugar?'.

entries.name: Economy workbench: Scatter tab
entries.plain: The Scatter tab plots one visible layer against another, one dot for each municipality, and gives the correlation between them. It needs two visible layers.
entries.definition: Pick the X and Y layers. Each dot is a municipality, and a click on a dot selects it on the map. 'Log scales' draws both axes on a logarithmic scale and keeps only dots where both values are above zero. 'Size by population' scales each dot by the population of the X layer's year. The note above the chart gives the number of municipalities and the correlation coefficient r. A dashed line shows the straight line of best fit (least squares), drawn only when log scales are off. Axis limits are set from the data with a small margin.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchScatter). r is the Pearson correlation of the plotted values. It is calculated on the values themselves, not on their logarithms, even when log scales are on. The chart is drawn with Chart.js.
entries.how_to_read: r runs from −1 to 1. Near 0 means little straight-line relationship. Near ±1 means the dots follow a line closely. The two layers can show different years, so check the chips in the axis titles. With log scales on, the dots look straighter but r still measures the straight-line fit of the raw values, and the fitted line is hidden.
caveats: A correlation across places is not cause and effect. Large places, small samples and survey noise can drive it.
The page says this in the note above the chart.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Scatter)

entries.plain_es: La pestaña "Dispersión" grafica una capa visible contra otra, con un punto por municipio, y da la correlación entre ambas. Necesita dos capas visibles.
entries.name_es: Mesa de trabajo de Economía: pestaña Dispersión
entries.how_to_read_es: r va de −1 a 1. Cerca de 0 significa poca relación lineal. Cerca de ±1 significa que los puntos siguen de cerca una línea. Las dos capas pueden mostrar años distintos, así que revise las etiquetas de año en los títulos de los ejes. Con las escalas logarítmicas activadas, los puntos se ven más alineados, pero r sigue midiendo el ajuste lineal de los valores sin transformar, y la línea ajustada se oculta.

entries.name: Economy workbench: Table tab
entries.plain: The Table tab lists the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico with one column for each visible layer. Sort by any column, find a municipality by name and download the table as a comma-separated values (CSV) file.
entries.definition: Puerto Rico is the first row. Municipalities follow in alphabetical order, in Spanish collation, until you sort by a column. A click on a column title sorts by it, and a second click reverses the order. A box finds municipalities by name. Each column title gives the dataset, its year and, when it is not 'as published', how it is shown. Values are shown rounded as the layer shows them. The button 'Download CSV' saves pr_economy_layers.csv. Its columns are GEOID (the geographic identifier code of the Census Bureau), Municipality and one column for each visible layer, named '<dataset> (<year note>; <show-as code>)'. The file has 79 rows, the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico, in the order of the data file whatever the sort on screen. Values in the file are not rounded for display.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchTable, ecSaveCsv).
entries.how_to_read: Use the table to look up exact values. Use the CSV to analyse them.
caveats: The CSV holds the values as currently shown, after any 'Show as' option or inflation adjustment. The file does not repeat the margins of error.
Download all years of one dataset, with margins, from its information dialog.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Table)

entries.plain_es: La pestaña "Tabla" enumera los 78 municipios y Puerto Rico, con una columna por cada capa visible. Ordene por cualquier columna, busque un municipio por su nombre y descargue la tabla como archivo CSV (valores separados por comas).
entries.name_es: Mesa de trabajo de Economía: pestaña Tabla
entries.how_to_read_es: Use la tabla para consultar valores exactos. Use el CSV para analizarlos.

entries.name: Economy workbench: Trend tab
entries.plain: The Trend tab draws one line for each chosen place over the years, for one visible layer. Add places, hide lines by clicking their names, and compare each place with Puerto Rico.
entries.definition: Pick a layer (datasets with only one year are not listed) and add places from the menu. The lines follow the layer's settings, such as per 1,000 residents or change since the base year. Years run from 2010 (datasets of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, FEMA, also show earlier years). The Puerto Rico line is thicker. A click on a name in the legend hides or shows that line. 'Reset places' keeps Puerto Rico and the selected municipality. Clicking municipalities on the map adds them. The chart shows up to eight places.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchTrend). Places are kept as a set. The chart draws up to eight of them: Puerto Rico first, then the municipalities in the order of the municipality list. Puerto Rico is never the one left out.
entries.how_to_read: Compare slopes between places. Check the unit on the vertical axis.
caveats: With more than eight places chosen, the municipalities that come last in the list drop out of the chart without a message. Puerto Rico always stays.

The horizontal axis lists only the years the dataset holds, evenly spaced. In Snapshot 2026-10, a missing year (the unemployment rate has no 2020) or uneven years (FEMA Public Assistance holds 12 declaration years from 2001 to 2024) do not show as gaps, so time can look compressed. The vertical axis is fitted to the data and need not start at zero, so slopes look steeper than the percentage change. A municipality with no value in a listed year is bridged by a straight line.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Trend)

entries.plain_es: La pestaña "Tendencia" dibuja una línea por cada lugar elegido a lo largo de los años, para una capa visible. Agregue lugares, oculte líneas con un clic en sus nombres y compare cada lugar con Puerto Rico.
entries.name_es: Mesa de trabajo de Economía: pestaña Tendencia
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare las pendientes entre lugares. Revise la unidad del eje vertical.

entries.name: Shading the Analysis tab's map by barrio
entries.plain: A shaded layer of the Analysis tab can be drawn on the 901 barrios instead of the 78 municipalities, for the datasets that have values for barrios: the American Community Survey estimates (population, housing, income, age and the others of acs_barrio.json). Datasets published only by municipality, such as jobs and wages, have no barrio values and keep the municipal map.
entries.definition: In the Analysis tab, Settings of a shaded layer, Area: Municipalities or Barrios. The choice is offered when the dataset is in acs_barrio.json (the data dictionary lists the barrio level for it) and the layer is the only shaded one; symbols and two shaded layers together stay municipal. The barrio values are the American Community Survey 5-year estimates for the 901 Census county subdivisions, with their margins of error: a barrio whose margin is above 30% of its estimate is hatched, as on the municipal map. A value is shown as published or as a percentile among the barrios; the rescalings that need a municipio's residents or land (per 1,000 residents, per km², share of Puerto Rico) fall back to the published value, and the legend says so. Hovering a barrio shows its name, municipality, value and margin of error. The link keeps the choice (mode code b). The workbench views, the table and the click pop-ups stay municipal.

coverage.frequency: The survey windows of acs_barrio.json.

entries.method: js/econ_level.js, loaded the first time a layer asks for it, reads the engine's contract for the layer at the barrio level (E.series with level 'barrio', from acs_barrio.json via economy.js ecLoadLevel), cuts five classes from the barrio values with the layer's own method (quantiles, equal intervals, natural breaks or own limits) and colours barrios.geojson by them.
entries.source_detail: acs_barrio.json (American Community Survey 5-year estimates for county subdivisions); barrios.geojson (Census TIGERweb county subdivisions).
entries.how_to_read: Small areas have wide margins: in the 2020-2024 window, 387 of the 901 barrios have a less reliable median household income and 112 have none. Read the hatching before comparing two barrios, and use the CSV by area for the exact margins.
caveats: Only datasets with barrio values in the files: municipal-only datasets are not split among barrios, because no source gives their barrio values and the observatory does not estimate them.
Barrios are Census county subdivisions; their boundaries are those of 2020.

view.label: Map, Analysis tab: a shaded layer, Settings, Area

entries.plain_es: Una capa sombreada de la pestaña Análisis puede dibujarse sobre los 901 barrios en vez de los 78 municipios, para los conjuntos de datos que tienen valores por barrio: los estimados de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad (población, vivienda, ingreso, edad y los demás de acs_barrio.json). Los datos que solo se publican por municipio, como los empleos y los salarios, no tienen valores por barrio y mantienen el mapa municipal.

entries.name: Trend lines (sparklines) and their length label
entries.plain: A small grey line with a blue dot shows how a value changed over the years for one municipality. The label under it says how many years the line covers, for example '12 yrs'.
entries.definition: The blue dot marks the year on screen. The label under the line gives the length of the trend: 'N yrs' ('yrs' means years) is the number of calendar years from the first to the last year drawn, both included. If some years have no value, the label adds how many values were drawn, for example '12 yrs, 9 values'. On the Analysis tab the label also gives the first and last year, for example '12 yrs · 2014–25'. The column header of the lines in the workbench's Inspector tab (the map popup has no trend lines) reads 'Trend', with the note 'years shown; dot = chosen year'. The label itself starts with the number of years. The Housing profile has no header. A line needs at least two yearly values, so datasets with one year have none. The line scales from the lowest to the highest value drawn, so a flat-looking line can hold a large change. Economy lines start in 2010 at the earliest. Housing profile lines use every year the dataset has.

coverage.frequency: Series are rebuilt with each snapshot. In Snapshot 2026-10 the year control runs from 2010 to 2025.

entries.method: economy.js (ecSpark) and housing.js (spark) draw the same small chart. The label is calculated from the years of the values drawn.
entries.how_to_read: Compare the shape and the length, not the height. Two lines of different datasets are each drawn to fill the same small space.
caveats: Survey series (American Community Survey, ACS) use overlapping five-year windows, so their lines are smoother than the real change.
A series with a break, such as the population series that steps up in 2020, shows the break as a jump.
For survey series the length counts window labels. Each label is a five-year window, so the line covers more time than the label says.
The Economy line follows the layer's 'Show as' and inflation settings. The Housing line shows values as published.

view.label: Housing page: municipality profile with trend lines

entries.source_detail: economy_series.json and housing_series.json (the series drawn). The small chart carries no credit line.
entries.plain_es: Una pequeña línea gris con un punto azul muestra cómo cambió un valor a lo largo de los años en un municipio. La etiqueta debajo indica cuántos años abarca la línea, por ejemplo "12 años".
entries.name_es: Líneas de tendencia (minigráficos) y su etiqueta de duración
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare la forma y la duración, no la altura. Dos líneas de conjuntos de datos distintos se dibujan cada una para llenar el mismo espacio pequeño.

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser from the datasets of the Analysis tab, each time the view is drawn

entries.name: Workbench: Compare two maps tab (swipe)
entries.plain: Two layers on one map of Puerto Rico with a divider you can drag: the left side shows one layer and the right side the other.
entries.definition: Pick the left and the right layer among the visible layers. The slider moves the divider across the island; each side keeps its own classes and has its own legend below the map. Hovering a municipality gives both values. The slider works with the keyboard (arrow keys).
entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchSwipe): one SVG with the second layer clipped at the divider.
entries.how_to_read: Move the divider slowly over a region to see whether the two layers are high in the same places.
caveats: The two sides have different classes: a dark colour on each side means high for that layer, not the same number.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Compare two maps)

entries.plain_es: Dos capas en un mismo mapa de Puerto Rico con una división que se puede arrastrar: el lado izquierdo muestra una capa y el derecho la otra.

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser from the datasets of the Analysis tab, each time the view is drawn

entries.name: Workbench: Correlations tab (correlation matrix)
entries.plain: A table of the correlation between every pair of visible layers, so you can see at a glance which ones move together across the municipalities.
entries.definition: Up to eight visible layers, each as it is on the map (its year, rescaling and settings). Each cell gives r and n, the number of municipalities that have a value for both layers of the pair; each pair uses its own municipalities (pairwise complete), so n can differ between cells. Pearson measures a straight-line pattern; Spearman (rank order) measures whether the ranks rise or fall together, which a few very large values do not dominate. A pair with fewer than 3 municipalities gets no r. Colours: dark red below −0.5, light red −0.5 to −0.1, grey −0.1 to 0.1, light blue 0.1 to 0.5, dark blue above 0.5.
entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchMatrix) with Core.stats.matrix and Core.stats.correlation (site/js/core/stats.js; Spearman is Pearson on the ranks, ties sharing the mean of their ranks).
entries.how_to_read: Read a cell as a pattern across places: a dark blue cell means municipalities with more of one tend to have more of the other. Check n before comparing two cells.
caveats: A correlation across places is not cause and effect, and it does not describe the people inside a place.
Large places, survey noise and a third factor can drive a correlation.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Correlations)

entries.plain_es: Una tabla con la correlación entre cada par de capas visibles, para ver de un vistazo cuáles se mueven juntas entre los municipios.

entries.name: Workbench: Scenarios tab (save, compare, model outputs)
entries.plain: Save what the map shows as a scenario, compare two scenarios figure by figure, and load the results of an outside model as a layer marked as model output, not observed data.
entries.definition: A scenario keeps the map's link (layers, year, composite, planned route), the figures it produced (the planned route's measures and Puerto Rico's value of each visible layer, with its year and settings) and any model output loaded with it. Scenarios stay in the browser (IndexedDB); 'Export' saves one as a JSON file and 'Import a scenario' reads it back after checking it. 'Open scenario' restores the view, and its model outputs, from the link. 'Compare two scenarios' lists every figure with A, B, B − A and the change in percent; when both scenarios hold a model output of the same variable, 'Map B − A' shades the difference. Names, labels and notes refuse e-mail addresses and telephone numbers: a scenario names a team or organisation, not a person's contact.

coverage.frequency: Kept in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere

entries.method: js/scenarios.js (loaded the first time the tab opens) and Core.scenario (site/js/core/scenario.js: make, check, read, diff, parseModel, diffSeries); economy.js (ecBenchScenarios, ecScenarioLib). The link part sc= reopens a scenario that holds model outputs.
entries.how_to_read: A difference between two scenarios is the difference between two views or two model runs, not a forecast.
caveats: Scenarios live in this browser only: clearing the browser's data deletes them. Export the ones to keep.
A figure saved with one year or setting is another figure from the same dataset with another year or setting.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Scenarios)

entries.plain_es: Guarde lo que muestra el mapa como un escenario, compare dos escenarios cifra por cifra y cargue los resultados de un modelo externo como una capa marcada como resultado de modelo, no datos observados.

coverage.frequency: Calculated in your browser from the datasets of the Analysis tab, each time the view is drawn

entries.name: Workbench: Small multiples tab
entries.plain: Many small maps side by side: one map for each year of a layer, or one map for each visible layer, so changes and differences show at a glance.
entries.definition: 'One map for each year of one layer' draws the chosen layer in each of its last 12 years that have values, with one set of classes for every map (worked out from all the years together), so a colour means the same in each year; the Puerto Rico value is under each map. 'One map for each visible layer' draws up to eight visible layers at the year each shows, each with its own classes, so colours are not comparable between maps. Hover a municipality for its value. The maps have no base map.
entries.method: economy.js (ecBenchMultiples, ecClassFill) with Core.minimap (site/js/core/minimap.js), which draws the 78 municipal outlines as SVG.
entries.how_to_read: In the maps by year, a municipality that darkens from map to map is rising against the same classes.
caveats: In the maps by layer each map has its own classes: compare where values are high or low, not the colours.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Small multiples)

entries.plain_es: Muchos mapas pequeños uno al lado del otro: un mapa por cada año de una capa, o un mapa por cada capa visible, para ver cambios y diferencias de un vistazo.

entries.name: Workbench: Study areas tab (your own polygons, summarised)
entries.plain: Load your own polygons, such as a neighbourhood or a service area, and see what each holds: residents, transit stops and, on request, tourism places and flood and protected land, plus every dataset of the Analysis tab estimated for each area.
entries.definition: A GeoJSON file of polygons in longitude and latitude, up to 200 areas, is read in the browser and never uploaded; only each area's name and shape are kept, with the set's name, source and description, in IndexedDB. For each area: its km², residents by Census 2020 block centroid, residents more than 800 m from a scheduled stop, scheduled transit stops and, on request, tourism places and the share of its land in a FEMA flood hazard area (zones A and V) and in a protected area. Every dataset of the Analysis tab is estimated for each area from the municipios it covers: totals by the share of each municipio's residents inside (land, for totals measured in km²), an exact sum when the area holds whole municipios; rates and levels as an average weighted by the residents inside. Each row names its method.
entries.geography: Polygons the user loads, within Puerto Rico

coverage.frequency: Kept in your browser; nothing is sent anywhere

entries.method: js/studyareas.js (loaded the first time the tab opens) and Core.study (site/js/core/study.js: parse, make, check, read, toGeoJSON, measure, estimate); economy.js (ecBenchStudy, ecStudyLib). docs/study-areas.md.
entries.how_to_read: The estimates assume a municipio is the same throughout: a small area inside one municipio gets that municipio's rate. Counted measures (residents, stops, places) are counts inside the area; the dataset rows are estimates.
caveats: Study areas live in this browser only: clearing the browser's data deletes them. Export the ones to keep.
Survey margins of error are not carried into the estimates.
Residents are placed at the centre of their census block, so a block cut by an edge counts wholly on the side of its centre.

view.label: 2D map: Analysis tab (press Workbench, then Study areas)

entries.plain_es: Cargue sus propios polígonos, como un vecindario o un área de servicio, y vea qué contiene cada uno: residentes, paradas de transporte y, si lo pide, lugares turísticos y terreno inundable o protegido, además de cada conjunto de datos de la pestaña Análisis estimado para cada área.

entries.name: 400 m walk radius switch (2D map and 3D view)
entries.plain: 'Show 400 m walk radius around stops' draws a circle of 400 metres around each stop, bus station, Tren Urbano station and ferry terminal. The circles appear only when you are zoomed in and the stops or stations layer is on.
entries.definition: 400 metres is about a quarter mile, a common planning distance for walking to a stop. It is a choice made for the observatory, not a measure of how far people walk. The rings are thin blue circles with a very light blue fill and a 400 m radius, drawn in Snapshot 2026-10 for 4,360 points (the 4,240 stops and the 120 stations and terminals, airports excluded). They show when the switch is on, the map zoom is 14 or higher, and 'Transit stops' or 'Stations, terminals & airports' is on. If only one of those two layers is on, the rings of both kinds still appear. Rings overlap where stops are close. The same distance defines 'within 400 m of any mapped stop' and 'within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable' in the statistics. The 3D view has the same switch, under the same conditions: the rings lie flat on the ground with a radius of 400 metres at every zoom (a MapLibre circle whose radius in pixels doubles at each zoom level, set from each point's latitude), and the chip counts them while they are drawn.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time.

entries.method: app.js (updateRings): ringLayer holds one circle for each point of kind transit_stop, bus_stop, bus_station, rail_station and ferry_terminal. twin3d.js (addRings, updateRings) draws the same points in the 3D view.
entries.how_to_read: Look at what the circles cover and what they leave out. Places outside every circle are more than 400 m, in a straight line, from the nearest stop.
caveats: The distance is a straight line. It ignores rivers, hills, fences and the street pattern.
Rings include stops of expired timetables and OpenStreetMap stops that have no timetable.
The rings say nothing about how often or when a vehicle comes.

A place inside a ring can still have no stop with a current timetable within 400 m: the ring may belong to a stop whose timetable has ended or to a volunteer-mapped stop. The place's pop-up gives its access class.

view.label: 2D map: 400 m rings at Santurce, San Juan
3D view: switch on Transit stops and the 400 m rings (Santurce, San Juan)

entries.source_detail: transport.json, Snapshot 2026-10: 4,360 points of kind transit_stop, bus_stop, bus_station, rail_station and ferry_terminal. The stops come from timetable feeds of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and of municipalities in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) form, and from OpenStreetMap. The rings carry no credit line of their own. The stops or stations layer that must be on shows its own credit line: see the entries on those two layers.
entries.plain_es: "Mostrar radio de 400 m a pie alrededor de las paradas" dibuja un círculo de 400 metros alrededor de cada parada, estación de guaguas, estación del Tren Urbano y terminal de lanchas. Los círculos solo aparecen al acercar el mapa y cuando la capa de paradas o la de estaciones está activada.
entries.name_es: Interruptor del radio de 400 m a pie (mapa 2D y vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Fíjese en lo que cubren los círculos y en lo que dejan fuera. Los lugares fuera de todos los círculos están a más de 400 m, en línea recta, de la parada más cercana.

entries.name: Barrios switch (2D map and 3D view)
entries.plain: The 'Barrios' switch draws the 901 barrios of the Census Bureau's January 2023 layer, the districts inside each municipality, as dashed outlines. Click inside one for its counts.
entries.definition: Barrios are dashed blue outlines. The layer is off when the page opens. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads barrios.geojson (about 1.0 MB in Snapshot 2026-10). With the switch on, a click adds a section to the popup. It gives the barrio's name, its municipality and its area in square kilometres. It also gives the number of tourism places, the places per square kilometre, how many of those places are in a flood hazard area, and how many are within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable (and how many of those are near a frequent stop) and within 400 m of any mapped stop. The 3D view has the same switch: the same dashed outlines and, for a click inside a barrio, the same section, last in the card after the other areas under the click, as on the 2D map.

coverage.frequency: Outline shapes are the Census Bureau's generalized county-subdivision layer, January 1, 2023 vintage, cut at the shoreline. Counts are rebuilt with each snapshot.

entries.method: app.js (loadBarrios), twin3d.js (addBarrios) and access.js (barrioPopup, shared by both views). The counts are stored in barrios.geojson.
entries.source_detail: barrios.geojson. Credit line on the map: 'Barrios: US Census Bureau'.
entries.how_to_read: Compare barrios by places per square kilometre, not by raw counts, because their areas differ a great deal.
caveats: A barrio is a Census statistical unit. It is not a neighbourhood or an electoral unit.
Barrio names repeat across municipalities. Read the municipality in the popup.

Barrio counts use the default filters (confidence 0.50, no places of worship). The confidence slider, the category buttons and the worship switch do not change them. The counts are rebuilt only at a full build, so between full builds they can lag the municipality figures.
Cite the outlines as the Census Bureau's generalized county-subdivision boundaries as of January 1, 2023, cut at the shoreline.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Barrios (Bayamón area)
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Barrios (Bayamón area)

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Barrios" dibuja con líneas discontinuas los 901 barrios de la capa de enero de 2023 del Negociado del Censo, que son las divisiones dentro de cada municipio. Haga clic dentro de uno para ver sus conteos.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Barrios (mapa 2D y vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare los barrios por lugares por kilómetro cuadrado, no por conteos brutos, porque sus áreas varían mucho.

entries.name: Category buttons (tourism places)
entries.plain: Four buttons under the Tourism places switch turn each tourism category on or off: Attractions, Gastronomy, Accommodations and Visitor Services. All four are on when the page opens.
entries.definition: Each button shows or hides every place of one category. A pressed button is on. A button that is off looks faded. The buttons change the pins, the live tiles and tables of the Municipality tab, the tourism results of the search box and the places file in comma-separated values (CSV) form. The 3D view has the same four buttons. The statistics of each municipality (Rankings tab, shading) do not follow the buttons. Pin and button colours: Attractions blue, Gastronomy green, Accommodations gold, Visitor Services red.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js (renderCatChips) keeps a set of the categories that are on and rebuilds the pins when a button is pressed. Colours and icons are defined once in icons.js. Pressing a button sets aria-pressed for screen readers.
entries.how_to_read: A category is a group of Overture categories that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) assigned. See the entry on classification for how the groups were made.
caveats: Places of Worship belong to Attractions, so they show only when the Attractions button and the worship switch are both on.
Colour is not the only cue. The pin icon and the type in the card also say what a place is.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: category buttons

values.ATTRACTIONS: Attractions, blue (#338CB3). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Beaches, Historic Sites, Nature Reserves, Scenic Areas, Parks, Tourist Attractions, Places of Worship, Cultural Attractions, Museums.
values.GASTRONOMY: Gastronomy, green (#79901E). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Restaurants, Bars, Cafes, Bakeries, Nightlife, Food Experiences.
values.ACCOMMODATIONS: Accommodations, gold (#FFA600). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Hotels, Lodging, Vacation Properties, Guest Houses, Resorts, Inns.
values.VISITOR_SERVICES: Visitor Services, red (#FF4D38). Types in Snapshot 2026-10: Transportation, Marinas, Tour Operators, Visitor Centers, Adventure Operators, Cultural Experience Providers.

entries.plain_es: Cuatro botones bajo el interruptor "Lugares turísticos" activan o desactivan cada categoría turística: "Atracciones", "Gastronomía", "Alojamientos" y "Servicios para visitantes". Las cuatro están activadas al abrir la página.
entries.name_es: Botones de categoría (lugares turísticos)
entries.how_to_read_es: Una categoría es un grupo de categorías de Overture que asignó Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR). Vea la ficha sobre la clasificación para saber cómo se formaron los grupos.

entries.name: Click on the 2D map: what opens
entries.plain: A click on the 2D map opens a popup for the overlays that are on at that spot. If no overlay has anything there, a click on a municipality opens its profile.
entries.definition: In this order, the popup can hold: up to two flood zones, up to two protected areas, the land-use class of one polygon (water and road polygons are skipped), and one barrio. If the boundaries layer is on and the click is inside a municipality, a link 'Open the <name> profile' is added. If no overlay has a feature at the point, the click selects the municipality (when Boundaries is on) and opens the Municipality tab. Pins, stops, routes and vehicle dots have their own popups. Two modes take the click away: choosing a point for the route planner, and having the Analysis tab open with at least one visible layer. In the second case the click opens the economy popup for the municipality.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: app.js (the map click handler) with featuresAt in plan.js. Overlays are not interactive, so a polygon layer cannot swallow clicks meant for the municipality below it.
entries.how_to_read: Switch on the overlays you want to read before you click.
caveats: The popup shows up to two flood zones and two protected areas. A point with more overlapping records shows only the first ones.

view.label: 2D map

entries.plain_es: Un clic en el mapa 2D abre una ventana emergente con las capas superpuestas que están activadas en ese lugar. Si ninguna tiene datos ahí, un clic en un municipio abre su perfil.
entries.name_es: Clic en el mapa 2D: qué se abre
entries.how_to_read_es: Active las capas superpuestas que quiera leer antes de hacer clic.

entries.name: Flood zones switch (2D map)
entries.plain: The 'Flood zones' switch shades the land that the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) maps as flood-prone, from its National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL). It is off when the page opens. With it on, a click on the map tells you the FEMA zone at that point.
entries.definition: The legend on the Map layers tab has four rows. Darkest blue is for V and VE zones (coastal high hazard, wave action). Mid blue is for A, AE, AH, AO and A99 zones (1% annual chance, the Special Flood Hazard Area). Red is for the regulatory floodway. Light blue is for the shaded X zone (0.2% annual chance). The first time you switch it on, the page downloads flood.geojson (about 8 MB in Snapshot 2026-10). With the switch on, a click adds a section 'Flood zone' to the popup, for up to two zones under the click, with a plain description (1% annual chance, 0.2% annual chance, or 'see FEMA zone definitions') and the zone subtype. The layer itself does not take clicks, so the municipality underneath still answers.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js (floodStyle, floodVisible, loadFlood, floodPopup). The 2D map draws a polygon when FEMA labels it as in the Special Flood Hazard Area or as the shaded 0.2% X zone. Minimal-hazard X, zone D and the labels OPEN WATER and AREA NOT INCLUDED are not drawn. Click answers use point-in-polygon tests on the same file (plan.js, featuresAt).
entries.source_detail: flood.geojson. Credit line on the map: 'Flood zones: FEMA NFHL'.
entries.how_to_read: Read the colour as the FEMA zone family, not as depth. An unshaded area is not proof of safety.
caveats: This is FEMA's mapped hazard at a location. It is not a forecast for any year and it says nothing about a building's elevation or insurance.
Drawn outlines are simplified. See the flood layer entry for the effect at zone edges.
If the file cannot be downloaded, the switch turns itself off.

This is a simplified copy of FEMA's data for context. FEMA's printed flood maps and Flood Insurance Study are the official designation. It is not a flood determination for any property. Read the source's terms before you rely on it.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Hazards and environment, Flood zones (FEMA)

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Zonas inundables" sombrea los terrenos que FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias) identifica como propensos a inundarse en su NFHL (Capa Nacional de Riesgo de Inundación). Está desactivado al abrir la página. Con el interruptor activado, un clic en el mapa muestra la zona de FEMA en ese punto.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Zonas inundables (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea el color como la familia de zonas de FEMA, no como profundidad. Un área sin sombrear no prueba que sea segura.

entries.name: Include places of worship switch
entries.plain: 'Include places of worship' adds churches and other places of worship to the pins. It is off when the page opens, because most of them are not tourism supply.
entries.definition: Places of worship are the listings of type 'Places of Worship', which belong to the Attractions category. The places file of Snapshot 2026-10 holds 5,032 of them, and 4,758 have a confidence score of 0.50 or more. With the switch off, none is drawn or counted. With it on, those that pass the other filters appear. Only the 2D map has this switch. The 3D view, the route planner, the municipality statistics and the Rankings tab always leave places of worship out.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js: a place is visible when the switch is on or its type is not 'Places of Worship'. The page's help text calls these places landmarks and heritage assets.
entries.how_to_read: Turn the switch on to see landmarks such as churches on the map. Do not read them as visitor attractions in the statistics, because the statistics leave them out.
caveats: The listing does not say whether a place of worship is open to visitors.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Include places of worship

entries.plain_es: "Incluir lugares de culto" agrega iglesias y otros lugares de culto a los marcadores. Está desactivado al abrir la página, porque la mayoría no forma parte de la oferta turística.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Incluir lugares de culto
entries.how_to_read_es: Active el interruptor para ver en el mapa lugares de interés como las iglesias. No los lea como atracciones para visitantes en las estadísticas, porque las estadísticas los excluyen.

entries.name: Land-use analysis (2D map)
entries.plain: A panel that shows how the land of Puerto Rico and of each municipality divides among the classes of the 2015 land use plan, as bars and tables, with all 78 municipalities side by side. It opens from the Land use group of the Map layers tab.
entries.definition: The button 'Land use by municipality and for Puerto Rico', in the Land use group of the Map layers tab, opens a panel under the map (it replaces the Economy workbench while open). It shows the chosen area (Puerto Rico or a municipality) as one bar split by class, with the km² and the share of land of each, and the 78 municipalities as bars sorted by the share of a class you choose. It can show the ten classes of the legend or the four groups (urban, for urban growth, ordinary rural, specially protected rural). Clicking a municipality shows it and moves the map there. The CSV holds the km² and shares of every area.
entries.method: js/landuse_view.js reads landuse_summary.json and divides each class (or group) by the land of the area in the plan: the sum of the classes with in_share, so water and road rights-of-way are left out. Nothing is computed from the map's simplified polygons.
