entries.source_detail: landuse_summary.json (landuse.py class_summary); the script js/landuse_view.js loads the first time the panel opens.

coverage.frequency: A single plan version, dated 30 November 2015.

entries.how_to_read: Each bar is 100% of the land in the plan of that area; water and road rights-of-way are left out. Hover a segment for its class and share. The table under the chosen area gives the exact figures.
caveats: A planning classification, not land cover.
The analysis always shows every class: unticking a class in the legend hides it on the map only.

view.label: Map, Map layers tab, Land use: Land use by municipality and for Puerto Rico

entries.plain_es: Un panel que muestra cómo se reparte el terreno de Puerto Rico y de cada municipio entre las clases del plan de uso de terrenos de 2015, con barras y tablas, y los 78 municipios uno al lado del otro. Se abre desde el grupo Uso de terrenos de la pestaña Capas del mapa.

entries.name: Minimum confidence slider (tourism places)
entries.plain: The 'Minimum confidence' slider hides tourism places that Overture rates below the chosen score. It starts at 0.50. Lower it to see more listings, or raise it to see fewer.
entries.definition: Overture gives each listing a confidence score from 0 to 1, its estimate that the listing is a real, current place. The slider runs from 0 to 1 in steps of 0.05. The number beside it changes as you move the slider, and the map redraws when you let go. In Snapshot 2026-10 the scores run from 0.024 to 1.0. At 0.50 the map shows 24,209 places. At 0 it shows 27,509. Places of worship are left out of both counts. The slider also sets the live numbers on the Municipality tab, the tourism results of the search box and the places file in comma-separated values (CSV) form.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js keeps the value in S.conf. A place is visible when its confidence is at or above it, its category button is on and it is not a place of worship (unless the worship switch is on).
entries.how_to_read: 0.50 is the observatory's own cut-off, not an Overture rule. In Snapshot 2026-10 it keeps 24,209 of the 27,509 listings (88%) that are not places of worship. A score is Overture's estimate, and a high score does not prove that a place is open today.
caveats: Only the 2D map has this slider. The 3D view, the route planner and the municipality statistics always use 0.50.
The slider does not change the numbers on the Rankings tab or in the shading. Those use the stored statistics.

The note under the slider on the page says 0.50 keeps 'the reliable majority'. The observatory has no test of reliability. 0.50 is a chosen cut-off, and the listings below it are not shown to be wrong.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Minimum confidence

entries.plain_es: El control deslizante "Confianza mínima" oculta los lugares turísticos a los que Overture da una puntuación menor que la elegida. Empieza en 0.50. Bájelo para ver más listados, o súbalo para ver menos.
entries.name_es: Control deslizante Confianza mínima (lugares turísticos)
entries.how_to_read_es: 0.50 es el umbral propio del observatorio, no una regla de Overture. En el corte de datos 2026-10 conserva 24,209 de los 27,509 listados (88%) que no son lugares de culto. Una puntuación es un estimado de Overture, y una puntuación alta no prueba que un lugar esté abierto hoy.

entries.name: Municipal boundaries switch (2D map and 3D view), labels and hover box (2D map)
entries.plain: The 'Municipal boundaries' switch draws the outlines of the 78 municipalities. It is on when the page opens. Pointing at a municipality shows a short summary, and a click opens its profile.
entries.definition: Outlines are blue lines. Names appear from zoom level 10. Pointing at a municipality (with a mouse) thickens its outline and shows a box with its name, its number of tourism places, the share of those places in a flood hazard area and its 2020 population. A click opens the Municipality tab and outlines the municipality in red. When a flood, protected-area, land-use or barrio layer is on and has a feature under the click, the popup comes first, with a link 'Open the <name> profile'. When the switch is off, a click no longer selects a municipality and the outlines and names disappear. The 3D view has the same switch, on when it opens and never counted, as on the 2D map: it shows or hides the outlines only (no labels, no hover box), and a click on a municipality opens its card with the outlines on or off. When a flood zone, protected area, land-use class, Comunidad Especial or barrio is under the click, the card of those areas comes first, with the same link 'Open the <name> profile', which opens the municipality's card.

coverage.frequency: Outline shapes are the Census Bureau's generalized layer, January 1, 2023 vintage, cut at the shoreline. Population is the 2020 Census count. Counts are rebuilt with each snapshot.

entries.method: app.js (init, muniStyle, selectMuni). In the 3D view, twin3d.js draws the outlines (muni-line) and the switch lyMuni shows or hides them.
entries.source_detail: municipios.geojson and municipalities.json. Credit line on the map: 'Boundaries & population: US Census 2020'.
entries.how_to_read: Use the outline to see which municipality a place is in. The summary box counts places with the default filters.
caveats: Outlines are generalized shoreline-clipped shapes. Do not use them to decide whether a lot lies inside a municipality.
Cite the outlines as the Census Bureau's generalized boundaries as of January 1, 2023, cut at the shoreline. Only the population is a 2020 count.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Boundaries
3D view, Layers tab: Territory, Municipal boundaries

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Límites municipales" dibuja los contornos de los 78 municipios. Está activado al abrir la página. Al pasar el cursor sobre un municipio aparece un resumen breve, y un clic abre su perfil.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Límites municipales (mapa 2D y vista 3D), etiquetas y recuadro al pasar el cursor (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Use el contorno para ver en qué municipio está un lugar. El recuadro de resumen cuenta los lugares con los filtros predeterminados.

entries.name: Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 switch (2D map)
entries.plain: The 'Land use 2015' switch shades the whole island by the Junta de Planificación's land-use plan: urban, urbanizable, ordinary rural and specially protected rural land. It is off when the page opens.
entries.definition: The legend has ten rows with their colours. Suelo Urbano (urban) is gray. Urbanizable programado (planned growth) is orange. Urbanizable no programado (reserve growth) is light gold. Rústico común (ordinary rural) is light green. Rústico especialmente protegido (protected rural) is green. The five special protection classes (ecological, agricultural, hydric, ecological and hydric, agricultural and hydric) are dark green, lime and blues. Other protection combinations in the data use the colour stored in the file. Water and road polygons are not drawn. Polygons are drawn at 50% opacity. A click adds a section to the popup with the class name, the class code and the municipio of the first polygon under the click. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads landuse.geojson (about 17.7 MB in Snapshot 2026-10), the largest file of the map. A note under the legend says that zoning districts (Calificación) are not shown, because the Junta's service did not answer when Snapshot 2026-10 was built. Since 2026-10-16 every class of the legend has a tick box, ticked when the layer opens: unticking a class hides it on the map and in the click pop-up. The button above the legend opens the land-use analysis (layers.landuse_analysis).

coverage.frequency: A single plan version, dated 30 November 2015.

entries.method: app.js (loadLanduse, landusePopup). The layer filters out the groups water and road. Colours are stored in the file.
entries.source_detail: landuse.geojson. File version label: 'PUT-2014, 30-NOV-2015', the plan of 30 November 2015, which the page calls Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015. Credit line on the map: 'Land use: Junta de Planificación'.
entries.how_to_read: Use it for the broad pattern of where the plan allows growth and where it protects land.
caveats: The plan is a classification for planning. It is not a zoning map and does not say what may be built on a lot.
The plan dates from 2015. Land may since have been built on, reclassified or protected.
Polygons are simplified, so do not use the layer to decide the class of one lot.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Uso de terrenos 2015" sombrea toda la isla según el plan de uso de terrenos de la Junta de Planificación (JP): suelo urbano, urbanizable, rústico común y rústico especialmente protegido. Está desactivado al abrir la página.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver el patrón general de dónde el plan permite el crecimiento y dónde protege el terreno.

entries.name: Protected areas switch (2D map)
entries.plain: The 'Protected areas' switch shades the protected areas of the Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) of the US Geological Survey (USGS), from national forests to local parks. It holds 665 records in Snapshot 2026-10. Records overlap, so this is not a count of separate areas. The switch is off when the page opens.
entries.definition: Areas are drawn in green at 30% opacity. With the switch on, a click adds a section to the popup for up to two protected areas under the click. It gives the name, the designation (in Snapshot 2026-10 the data hold 22 codes: the card spells out 10 of them, for example National Forest or Local Park, and shows the raw code for the other 12, such as SCA, SRMA and MIL, which covers 126 of the 665 records), the manager, the public access (open access, restricted access, closed or unknown), the acres and the Gap Analysis Project (GAP) status. The GAP status is a rating from 1 to 4 of how strictly the land is managed for nature. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads protected.geojson (about 1.5 MB in Snapshot 2026-10).

coverage.frequency: PAD-US 4.1, downloaded for each snapshot.

entries.method: app.js (protStyle, protPopup, padTxt, loadProt). The codes are spelled out with the lists in the PAD constant, taken from the PAD-US data dictionary.
entries.source_detail: protected.geojson. Credit line on the map: 'Protected areas: USGS PAD-US'.
entries.how_to_read: Check the designation and the GAP status before you read a patch as a nature reserve.
caveats: 'Protected' has a wide meaning here. It includes recreation areas, local parks and military land.
Overlapping areas are stacked, so a darker patch can be several records.

In Snapshot 2026-10 the card spells out the designation for 539 of the 665 records. For the other 126 records (codes such as SCA, SRMA and MIL) it shows the raw PAD-US code. Look the code up in the entry on the designation. A military area, for example, shows only 'MIL'.

In Snapshot 2026-10 two thirds of the records (440 of 665) have GAP status 4, which the card words as 'no known biodiversity mandate'. Read the GAP status before you treat a patch as a nature reserve.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Protected areas

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Áreas protegidas" sombrea las áreas protegidas de PAD-US (Base de Datos de Áreas Protegidas de Estados Unidos), del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos), desde bosques nacionales hasta parques locales. Tiene 665 registros en el corte de datos de 2026-10. Los registros se superponen, así que no es un conteo de áreas separadas. El interruptor está desactivado al abrir la página.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Áreas protegidas (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Revise la designación y el estatus GAP antes de leer una mancha como reserva natural.

entries.name: Quintile shading of municipality statistics
entries.plain: The map ranks the 78 municipalities on the chosen statistic and splits them into five groups of about the same size. It shades the groups from light blue (lowest) to dark blue (highest).
entries.definition: The municipalities that have a value are sorted from lowest to highest. The class limits are the values found one fifth, two fifths, three fifths and four fifths of the way along the sorted list. On the 2D map a municipality takes the first class whose upper limit is at or above its value. With 78 municipalities each class holds about 15 or 16, fewer or more when several municipalities share a value. The five blues run from light (lowest) to dark (highest). Municipalities with no value are not shaded.

coverage.frequency: Class limits are recalculated each time the page loads

entries.method: Functions breaks and setChoro in site/js/app.js. The legend lists the range and the number of municipalities in each class. The 3D view colours its columns with the same four class limits and sets each column's height in proportion to the value, with the largest value tallest. Population change 2010 to 2020 is drawn as a one-sided scale in the 3D view because all 78 municipalities lost population: taller and redder columns mean bigger losses. The 2D map shades any dataset this way from Explore, the Catalog or Rankings (the 'Shade municipalities by' menu with its 25 options was retired on 2026-11-05); the 3D menu of Columns by municipality has 17 (see '3D view: Columns by municipality').
entries.source_detail: Inputs are the municipalities.* fields named in the method; the classes are a display choice of the observatory.
entries.how_to_read: Read the legend, because the same colour means different numbers for each statistic. Darker means a higher value than most other municipalities, not a good or bad result. Some fields of the municipality table cannot be shaded, such as land area, the housing unit counts, the 2010 population, places by category, the average confidence, the shares of places within 800 m of a stop with a current timetable or within 400 m of a rail station or ferry terminal, and the stop counts by timetable state. Population change 2010 to 2020 is shaded in the 3D view only. Places inside protected areas and places with a website are offered on the Rankings tab, not in the shading menu.
caveats: The groups have equal size, not equal width. A municipality at the top of one class can have almost the same value as one at the bottom of the next.

The 3D view uses the same four limits, but a municipality whose value equals a limit takes the lower class on the 2D map and the higher class in the 3D view. Its colour can therefore differ by one step between the two views.

The legend and the Rankings tab round values: whole numbers for counts and most percentages; one decimal for places per 1,000 residents, places per km² and the seasonal share; two decimals for the affordability ratio. The stored values can have more decimals (two for places per 1,000 residents and per km², one for the share in a flood hazard area). Cite the stored value from the CSV (comma-separated values) download.
Shading shows rank among the 78 municipalities, not distance from any target.

view.label: Map, a dataset shaded in five classes (an old 'Shade municipalities by' link)
3D view: 'Columns by municipality'

entries.plain_es: El mapa ordena los 78 municipios según la estadística escogida y los divide en cinco grupos de tamaño parecido. Colorea los grupos de azul claro (el más bajo) a azul oscuro (el más alto).
entries.name_es: Sombreado por quintiles de las estadísticas municipales
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea la leyenda, porque el mismo color corresponde a números distintos en cada estadística. Más oscuro significa un valor más alto que el de la mayoría de los demás municipios, no un resultado bueno o malo. Algunos campos de la tabla de municipios no se pueden sombrear, como la superficie terrestre, los conteos de unidades de vivienda, la población de 2010, los lugares por categoría, la confianza promedio, las proporciones de lugares a 800 m o menos de una parada con horario vigente o a 400 m o menos de una estación de tren o una terminal de lanchas, y los conteos de paradas según el estado de su horario. El cambio en la población de 2010 a 2020 se sombrea solo en la vista 3D. Los lugares dentro de áreas protegidas y los lugares con sitio web se ofrecen en la pestaña Posiciones, no en el menú de sombreado.

entries.name: Sea level rise switch and slider (2D map)
entries.plain: The 'Sea level rise' switch shows a map from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) of land that would be flooded at the highest regular high tides if the sea rose by 1 to 10 feet. The slider picks the number of feet, and it starts at 3.
entries.definition: The layer is off when the page opens. The slider runs from 1 to 10 feet in steps of 1. The label beside it says the chosen height, for example '3 ft'. When the layer is on, NOAA's tiles are drawn at 65% opacity. Moving the slider swaps the layer when you let go. The page address keeps the choice as slr=N. If NOAA does not answer, a message appears. The tiles are enlarged beyond zoom level 16. The page keeps no copy of the sea level data.

coverage.frequency: Live from NOAA each time the layer is shown.

entries.method: app.js (setSlr, slrUrl) asks https://coast.noaa.gov/arcgis/rest/services/dc_slr/slr_{N}ft/MapServer for tiles, where N is the slider value.
entries.source_detail: NOAA Office for Coastal Management, Sea Level Rise Viewer. Credit line on the map: 'Sea level rise: NOAA OCM'.
entries.how_to_read: Read it as a what-if for planning: 'land that would be wet at this height'. It is not a timeline and it names no year.
caveats: The page calls this a what-if for planning, not a timeline. NOAA says the layer shows water at the highest high tides and does not model storm surge, erosion, subsidence or new construction. NOAA calls it a planning reference that should not be used for navigation, permitting or other legal purposes.
If NOAA changes or removes the service, the layer stops working. The observatory cannot restore it.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Sea level rise, 5 ft

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Aumento del nivel del mar" muestra un mapa de NOAA (Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica) con los terrenos que se inundarían en la marea alta más alta de cada día si el mar subiera de 1 a 10 pies. El control deslizante elige la cantidad de pies y empieza en 3.
entries.name_es: Interruptor y control deslizante del aumento del nivel del mar (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Léalo como un escenario hipotético para planificar: 'terreno que estaría bajo agua a esta altura'. No es una línea de tiempo y no indica ningún año.

entries.name: Shade municipalities by (2D map, retired)
entries.plain: A menu of the 2D map that coloured the 78 municipalities by one of 35 measures. It was retired on 2026-11-05 (navigation plan, decision 81): each measure is now a dataset, shaded from Explore, the Catalog or Rankings, and an old link with s=<field> opens the same measure as that dataset.
entries.definition: app.js SHADE_DS lists the 35 fields the menu had and the dataset each now opens, with its scale where the menu used one (tourism places per 1,000 residents or per square kilometre). An address with s=<field> is read when the data of the Analysis tab load (economy.js econInit): the dataset is shaded in five classes, the tab does not change, and the address is rewritten with e=. Eleven of the fields became datasets for this (core/adapters.js SNAPSHOT_FIELDS): nine shares of tourism places near transit, the change in median gross rent since 2008-2012 and Uber's listing (1 or 0).

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (Snapshot 2026-10). The measures use different years: tourism places and flood exposure 2026; population 2020 Census; housing measures American Community Survey (ACS) 2020-2024, with the rent change starting from the 2008-2012 window; land use plan of 30 November 2015; residents served 2020 census blocks against the stops of the latest build; the access shares of places as of the date in access_as_of; the Uber list checked 2026-10-01. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js SHADE_DS; economy.js econInit; core/adapters.js SNAPSHOT_FIELDS. tests/test_catalog.py checks that every one of the 35 fields opens a dataset.
entries.how_to_read: Read the dataset the measure now opens: its legend, its scale and its own dictionary entry.
caveats: The three 'places shown' measures counted only the places the filters let through; their dataset counts every tourism place.
'Population 2020' opens the population dataset, which shows its latest year.
The 14 municipalities with no mapped transit stop have no value for the transit shares of places, not 0%: there is no measurement.

2D map: shade by affordability ratio

values.assets: Tourism places. Count of places in Snapshot 2026-10 (confidence 0.50 or more, no places of worship).
values.assets_per_1000_residents: Places per 1,000 residents. Places divided by 2020 Census residents, times 1,000.
values.assets_per_km2: Places per km². Places divided by land area in square kilometres.
values.sfha_pct: % of places in flood hazard area. Share of the municipality's places inside a Special Flood Hazard Area.
values.in_sfha: Places in flood hazard area. Count of places.
values.in_protected: Places inside protected areas. Count of places.
values.with_website: Places with a website. Count of places.
values.acc_cur400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable. The nearest stop with a published timetable (ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or a municipal system, in a feed that has not ended) is 400 m or less away in a straight line. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_freq400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a frequent stop (20+ weekday departures). A stop with a current timetable and 20 or more departures on a typical weekday is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_sat400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with Saturday service. A stop with a current timetable and at least one Saturday departure in the published timetable is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_sun400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with Sunday service. A stop with a current timetable and at least one Sunday departure in the published timetable is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.acc_paper_pct: % of places near only an expired or unscheduled stop. A mapped stop is 400 m or less away but none with a current timetable: its timetable has ended, or volunteers mapped it and there is none. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.transit_pct: % of places within 400 m of any mapped stop. The nearest stop, station or terminal of any kind is 400 m or less away in a straight line, including stops whose timetable has ended and stops that volunteers mapped. Municipalities with no stop counted are left unshaded.
values.transit_stops: Transit stops and stations. Count of scheduled stops, OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, Tren Urbano stations and ferry terminals inside the municipality. Airports, taxi stands and electric vehicle chargers are not counted.
values.uber_listed: Uber lists service (yes or no). Two colours: listed or not listed. It is a hand-typed copy of Uber's Puerto Rico cities page checked 2026-10-01 (57 of 78 municipalities listed). A listing, not measured coverage. 'Not listed' does not mean Uber is absent, because Uber says its service reaches beyond the places it lists.
values.affordability_ratio: Housing: affordability ratio. Median home value divided by the largest 30-year loan a household with the median income can carry (30% of income for housing, 78% of that for principal and interest, 5% rate). American Community Survey (ACS) 2020-2024. Above 1 means out of reach.
values.median_home_value: Housing: median home value, in dollars, ACS 2020-2024.
values.median_gross_rent: Housing: median gross rent, in dollars a month, ACS 2020-2024.
values.renter_cost_burden_pct: Housing: share of renter households that pay 30% or more of income on rent, ACS 2020-2024.
values.vacancy_pct: Housing: share of housing units that are vacant, ACS 2020-2024.
values.seasonal_pct: Housing: share of housing units that are vacant seasonal, recreational or occasional-use units, ACS 2020-2024.
values.gross_rent_change_pct: Housing: change in median gross rent from the 2008-2012 window to the 2020-2024 window, in percent. It is not adjusted for inflation. US consumer prices rose 36.6% from 2012 to 2024. In Snapshot 2026-10, 54 of the 78 municipalities changed by less than that (2 of them fell).
values.urban_pct: Land use: % of land classified Suelo Urbano in the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.
values.protected_land_pct: Land use: % of land classified Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido (specially protected rural land) in the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.
values.pop_served_active_pct: Transit: share of residents (2020 Census blocks) within 400 m of a scheduled stop with a current timetable, in Snapshot 2026-10.
values.pop_served_pct: Transit: share of residents (2020 Census blocks) within 400 m of a scheduled stop, expired timetables included, in Snapshot 2026-10.

entries.source_detail: municipalities.json, the fields named in the codes below. Class limits are calculated in your browser. Credit line on the map: 'Boundaries & population: US Census 2020'. See the boundaries entry for the vintage of the shapes.
entries.plain_es: Un menú del mapa 2D que coloreaba los 78 municipios según una de 35 medidas. Se retiró el 2026-11-05 (plan de navegación, decisión 81): cada medida es ahora un conjunto de datos que se colorea desde Explorar, el Catálogo o Posiciones, y un enlace antiguo con s=<campo> abre la misma medida como ese conjunto de datos.
entries.name_es: Sombrear municipios por (mapa 2D, retirado)
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea el conjunto de datos que la medida abre ahora: su leyenda, su escala y su propia entrada del diccionario.

entries.name: Stations, terminals and airports switch (2D map and 3D view)
entries.plain: The 'Stations, terminals & airports' switch shows the larger mobility points: bus stations and terminals, Tren Urbano stations, ferry terminals and airports.
entries.definition: The layer holds 145 points in Snapshot 2026-10: 91 bus stations and terminals, 16 Tren Urbano stations, 13 ferry terminals and 25 airports and airfields (14 from the list of the Federal Aviation Administration, FAA, and 11 from OpenStreetMap). Icons are larger than stop icons and are not clustered. A click opens the same card as a stop. For an airport the card also says 'Public use' or 'Private use' and gives its codes. The layer is off when the page opens. The 3D view has the same switch: the same points as dots (Tren Urbano red, ferry terminals teal, bus stations and airports charcoal, airports larger), with the same card.

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stations are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time. OpenStreetMap points and FAA airports are read at each full build.

entries.method: app.js (loadTransport) and twin3d.js (addHubs): points whose kind is bus_station, rail_station, ferry_terminal or airport go to this layer. The card is transportPopup in access.js, which both views load.
entries.source_detail: transport.json (kinds bus_station, rail_station, ferry_terminal and airport). Timetable data are from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and municipal feeds in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) form. Credit line on the map: 'Stations: ATI GTFS, OpenStreetMap, FAA'.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see where the main interchange and entry points are. An airport is not a transit stop.
caveats: In Snapshot 2026-10, the card says 'Public use' for every airport that is not marked private. That includes 11 airports from OpenStreetMap, which carry no public-use flag. Only the 14 FAA records state it (10 public use, 4 private use). The names of some OpenStreetMap airfields say closed, historic or military, and one includes 'CERRADO' (closed). The municipality chip counts only FAA airports marked public use, so the chip and the card can differ. Treat OpenStreetMap airfields as mapped, not confirmed open.
A station from OpenStreetMap shows that someone mapped it, not that it is staffed or served today.

The credit line on the map names the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), OpenStreetMap and the FAA. In Snapshot 2026-10, 29 bus stations come from municipal feeds, so credit those feeds too when you cite.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Stations, terminals & airports
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Stations, terminals & airports

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Estaciones, terminales y aeropuertos" muestra los puntos de movilidad más grandes: estaciones y terminales de guaguas, estaciones del Tren Urbano, terminales de lanchas y aeropuertos.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Estaciones, terminales y aeropuertos (mapa 2D y vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver dónde están los principales puntos de trasbordo y de entrada. Un aeropuerto no es una parada de transporte colectivo.

entries.name: Taxi stands and EV charging switch (2D map and 3D view)
entries.plain: The 'Taxi stands & EV charging' switch shows taxi stands and electric vehicle (EV) chargers that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. There are 9 taxi stands and 11 chargers in Snapshot 2026-10.
entries.definition: The layer reads points of kind taxi, ev_charging, bike_rental and helipad. Snapshot 2026-10 holds only taxi stands and chargers. Click for a card with the name, the kind and the municipality. Ride-hailing is not drawn here. Whether Uber lists a municipality is a yes or no, shown by shading the map by 'Uber lists service' or by the chip on the Municipality tab. The 3D view has the same switch and card; its dots take the colour of their kind (taxi stands amber, chargers green).

coverage.frequency: Read at each full build.

entries.method: app.js (loadTransport) and twin3d.js (addTaxi): kinds in TAXI_KINDS (access.js) go to this layer.
entries.source_detail: transport.json. Credit line on the map: '© OpenStreetMap contributors'.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see where such points are known. It is not a list of all taxis or chargers.
caveats: OpenStreetMap volunteers add these points, so the layer shows what has been mapped (9 taxi stands and 11 chargers in Snapshot 2026-10), not what exists.
Taxi stands and chargers are not scheduled transit and are not counted in the stop totals.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Taxi stands & EV charging
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Taxi stands & EV charging

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Paradas de taxis y carga de vehículos eléctricos" muestra las paradas de taxis y los cargadores de vehículos eléctricos que personas voluntarias trazaron en OpenStreetMap. Hay 9 paradas de taxis y 11 cargadores en el corte de datos de 2026-10.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Paradas de taxis y carga de vehículos eléctricos (mapa 2D y vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver dónde se conocen estos puntos. No es una lista de todos los taxis ni de todos los cargadores.

entries.name: Tourism places switch (2D map)
entries.plain: Tourism places are the pins on the map: attractions, restaurants and bars, places to stay and visitor services listed by Overture Maps. Pins are coloured by category, and a dark ring marks a place inside a high-risk flood area mapped by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA).
entries.definition: The switch 'Tourism places' is off when the page opens, and the listings are not loaded yet. The label beside the switch says how much they weigh (about 3.0 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10, the listings and their transit access columns together). The first time you switch the layer on, download a municipality's places, search the listings or press 'Load the place listings' in the Municipality tab, the page fetches places.json and place_access.json. The pins are the listings in places.json that pass the current filters: the four category buttons, the minimum confidence slider and the places-of-worship switch. With the defaults the map counts 24,209 of the 32,541 listings in Snapshot 2026-10 (built 2026-10-02) and draws 23,467 of them as pins (holiday rentals are counted, not drawn), and the label beside the switch says how many are shown. Pins join into numbered clusters until zoom level 16. A click on a pin opens a card with the name, the type, the municipality and region, the street address when there is one, badges, links and a source line. The badges are listed below. Links go to the place's website, when it has one, and to OpenStreetMap at the place's location.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js (ensurePlaces, rebuildPlaces, placePopup) loads the listings on first use and makes one Leaflet marker for each visible place and groups the markers with Leaflet.markercluster: clusters of pins within 55 pixels, no clustering from zoom 16. Each pin is 26 pixels wide and carries the icon of the place type. When a filter changes, the pins are rebuilt in chunks of 4,000 so that the page stays responsive.
entries.source_detail: places.json, Snapshot 2026-10: 32,541 listings, 24,209 of them on the default basis. Overture Maps Places release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded 1 October 2026. Credit line on the map: 'Places © Overture Maps Foundation'.
entries.how_to_read: A cluster number counts listings under the current filters. A pin is a listing, not a count of visitors or sales. The dark ring says the place's coordinates fall inside a mapped flood zone, not that the building floods. The Cite button of this entry cites the control. To cite the data, use the Cite button on the entries listed under Related, for example places.category.
caveats: Overture listings can be missing, duplicated, closed or out of date. The confidence slider filters them but does not remove every error.

The filters change the pins, the live numbers on the Municipality tab, the tourism results of the search box and the places download in comma-separated values (CSV) form. They do not change the statistics of each municipality (Rankings tab, shading, municipality download), which use the default filters: confidence 0.50 and no places of worship.

The badges come from point tests made when the data were built. The access class comes from the stored distances, which the nightly transit refresh can update. No badge is recalculated when you change a filter.

Until the listings are loaded, the Municipality tab shows the figures stored for the default filters, the search box offers to load them and the route planner leaves its tourism count out. Loading them is a download of about 3.0 MB compressed (Snapshot 2026-10), which matters on a phone or a slow connection.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Tourism places

values.Flood hazard area, zone <code>: The pin lies in a Special Flood Hazard Area. The badge prints the FEMA zone letter: AE, VE, AO, A or A99. It is a mapped hazard at a point, not an official flood determination (see the flood zone entry).
values.Zone X (0.2% annual chance): The pin lies in the lighter 0.2% annual chance zone. This is not a Special Flood Hazard Area.
values.Protected area: The badge gives the name of the protected area that holds the pin.
values.Transit access (class and distances): A badge names the place's access class: 'Frequent stop within 400 m', 'Stop within 400 m', 'Stop 400–800 m away', 'Only expired or unscheduled stops within 800 m' or 'No stop within 800 m'. Each badge has an icon as well as a colour, and hovering over it gives a note: the figures are schedule-based and in a straight line, a stop counts when its timetable has not ended, and real-time service, walking distance, públicos and taxis are not included. Under the badge, the line 'Nearest stop with a current timetable: <distance>' gives the distance and, within 400 m, the weekday departures and the Saturday and Sunday service. When a stop without a current timetable is closer than that stop, a line 'Any mapped stop (expired timetables and volunteer-mapped stops included): <distance>' follows, and hovering over it shows the stop's name. If the access file is missing or does not match the places file, the card shows only the badge 'any mapped stop <distance>'. The classes are described in methods.access_profile.
values.Confidence: Overture's confidence score for the listing, from 0 to 1.
values.Duplicates folded: How many duplicate listings were folded into the place.
values.Source line: Names Overture Maps, the contributing source and the original Overture category.

entries.plain_es: Los lugares turísticos son los marcadores del mapa: atracciones, restaurantes y bares, lugares para hospedarse y servicios para visitantes que lista Overture Maps. Cada marcador tiene el color de su categoría, y un anillo oscuro señala un lugar dentro de una zona de alto riesgo de inundación según los mapas de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias).
entries.name_es: Interruptor Lugares turísticos (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: El número de un grupo de marcadores cuenta los listados con los filtros actuales. Un marcador es un listado, no un conteo de visitantes ni de ventas. El aro oscuro indica que las coordenadas del lugar caen dentro de una zona inundable mapeada, no que el edificio se inunde. El botón Citar de esta ficha cita el control. Para citar los datos, use el botón Citar de las fichas que aparecen en Relacionado, por ejemplo places.category.

entries.name: Transit routes switch (2D map)
entries.plain: The 'Transit routes' switch draws every public route in the observatory's data. These are the Tren Urbano, buses and ferries of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI, the Integrated Transport Authority), municipal buses and trolleys, and routes mapped in OpenStreetMap. Thicker lines have more weekday trips.
entries.definition: Width grows with the weekday trips of the route, from 2 to 7 pixels. The Tren Urbano is one pixel wider than a bus line with the same trips. Routes mapped in OpenStreetMap are 2.5 pixels wide and ferries 3. Pointing at a line thickens it. A click opens a card with the route name, the operator and network, weekday, Saturday and Sunday trips, the first and last weekday departure, how the line was drawn, the state of the timetable with its dates, and a credit line. The routes load from transit_routes.geojson (about 1.0 MB in Snapshot 2026-10) the first time the switch is on. The colours and line styles are listed below.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time. Files are rewritten only when a feed changes. The OpenStreetMap routes (16 in Snapshot 2026-10) are refreshed only by a full build. The nightly job keeps the last copy.

entries.method: app.js (loadRoutes) and network.js (routeColor, routeStyle, routePopup). width = 2 + 0.7 x log2(1 + weekday trips), at most 7. The 'Show' button of an operator on the Transit tab dims every other operator's lines to 12% opacity.
entries.source_detail: transit_routes.geojson. Timetable feeds are in the General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) format. Credit line on the map: 'Routes: ATI, municipal GTFS feeds, OpenStreetMap'.
entries.how_to_read: Read a line as a guide to where a route runs. Open its card to see whether its timetable is current, expiring or expired.
caveats: Routes of operators whose timetable has expired stay on the map.
A route in a feed is not proof that the service runs today.
In Snapshot 2026-10, the 16 routes from OpenStreetMap have no timetable, so their trip counts are 0, meaning none published.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Transit routes

values.ATI buses: Blue line. It includes the buses of the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA, the Metropolitan Bus Authority), Metrobús and Metro Urbano.
values.Routes mapped in OpenStreetMap: Gold dashes. In Snapshot 2026-10 there are 16 routes that volunteers mapped: 9 carros públicos and 7 bus or trolley lines. None has a timetable.
values.Solid line: The line follows the operator's own route shape or the road network.
values.Dashed, lighter line: The feed lists the stops out of order, so the visiting order was inferred.
values.Dotted line: No road path was found, so the line joins the stops straight.

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Rutas de transporte colectivo" dibuja todas las rutas públicas de los datos del observatorio. Son el Tren Urbano, las guaguas y las lanchas de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado), las guaguas y los trolleys municipales, y las rutas trazadas en OpenStreetMap. Las líneas más gruesas tienen más viajes los días de semana.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Rutas de transporte colectivo (mapa 2D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea una línea como una guía de por dónde pasa una ruta. Abra su tarjeta para ver si su horario está vigente, por vencer o vencido.

entries.name: Transit stops switch (2D map and 3D view)
entries.plain: The 'Transit stops' switch shows boarding points: scheduled stops from the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and from municipal timetable feeds in General Transit Feed Specification (GTFS) form, plus bus stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap. The number beside the switch counts them.
entries.definition: The layer holds the points of kind transit_stop (scheduled stops, 3,781 in Snapshot 2026-10) and bus_stop (OpenStreetMap stops that are not within 30 metres of a scheduled stop, 459), 4,240 in all. The 3,781 are the scheduled stops that are not stations. In Snapshot 2026-10 there are 3,847 scheduled stops in all. The other 66 are bus stations, ferry terminals and Tren Urbano stations, and they appear on the stations layer. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads transport.json (about 1.3 MB in Snapshot 2026-10), which the stations and taxi layers share. Points join into numbered blue clusters until zoom 15. A click opens a card with the stop's name, kind and municipality, the routes and modes that call there, weekday departures, a weekend line ('Weekend departures: Saturday N · Sunday N', with 'none listed' for a day that has no departures, or 'No weekend departures in the published timetable' when neither day has any; scheduled stops only), the end date of the stop's timetable ('Timetable valid until' a date, or 'Timetable ended' with a warning sign when the date has passed), the operator, a note when the source says wheelchair boarding is possible, and a source line. The 400 m walk rings use these points. The 3D view has the same switch, in the same group: the same points, in blue clusters that give their count up to zoom 14 and as single dots from zoom 15, with the same card (a click on a cluster zooms in).

coverage.frequency: Scheduled stops are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time. OpenStreetMap points are read at each full build.

entries.method: app.js (loadTransport) and twin3d.js (addStops); the card is transportPopup in access.js, which both views load. The clusters group points within 40 pixels, in both views.
entries.source_detail: transport.json (kinds transit_stop and bus_stop). Credit line on the map: 'Stops: ATI GTFS · © OpenStreetMap contributors'.
entries.how_to_read: Check the source line first. A scheduled stop appears in a published timetable. An OpenStreetMap stop only shows that someone mapped a stop there.
caveats: Stops of operators whose timetable has expired stay on the map.
OpenStreetMap stops can be missing, out of date or wrong. The observatory does not check them on the ground.

The credit line on the map names ATI and OpenStreetMap only. In Snapshot 2026-10, 2,381 of the 3,781 scheduled stops come from municipal feeds, so credit both when you cite. The stop card's type label reads 'Transit stop (ATI)' for every scheduled stop, municipal ones included. The source line at the bottom of the card names the actual feed.

The card says 'wheelchair accessible' only when the source states that boarding is possible (feed field wheelchair_boarding = 1, or OpenStreetMap tag wheelchair=yes). Stops without the note are unknown or not stated, not inaccessible. In Snapshot 2026-10, none of the 1,400 ATI scheduled stops carries the note. In the feed standard, value 1 means that some vehicles can be boarded, not all. The note is not an accessibility audit.
The card compares the timetable end date with the date on your device. For a stop of an operator whose timetable has ended, it still shows the departures that the old timetable lists.

The weekend line shows what the published timetable lists. Many feeds list no weekend departures at all (in the 2026-10 snapshot only 3 of the 18 current feeds list Saturday departures and 1 lists Sunday departures), so 'none listed' often means that the feed does not cover weekends, not that there is no service.

view.label: 2D map, Map layers tab: Transit stops (zoom in to see points)
3D view, Layers tab: switch on Transit stops (Santurce, San Juan)

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Paradas de transporte colectivo" muestra los puntos donde se aborda: paradas con horario de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) y de los horarios municipales en formato GTFS (formato estándar de horarios de transporte colectivo), además de paradas de guaguas que personas voluntarias trazaron en OpenStreetMap. El número junto al interruptor las cuenta.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Paradas de transporte colectivo (mapa 2D y vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Revise primero la línea de la fuente. Una parada con horario aparece en un horario publicado. Una parada de OpenStreetMap solo indica que alguien mapeó una parada en ese lugar.

entries.name: Municipality profile, rankings and CSV download
entries.plain: The Municipality tab, the Rankings tab and the comma-separated values (CSV) download show the municipality statistics in different ways. Some Municipality tab numbers follow your map filters; the Rankings tab and the CSV do not.
entries.definition: Municipality tab: the header shows the region, 'residents (Census 2020)' and land area rounded to whole km². The tiles 'tourism places (current filters)', 'in flood hazard area', 'inside protected areas' and 'with a website' are counted live from the places the map is showing, so they follow the category chips, the confidence slider and the worship toggle. The tiles 'places per 1,000 residents' and 'places per km²' show the stored values, which use the default filters. The 'By category' bars and the 'Top types' chips are also live and do not read by_category. The rank note ('#n of 78 by tourism places', '#n by share in flood hazard area') uses the stored assets and sfha_pct and states that ranks use the default filters. Rankings tab: the table lists the stored value of the chosen statistic for every municipality that has one, highest first, with a second column holding assets (except when ranking by tourism places itself); a click on the column heading reverses the order. CSV (comma-separated values): the button 'Download municipality table (CSV)' on the Rankings tab writes one row per municipality with every field of municipalities.json.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot

entries.method: Functions renderMuni, renderRank and downloadCsv in site/js/app.js. In the CSV the object by_category is split into four columns named by_category_ATTRACTIONS, by_category_GASTRONOMY, by_category_ACCOMMODATIONS and by_category_VISITOR_SERVICES (landuse_km2 is split the same way). The file is UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so Excel shows the accents, and it is named pr_digital_twin_municipalities_ followed by the snapshot label, for example pr_digital_twin_municipalities_Snapshot_2026-10.csv. Rankings options for the fields in this file: Tourism places, % of places in flood hazard area, Places in flood hazard area, Places per 1,000 residents, Places per km², Places inside protected areas, Places with a website and Population 2020.
entries.source_detail: Inputs are the fields of municipalities.json documented in the municipalities.* entries.
entries.how_to_read: To cite or analyse numbers, use the stored values in the CSV download or in municipalities.json. Numbers read from the Municipality tab tiles can differ from them when you have changed a filter.
caveats: A separate button on the Municipality tab, 'Download <municipality> places (CSV)', exports the places the map is showing, not these statistics.
The CSV holds every field of municipalities.json, including fields documented in other entries.

The Rankings tab rounds the numbers it shows (see the entry 'Rankings tab' for the decimals of each measure). The order uses the unrounded value, so two rows can show the same number. Use the CSV for exact values.

view.label: Map, Municipality tab
Map, Rankings tab

entries.plain_es: La pestaña "Municipio", la pestaña "Posiciones" y la descarga en CSV (valores separados por comas) muestran las estadísticas de los municipios de formas distintas. Algunas cifras de la pestaña "Municipio" siguen los filtros del mapa; la pestaña "Posiciones" y el CSV no.
entries.name_es: Perfil del municipio, posiciones y descarga CSV
entries.how_to_read_es: Para citar o analizar cifras, use los valores guardados en la descarga CSV o en municipalities.json. Las cifras que se leen en los recuadros de la pestaña Municipio pueden diferir de ellos si se ha cambiado un filtro.

entries.name: Municipality tab (profile of one municipality)
entries.plain: The Municipality tab is a one-page profile of one municipality: tourism places, flood and protected-area exposure, transit access, housing and land use. Click a municipality on the map, or pick one in the search box or the Rankings tab.
entries.definition: The tab opens when you click a municipality on the map, pick one in the search box or the Rankings tab, or follow a link such as index.html#San%20Juan. The first block is headed 'Visitor economy'. Once the tourism place listings are loaded, its tiles are counted from the places the map is showing, so they follow the category buttons, the confidence slider and the worship switch. Before that (the listings are not part of the first load) the tiles show the figures stored for the default filters, a line says so and offers a button 'Load the place listings', and the top types and the list of places in a flood hazard area wait for the listings. Places per 1,000 residents and per square kilometre are the stored values, which use the default filters. The rank line uses the stored values too. The housing section is headed 'ACS 2024', the 2020-2024 window of the American Community Survey (ACS). The parts of the tab are listed below.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js (selectMuni, renderMuni). The rank line uses the stored assets and sfha_pct fields.
entries.how_to_read: Compare a tile with the same tile for other municipalities, not with a target. Read the housing figures as survey estimates.
caveats: Tiles that follow the filters can differ from the stored statistics when you change a filter. The rank line ignores your filters and says so.
The housing tiles are survey estimates. Their margins of error are large in small municipalities, and this tab does not show them. The Housing page does.
The Uber chip is a yes or no from Uber's own cities page. It does not show that a driver is nearby.

In Snapshot 2026-10, the airport chip counts as public only the 10 airports of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) that are marked public use. The card on the stations layer says 'Public use' for 21 airports: those 10 and 11 airports from OpenStreetMap that carry no flag. See the entry on the stations layer.

Without the place listings the tiles show the stored figures for the default filters (confidence 0.50 or higher, no places of worship). In Snapshot 2026-10 they agree with the tiles counted from the listings for every municipality.

view.label: 2D map: Municipality tab for Ponce

values.Header: The municipality's name, its tourism region, its residents (2020 Census) and its land area in square kilometres.
values.Tourism tiles: Tourism places, the share in a flood hazard area, places per 1,000 residents, places per square kilometre, places inside protected areas and places with a website.
values.Mobility tiles: There are up to five mobility tiles. The first two are shares of the places shown and appear when the access file has loaded: places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable, and places with frequent service (20+ weekday departures). The third is the share of the places shown within 400 m of any mapped stop. The first three tiles show a dash when the municipality has no stop counted. The fourth is the number of stops and stations. The fifth is the share of residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable (the share for any scheduled stop, expired timetables included, if the field is missing). A line under the tiles gives the stops by state: 'Stops: N with a current timetable · N with an expired timetable · N mapped by volunteers (no timetable)'.
values.Tile colours: Three tiles change colour. The flood tile warns when more than 25% of the places shown are in a flood hazard area. The residents-served tile warns when fewer than 25% of residents live within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable. The affordability tile warns when the ratio, rounded to two decimals, is above 1, and is green otherwise. These are the observatory's own signals, not standards. The tile for places inside protected areas is always green.
values.Chips: Tren Urbano stations, bus stations, ferry terminals, airports (with the number open to the public), scheduled stops, taxi stands, electric vehicle (EV) charging points, the state of the municipal bus schedule, and whether Uber lists the municipality.
values.Rank line: The rank among the 78 by tourism places and by share in a flood hazard area, with the default filters. It ignores your filters and says so.
values.Housing section: Headed 'ACS 2024'. It shows the affordability ratio, the median home value and rent, the share of renters who are cost-burdened and the share of seasonal or recreational units.
values.Land use line: The shares of land that are urban, urbanizable and especially protected (Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015), with a link to the full profile on the Housing page.
values.Lists and buttons: Bars by category, the eight most common place types, and a list of up to 60 places inside a flood hazard area (click a row to fly to the place). Two buttons download the shown places as a comma-separated values (CSV) file and zoom to the municipality.

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Municipio es un perfil de una página sobre un municipio: lugares turísticos, exposición a inundaciones y a áreas protegidas, acceso al transporte colectivo, vivienda y uso de terrenos. Haga clic en un municipio en el mapa, o elíjalo en el buscador o en la pestaña Posiciones.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Municipio (perfil de un municipio)
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare un recuadro con el mismo recuadro de otros municipios, no con una meta. Lea las cifras de vivienda como estimados de encuesta.

entries.name: Rankings tab
entries.plain: The Rankings tab lists the 78 municipalities in order of one measure, highest first. Pick the measure from the menu, reverse the order with a click, and download the whole municipality table as a comma-separated values (CSV) file.
entries.definition: The menu 'Rank municipalities by' has 26 options, listed below with the field they read. It starts on 'Tourism places'. The table has the rank, the municipality and the value, and a second column with the number of tourism places (not shown when you rank by tourism places). Only municipalities with a value are listed. A click on the column title reverses the order, and the arrow shows the direction. A click on a row selects the municipality and opens the Municipality tab. Numbers are rounded: whole numbers for counts and most percentages, one decimal for places per 1,000 residents, places per square kilometre and the seasonal share, and two decimals for the affordability ratio. The button 'Download municipality table (CSV)' saves one row per municipality.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (Snapshot 2026-10). The measures use different years: see the codes below and the entry on shading. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: app.js (renderRank, downloadCsv). The table is built from the stored statistics, so it does not follow the category buttons, the confidence slider or the worship switch.
entries.how_to_read: Rank 1 is the highest value, not the best result. Compare ranks only within one measure.
caveats: Tied values get consecutive ranks. Their order follows the order of the municipalities in the data file.

In Snapshot 2026-10, 14 municipalities have no stop counted inside their border. They are left out of the ranking by the share of places within 400 m of any mapped stop and by the five access shares (a stop with a current timetable, a frequent stop, Saturday service, Sunday service and only an expired or unscheduled stop).
The table rounds. For citation, use the stored values in the download.
A percentage of places can swing widely where a municipality has few places. In Snapshot 2026-10 the smallest has 36, so one place is 2.8 points. Check the count of places before you compare shares.

Transit stops and stations counts every mapped stop, station and terminal, including OpenStreetMap stops and stops of expired timetables. It reflects mapping and stop density, not how often vehicles run.

The rent change is not adjusted for inflation. In Snapshot 2026-10, 76 municipalities have a rise, and 52 of them rose by less than US consumer prices (36.6% from 2012 to 2024), so by that measure they had a fall in real terms.

view.label: 2D map: Rankings tab (open the tab after the page loads)

values.assets: Tourism places. Count of places in Snapshot 2026-10 (confidence 0.50 or more, no places of worship).
values.sfha_pct: % of places in flood hazard area.
values.in_protected: Places inside protected areas. Count of places.
values.with_website: Places with a website. Count of places.
values.acc_cur400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable. The nearest stop with a published timetable (ATI, the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, or a municipal system, in a feed that has not ended) is 400 m or less away in a straight line. Municipalities with no stop counted are not ranked.
values.acc_freq400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a frequent stop (20+ weekday departures). A stop with a current timetable and 20 or more departures on a typical weekday is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are not ranked.
values.acc_sat400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with Saturday service. A stop with a current timetable and at least one Saturday departure in the published timetable is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are not ranked.
values.acc_sun400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with Sunday service. A stop with a current timetable and at least one Sunday departure in the published timetable is 400 m or less away. Municipalities with no stop counted are not ranked.
values.acc_paper_pct: % of places near only an expired or unscheduled stop. A mapped stop is 400 m or less away but none with a current timetable: its timetable has ended, or volunteers mapped it and there is none. Municipalities with no stop counted are not ranked.
values.transit_pct: % of places within 400 m of any mapped stop. Municipalities with no stop counted are not ranked.
values.transit_stops: Transit stops and stations. Count of scheduled stops, OpenStreetMap bus stops, bus stations, Tren Urbano stations and ferry terminals inside the municipality. Airports, taxi stands and electric vehicle chargers are not counted.
values.affordability_ratio: Housing: affordability ratio. Median home value divided by the largest 30-year loan a household with the median income can carry (30% of income for housing, 78% of that for principal and interest, 5% rate). American Community Survey (ACS) 2020-2024. Above 1 means out of reach.
values.median_home_value: Housing: median home value, in dollars, ACS 2020-2024.
values.median_gross_rent: Housing: median gross rent, in dollars a month, ACS 2020-2024.
values.renter_cost_burden_pct: Housing: share of renter households that pay 30% or more of income on rent, ACS 2020-2024.
values.vacancy_pct: Housing: share of housing units that are vacant, ACS 2020-2024.
values.seasonal_pct: Housing: share of housing units that are vacant seasonal, recreational or occasional-use units, ACS 2020-2024.
values.gross_rent_change_pct: Housing: change in median gross rent from the 2008-2012 window to the 2020-2024 window, in percent. It is not adjusted for inflation: US consumer prices rose 36.6% from 2012 to 2024. In Snapshot 2026-10, 54 of the 78 municipalities changed by less than that (2 of them fell).
values.urban_pct: Land use: % Suelo Urbano, Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.
values.protected_land_pct: Land use: % Suelo Rústico Especialmente Protegido, Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015.
values.pop_served_active_pct: Transit: share of residents (2020 Census blocks) within 400 m of a scheduled stop with a current timetable, in Snapshot 2026-10.
values.pop_served_pct: Transit: share of residents (2020 Census blocks) within 400 m of a scheduled stop, expired timetables included, in Snapshot 2026-10.

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Posiciones ordena los 78 municipios según una medida, de mayor a menor. Elija la medida en el menú, invierta el orden con un clic y descargue la tabla completa de municipios como archivo CSV (valores separados por comas).
entries.name_es: Pestaña Posiciones
entries.how_to_read_es: La posición 1 es el valor más alto, no el mejor resultado. Compare posiciones solo dentro de una misma medida.

entries.name: Catalog tab (find data and add it to the map)
entries.plain: The Catalog tab searches everything the dictionary documents and puts it on the map with one button. You can filter by field, geography, year covered, license of the sources and source.
entries.definition: The tab lists the dictionary's entries, 40 at a time. At first it lists only what can go on the map: a yearly series (it joins the Analysis tab), a measure held for each municipality (it shades the municipalities) or a layer (it is switched on). Clear 'Only what can go on the map' to list every entry, methods and categories included. The search box matches the name, the identifier and the field of an entry; on a Spanish page it also matches the Spanish name, where the entry has one, and the words of the entry's Spanish summary. The filters are Domain (the fields and sub-fields of the registry), Geography (the level of the published file an entry describes), Covers year, License of the sources (strictest) and Source. Each row shows the name, the field, the years, the geography and the license class, an 'Add to map' button when the entry can go on the map, and a link to its dictionary entry. 'Open these in the data dictionary' opens the dictionary with the same search and field.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (python catalog.py, run by build.py after the dictionary). The nightly transit refresh does not rewrite it.

entries.method: catalog.js (rows, results, rowHtml, apply) reads the index of the dictionary in catalog_index.json, which it fetches the first time the tab opens, with the Spanish names of the entries (site/i18n/es.map.catalog.js) and, on a Spanish page, the words of the Spanish summaries (catalog_es.json). How an entry goes on the map is worked out when the catalog is built (catalog.py map_action): from where the entry says its data live (a yearly series, a field of municipalities.json) or, for a layer, from the list in dictionary_src/map_layers.json. It is checked again in the page: the button appears only when the page knows the target and the menu offers it.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to find a dataset by topic, then open its dictionary entry before you rely on it. The geography, the years and the license class are there to help you choose, not to replace the entry.
caveats: In Spanish most names of the data stay in English for now; the search also finds an entry by the words of its Spanish summary.

The license is the strictest class among the entry's sources, as recorded in the sources list. It is not a legal review, and it can be strict for an entry that only cites a study. Open the entry to see which source sets it.
An entry with no file or layer link has no 'Add to map' button, although it may be documented.
Adding a layer to the map does not remove the layers already on it. Switch layers off in the Map layers tab or the Analysis tab.

view.label: 2D map, Catalog tab

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Catálogo busca todo lo que documenta el diccionario y lo pone en el mapa con un botón. Se puede filtrar por área, geografía, años cubiertos, licencia de las fuentes y fuente.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Catálogo (buscar datos y agregarlos al mapa)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úsela para encontrar un conjunto de datos por tema y luego abra su ficha del diccionario antes de usarlo. La geografía, los años y la clase de licencia están ahí para ayudar a elegir, no para reemplazar la ficha.

entries.name: Topics tab (the headline figure of each field)
entries.plain: The Topics tab is what the 2D map shows first. It has one card for each field of the observatory, with a headline figure for the whole island, a small trend line when the figure has a history, and a button that puts its data on the map. Only the municipal boundaries are on the map at the start.
entries.definition: The cards come from the domain registry through catalog.json, so a new field appears with no change to the page. A card has the field's name and description in the page language, a status ('Some data' or 'No data yet') when the field is not fully covered, and one block for the field's headline figure and one for each sub-field that has its own. A block has the name of the figure, its value, the period it covers ('Puerto Rico · 2020–2024, five-year estimate') and, for a yearly series, a trend line of the Puerto Rico value for every year. 'Show on map' puts the figure's data on the map: a yearly series is added to the Analysis tab, and a measure held for each municipality joins it too, as a dataset; both are listed in the On the map panel. 'What it means' opens the dictionary entry of the figure. 'Browse N documented items' opens the Catalog tab for the field. A field with no data yet says so. A field with datasets on the wish list gives their number and a button 'What is planned', which lists them: title, status (candidate, checked, building or blocked) and source, read from wanted.json when the button is pressed (about 21 KB compressed). The titles are in English for now. The tab ends with buttons for the Catalog tab and the chat, and a note on what the figures are.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot (python catalog.py, run by build.py after the dictionary). The nightly transit refresh does not rewrite it.

entries.method: catalog.js (renderOverview, cardHtml, metricHtml, spark, apply) reads S.catalog, which app.js fetches at the start from data/catalog.json (the index of the dictionary is in catalog_index.json, which loads when the Catalog tab first opens), and data/wanted.json for the planned datasets. How each figure is worked out: methods.headline_figures.
entries.how_to_read: Read each figure as the number for the whole of Puerto Rico over the period shown. It is not a score, and the fields are not ranked against one another. Press 'What it means' before you quote a figure: tourism figures count listings, and an estimate has a margin of error.
caveats: The names of the figures are in Spanish and English; the long text of the dictionary entries behind 'What it means' is English for now.
The trend line shows the Puerto Rico value for each year the series has. It starts at the lowest value of its own range, so two lines should not be compared by height.
'Show on map' for a yearly series opens the Analysis tab, which loads its data the first time (about 0.4 MB compressed).

view.label: 2D map, Topics tab

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Temas es lo primero que muestra el mapa 2D. Tiene una tarjeta por cada área del observatorio, con una cifra principal para toda la isla, una pequeña línea de tendencia cuando la cifra tiene historial y un botón que pone sus datos en el mapa. Al inicio, el mapa solo muestra los límites municipales.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Temas (la cifra principal de cada campo)
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea cada cifra como el número de todo Puerto Rico en el período que se muestra. No es una puntuación, y los campos no se ordenan unos frente a otros. Presione 'Qué significa' antes de citar una cifra: las cifras de turismo cuentan listados, y un estimado tiene un margen de error.

entries.name: Integration points switch (2D Transit tab and 3D Route tab)
entries.plain: 'Integration points' marks the places where a stop of one transit system lies within 250 metres of a stop of another system. These are natural places to line up timetables, fares and signs.
entries.definition: The switch is off when the page opens. Each point is a white circle with a blue outline, placed midway between the two stops. There are 366 in Snapshot 2026-10, and all are drawn. Pointing at a point names the two operators, the two stops and the distance between them. A note under the switch gives the number found and, when some are left out, says how many are drawn. The 3D view has the same switch in its Route tab, under Planning layers; there a click on a point gives what pointing at it gives on the 2D map.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time.

entries.method: network.js (setXfer) and twin3d.js (setXfer) draw the transfers list of operators.json.
entries.how_to_read: A short distance means two systems have stops at almost the same place.
caveats: A pair shows that stops are close. It does not show that riders can transfer: the observatory does not compare timetables, walking routes or fares.
Stops of expired timetables are included.

view.label: 2D map: Integration points
3D view, Route tab: switch on Integration points

entries.source_detail: operators.json, list transfers (366 pairs in Snapshot 2026-10). The points carry no credit line of their own.
entries.plain_es: "Puntos de integración" marca los lugares donde una parada de un sistema de transporte colectivo queda a 250 metros o menos de una parada de otro sistema. Son lugares naturales para coordinar horarios, tarifas y rótulos.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Puntos de integración (pestaña Transporte del mapa 2D y pestaña Ruta de la vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Una distancia corta significa que dos sistemas tienen paradas casi en el mismo lugar.

entries.name: Residents far from service switch (2D Transit tab and 3D Route tab)
entries.plain: 'Residents far from service' draws a circle for each census block with at least 40 residents whose nearest scheduled stop is more than 800 metres away. Bigger circles mean more residents.
entries.definition: The switch is off when the page opens. The layer has 14,405 circles in Snapshot 2026-10 (distances walked along mapped roads). Circle radius grows with the square root of the residents, from about 5 pixels at 40 residents to at most 14 pixels. Pointing at a circle gives its residents and its distance to the nearest scheduled stop. A note under the switch says how many residents live more than an 800 m walk from any scheduled stop (2,251,110 in Snapshot 2026-10, about 69%) and that circles show blocks with 40 or more residents. The note counts blocks of every size. The circles show only the larger ones. The 3D view has the same switch in its Route tab, under Planning layers, with the same circles and note; there a click on a circle gives what pointing at it gives on the 2D map.

coverage.frequency: 2020 population against the stops of the latest build. Stops are re-read every night.

entries.method: network.js (setGaps) and twin3d.js (setGaps). Both filter the rows of population_blocks.json in your browser: distance above 800 and residents of 40 or more.
entries.how_to_read: Large circles in low-service areas mean many residents far from a scheduled stop.
caveats: Stops from expired timetables still count as stops, so a gap can be larger than shown. Públicos, systems with no published timetable and stops mapped only in OpenStreetMap are not counted, so a gap can also be smaller.
Distances are straight lines and counts are from 2020. It is a planning aid, not a demand forecast.

view.label: 2D map: Residents far from service
3D view, Route tab: switch on Residents far from service

entries.source_detail: population_blocks.json, Snapshot 2026-10: 36,570 rows of 2020 Census blocks, each with longitude, latitude, residents and metres to the nearest scheduled stop. The circles carry no credit line of their own.
entries.plain_es: "Residentes lejos del servicio" dibuja un círculo por cada bloque censal con al menos 40 residentes cuya parada con horario más cercana queda a más de 800 metros. Los círculos más grandes indican más residentes.
entries.name_es: Interruptor Residentes lejos del servicio (pestaña Transporte del mapa 2D y pestaña Ruta de la vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Los círculos grandes en áreas con poco servicio indican muchos residentes lejos de una parada con horario.

entries.name: Route planner (2D Transit tab and 3D Route tab)
entries.plain: The route planner draws a route between places you name or click, along roads, and then counts the residents and places it would reach. It is on the Transit tab of the 2D map and on the Route tab of the 3D view.
entries.definition: The planner draws a route between up to eight points and scores it against the open data. Drag a lettered marker to move a point. The route follows roads unless you switch 'Follow roads' off. The card shows the length and an indicative running time, then what the route would reach. The parts are listed below. The chosen points are kept in the page address as r=lat,lng;lat,lng, to 4 decimals (about 11 metres).

coverage.frequency: Computed in your browser each time you plan a route, from the files of the latest build.

entries.method: plan.js is shared by both pages. It matches names against the place-name index (gazetteer.json), routes along the roads with roads.js on roads.bin, and scores the route against the open data. The 2D map draws the route with network.js. The 3D view draws it with twin3d.js. Everything runs in the browser.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to compare options. Read each number on the card with its own entry.
caveats: It is a planning aid. It is not an engineering study or a demand forecast.

The running time uses planning speeds without stops or traffic. When some legs cannot follow roads (for example between islands), the length and the time still include them, as straight lines timed at 8 m/s (28.8 km/h).
The place boxes can offer an online address lookup. That sends the text you typed to OpenStreetMap Nominatim. See the search entry.
The GeoJSON file carries the licenses of its inputs. Check each before you publish it.

The address holds the exact coordinates of every point, to about 11 metres. If a start, end or stop is your home or workplace, anyone with the link can see it. Remove the r= part before you share a link, or use points that are not private.

Tourism places within 400 m of the route are counted only when the tourism place listings are loaded (switch on 'Tourism places' in the Map layers tab, then plan again). Otherwise that tile shows a dash and says so; it is never a zero.
Tourism places are offered as start, stop or end points only once the tourism place listings are loaded; until then the place boxes search the town, street, landmark, stop and route index only.

view.label: 2D map: example route
3D view: the same route

values.Boxes: From, To and up to six added stops, eight points in all. Type a town, street, landmark, stop or Puerto Rico (PR) route number, or press the pin button to click the map. 'Add points by clicking the map' fills the next empty box and then extends the route.
values.Buttons: 'Reverse' swaps the order. The arrows move an added stop, and the cross removes it. 'Follow roads' is on by default. With it off the route is drawn as straight lines. 'Plan route' matches boxes that hold text to the best result and then routes. 'Clear' empties the planner. 'GeoJSON' saves the route. Press Escape to stop choosing points.
values.Route card: The length and an indicative running time. Once the data have loaded it also shows the residents and tourism places within 400 m, the share of the route that runs beside existing routes, the shares in flood and protected areas, the municipalities crossed and the connections at its ends.
values.Red dotted line: A leg that cannot follow roads.
values.3D page: A button flies the camera along the route.

entries.plain_es: El planificador de rutas traza una ruta por las carreteras entre lugares que se escriben o se marcan con un clic, y luego cuenta las personas residentes y los lugares a los que llegaría. Está en la pestaña Transporte del mapa 2D y en la pestaña "Ruta" de la vista 3D.
entries.name_es: Planificador de rutas (pestaña Transporte del mapa 2D y pestaña Ruta de la vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para comparar opciones. Lea cada cifra de la tarjeta con su propia ficha.

entries.name: Transit tab: Operators list
entries.plain: The Operators list names every transit operator in the observatory and the state of its public timetable: current, expiring, expired or none. Press 'Show' to highlight an operator's routes on the map.
entries.definition: In Snapshot 2026-10 the list has 44 operators. The menu 'Show' filters it (see the codes below). Each row has a coloured dot for the type of operator, a short name with a status pill, and the full name. A line of details gives the routes, stops, weekday trips and the last date of the timetable. It adds flags such as 'no route shapes (drawn along roads)' and 'N routes list stops out of order'. An operator with no timetable feed (a General Transit Feed Specification, or GTFS, file) shows 'No GTFS feed found' (or 'Públicos run without a published schedule') and, when it has one, its number in the federal National Transit Database. 'Show' switches the routes layer on, dims every other operator's lines and zooms to that operator. Press it again to clear. An operator without routes but with a municipality has an 'Open <municipality>' button. The codes below give the filter menu, the status pills and the operator types, with their counts on 4 October 2026.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time. States are recalculated each time the page opens.

entries.method: network.js (opStatus, renderOpList, highlightOperator). The state is recalculated from the feed's end date every time the page opens. Expired means the end date has passed. Expiring means 60 days or fewer remain. States other than these three come from the stored file.
