entries.how_to_read: A current state means the timetable's dates cover today. It does not mean service runs as planned.
caveats: The state is judged from one date in the feed. A feed can be out of date in practice while its end date is still ahead.
Operators in none of the sources the observatory reads are not listed.

view.label: 2D map: routes on, then open the Transit tab

values.Filter menu 'Show': All operators; Operators with route data (current, expiring, expired and community-mapped); Expired, expiring or no data; and No public data.
values.current: Pill 'Current'. The timetable's end date is more than 60 days ahead. On 4 October 2026: 17 operators.
values.expiring: Pill 'Expires soon'. The end date is 60 days or fewer ahead. On 4 October 2026: 1 operator (Canóvanas, timetable ends 2026-10-31).
values.expired: Pill 'Expired'. The end date has passed. On 4 October 2026: 7 operators.
values.none: Pill 'No public feed'. No timetable data were found. On 4 October 2026: 16 operators.
values.in_ati: Pill 'In the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) feed'. The operator runs inside the ATI network. On 4 October 2026: 2 operators.
values.community: Pill 'Community-mapped'. Routes mapped by volunteers in OpenStreetMap, with no timetable. On 4 October 2026: 1 operator.
values.broken: Pill 'Feed error'. The feed could not be read. Not used on 4 October 2026.
values.unknown: Pill 'Dates unknown'. The feed has no end date. Not used on 4 October 2026.
values.regional (type): Blue dot. The ATI itself. In Snapshot 2026-10: 1 operator.
values.ama (type): Blue dot. The Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA, the Metropolitan Bus Authority). In Snapshot 2026-10: 1 operator.
values.municipal (type): Green dot. A municipal bus or trolley system. In Snapshot 2026-10: 39 operators.
values.community (type): Gold dot. Routes mapped in OpenStreetMap. In Snapshot 2026-10: 1 operator.
values.publico (type): Gold dot. Públicos. In Snapshot 2026-10: 1 operator.
values.ferry (type): Teal dot. The ferry authority. In Snapshot 2026-10: 1 operator.

entries.plain_es: La lista "Operadores" nombra cada operador de transporte colectivo del observatorio y el estado de su horario público: vigente, por vencer, vencido o ninguno. Oprima "Mostrar" para resaltar en el mapa las rutas de un operador.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Transporte: lista de Operadores
entries.how_to_read_es: El estado vigente significa que las fechas del horario cubren el día de hoy. No significa que el servicio opere según lo planificado.

entries.name: Transit tab: summary figures and 'Show transit only'
entries.plain: The top of the Transit tab shows four figures. Two count operators: those that publish a schedule and those that publish none. One counts the routes on the map. One gives the share of residents who live within 400 metres of a scheduled stop.
entries.definition: The first figure counts operators whose timetable is current, expiring or expired, with the three counts in brackets. The second counts operators with no public schedule data. The third is the number of routes on the map (165 in Snapshot 2026-10). The fourth divides the residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop, summed over the municipalities, by all residents, and adds the same share counting only operators whose timetable has not expired. The state of each operator is worked out in your browser from the end date of its timetable and today's date in Puerto Rico, so the counts can differ from those on the build date. The button 'Show transit only on the map' switches tourism places off and transit routes on. Other layers stay as they are.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time. The counts of operator states are recalculated each time the page opens.

entries.method: network.js (renderNetSummary). Residents come from the coverage records of operators.json, which use 2020 Census blocks.
entries.how_to_read: Read the last figure as a share of residents near a stop in a straight line. It does not say how often vehicles come.
caveats: An operator with no feed may still run service. 'No public schedule' means no timetable data were found.
Stops of expired timetables count in the first residents figure. The second figure leaves them out.

view.label: 2D map: transit routes on, then open the Transit tab

entries.plain_es: La parte superior de la pestaña Transporte muestra cuatro cifras. Dos cuentan operadores: los que publican un horario y los que no publican ninguno. Una cuenta las rutas del mapa. Otra da la proporción de residentes que viven a 400 metros o menos de una parada con horario.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Transporte: cifras de resumen y 'Mostrar solo el transporte colectivo'
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea la última cifra como la proporción de residentes cerca de una parada en línea recta. No indica con qué frecuencia pasan los vehículos.

entries.name: Transit tab: What is live
entries.plain: The 'What is live' box says that real-time bus positions are not available to the public and lists what exists, with a status for each source and a link.
entries.definition: The box opens with 'Real-time bus positions are not available to the public' and the date of the check. Below it each source has a coloured status and a one-line detail. There are six sources in Snapshot 2026-10: the real-time feed of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI), the Autoridad Metropolitana de Autobuses (AMA) Móvil app, ATI express buses, municipal systems, the AcuaExpreso ferries and aircraft near Puerto Rico.

coverage.frequency: Last checked 2026-10-02.

entries.method: network.js (renderLiveStatus) reads the live list of operators.json. Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) enters the statuses by hand after each check. The observatory does not test the sources automatically.
entries.how_to_read: Where the observatory shows vehicles moving, it replays a timetable. See 'Vehicles on their timetable now'.
caveats: The check is a snapshot. A feed published after the check date is not shown until the list is updated.

view.label: 2D map: Transit tab, What is live

values.not published: The operator has announced a feed but no address exists yet.
values.app only: Positions show in a mobile app, and no public data feed sits behind it.
values.private feed: A third-party app says the operator publishes positions, but no public feed address exists. Access is said to require a request to the operator.
values.none found: No real-time feed exists in the public registries.
values.available, needs a relay: Free live data exist, but their servers do not accept calls from a web page, so a small relay service is needed.

entries.plain_es: El recuadro "Qué está en vivo" indica que las posiciones de las guaguas en tiempo real no están disponibles al público, y enumera lo que existe, con el estado de cada fuente y un enlace.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Transporte: Qué está en vivo
entries.how_to_read_es: Donde el observatorio muestra vehículos en movimiento, reproduce un horario. Vea 'Vehículos según su horario ahora'.

entries.name: Vehicles on their timetable now switch (Transit tab)
entries.plain: 'Vehicles on their timetable now' draws a dot for each scheduled vehicle that should be in service at this moment, in Puerto Rico time. It replays timetables. It is not tracking by Global Positioning System (GPS).
entries.definition: The switch is off when the page opens. When it is on, the dots update every 5 seconds. The map picks the Sunday, Saturday or weekday file for today in Puerto Rico. A dot is red for the Tren Urbano, teal for ferries, blue for buses of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and green for municipal buses. Pointing at a dot names the route and the operator and repeats that the position is not GPS. A note under the switch gives the number of vehicles, the day type, the time, and the six operators with the most vehicles. Trips of operators whose timetable has expired are left out. Holidays are not modelled. The first time you switch it on, the page downloads the timetable file for the day type (the weekday file is about 2.2 MB in Snapshot 2026-10).

coverage.frequency: Timetables are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time. Positions are recalculated every 5 seconds.

entries.method: network.js (updateNow, setNow). A trip is in service when the time lies between its first and last stop time. Its position is worked out between the two stops around the current time, in proportion to the time elapsed.
entries.how_to_read: Read a dot as where the schedule says a vehicle is, not where it is.
caveats: No public real-time bus feed exists, so a late or cancelled vehicle is shown as on time.

The position follows the route line between stops at an even speed. A trip whose stops fit no line of its route (106 of 3,297 weekday trips in Snapshot 2026-10) moves in a straight line, so its dot can sit off the road.
Operators with no published timetable, públicos and OpenStreetMap routes are absent.

In Snapshot 2026-10, on Saturday only 4 operators have a timetable file (ATI, Guaynabo, Juncos and Vega Alta). On Sunday only ATI does, so municipal buses are absent on those days even where they run.

A dot moves between the stops that have a scheduled time. In Snapshot 2026-10, 532 of the 3,297 weekday trips list only their first and last stop; 523 of them still follow their route line, so their dots keep to the road, but the time in between is spread evenly.

view.label: 2D map: Vehicles on their timetable now

entries.source_detail: Snapshot 2026-10: trips.json (weekday, 3,297 trips), trips_sa.json (Saturday, 1,648 trips) and trips_su.json (Sunday, 381 trips). The vehicle dots carry no credit line of their own. Name ATI and the municipal operators when you cite.
entries.plain_es: "Vehículos según su horario ahora" dibuja un punto por cada vehículo con horario que debería estar en servicio en este momento, en la hora de Puerto Rico. Reproduce los horarios. No es un rastreo por GPS (sistema de posicionamiento global).
entries.name_es: Interruptor Vehículos según su horario ahora (pestaña Transporte)
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea un punto como el lugar donde el horario dice que está un vehículo, no donde está.

entries.name: 2D map: base map, side panel and map controls
entries.plain: The 2D map shows Puerto Rico on an OpenStreetMap base map. A side panel has eight tabs: Overview, Layers, Catalog, Municipality, Rankings, Transit, Economy and About. A top bar links to the 3D view, the Housing page and the data dictionary.
entries.definition: The base map is OpenFreeMap vector tiles in the OpenMapTiles schema, made from OpenStreetMap data and drawn by MapLibre GL JS under every other layer. It opens on the 'Positron' style, a light map for data; the 'Base map' choice, first in the Territory group of the Map layers tab, switches to another OpenFreeMap style ('Liberty', detailed, with streets, places and buildings; 'Bright', colorful; 'Dark'; 'Fiord', dark blue), to a map of the USGS National Map (aerial imagery, topographic or shaded relief: picture tiles of its own, with no OpenStreetMap data, which the map inspector cannot read) or to no base map (the data alone, on a plain background, with 'Base map off' in the credit line). The choice changes only the base map, is kept in the page address (bm=positron, liberty, bright, dark, fiord, imagery, topo, relief or none) and in the link to the 3D view, and is remembered in this browser as the default for the next visit. It is added once the map is ready, so the data come first; a short 'Loading the base map…' note shows in the credit line until it appears. The map opens on all of Puerto Rico. Zoom buttons and a scale bar with a metric and an imperial scale sit at the bottom right, with the credit lines of the base map ('© OpenStreetMap contributors · © OpenMapTiles · OpenFreeMap', or on a USGS map 'Base map: U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program') and of the layers that are switched on. The top bar holds the search box, the 'Ask' chat button, links to the 3D + Time view, the Housing page and the data dictionary, and a label such as 'Snapshot 2026-10' that names the build of the data files the page shows. Hover over the label to see the build date. Transit timetables, routes and stops are refreshed every night and are not tied to that label. The codes below list the other details of the page.

coverage.frequency: Base map tiles are requested from OpenFreeMap while you browse. The data layers are rebuilt with each snapshot.

entries.method: app.js builds the map with Leaflet 1.9.4, up to zoom 19. Once the map is ready it loads site/js/core/basemap.js, the one configuration of every base map, which loads MapLibre GL JS 4.7.1 (the same file as the 3D view) and MapLibre GL Leaflet 0.1.4 and draws the OpenFreeMap style in Leaflet's tile pane, under every overlay pane. The base map does not answer clicks: every click goes to the observatory's layers, as before. If the browser has no WebGL, the style does not load within 30 seconds or eight tile requests in a row fail, the base map is removed, the map keeps its layers over a plain light background and a message says 'Base map unavailable'; the map never falls back to the OpenStreetMap Foundation's own tile servers. The opening view fits the box from 17.86 N, 67.30 W to 18.52 N, 65.20 W. Each overlay has its own stacking level, so flood zones and routes draw above land use and protected areas. common.js runs the panel, the tabs (following the accessible tab pattern of the Web Accessibility Initiative, WAI-ARIA) and the help boxes. docs/basemap.md describes the base map.
entries.how_to_read: Use the credit lines in the attribution box when you share a picture of the map. Every dictionary entry has a Cite button. On an entry for a layer or tool it cites that control and names its sources. To cite the data themselves, use the Cite button on the dataset entries listed under Related.
caveats: The base map is made from OpenStreetMap, mapped by volunteers. It shows roads and place names, not official boundaries.

The page needs JavaScript and an internet connection. The map code, the fonts and the base map tiles come from other servers. If the map code does not load, the page says so and offers 'try again'. If the base map cannot be drawn (no WebGL, or OpenFreeMap does not answer), the data still show, over a plain background.
The snapshot label covers the files built together. It does not say when each source last changed.

view.label: 2D map

values.Panel and keyboard: The panel's tabs change with a click or with the left and right arrow keys. Press / to jump to the search box.
values.Phone: On a phone the panel stays hidden until you press the menu button. It closes with its close button, a tap on the grey backdrop or the Escape key.
values.Top bar links: Map (this page), 3D + Time, Housing and Data dictionary. The Data dictionary link opens dictionary.html, the page for definitions, sources, licenses and citations.
values.Files and loading: The page opens with only the municipal boundaries. Its first load is the build information, the municipality statistics, the boundaries and the catalog (about 0.16 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10). Every layer, the tourism places included, loads its data file the first time you switch it on (1 MB is 1 million bytes). In Snapshot 2026-10 the largest are land use (about 17.7 MB), the tourism place listings (about 16.7 MB, plus a 0.3 MB file of transit access), flood zones (about 8.0 MB) and protected areas (about 1.5 MB). If a file cannot be loaded, the layer's switch turns itself off and a message appears.
values.Inside another page: When the map sits inside another web page, the mouse wheel scrolls that page until you click the map.

entries.source_detail: Credit lines are drawn by each layer, so they depend on which layers are on. Base map credit line: '© OpenStreetMap contributors · © OpenMapTiles · OpenFreeMap'; on a USGS map, 'Base map: U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program', with 'Orthoimagery: USDA, USGS' on the aerial imagery. Page code: app.js, network.js, economy.js, chat.js and common.js. The entry of each layer names its data file.
entries.plain_es: El mapa 2D muestra a Puerto Rico sobre un mapa base de OpenStreetMap. Un panel lateral tiene ocho pestañas: Resumen, Capas, Catálogo, Municipio, Posiciones, Transporte, Economía e Info. Una barra superior lleva a la vista 3D, a la página de Vivienda y al diccionario de datos.
entries.name_es: Mapa 2D: mapa base, panel lateral y controles del mapa
entries.how_to_read_es: Use las líneas de crédito del cuadro de atribución cuando comparta una imagen del mapa. Cada ficha del diccionario tiene un botón Citar. En la ficha de una capa o herramienta, ese botón cita el control y nombra sus fuentes. Para citar los datos mismos, use el botón Citar de las fichas de los conjuntos de datos que aparecen en Relacionado.

entries.name: About tab and top bar (2D map and 3D view)
entries.plain: The About tab explains what the PR Data Observatory is, who it is for, how to start and how to cite it. It says that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) developed the observatory as a tool for public use and benefit. It also shows seven headline counts.
entries.definition: The 2D map's About tab has these parts, in order. An introduction says what the observatory is and that it is free, needs no account and is built from open and public data. Seven counts follow. Then come a list of the fields the observatory covers (written from the registry, so it grows with the observatory); a list of four groups the observatory is for; six 'Start here' steps, with buttons for the chat and the data dictionary; five example questions for the chat; a guide to the eight tabs and to the top bar; a note on where the data come from; six 'Keep in mind' points; and a privacy note. The tab ends with a closing section that gives the citation line and the current snapshot, and says where to send a correction or a dataset to add. Five of the seven counts come from meta.json when the page loads. The other two come from dictionary_summary.json when the tab is first opened. The 3D + Time view has its own About tab. It has a short description, a 'How to use it' list of five items (move around, pick a clock, turn layers on and off, plan a route, see it in 2D) and a 'Sources, licenses and how to cite' section with a button that opens the data dictionary. The codes below list the counts and summarise each part.

coverage.frequency: The five counts from meta.json are rebuilt with each snapshot. The two dictionary counts change when the dictionary changes.

entries.method: app.js (renderAbout, loadAboutNumbers). The five counts are read from data/meta.json. The two dictionary counts are fetched from data/dictionary_summary.json the first time the tab is opened, and they are left out if the file does not load. The texts are in index.html and 3d.html. The tab's cite line reads 'Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory' followed by the snapshot label. The last line of the tab gives the same label and the build date.
entries.source_detail: meta.json (counts, network and transport fields) and dictionary_summary.json (the number of dictionary items and of data sources). Cite line on the tab: 'Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, <snapshot label>'. The tab asks you to credit the original sources as well, which the data dictionary writes out.
entries.how_to_read: Quote a count with the snapshot label. The tourism place count follows the default counting rules (see Related), not the filters you set on the Map layers tab.
caveats: The counts are the observatory's own counts of listings and mapped points. They are not counts of businesses, visitors or services in operation.
The stops-and-stations count includes stops of operators whose timetable has expired and stops that volunteers mapped in OpenStreetMap.

The tab calls the observatory free, with no account, and built from open and public data. It also says that not every source has an open license: some, such as the municipal transit feeds and the Junta de Planificación's maps, state no license.
The tab also says that hazards are mapped zones, that timetables are not live and that survey numbers are estimates. The entries on those layers give the details.

The tab suggests setting disaster and federal money beside housing and the economy. Federal and recovery amounts in the observatory are amounts obligated (committed) or approved. They are not money spent, damage or need.

The Privacy section says that what you type in the search box or the chat stays in your browser, except the online address lookup. The chat also has a button that opens a GitHub request form with your unanswered questions in the web address. See the entry on what the chat keeps on your device.

view.label: 2D map: About tab (open the tab)
3D + Time view: About tab (open the tab)

values.Residents (2020 Census): 3,285,874. The 2020 Census count of residents (counts.population_2020). It is not a current estimate.
values.Tourism places: 24,209 in Snapshot 2026-10 (built 2026-10-02). Overture listings with confidence 0.50 or more, with places of worship left out (counts.tourism_places).
values.Transit routes, all operators: 165 in Snapshot 2026-10. It includes 16 routes mapped in OpenStreetMap that have no timetable (network.routes).
values.Stops and stations: 4,360 in Snapshot 2026-10: 3,781 scheduled stops, 459 OpenStreetMap bus stops, 91 bus stations, 16 Tren Urbano stations and 13 ferry terminals. In Snapshot 2026-10 the airports (25), taxi stands (9) and electric vehicle charging points (11) are not counted.
values.Documented datasets, variables and measu: The number of items in the data dictionary. It is read from dictionary_summary.json, so it grows as entries are added.
values.Data sources, each with its license: The number of data sources in the dictionary, not counting software and base-map sources. It is read from dictionary_summary.json.
values.What the observatory covers: A list of the fields (domains) of the registry with their descriptions, written when the page loads, so a new field appears with no change to the page. A field with no data yet is marked. A line under the list says that the observatory keeps growing.
values.Who the observatory is for: The tab names four groups: residents and community groups; local and island planners; researchers, students and journalists; and funders, nonprofits and recovery teams.
values.Start here: six steps: 1. Start with the overview (the Topics tab gives one headline figure for each field; the Catalog tab finds any dataset and adds it to the map). 2. Turn on layers (Map layers tab). 3. Click a municipality or a place (Municipality tab). 4. Put economic data on the map (Analysis tab). 5. Ask a question (the Ask button, in English or Spanish). 6. Check and share: open the Data dictionary, copy a link and download tables as comma-separated values (CSV) files.
values.Questions to try: Where is unemployment highest? Show poverty and unemployment together. Tell me about Ponce. What are the most interesting patterns? What data is missing?
values.The eight tabs, as the About tab describ: Overview (one headline figure for each field, with a trend), Layers (map layers, and shading by any of the measures in the menu), Catalog (search everything the observatory documents, filter it and add it to the map), Municipality (the profile of one municipality), Rankings (rank the 78 municipalities and download the table), Transit (operators and the state of their timetables, vehicles on schedule, residents far from service and a route planner), Economy (the tab says 'more than 100 yearly datasets'; there are 103 in Snapshot 2026-10) and About.
values.The top bar, as the About tab describes: Search (press / to jump to it); Ask (a chat that builds every answer from the data loaded on the page and is not generative artificial intelligence); Map; 3D + Time; Housing; and Data dictionary (what every dataset, variable and measure means, its source and license, the glossary, the published data files and how to cite).
values.Keep in mind: Six points: it is a snapshot; places are listings, not a census of businesses; hazards are mapped zones; timetables are not live; survey numbers are estimates; and patterns are not causes. The last point adds that the observatory is for asking better questions and planning, not a legal, financial or engineering determination.
values.Privacy: No accounts. What you type in the search box or the chat stays in your browser, except the online address lookup, which sends that text to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service. Like any web page, the observatory loads fonts, code libraries and map tiles from other servers (the tab names Google Fonts, cdnjs, OpenStreetMap and the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, NOAA), which can see your Internet Protocol (IP) address.
values.Cite it and tell us what is missing: To cite: Foundation for Puerto Rico, PR Data Observatory, followed by the snapshot label. The tab asks you to credit the original sources too, and says the data dictionary writes them out. It also says the database keeps growing, points to the chat question 'What data is missing?' and gives FPR's website for a correction or a dataset to add.
values.3D + Time About tab: A short description (real terrain and building heights, and three clocks), a 'How to use it' list of five items, and 'Sources, licenses and how to cite' with the button 'Open the data dictionary'. It says the view uses public data, that most sources have an open license but some (the municipal transit feeds, the Junta de Planificación's maps) state none, and that the Data management page gives each file's license class.

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Info explica qué es el Observatorio de Datos de PR, para quién es, cómo empezar y cómo citarlo. Indica que Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) desarrolló el observatorio como una herramienta para uso y beneficio público. También muestra siete cifras principales.
entries.name_es: Pestaña Info y barra superior (mapa 2D y vista 3D)
entries.how_to_read_es: Cite un conteo junto con la etiqueta del corte de datos. El conteo de lugares turísticos sigue las reglas de conteo predeterminadas (vea Relacionado), no los filtros que se fijen en la pestaña Capas del mapa.

entries.name: Help buttons (?) beside layers and figures
entries.plain: A round '?' button beside a layer, a tile or a chart opens a small box with a short explanation of what it shows and where it comes from.
entries.definition: On the 2D map the box opens for the items listed below. The 3D view has 20 (2026-10-19): the layers it shares with the 2D map have the same help texts in both views (the six facility layers bring theirs with them, from core/facilities.js), except Municipal boundaries, whose 3D text points to the columns instead of the shading. On the Housing page each of the 28 variable blocks (a map and its ranked chart) has a '?' that shows the dataset's definition and its source reference. The other charts and tables on the Housing page have no '?'. A box closes with its close button, with Escape or with a click elsewhere. The texts are short summaries written into the page code. This dictionary gives the full account of each layer and variable.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: common.js (initHelp) opens a box for any element that carries a data-help key and looks the key up in a list: help.js (2D, loaded with its Spanish on the first press), core/facilities.js (the facility layers, both views, loaded with them), twin3d.js (3D) or housing.js (Housing page).
entries.how_to_read: Read the box as a reminder. For a figure you plan to cite, use the dictionary entry.
caveats: The Tourism places help boxes (2D and 3D) call the classification 'the VIEWPR taxonomy'. This means the grouping of Overture categories into four tourism categories that Foundation for Puerto Rico (FPR) made. See the entry on classification.

entries.plain_es: Un botón redondo "?" junto a una capa, un recuadro o una gráfica abre una cajita con una explicación breve de lo que muestra y de dónde proviene.
entries.name_es: Botones de ayuda (?) junto a capas y figuras
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea el cuadro como un recordatorio. Para una cifra que piense citar, use la ficha del diccionario.

entries.name: 3D + Time view: scene, tabs and base map
entries.plain: The 3D + Time view shows Puerto Rico as a tilted 3D scene with terrain and buildings, and three clocks: a day of transit, sea level by year and hurricanes since 1851.
entries.definition: The top bar has the search box and links to the 2D map, the Housing page and the data dictionary. The side panel has four tabs: Layers, Time (the three clocks), Route (the route planner) and About. The About tab describes the view and links to the data dictionary (see the entry on the About tab). A time bar at the bottom switches between the clocks. The base map is the OpenFreeMap 'Liberty' style, which draws OpenStreetMap data; the 'Base map' choice, first in the 3D scene group of the Layers tab, switches to another OpenFreeMap style ('Positron', a light map for data; 'Bright'; 'Dark'; 'Fiord'), to a map of the USGS National Map (aerial imagery, topographic or shaded relief, draped over the terrain) or to no base map. A switch keeps every data layer, the terrain and the animated layers. The 3D buildings need OpenStreetMap's building tiles, so they are off on a USGS map and with no base map, and come back with an OpenFreeMap style; the counts on the clusters of stops need fonts, which every style but 'No base map' has. The choice is kept in the page address (bm=) and in the link to the 2D map, and remembered in this browser. The view needs WebGL, a browser feature for 3D graphics. Without it the page says so and points to the 2D map and the Housing page. The page opens on the whole island, tilted 50 degrees (35 on a phone). The codes below give the contents of the Map layers tab, the camera limits, what loads when and how the page behaves inside another page.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: twin3d.js. MapLibre GL JS 4.7.1 draws the terrain, the buildings and the data layers, which follow the terrain. deck.gl 9.0.38 draws the animated layers (transit trips and storm tracks) over the map. The data are the same data files as on the 2D map.
entries.source_detail: Credit line on the map, in the attribution box shared by every 3D layer: 'Places © Overture Maps Foundation · FEMA NFHL · NOAA (SLR, HURDAT2) · USGS PAD-US · US Census · ATI GTFS · © OpenStreetMap contributors · © OpenMapTiles · OpenFreeMap', followed by the terrain's own line (see the 3D terrain entry). In that line, FEMA NFHL is the National Flood Hazard Layer of the Federal Emergency Management Agency, NOAA is the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, SLR is sea level rise, HURDAT2 is the Atlantic hurricane database of the NOAA National Hurricane Center, AWS is Amazon Web Services, USGS PAD-US is the Protected Areas Database of the US Geological Survey, and ATI GTFS is the timetable data of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado in General Transit Feed Specification format.
entries.how_to_read: Use the 3D view to see how places sit in the land. Use the 2D map for numbers, the Analysis tab and the chat.
caveats: The 3D view needs a recent browser with WebGL and downloads more data than the 2D map.
The 3D view has no confidence slider, no worship switch, no economy layers and no layer links. Its address keeps only the camera and a route.

The credit line names the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) for transit. Municipal feeds also supply routes, stops and trips in the 3D view, so credit them too when you cite. The route card names the right source.

view.label: 3D + Time view

values.Map layers tab: 3D scene (terrain and buildings), then the groups of the 2D map, in the same order and with the same layers where both views can draw them: Territory (municipal boundaries, barrios, columns by municipality), Hazards and environment, Land and housing (with public housing), Infrastructure and mobility (routes, stops, stations, taxi stands and EV charging, the walk rings, the vehicle replay), Community services (fire and EMS stations, police stations, city halls, public libraries, historic places), Communities and Visitor economy (tourism places).
values.Base map fallback: If the base map style cannot be loaded, the data layers appear on a plain background with a message.
values.Camera limits: The camera stays inside the box from 16.8 N to 19.6 N and from 69.5 W to 63.5 W, zooms out no further than level 5.5 and tilts up to 80 degrees.
values.Loading: In Snapshot 2026-10 the first screen loads the municipality statistics and boundaries, the routes, the stops and stations (transport.json), the operators and the service figures. The timetable replay and the storm tracks load after the first screen is drawn. The tourism places and every other layer load when you first switch them on.
values.Inside another page: When the page sits inside another page, the map takes two-finger gestures or Ctrl and scroll, so that the host page can still scroll.

entries.plain_es: La vista "3D + Tiempo" muestra a Puerto Rico como una escena 3D inclinada, con terreno y edificios, y tres relojes: un día de transporte colectivo, el nivel del mar por año y los huracanes desde 1851.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D + Tiempo: escena, pestañas y mapa base
entries.how_to_read_es: Use la vista 3D para ver cómo se sitúan los lugares en el terreno. Use el mapa 2D para las cifras, la pestaña Análisis y el chat.

entries.name: 3D buildings
entries.plain: The '3D buildings' switch raises building footprints to the height stored in the OpenFreeMap map tiles, which draw OpenStreetMap data. A building with no height value is drawn 6 metres tall.
entries.definition: The switch is on at the start. Buildings appear from zoom level 13. Each is a prism standing on the terrain. Its height is the render_height value in the OpenFreeMap tiles, and 6 metres where the tile has none. A building part raised above the ground starts at its minimum render height. Colour runs from light beige at 0 metres through grey-beige at 30 metres to darker brown-grey at 90 metres. Buildings are 85% opaque.

coverage.frequency: Tiles are requested live while you browse.

entries.method: twin3d.js (setupScene): a fill-extrusion layer on the 'building' layer of the base map's vector tiles.
entries.source_detail: Credit line on the map: '© OpenStreetMap contributors · © OpenMapTiles · OpenFreeMap'.
entries.how_to_read: Use it to see the scale of the built area. A tall prism means a height value in the tile, not a measured height.
caveats: Buildings that nobody mapped are missing. A mapped building with no height value is drawn at the default 6 metres, so a tall building can look low.

The heights come from the OpenFreeMap tiles. The observatory has not checked how OpenFreeMap sets the render_height value, so it cannot say whether a height was recorded by volunteers or estimated. The heights are not surveyed and must not be used for engineering.

view.label: 3D + Time view: San Juan

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Edificios en 3D" levanta la huella de cada edificio hasta la altura guardada en los mosaicos de mapa de OpenFreeMap, que dibujan datos de OpenStreetMap. Un edificio sin valor de altura se dibuja con 6 metros de alto.
entries.name_es: Edificios en 3D
entries.how_to_read_es: Úselo para ver la escala del área construida. Un prisma alto significa un valor de altura en el mosaico, no una altura medida.

entries.name: 3D terrain, relief shading and exaggeration
entries.plain: The '3D terrain' switch lifts the map into relief. The 'Terrain exaggeration' slider stretches the heights, from 1 to 3 times, so hills are easier to see.
entries.definition: The switch is on at the start. The slider runs from 1× to 3× in steps of 0.1 and starts at 1.3×. It stretches heights for display. Light and dark relief shading (hillshade) is always on, at a fixed strength. The map also draws a sky and haze at the horizon. Heights come from elevation tiles in the Mapzen 'terrarium' format, served by Amazon Web Services (AWS) Open Data, which hold data up to zoom level 15. Beyond that level the tiles are enlarged. Data layers such as flood zones, routes and land use are draped on the relief.

coverage.frequency: Tiles are requested live while you browse.

entries.method: twin3d.js (setupScene, setTerrain), with the terrain source, its Terrarium encoding and its credit read from site/js/core/basemap.js. The terrain source is https://s3.amazonaws.com/elevation-tiles-prod/terrarium.
entries.source_detail: Credit line on the map: 'Terrain: Mapzen / AWS Open Data · 3DEP, SRTM and GMTED2010 data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey · ETOPO1: NOAA', as the terrain tiles' attribution page asks.
entries.how_to_read: Read the relief as a picture of the land. Do not read heights off the screen.
caveats: Exaggeration changes the picture, not the data. Slopes look steeper than they are above 1×.
The license of the elevation tiles is in the AWS Open Data registry entry. Check it before you reuse the tiles.

view.label: 3D + Time view: El Yunque

entries.plain_es: El interruptor "Terreno en 3D" levanta el mapa en relieve. El control deslizante "Exageración del terreno" estira las alturas de 1 a 3 veces, para que las lomas se vean mejor.
entries.name_es: Terreno en 3D, sombreado del relieve y exageración
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea el relieve como una imagen del terreno. No mida alturas en la pantalla.

entries.name: 3D view: A day of transit (scheduled vehicles)
entries.plain: 'A day of transit' replays every scheduled weekday trip of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) and municipal timetables as a coloured trail that moves across the map. It is a timetable replay, not tracking by Global Positioning System (GPS).
entries.definition: The switch 'Scheduled vehicles' is on at the start. The clock runs from 00:00 to 23:59 and starts at 07:00. Speeds are 30×, 60× (one minute of clock each second, the start setting), 180× and 600×. The clock wraps around at midnight. A trail shows the last 7 minutes of each trip, fading behind the head. The colours are red for the Tren Urbano, gold for ATI buses, green for municipal buses and teal for ferries. These are not the route colours of the 3D map, where ATI buses are blue. The label beside the controls says 'N vehicles in service', counted once a minute of the clock as trips whose first stop time is at or before the clock and whose last stop time is at or after it. On a computer the replay starts by itself. On a phone, or when your device asks for reduced motion, it waits for Play.

coverage.frequency: Timetables are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time.

entries.method: twin3d.js (tripsLayer, tickBody). deck.gl draws the TripsLayer from trips.json, the weekday file of a typical Wednesday (3,297 trips from 25 operators in Snapshot 2026-10). Each trail follows its trip's route line (the operator's shape, or the roads the route is snapped to), timed between the stops that have a scheduled time (tripPoints in common.js). In Snapshot 2026-10, 3,191 of the 3,297 trips follow their route line; 106 whose stops fit no line of their route run in straight lines between stops.
entries.how_to_read: Read the trails as where the timetable says vehicles are at that time. A quiet map at night is a quiet timetable.
caveats: The replay includes trips of operators whose timetable has expired. In Snapshot 2026-10, 372 of the 3,297 weekday trips belong to operators whose feed had ended by the build date. The 2D map leaves them out.
Only the weekday file is used. The Saturday and Sunday files are not replayed in 3D, and holidays are not modelled.
No public real-time bus feed exists, so late or cancelled vehicles run on time here.
The credit line on the map names ATI only. In Snapshot 2026-10, 1,168 of the 3,297 weekday trips come from municipal feeds (ATI has 2,129), so credit the municipalities too when you cite.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Time tab, A day of transit

entries.source_detail: trips.json, Snapshot 2026-10: the weekday file, a typical Wednesday, with 3,297 trips. The shared attribution box on the map names 'ATI GTFS' (the timetable data of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, in General Transit Feed Specification format). The trails carry no credit line of their own.
entries.plain_es: "Un día de transporte colectivo" reproduce cada viaje con horario de un día de semana de la ATI (Autoridad de Transporte Integrado) y de los horarios municipales como una estela de color que avanza por el mapa. Es una reproducción de horarios, no un rastreo por GPS (sistema de posicionamiento global).
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: Un día de transporte colectivo (vehículos con horario)
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea las estelas como el lugar donde el horario dice que están los vehículos a esa hora. Un mapa tranquilo de noche es un horario tranquilo.

entries.name: 3D view: Columns by municipality
entries.plain: 'Columns by municipality' raises each municipality into a column whose height shows one measure. The menu has 33 measures (the 35 of the 2D map's shading less its three 'shown' measures, plus population change 2010 to 2020) and any dataset of the Analysis tab. The columns start off.
entries.definition: With a measure chosen, each municipality rises as a column standing on its own area. The column height is proportional to the value, starting at zero. The largest value reaches 14,000 display metres (12,000 for population change). These are map heights, not real heights. Colour follows five groups of about equal size, in the same light-to-dark blue as the 2D map. The legend under the menu shows three numbers: the lowest value, the second class limit (the value two fifths of the way along the sorted list) and the highest value. A click on a column, or on the municipality when columns are off, opens a card with a link to the 2D map. The codes below list the 33 measures and the card. A yes/no measure (whether Uber lists the municipality) raises the listed municipalities to one height and leaves the others as a flat grey sheet; rent change, which can fall, uses the red-to-blue scale of population change.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: twin3d.js (METRIC, setMetric, addMunicipalities). The menu lists the fields below.
entries.how_to_read: Read heights as 'more or less than other municipalities'. The tallest column is the largest value, not a target.
caveats: A value that equals a class limit takes the lower class in both the 3D view and the 2D map. The limits themselves can still differ for the shares of places near stops (see the caveat on municipalities with no stop counted).

In Snapshot 2026-10, 14 municipalities have no stop counted. The 3D view uses the stored shares of places near stops (any mapped stop, a stop with a current timetable, a frequent stop, only an expired or unscheduled stop) for every municipality, in the columns and on the card. For those 14 the stored value is 0% or close to it (0.5% for Toa Alta and 0.9% for Arroyo, for the shares near any mapped stop and near a stop with a current timetable), which means not measured. The 2D map leaves those 14 unshaded for those shares and works out their class limits from the other 64 municipalities, while 3D keeps all 78 in the limits, so the limits and a few colours of these shares can differ between the two views.
Tall columns hide what is behind them. Rotate or tilt the view.

Heights start at zero, so a column twice as tall is not twice as different when the values of all municipalities are close together. In Snapshot 2026-10 the affordability ratio, for example, runs only from 0.97 to 1.92.

When many municipalities share a value, several class limits are equal, and the classes between them stay empty, as in the 2D map. In Snapshot 2026-10 this happens for the measure 'Transit: % of residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (incl. expired timetables)' (40 of the 78 municipalities have 0%), for residents near a stop with a current timetable (46 at 0%) and for the shares of places near a stop with a current timetable (47), near a frequent stop (59) and near only an expired or unscheduled stop (33). The legend then repeats a number (for the first of these measures it reads 0%, 0% and 81%), but the colours and the heights follow the measure.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Layers tab, Territory, Columns by municipality

values.sfha_pct: % of places in flood hazard area.
values.transit_pct: % of places within 400 m of any mapped stop.
values.acc_cur400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable.
values.acc_freq400_pct: % of places within 400 m of a frequent stop (20+ weekday departures).
values.acc_paper_pct: % of places near only an expired or unscheduled stop.
values.pop_change_pct: Population change 2010 to 2020 (%). In Snapshot 2026-10 every municipality lost population (from −29.0% to −0.1%), so the scale is one-sided: column height and red shade show the size of the loss. If a measure had both gains and losses, red would mean loss and blue would mean gain.
values.affordability_ratio: Housing: affordability ratio (value divided by maximum loan).
values.pop_served_active_pct: Transit: % of residents within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable.
values.pop_served_pct: Transit: % of residents within 400 m of a scheduled stop (incl. expired timetables).
values.gross_rent_change_pct: Housing: rent change 2012 to the latest year (%). Column height is the size of the change; red is a fall, blue a rise.
values.pop_walk_active_pct: Transit: % of residents within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable.
values.pop_walk_pct: Transit: % of residents within a 400 m walk of a scheduled stop (incl. expired timetables).
values.uber_listed: Uber lists service (yes/no). Listed municipalities stand at one height; the others stay flat and grey. A listing on Uber's cities page, not measured coverage.
values.acc_walk400_pct: % of places within a 400 m walk of a stop with a current timetable.
values.acc_wfreq400_pct: % of places within a 400 m walk of a frequent stop (20+ weekday departures).
values.acc_walk800_pct: % of places within an 800 m walk of a stop with a current timetable.
values.acc_sat400_pct: % of places within 400 m (straight line) of a stop with Saturday service.
values.acc_sun400_pct: % of places within 400 m (straight line) of a stop with Sunday service.
values.Municipality card: The region, the residents (2020, and the change since 2010), the tourism places, the share in a flood hazard area, the share within 400 m of a stop with a current timetable and of any mapped stop, the stops and stations, the Tren Urbano stations, the airports and whether Uber lists the municipality.

entries.source_detail: municipalities.json (the fields named in the codes below) and municipios.geojson, joined in your browser. The shared attribution box on the map names 'US Census' and 'Places © Overture Maps Foundation', among other sources. See the entry on the 3D scene for the full line.
entries.plain_es: "Columnas por municipio" levanta cada municipio como una columna cuya altura muestra una medida. El menú tiene 33 medidas (las 35 del sombreado del mapa 2D menos sus tres medidas de lugares mostrados, más el cambio de población de 2010 a 2020) y cualquier conjunto de datos de la pestaña Análisis. Las columnas empiezan desactivadas.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: Columnas por municipio
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea las alturas como 'más o menos que otros municipios'. La columna más alta es el valor más grande, no una meta.

entries.name: 3D view: flood zones and sea level switches
entries.plain: In the 3D group Hazards and environment, 'Flood zones' drapes the flood zones of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) on the terrain. 'Sea level rise' draws a sea level layer whose height comes from the Time tab. Both are off when the page opens.
entries.definition: Flood zones are filled at 45% opacity with the same four colours as the 2D map. Red is for floodways, darkest blue for V and VE zones, mid blue for other Special Flood Hazard Area zones and light blue for the 0.2% annual chance zone. A click opens the 2D map's section for up to two zones under the click: the zone, whether it is a Special Flood Hazard Area (1% annual chance) or a 0.2% annual chance zone, the subtype spelled out and the credit 'FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer'. Where other areas are under the click too (land use, a protected area, a Comunidad Especial, a barrio), the same card has a section for each, as on the 2D map. The flood file (about 8 MB) downloads the first time you switch it on. The 'Sea level rise' switch draws the tile layer of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) at 70% opacity below the flood zones. The label beside it gives the feet and the year, for example '1 ft · 2050' (the start setting: Intermediate scenario, year 2050). The height comes from the year and scenario set in the Time tab. Choosing the Years clock switches this layer on by itself.

coverage.frequency: Flood zones are rebuilt with each snapshot. Sea level tiles are requested live from NOAA.

entries.method: twin3d.js (addFlood, setSlr, currentFeet); the card's section is floodPopup in access.js, which both views share. The flood filter keeps polygons in the Special Flood Hazard Area or in the 0.2% zone.
entries.source_detail: flood.geojson. The sea level tiles are streamed live from NOAA, and the year and scenario curves are typed into the page code. Credit lines on the map: 'FEMA NFHL' and 'Sea level rise: NOAA OCM' (the NOAA Office for Coastal Management).
entries.how_to_read: Read the flood zones as FEMA's mapped hazard. Read the sea level layer as a what-if at the chosen height.
caveats: Flood zones are mapped hazards, not predictions. They say nothing about a building's elevation or insurance.
The sea level layer is a screening tool. It is not a forecast for a year. See the sea level entries.
If NOAA's tiles do not answer, a message appears and the layer stays empty.

The flood zones are a simplified copy of FEMA's data for context. FEMA's printed flood maps and Flood Insurance Study are the official designation. This is not a flood determination for any property. Read the source's terms before you rely on it.

NOAA says the sea level layer shows water at the highest high tides and does not model storm surge, erosion, subsidence or new construction. NOAA calls it a planning reference that should not be used for navigation, permitting or other legal purposes.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Layers tab, Hazards

entries.plain_es: En el grupo "Riesgos y ambiente" de la vista 3D, "Zonas inundables" cubre el terreno con las zonas inundables de FEMA (Agencia Federal para el Manejo de Emergencias). "Aumento del nivel del mar" dibuja una capa de nivel del mar cuya altura viene de la pestaña "Tiempo". Ambos están desactivados al abrir la página.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: interruptores de zonas inundables y nivel del mar
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea las zonas inundables como el riesgo cartografiado por FEMA. Lea la capa del nivel del mar como un escenario hipotético a la altura elegida.

entries.name: 3D view: Hurricane controls
entries.plain: The Hurricane controls draw the tracks of storms that came within 250 kilometres of Puerto Rico since 1851. You can filter by years and strength, play them through time and open any storm from a list.
entries.definition: The switch 'Storm tracks within 250 km' is off at the start and shows the number of storms drawn. Two sliders set a year window from 1851 to 2025 (all years at the start). The menu 'Minimum category near PR' (Puerto Rico) offers All (including tropical storms), Hurricane (Category 1 or more), Major (Category 3 or more, the start setting) and Category 4 or more. In Snapshot 2026-10, at the start (Major), the map shows 29 of the 157 storms. Lines are coloured by the category near the island, and line width grows with the category. Dots mark recorded positions, coloured and sized by wind. Pointing at a line shows the name, the year, the category near Puerto Rico, the peak wind in knots and the closest approach in kilometres; a click on a line shows the same in a card (on a phone, which has no pointing). 'Strongest in window' lists up to 25 storms by category, then wind, then newest. A click on a row fits the map to that storm's whole track.
entries.geography: Atlantic storms within 250 km of Puerto Rico

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. NOAA adds each season after it ends.

entries.method: twin3d.js (stormsLayers, renderStormList, tickBody). deck.gl draws the lines and dots from hurricanes.json.
entries.source_detail: hurricanes.json, Snapshot 2026-10: 157 storms from 1851 to 2025. Credit line on the map: 'NOAA (SLR, HURDAT2)'. NOAA is the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, SLR is sea level rise and HURDAT2 is the Atlantic hurricane database of the NOAA National Hurricane Center.
entries.how_to_read: Thicker, darker lines are stronger near the island. A long line is the whole track, which can reach far from Puerto Rico.
caveats: Old tracks and winds are less certain than recent ones. Counts by decade are not a trend.
Lines join recorded positions with straight segments.
The list and the card label every category 0 storm 'Tropical storm'.
The minimum-category menu has no Category 2 or more choice.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Time tab, Hurricanes 1851–2025

values.0: Category 0, grey: tropical storm or depression strength near the island. 92 storms in Snapshot 2026-10.
values.5: Category 5, dark red. 5 storms in Snapshot 2026-10.
values.Play through the years: Moves a year forward 4 times each second and shows the storms of the chosen year and the 10 years before it (11 calendar years), with older ones fading. Dragging a window slider returns to the whole window.

entries.plain_es: Los controles de huracanes dibujan las trayectorias de las tormentas que pasaron a 250 kilómetros o menos de Puerto Rico desde 1851. Se puede filtrar por años y por fuerza, reproducirlas en el tiempo y abrir cualquier tormenta desde una lista.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: controles de huracanes
entries.how_to_read_es: Las líneas más gruesas y oscuras indican tormentas más fuertes cerca de la isla. Una línea larga es la trayectoria completa, que puede llegar muy lejos de Puerto Rico.

entries.name: 3D view: land use and protected areas
entries.plain: The 3D view can drape the Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 and the protected areas of the US Geological Survey (USGS) on the terrain. Both are off when the page opens.
entries.definition: Land use is drawn from the class colours stored in the file at 45% opacity, with water and road polygons left out. A click opens the 2D map's section: the class name, code and municipio, and the credit. In Snapshot 2026-10 the land-use file is about 17.7 MB and loads the first time you switch the layer on. Protected areas are green at 35% opacity with a dark green outline. A click opens the 2D map's section for up to two records under the click: the name, the designation spelled out (Local Park for LP, for example; a code the card does not know is shown as stored), the manager, the public access, the acres and the Gap Analysis Project (GAP) status. Overlapping areas share one card, with a section for each, as on the 2D map.

coverage.frequency: Land use is the plan version of 30 November 2015. Protected areas are PAD-US 4.1.

entries.method: twin3d.js (addLanduse, addProtected); the card's sections are landusePopup and protPopup in access.js, which both views share.
entries.source_detail: landuse.geojson and protected.geojson. Credit lines on the map: 'Junta de Planificación' for land use and 'USGS PAD-US' for protected areas (PAD-US is the Protected Areas Database of the United States).
entries.how_to_read: Use the drape to see the pattern. For the full meaning of a code, read the dictionary entry.
caveats: The land-use plan is a planning classification, not zoning, and dates from 2015.
'Protected' has a wide meaning. It includes recreation areas and military land.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Layers tab, Land use and Protected areas

entries.plain_es: La vista 3D puede cubrir el terreno con el Plan de Uso de Terrenos 2015 y con las áreas protegidas del USGS (Servicio Geológico de Estados Unidos). Ambas capas están desactivadas al abrir la página.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: uso de terrenos y áreas protegidas
entries.how_to_read_es: Use la capa sobre el terreno para ver el patrón. Para el significado completo de un código, lea la ficha del diccionario.

entries.name: 3D view: moving around, quick views and buttons
entries.plain: You move the 3D view with the mouse, with touch, with the keyboard or with the buttons at the right. Four quick-view buttons fly to San Juan, El Yunque, Ponce and the whole island.
entries.definition: The 3D view has four ways to move: the mouse, touch, the keyboard and the buttons at the right. The codes below describe each way and the four quick views. Letter keys steer the map only when nothing else has the focus.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: twin3d.js (NavPad, goHome, topDown, the keydown handler) with MapLibre's own controls. The quick views are the VIEWS list.
entries.how_to_read: Press the keyboard button in the controls to see these keys in the page.
caveats: Keyboard keys need the map or the page to have the focus. A key typed in a box does nothing to the map.

view.label: 3D + Time view

values.Mouse: Drag to pan, right-drag or Ctrl-drag to rotate and tilt, scroll to zoom, double-click to zoom in.
values.Touch: One finger pans, two fingers zoom and rotate, and two fingers dragged up or down together tilt.
values.Keyboard: Click the map first. Arrow keys pan, and Shift with arrow keys rotates and tilts. The + and − keys zoom. N turns north up. T looks straight down or returns to the tilted view. H shows the whole island. Q and E rotate 15 degrees. The / key jumps to the search box. Escape closes the keyboard help and stops a camera flight.
values.Buttons: Buttons at the right zoom in and out, and a compass resets north and shows the tilt. Other buttons rotate left and right (30 degrees each press), tilt up and down (10 degrees), look straight down or return, show the whole island, show keyboard help and 'find my location'.
values.Find my location: Asks your browser for your position when you press it. The observatory does not store or send it.
values.Reduced motion: If your device asks for reduced motion, camera moves are instant and the replay does not start by itself.
values.San Juan: Quick view: centre 18.44 N, 66.09 W, zoom 12.6, tilt 62°, rotated −20°.
values.El Yunque: Quick view: centre 18.30 N, 65.79 W, zoom 11.5, tilt 68°, rotated 30°.
values.Ponce: Quick view: centre 18.00 N, 66.61 W, zoom 12.5, tilt 60°, rotated 10°.
values.Island: Quick view of the whole island: centre 18.20 N, 66.45 W, zoom 8.4 (6.6 on a phone), tilt 50° (35° on a phone), rotated −8°.

entries.plain_es: La vista 3D se mueve con el ratón, con el tacto, con el teclado o con los botones de la derecha. Cuatro botones de vista rápida llevan la cámara en vuelo a San Juan, El Yunque, Ponce y toda la isla.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: cómo moverse, vistas rápidas y botones
entries.how_to_read_es: Presione el botón del teclado en los controles para ver estas teclas en la página.

entries.name: 3D view: Places layer
entries.plain: The 3D 'Tourism places' layer shows tourism places as a heat map from far away and as coloured points when you zoom in. Four category buttons filter them.
entries.definition: The layer holds the same places as the 2D map with confidence 0.50 or more and no places of worship (23,467 with a pin in Snapshot 2026-10, shown beside the switch once loaded; holiday rentals are counted but not drawn). The layer starts switched off: its file (about 2.8 MB compressed) loads the first time it is switched on, and from then the place search also lists tourism places. The 'Render as' menu offers 'Heat at island scale, points when zoomed' (start), 'Points' and 'Heat'. Points show from zoom level 10.5 (everywhere in 'Points' mode), grow as you zoom and take the category colour. A point inside a Special Flood Hazard Area of the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) has a dark blue rim. The heat map adds one unit for each place and fades out between zoom levels 11 and 13. A click on a point opens a card with the name, the type, the municipality, the flood zone when the place is in a hazard area, the access badge and the distance to the nearest stop with a current timetable (the same lines as the 2D pop-up), and the credit 'Overture Maps'.

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt with each snapshot. Transit data are refreshed every night.

entries.method: twin3d.js (addPlaces, updatePlacesMode, placesFilter). The filter keeps places of the chosen categories, with a confidence of at least 0.50, that are not places of worship.
entries.source_detail: places.json. Credit line on the map: 'Places © Overture Maps Foundation'.
entries.how_to_read: Use the heat to see where visitor places cluster. Use the points to see single places.
caveats: In 'Heat' mode the heat fades out between zoom levels 11 and 13, so a close-up shows no places.
Overture listings can be missing, duplicated or out of date. The 3D view has no confidence slider and no worship switch.
The 3D view does not recalculate flags when you change a button. The rim and the card come from the build and from the stored access columns.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Places layer, San Juan

entries.plain_es: La capa "Lugares turísticos" de la vista 3D muestra los lugares turísticos como un mapa de calor desde lejos y como puntos de colores al acercar el mapa. Cuatro botones de categoría los filtran.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: capa Lugares
entries.how_to_read_es: Use el mapa de calor para ver dónde se concentran los lugares para visitantes. Use los puntos para ver lugares individuales.

entries.name: 3D view: route planner and fly-along
entries.plain: The Route tab of the 3D view plans a route like the 2D planner, drapes it on the terrain and can fly the camera along it.
entries.definition: The boxes, buttons and results are the same as in the 2D planner. The route is drawn as a dark line with a white edge. A leg that cannot follow roads is a red dotted line. Lettered markers can be dragged. After a route is planned a button 'Fly along the route' appears. The camera then follows the line at tilt 64 degrees and zoom 14.8, turning to face ahead, and covers the route in about 45 seconds, at a speed between 120 and 1,500 metres per second. A mouse press, a touch, the wheel or Escape stops the flight, and the button reads 'Stop flying' while it runs. If your device asks for reduced motion, the flight does not start and a message says why. The chosen points are kept in the page address as r=.

coverage.frequency: Computed in your browser each time you plan a route.

entries.method: twin3d.js (planHost, flyAlong) with plan.js. The route is drawn as fresh map layers each time it changes, and the routes layer is refreshed so that the whole route shows on the terrain.
entries.how_to_read: Fly along a route to see what it passes. Read the numbers on the card with the 2D planner's entries.
caveats: A flight is a visual aid. It is not a drive time. The running time on the card uses planning speeds.
The planner's other limits apply. See the route planner entry.

The address holds the exact coordinates of every point, to about 11 metres. If a start, end or stop is your home or workplace, anyone with the link can see it. Remove the r= part before you share a link, or use points that are not private.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Route tab with an example route

entries.plain_es: La pestaña "Ruta" de la vista 3D planifica una ruta igual que el planificador 2D, la coloca sobre el terreno y puede llevar la cámara en vuelo a lo largo de ella.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: planificador de rutas y vuelo por la ruta
entries.how_to_read_es: Vuele por una ruta para ver por dónde pasa. Lea las cifras de la tarjeta con las fichas del planificador 2D.

entries.name: 3D view: Sea level by year
entries.plain: The 'Sea level by year' controls turn a year and a scenario of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) into the sea level layer. Pick a year from 2020 to 2150 and one of four scenarios, and the map shows the matching NOAA layer.
entries.definition: The year slider runs from 2020 to 2150 in steps of 5 and starts at 2050. The scenario menu offers Intermediate-Low, Intermediate (start), Intermediate-High and High, the NOAA 2022 scenarios. A note says, for example, '2050 · Intermediate ≈ 1.0 ft (0.30 m) above the 2000 baseline → showing the NOAA 1 ft layer'. The height is rounded to whole feet and held between 1 and 10 feet. Moving either control swaps the layer when the height in whole feet changes. Play moves the year forward 12 years each second until 2150, then stops. Pressing Play again at 2150 restarts at 2020. Playing needs the Years clock, and choosing it switches the layer on.

coverage.frequency: NOAA's tiles are requested live. The scenario curves are fixed in the page code.

entries.method: twin3d.js (currentFeet, setSlr, the year and scenario handlers). The conversion from year and scenario to feet is described in the entry 'Sea level rise by year and scenario'.
entries.how_to_read: Read a year as a position on a scenario curve. Several years show the same layer, because heights are rounded to whole feet.
caveats: The curves are global average sea level above the 2000 level, read approximately from the tables of NOAA's 2022 report and typed into the page. They are not NOAA's published values for Puerto Rico.
The map is a what-if at a height, not a forecast for a year.
The note on the page calls the scenarios 'planning what-ifs'.
The layer never shows less than 1 ft, so the first years show more water than the scenario gives (see the entry 'Sea level rise by year and scenario').
The layer never shows more than 10 ft, so the highest part of the High scenario is capped (see the same entry).

NOAA says the sea level layer shows water at the highest high tides and does not model storm surge, erosion, subsidence or new construction. NOAA calls it a planning reference that should not be used for navigation, permitting or other legal purposes.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Time tab, Sea level by year

values.Scenario curves: The four curves (metres above the 2000 level for 2020, 2050, 2100 and 2150) are listed in the entry 'Sea level rise by year and scenario'.

entries.source_detail: twin3d.js, SCENARIOS: the curves, typed into the page from NOAA's 2022 report (no data file). The layer itself is NOAA's tile service. Credit line on the map: 'Sea level rise: NOAA OCM' (the NOAA Office for Coastal Management).
entries.plain_es: Los controles de "Nivel del mar por año" convierten un año y un escenario de NOAA (Administración Nacional Oceánica y Atmosférica) en la capa de nivel del mar. Elija un año de 2020 a 2150 y uno de los cuatro escenarios, y el mapa muestra la capa de NOAA correspondiente.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: Nivel del mar por año
entries.how_to_read_es: Lea un año como una posición en la curva de un escenario. Varios años muestran la misma capa, porque las alturas se redondean a pies enteros.

entries.name: 3D view: the time bar and the three clocks
entries.plain: A bar at the bottom of the 3D view has a play button, a label, a slider and three buttons that choose the clock: Day, Years or Storms.
entries.definition: Day: the slider runs from 00:00 to 23:59 in one-minute steps and the label reads like '07:00 · weekday transit'. Years: the slider runs from 2020 to 2150 in steps of 5 and the label reads like '2050 · Intermediate sea level'. Storms: the slider runs over the storm window and the label reads like '2024 · storms, trailing 10 years'. The window is the chosen year and the 10 years before it (11 calendar years). Choosing Years switches the sea level layer on. Choosing Storms switches the storm tracks on. Leaving Years switches off a sea level layer that Years switched on, but not one you switched on yourself. Play advances the Day clock at the chosen speed, the Years clock by 12 years each second and the Storms clock by 4 years each second. The Years and Storms clocks stop at their end. The Day clock wraps around at midnight. The Time tab in the side panel has the same controls with explanations. The three clocks are independent: each keeps its own value.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: twin3d.js (setMode, tick, togglePlay, syncClock). Animation uses the browser's frame timer. A long pause between frames (for example a background tab) counts as at most a quarter of a second of play.
entries.how_to_read: Press Play on a clock, then change the clock with the buttons to compare.
caveats: The clocks do not move together. The Day clock is a time of day, not a date.

view.label: 3D + Time view: time bar

values.Day: The transit replay clock. See 'A day of transit'.
values.Years: The sea level clock. See 'Sea level by year'.

entries.plain_es: Una barra en la parte inferior de la vista 3D tiene un botón para reproducir, una etiqueta, un control deslizante y tres botones que eligen el reloj: "Día", "Años" o "Tormentas".
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: la barra de tiempo y los tres relojes
entries.how_to_read_es: Presione Reproducir en un reloj y luego cambie de reloj con los botones para comparar.

entries.name: 3D view: transit routes, stops, stations and taxi stands
entries.plain: The 3D Mobility section draws transit routes (on at the start) and, if you switch them on, stops, stations, terminals and airports, taxi stands and EV chargers and the 400 m walk rings, as the 2D map does. Another switch controls the vehicle replay.
entries.definition: Routes use the operator colours of the 2D map: Tren Urbano red (4 pixels), buses of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) blue, municipal systems green, públicos gold and ferries teal (2.5 pixels). All other lines are 2 pixels. Dashed lines mean the feed lists stops out of order. Dotted lines mean no road path was found. Width does not change with trips. A click opens a card with the route name, the operator, the route label, weekday trips, how the line was drawn and the credit. Stations show as dots: Tren Urbano red, ferry terminals teal, bus stations and airports charcoal, with airports slightly larger. A click on a station opens the same card as on the 2D map (name, kind, municipality, routes, modes, departures, timetable dates, operator and source). Stops, taxi stands and EV chargers and the walk rings are the 2D map's layers, with the same cards: see the entries of their switches, which both views share.

coverage.frequency: Feeds are re-read every night at 04:17 Puerto Rico time.

entries.method: twin3d.js (addRoutes, addHubs, addStops, addTaxi, addRings). The files are transit_routes.geojson and transport.json; the cards are transportPopup in access.js.
entries.how_to_read: Compare the line style with the 2D legend to see how a line was drawn.
caveats: Routes of operators whose timetable has expired stay on the map.
A route in a feed is not proof that the service runs today.

The credit line on the map names the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado (ATI) only. In Snapshot 2026-10, municipal feeds supply most routes: 127 of the 165 routes are not ATI routes, and 111 of them are municipal. The route card names the right source (ATI, a municipal feed or OpenStreetMap). The station card names its source, as on the 2D map. Of the 145 stations, terminals and airports in Snapshot 2026-10, 29 bus stations come from municipal feeds, 65 points (47 bus stations, 7 ferry terminals and 11 airports) from OpenStreetMap and 14 airports from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). Credit those sources too when you cite.

view.label: 3D + Time view: Layers tab, Mobility

entries.source_detail: transit_routes.geojson (routes) and transport.json (kinds bus_station, rail_station, ferry_terminal and airport). The shared attribution box on the map names, for transit, 'ATI GTFS' (the timetable data of the Autoridad de Transporte Integrado, in General Transit Feed Specification format) and 'OpenFreeMap © OpenStreetMap contributors'.
entries.plain_es: La sección "Infraestructura y movilidad" de la vista 3D dibuja las rutas de transporte colectivo (activadas al inicio) y, si se activan, las paradas, las estaciones, terminales y aeropuertos, las paradas de taxis y la carga de vehículos eléctricos y los radios de 400 m a pie, como el mapa 2D. Otro interruptor controla la reproducción de vehículos.
entries.name_es: Vista 3D: rutas, paradas y estaciones de transporte colectivo y paradas de taxis
entries.how_to_read_es: Compare el estilo de la línea con la leyenda del mapa 2D para ver cómo se trazó una línea.

entries.name: Area profile page (profile.html)
entries.plain: One page for each municipio with every dataset of the observatory for that place, grouped by field, with its rank among the 78 municipios, Puerto Rico's value and its trend.
entries.definition: Open it from a municipality on the map (the pop-up's 'Area profile' link or the Municipality tab) or as profile.html?area= and the municipio's five-digit code (72127 is San Juan). The page reads the same files as the Analysis tab. Each field of the registry has a table; each row is a dataset with its latest value as published and its margin of error, the value a shaded map compares (per 1,000 residents, per resident or a share), its rank among the municipios that have a value (1 is the highest), Puerto Rico's value on the same measure, and a trend line of up to 15 years. Datasets with no value for the place are left out, unless an empty place has a meaning (a shortage area: 'No area shortage designation'). A small map marks the municipio and its five similar municipios. 'Download CSV' saves the rows.

coverage.frequency: Built in your browser from the published files of the snapshot

entries.method: profile.js with Core.datasets (the list of files the Analysis tab also reads), Core.engine, Core.stats and Core.minimap. The page draws its first field (Housing) and the similar municipios as soon as their files arrive, then fetches the other files and draws every field; until then it says it is loading the other fields, and 'Download CSV' waits for them.
entries.how_to_read: A rank says where the place stands among the municipios, not whether that is good: rank 1 in poverty is the highest poverty.
caveats: Datasets of different years sit side by side: read each row's year.
Survey values have margins of error; read them before comparing two places.

view.label: Area profile of San Juan

entries.plain_es: Una página por municipio con todos los conjuntos de datos del observatorio para ese lugar, agrupados por campo, con su posición entre los 78 municipios, el valor de Puerto Rico y su tendencia.

entries.name: Ask the observatory (chat)
entries.plain: 'Ask the observatory' is a chat box that answers questions about the Analysis tab's datasets, in English or Spanish. It is not a language model. Every answer is built from numbers computed in your browser, and nothing you type leaves your browser unless you choose to open the GitHub request form.
entries.definition: 'Ask the observatory' answers questions about the datasets of the Analysis tab (549 in Snapshot 2026-10) and the map layers, in English or Spanish. Type up to 400 characters. Each answer is in the language of the question. A reply can hold text, small tables, links and buttons. It can also change the map: shade datasets, switch on layers, set the year, select a municipality, move the map to a place, shade the barrios of a municipality or open the workbench. When the observatory has no data for what you ask, the answer shows the nearest dataset and says that it is an approximation and what is missing. A question the chat cannot match, or answers only with an approximation, is saved on your device in a wishlist without asking, so do not type personal information. The codes below describe how to open it, what it remembers and what it can and cannot answer.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: chat.js and ask.js. 1. The question is cleaned: accents and capitals are removed. In a short question, a word one letter from a topic of the observatory is read as that topic (two letters from eight letters on), and the answer says so. 2. Municipality names are found, and some well-known place names (Santurce, Isla Verde, Levittown) with their municipality. 3. chat.js's word list turns words into dataset keys, from specific phrases to general ones. 4. ask.js (loaded with the first question) reads the question again with a lexicon of everyday words in both languages, Puerto Rican ones included (guagua, carro público, la AMA, la AAA, la luz, cuido, chavos, derrumbes, envejecientes), the names of the map layers, the glossary terms and the words of the datasets' own names. It finds the topics that step 3 left, the layers, a time ("después de María" is 2017) and what must not be drawn. 5. Two topics are composed: a topic that a map layer shows (transit) turns that layer on, the other is shaded, and the answer gives the correlation of the two across municipalities. 6. Rules choose the kind of answer (see the entry on answer types). 7. A handler computes the answer from the Analysis tab's dataset values and writes the sentences from templates, with the source, period and geography of what it shows. No server is called. No language model is used.
entries.how_to_read: Ask short questions that name a dataset: 'unemployment', 'rent', 'tourism jobs'. Add a municipality or a year to narrow the answer.
caveats: The chat matches words. An unusual phrasing can still fail, and a word can match a dataset by chance: the word 'bar', for example, selects restaurant and bar jobs.
Answers find patterns across places. They do not show causes.
An approximation is not the measure you asked for: the answer names what is missing (for example, there are no traffic data, so commutes of 45 minutes or more stand in).
Transit layers and vehicles follow scheduled timetables (GTFS), not live positions.

An answer that puts datasets on the map replaces the layers on the Analysis tab. It also switches off tourism places, transit routes, barrios, flood zones, protected areas and land use, unless the question names them. A question that names only layers adds them and leaves the rest as it is.
Sensitive places are counted, never drawn: the chat never shows shelters for victims of violence, a person's home or contact details, or health facilities as points.
When the chat saves a question, its reply says it added the request 'so the team can see what people ask for'. The request stays on your device unless you copy it or open the GitHub form.

view.label: 2D map: press 'Ask' in the top bar

values.Opening it: Press the 'Ask' button in the top bar of the 2D map, or a suggested question in the About tab. The window's language follows your browser at first and changes with the 'ES' or 'EN' button. The bin button clears the conversation.
