coverage.frequency: Rebuilt only when the place-name index is rebuilt, from the OpenStreetMap extract downloaded for the road network; not on a fixed schedule

entries.method: 1. Read OpenStreetMap nodes and ways that have a name and a matching tag. Place tags (town, city, village, hamlet, suburb, neighbourhood, quarter, locality, island, islet) are read from points only. Ways that are not roads are placed at the average of their corner points. 2. Add one row for each municipality and each barrio in the published boundaries. 3. Give each name its municipality by point-in-polygon (checking which boundary contains the point) on the municipality boundaries. A point offshore (a pier or a cay) goes to the nearest municipality when it is within about 2 km (0.02 degree); any other name outside every municipality is dropped. 4. For roads, give each way to the municipality that holds its middle point (the middle mapped point by count of points, not by length). Group ways by name and municipality, place the row at that middle point of the longest piece, and drop street names whose pieces total less than 60 m. A road with a Puerto Rico (PR) route number but no name is also read. Route numbers are taken from the ref tag (the first one, for example PR-52, with an optional letter) and grouped the same way, with the road's local name as the note. Highway numbers are not dropped for length. 5. Drop exact repeats: the same name (ignoring accents and capitals), the same type, and latitude and longitude that are equal when rounded to 3 decimals (cells of about 110 m). 6. Sort by type, then name, round coordinates to 5 decimals and write the file.
entries.source_detail: gazetteer.py (read, main); municipality boundaries from US Census Bureau TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (Counties 500K) and barrio boundaries from TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD MapServer layer 7 (County Subdivisions 500K), both shoreline-clipped (municipios.geojson, barrios.geojson)
entries.how_to_read: A road has one point for each municipality in which the middle point of one of its mapped pieces lies, placed at the middle point of its longest piece there, so the point may not be where you expect. In the 2026-10 snapshot the boundaries give 78 municipality rows and 901 barrio rows.
caveats: The index uses the OpenStreetMap 'name' tag only. Alternative names and translations are not read.
Place polygons mapped as relations are not read.
Place tags (town, city, village, hamlet, suburb, neighbourhood, quarter, locality, island, islet) are read from points only. A place mapped only as an area (a closed way) is not in the index.
The note on a place is the OpenStreetMap place type, for example hamlet or suburb. It is not an official classification.
entries.plain_es: El índice parte de los nombres de OpenStreetMap y agrega filas del Censo para los municipios y los barrios. Cada nombre recibe un municipio. Una calle mapeada en varios pedazos que caen en municipios distintos tiene una fila en cada uno.
entries.name_es: Cómo se construye el índice de nombres de lugares
entries.how_to_read_es: Una carretera tiene un punto por cada municipio en el que cae el punto medio de uno de sus tramos cartografiados, colocado en el punto medio de su tramo más largo en ese municipio, así que el punto puede no estar donde se espera. En el corte de datos 2026-10, los límites dan 78 filas de municipio y 901 filas de barrio.

entries.name: Place-name index
entries.plain: A list of named places, streets, highway numbers and landmarks (48,450 names in the 2026-10 snapshot), each with a point on the map. The search boxes and the route planner look names up in it, inside your browser.
entries.definition: The file has three parts. 'munis' lists the 78 municipality names in alphabetical order. 'kinds' lists the 19 type codes in a fixed order. 'items' lists the names. Each item is [name, latitude, longitude, kind number, municipality number] with an optional sixth value, a note. The kind number and the municipality number are positions in the 'kinds' and 'munis' lists. Items are sorted by kind, then by name without accents.
entries.unit: Rows of name, point and codes (counts of names); latitude and longitude in decimal degrees rounded to 5 places (about 1 m)
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: 78 municipalities, with places on Vieques, Culebra and Mona Island

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt only when the place-name index is rebuilt, from the OpenStreetMap extract downloaded for the road network; not on a fixed schedule

entries.method: gazetteer.py reads named points and ways from the OpenStreetMap extract, adds the municipality and barrio boundaries from the Census Bureau (TIGERweb generalized 500k, shoreline-clipped), gives each name its municipality by point-in-polygon (checking which boundary contains the point), and writes one compact file. The entries on kinds and on how the index is built give the rules.
entries.source_detail: OpenStreetMap, Geofabrik Puerto Rico extract with data timestamp 2026-10-01T20:22:06Z; municipality boundaries from US Census Bureau TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (Counties 500K) and barrio boundaries from TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD MapServer layer 7 (County Subdivisions 500K), both shoreline-clipped (municipios.geojson, barrios.geojson)
entries.how_to_read: The index holds names with one point each. It has no house numbers or postal addresses. It does not hold the tourism listings; the pages search those separately.
caveats: Names are as OpenStreetMap volunteers wrote them. Spelling, capital letters and abbreviations vary.
Only OpenStreetMap points and ways are read. A place mapped only as a multi-part area (a relation) is missing.
Place tags (place=village, hamlet, suburb, neighbourhood, island and so on) are read from points only. A place mapped only as an area (a closed way) is not in the index.

A road name has one row for each municipality that holds the middle point of at least one of its mapped pieces (OpenStreetMap ways). A road mapped as several pieces usually has a row in each municipality it crosses. A single piece that crosses a boundary counts only where its middle point lies, so a long road mapped as one piece has one row.
A road or place that is not mapped with a name in OpenStreetMap is not in the index.

License: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0. Credit line: Data © OpenStreetMap contributors, available under the Open Database License (ODbL). Read the terms at openstreetmap.org/copyright before reusing the names.

values.munis: List of the 78 municipality names, sorted alphabetically without accents. A row's municipality number is its position in this list, starting at 0.
values.kinds: List of the 19 type codes: municipio, town, village, barrio, neighborhood, road, route, hospital, school, university, civic, transport, park, beach, peak, water, landmark, airport, mall. A row's kind number is its position in this list, starting at 0.
values.items: List of rows [name, latitude, longitude, kind number, municipality number] with an optional note as a sixth value. In the 2026-10 snapshot, 7,506 rows carry a note.

view.label: Map: the search box in the header and the Plan a route boxes in the Transit tab

entries.plain_es: Una lista de lugares con nombre, calles, números de carretera y puntos de referencia (48,450 nombres en el corte de datos de 2026-10), cada uno con un punto en el mapa. Los buscadores y el planificador de rutas buscan los nombres en ella, dentro del propio navegador.
entries.name_es: Índice de nombres de lugares
entries.how_to_read_es: El índice contiene nombres con un punto cada uno. No tiene números de casa ni direcciones postales. No contiene los listados turísticos; las páginas los buscan por separado.

entries.name: Place-name types
entries.plain: Each name in the place-name index has one of 19 types, such as municipality, street, highway number, hospital or beach. The type sets how the name is ranked and labelled in search results.
entries.definition: The kind is a number in each row of the index: its position in the 'kinds' list. The observatory's pages show a plain label for it in search results and rank some types ahead of others (a municipality ahead of a street).
entries.unit: Type code (19 values) and count of names
entries.geography: Puerto Rico: 78 municipalities, with places on Vieques, Culebra and Mona Island

coverage.frequency: Rebuilt only when the place-name index is rebuilt, from the OpenStreetMap extract downloaded for the road network; not on a fixed schedule

entries.method: gazetteer.py assigns the type from OpenStreetMap tags. For a named point it tests place, amenity, natural, historic, aeroway, leisure and shop, in that order. For a named area that is not a road it tests amenity, leisure, natural, aeroway, shop and historic. Roads are ways with a highway tag and a name or a PR route number. The first match wins. Place tags are read from points only. Only OpenStreetMap points and ways are read; the municipality and barrio rows come from Census Bureau boundaries (TIGERweb generalized, 500k, shoreline-clipped).
entries.source_detail: gazetteer.py (KINDS, PLACE_KIND, AMENITY, LEISURE, NATURAL, HISTORIC, ROAD_CLASSES); labels from site/js/plan.js (KIND_INFO); municipality boundaries from US Census Bureau TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 State_County MapServer layer 11 (Counties 500K) and barrio boundaries from TIGERweb Generalized_ACS2023 Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD MapServer layer 7 (County Subdivisions 500K), both shoreline-clipped (municipios.geojson, barrios.geojson)
entries.how_to_read: The counts show what OpenStreetMap volunteers have named. A low count can mean that few features exist or that few are mapped with a name. For example, the 2026-10 snapshot has 32 airport rows.
caveats: The types follow OpenStreetMap tags, not official categories. A clinic is filed under 'hospital'; a marina, a bay and an island mapped as a point are filed under 'water'.
Tourism listings (restaurants, hotels, attractions) are not part of this index.
The 'barrio' rows come from Census boundaries, not from OpenStreetMap.

values.municipio: Municipality. 78 rows, one per municipality. The point is the location of the OpenStreetMap town or city of the same name when it lies inside the boundary, otherwise a point inside the boundary. Search shows it as 'Municipality'.
values.town: Town or city: a point tagged place=town or place=city, except towns named like a municipality (those are the municipality rows). In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2 rows. Search shows it as 'Town'.
values.village: Small community: a point tagged place=village or place=hamlet. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 3,102 rows, all tagged hamlet. The note holds the OpenStreetMap place type. Search shows it as 'Community'.
values.barrio: Barrio (a division of a municipality): the barrio boundaries from the Census Bureau (TIGERweb county subdivisions; 901 in the 2026-10 snapshot), written as 'Barrio' followed by the name and placed at a point inside the boundary. The note holds the barrio name alone. Search shows it as 'Barrio'.
values.neighborhood: Neighbourhood: a point tagged place=suburb, neighbourhood, quarter or locality. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 2,277 rows. The note holds the place type. Search shows it as 'Neighborhood'.
values.road: Named street: a way with a name and highway=motorway, trunk, primary, secondary, tertiary, unclassified, residential, living_street or pedestrian. One row for each name and each municipality that holds the middle point of at least one of the name's pieces; names whose pieces total less than 60 m are dropped. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 34,781 rows. Search shows it as 'Street'.
values.route: Highway number: Puerto Rico (PR) route numbers read from the ref tag, for example PR-52. One row for each number and each municipality that holds the middle point of at least one of its pieces. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,679 rows, of which 1,224 carry a note with the road's local name. Search shows it as 'Highway'.
values.hospital: Hospital or clinic: amenity=hospital or clinic. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 372 rows. Search shows it as 'Hospital'.
values.school: School: amenity=school. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,679 rows. Search shows it as 'School'.
values.university: College or university: amenity=college or university. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 99 rows. Search shows it as 'College'.
values.civic: Public building: amenity=townhall, courthouse, police, fire_station, library, community_centre or post_office. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 704 rows. Search shows it as 'Public building'.
values.transport: Terminal: amenity=bus_station or ferry_terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 82 rows. Search shows it as 'Terminal'.
values.park: Park or sports ground: leisure=park, stadium, nature_reserve, sports_centre or golf_course. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 1,451 rows. Search shows it as 'Park'.
values.beach: Beach: natural=beach. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 195 rows. Search shows it as 'Beach'.
values.peak: Mountain: natural=peak or volcano. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 308 rows. Search shows it as 'Mountain'.
values.water: Water feature: leisure=marina, natural=bay or cape, or a point tagged place=island or islet. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 172 rows. Search shows it as 'Water'.
values.landmark: Landmark: amenity=theatre or arts_centre, natural=cave_entrance, or historic=castle, fort, monument, memorial, ruins, lighthouse, archaeological_site, building or church. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 470 rows. Search shows it as 'Landmark'.
values.airport: Airport: aeroway=aerodrome or terminal. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 32 rows. Search shows it as 'Airport'.
values.mall: Shopping centre: shop=mall or amenity=marketplace. In the 2026-10 snapshot: 66 rows. Search shows it as 'Shopping center'.

entries.plain_es: Cada nombre del índice de lugares tiene uno de 19 tipos, como municipio, calle, número de carretera, hospital o playa. El tipo decide en qué orden aparece el nombre en los resultados de búsqueda y cómo se rotula.
entries.name_es: Tipos de nombres de lugares
entries.how_to_read_es: Los conteos muestran lo que han nombrado las personas voluntarias de OpenStreetMap. Un conteo bajo puede significar que existen pocos elementos o que pocos están cartografiados con nombre. Por ejemplo, el corte de datos 2026-10 tiene 32 filas de aeropuerto.

entries.name: Search box (2D map, 3D view and route planner)
entries.plain: The search box at the top finds municipalities, barrios, towns, streets, Puerto Rico (PR) highway numbers, landmarks, transit stops and routes, and tourism places. What you type is matched in your browser, except when you choose the online address lookup.
entries.definition: Press / to jump to the box. Results start after 2 characters, and up to 12 are listed, each with an icon, a label and a line of detail. The arrow keys move through the list, Enter picks the first or the focused result, and Escape closes it. Two decimal numbers such as 18.4655, -66.1057 are read as coordinates. After 4 characters the list ends with 'Look up ... as an address online'. A pick flies the map there and drops a pin whose popup has 'Route from here' and 'Route to here'. What the box searches and what a pick does are listed below.

coverage.frequency: The place-name index is rebuilt with each full build. Stops and routes are re-read every night.

entries.method: plan.js (parseQuery, textScore, Gaz, attachSearch, searchEverything), shared by the 2D and 3D pages. Names are compared without accents or capitals. The online lookup asks nominatim.openstreetmap.org for up to 6 results inside a box around Puerto Rico (countrycodes=pr, bounded) and shows the first two parts of each address.
entries.how_to_read: Type part of a name. If a street has several matches, add the municipality.
caveats: The online address lookup sends the text you typed to OpenStreetMap's Nominatim service, which has its own usage policy. It runs only when you pick that line. Nothing else you type leaves the page.
A misspelling finds nothing. Matching is on letters, after accents and capitals are removed.

The 2D tourism results follow your category, confidence and worship filters, so a place can be missing because a filter hides it. They appear only once the tourism place listings are loaded: until then the last line of the results offers to load them (about 3.0 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10).

view.label: 2D map: search box
3D view: search box

values.Places and areas: Municipalities and the place-name index. The index holds towns, communities, barrios, neighbourhoods, PR highways, named streets, hospitals, schools, colleges, public buildings, terminals, parks, beaches, mountains, water, landmarks, airports and shopping centres.
values.Tourism places: Searched by name or type. On the 2D map the box follows the current category, confidence and worship filters. In the 3D view it follows the category buttons, confidence 0.50 and no places of worship.
values.Transit: Scheduled stops, stations, terminals and airports by name. The header box also searches transit routes by number, name or operator. The planner's boxes search the same list without routes.
values.A pick on the 2D map: A municipality opens its profile, a tourism place opens its card, a stop opens its card and a route fits on the screen.
values.A pick in the 3D view: The camera flies to the result, or fits the municipality or route, and a pin card opens.

entries.plain_es: El buscador de la parte superior encuentra municipios, barrios, pueblos, calles, números de carreteras de Puerto Rico (PR), lugares emblemáticos, paradas y rutas de transporte colectivo, y lugares turísticos. Lo que se escribe se busca en el navegador, excepto cuando se elige la búsqueda de direcciones en línea.
entries.name_es: Cuadro de búsqueda (mapa 2D, vista 3D y planificador de rutas)
entries.how_to_read_es: Escriba parte de un nombre. Si una calle tiene varias coincidencias, agregue el municipio.

entries.name: CSV and GeoJSON downloads
entries.plain: Six buttons on the map and Housing pages save data as files: a municipality table, the places of a municipality, two economy tables, a housing table and a planned route. These files are made in your browser. The data dictionary page adds two more download buttons and a download link for each published data file.
entries.definition: All comma-separated values (CSV) files are UTF-8 with a byte-order mark, so that Excel shows accents correctly. Cells are separated by commas, and text that holds a comma, a quote or a line break is put in quotes. A text cell that starts with =, +, - or @ gets a leading apostrophe, so that a spreadsheet does not run it as a formula. Empty cells mean no value. The buttons are listed below with the file each one saves.

coverage.frequency: Made from the data of the latest build each time you press the button.

entries.method: app.js (downloadCsv), economy.js (ecSaveCsv), housing.js (saveCsv) and plan.js (download). On the dictionary page, dictionary.js (downloadSeries, downloadDictionary, saveCsv) does the same. Files are built in the browser and nothing is uploaded.
entries.how_to_read: Cite the stored values in the files, not the rounded numbers on screen. Add the snapshot label and the date you downloaded them. A file has no citation of its own. Use the Cite button on the dictionary entries of the datasets it holds.
caveats: The files carry the licenses of their sources. Check each source's terms before you reuse or publish a file.
The places file can include helper columns whose names start with an underscore. They are search aids and can be ignored.
A file records what the page held when you pressed the button. Filters and settings on screen change what a places or table file holds.

view.label: 2D map: Rankings tab
Housing page: Data catalog
Data dictionary page: download buttons

values.Download municipality table (CSV): Rankings tab. File pr_digital_twin_municipalities_<snapshot label>.csv, for example pr_digital_twin_municipalities_Snapshot_2026-10.csv. One row for each of the 78 municipalities with every field of municipalities.json. Nested fields (places by category, land use in km²) become columns named with their parent. In Snapshot 2026-10 eight shares of places are blank for the 14 municipalities with no stop counted: transit_pct, acc_cur400_pct, acc_cur800_pct, acc_freq400_pct, acc_sat400_pct, acc_sun400_pct, acc_hub400_pct and acc_paper_pct. The other access fields (the stop counts by state, access_n and access_as_of) are included.
values.Download <municipality> places (CSV): Municipality tab. File <municipality>_places.csv. The button loads the place listings first when they are not loaded yet (about 3.0 MB compressed in Snapshot 2026-10). One row for each place the map is showing in that municipality, so it follows the category buttons, the confidence slider and the worship switch. Columns are the fields of places.json and, when the access file has loaded, ts_m, ts_calls and ts_we of place_access.json. A column named id is never exported, and neither are socials, phone or email.
values.Download CSV (workbench table): Economy workbench, Table tab. File pr_economy_layers.csv. GEOID (the geographic identifier code of the Census Bureau), Municipality and one column for each visible layer, for the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico.
values.Download all years (CSV): Economy dataset dialog. File pr_economy_<dataset>.csv. GEOID, Municipality and one column for each year, with a margin-of-error column per year when the source publishes margins. Values as published.
values.Download CSV (Full data): Housing page, in a dataset's 'Full data' dialog. File pr_housing_<name>.csv. GEOID, Municipality and one column for each year, with a margin-of-error column per year when published. Published tables give their own rows. The Puerto Rico row has GEOID 72.
values.GeoJSON (route planner): Route planner. File planned_route.geojson. This is a GeoJSON file, not a CSV: the route line with a few results and one point for each chosen place.
values.Download all years (CSV), dictionary pag: Data dictionary page, on the entries that describe a yearly series (a field of economy_series.json or housing_series.json). File pr_digital_twin_<id>.csv, with each dot of the id turned into an underscore, for example pr_digital_twin_economy_qcew_jobs.csv. GEOID, Municipality and one column for each year, with a margin-of-error column per year when the source publishes margins. Values as published. The file has 79 rows: the 78 municipalities and Puerto Rico (GEOID 72).
values.Download the dictionary (CSV): Data dictionary page. File pr_digital_twin_data_dictionary.csv. One row for each entry, whatever the filters on the page, with these columns: id, name, area, group, kind, type, unit, geography, years, updates, plain description, definition, how it is computed, how to read it, cautions, sources, source detail, data fields, related entries and the date added.
values.Data file links, dictionary page: The data file names under 'Where it appears' on an entry and in the table of published data files are download links to the files themselves, as published in the data folder. These files are not made in your browser.

entries.plain_es: Seis botones en las páginas del mapa y de Vivienda guardan datos como archivos: una tabla de municipios, los lugares de un municipio, dos tablas económicas, una tabla de vivienda y una ruta planificada. Estos archivos se crean en el navegador. La página del diccionario de datos agrega dos botones de descarga más y un enlace de descarga para cada archivo de datos publicado.
entries.name_es: Descargas en CSV y GeoJSON
entries.how_to_read_es: Cite los valores guardados en los archivos, no las cifras redondeadas de la pantalla. Agregue la etiqueta del corte de datos y la fecha de descarga. Un archivo no tiene una cita propia. Use el botón Citar de las fichas del diccionario de los conjuntos de datos que contiene.

entries.name: Planned route download (GeoJSON)
entries.plain: The GeoJSON button saves the planned route as planned_route.geojson. The file holds the line, the points you chose and six of the results shown.
entries.definition: A GeoJSON file (a standard text format for map shapes) with one line feature (the route) and one point feature for each chosen point. The line has the properties name, created, source, follows_roads, length_km, stops, residents_within_400m, tourism_places_within_400m, share_parallel_to_existing_routes_pct, share_in_flood_hazard_area_pct and municipalities. Each point has name, order and role.
entries.geography: Any route in Puerto Rico (calculated for the route you draw)

coverage.frequency: Created in your browser when you press the GeoJSON button; nothing is stored on a server

entries.method: plan.js builds the file from the current result. Coordinates are longitude and latitude (World Geodetic System 1984, WGS 84). A line that follows roads has 5 decimals; points have 6.
entries.source_detail: site/js/plan.js (geojson, download)
entries.how_to_read: Open the file in a mapping program to keep or share a plan. The numbers are those shown when you pressed the button.
caveats: Not in the file: the running time, residents with no scheduled stop, lodgings, the protected-area share and the connections.
'created' is the date in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time), so it can be one day ahead of the date in Puerto Rico in the evening.
A number that had not finished loading when you pressed the button is left out of the file.
The file carries the data licenses of its inputs (OpenStreetMap roads, Overture places, FEMA, Census and timetable feeds). Check the terms of each before you publish it.
The file holds the points you chose to 6 decimals (about 0.1 m) with their labels. If you chose a home address, the file shows it. Remove it before you share the file.

values.name: 'Planned route' for the line; the place label for a point.
values.created: Date the file was made, as YYYY-MM-DD in UTC.
values.follows_roads: true when Follow roads is on and every leg follows roads; false otherwise.
values.length_km: Route length in km with two decimals (the number in the 'Route length' entry).
values.stops: Labels of the chosen points joined with ' > '.
values.residents_within_400m: Residents within 400 m of the route.
values.tourism_places_within_400m: Tourism places within 400 m of the route.
values.share_parallel_to_existing_routes_pct: Share of the route within 150 m of an existing route (percent).
values.share_in_flood_hazard_area_pct: Share of the route in a flood hazard area (percent).
values.municipalities: Names of the municipalities crossed, joined with ', '.
values.order: Position of the point along the route, from 1.
values.role: 'from' for the first point, 'to' for the last, 'stop' for points between.

entries.plain_es: El botón "GeoJSON" guarda la ruta planificada como planned_route.geojson. El archivo tiene la línea, los puntos escogidos y seis de los resultados que se muestran.
entries.name_es: Descarga de la ruta planificada (GeoJSON)
entries.how_to_read_es: Abra el archivo en un programa de mapas para guardar o compartir un plan. Los números son los que se mostraban cuando presionó el botón.

entries.name: Shareable link of the 2D map
entries.plain: The 2D map keeps its view in the part of the page address after the # sign: municipality, position, layers that are on, shading, planned route and economy layers. Copy the address to share the view.
entries.definition: The address is rewritten about a quarter of a second after each change, without adding steps to the browser's back button. Its form is #<Municipality>&c=<lat>,<lng>,<zoom>&l=<layers>&s=<shading>&r=<route>&e=<economy>&ey=<year>&eb=<base>&slr=<feet>. Parts that do not apply are left out, except c and l, which are always written. The parts are listed below. When the address changes while the page is open, the municipality, position, layers, shading and sea level are applied again. The route (r) and the economy parts (e, ey, eb) are read only when the page loads. To use a changed one, reload the page. The page's title carries the municipality name. The '3D + Time' link in the header carries the position (c) and the route (r) to the 3D view.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: app.js (writeHash, parseHash, applyHash, LAYER_KEYS), network.js and economy.js.
entries.how_to_read: Open the link in a new tab to check it before you share it. A hand-made link must list every layer you want on. Example: index.html#c=18.4400,-66.0900,12&l=muni,flood&s=sfha_pct shows the flood zones and shades the municipalities by the share of places in a flood hazard area, with no pins.
caveats: Layer settings other than those listed, such as the category buttons, the confidence slider, the worship switch and the open tab, are not kept in the address.
A link records choices, not data. If the observatory's data change after a new snapshot, the same link can show different numbers.

The r= part holds the exact coordinates of every point of a planned route, to about 11 metres. If a start, end or stop is your home or workplace, anyone with the link can see it. Remove the r= part before you share a link, or use points that are not private.

view.label: 2D map: flood zones, shaded by flood exposure
2D map: a municipality

values.#<Municipality>: A municipality name, URL-encoded, such as #San%20Juan. It is matched ignoring accents and capitals. An unknown name gives a message. A link with a municipality opens the Municipality tab.
values.c: c=<latitude>,<longitude>,<zoom>: the map centre (4 decimals) and the zoom level, a whole number on the 2D map's scale. When c is present the map does not fly to the municipality.
values.l: l=<layers>: the layers that are ON, separated by commas. The list is complete: a layer that is not named is switched off, including tourism places (places) and boundaries (muni). A link with l=flood therefore shows no pins and no boundaries.
values.l=taxi: Taxi stands and electric vehicle charging.
values.s: s=<field>: a measure of the retired 'Shade municipalities by' menu, for example s=sfha_pct. Old links keep working: the measure opens as its dataset (app.js SHADE_DS) and the address is rewritten with e=.
values.slr: slr=<feet>: the sea level slider, a whole number from 1 to 10. It is written only when the sea level layer is on.
values.r: r=<lat>,<lng>;<lat>,<lng>...: the points of a planned route, 4 decimals, from 2 to 8 points. The link opens the Transit tab and plans the route.
values.e, ey, eb: The Analysis tab's layers, year and base year. See the entry on Economy links.

entries.plain_es: El mapa 2D guarda su vista en la parte de la dirección de la página que va después del signo #: municipio, posición, capas activadas, sombreado, ruta planificada y capas económicas. Copie la dirección para compartir la vista.
entries.name_es: Enlace para compartir del mapa 2D
entries.how_to_read_es: Abra el enlace en una pestaña nueva para verificarlo antes de compartirlo. Un enlace hecho a mano debe incluir cada capa que se quiera activar. Ejemplo: index.html#c=18.4400,-66.0900,12&l=muni,flood&s=sfha_pct muestra las zonas inundables y sombrea los municipios por la proporción de lugares en zona de riesgo de inundación, sin marcadores.

entries.name: Shareable link of the 3D view
entries.plain: The 3D view reads two items from the page address: the camera centre and zoom (c) and a planned route (r). Layers and clocks are not kept in the address.
entries.definition: The form is 3d.html#c=<lat>,<lng>,<zoom>&r=<lat>,<lng>;<lat>,<lng>. The zoom number is on the 2D map's scale: the 3D view subtracts 1 when it opens the link and adds 1 when it writes one. The 3D page writes the address when it opens and again whenever the route changes. It does not follow the camera as you move. The 'Map' link in the header carries the camera and route to the 2D map. An address with r= opens the Route tab and plans the route.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: twin3d.js (start, planHost.drawRoute, syncViewLinks).
entries.how_to_read: Open the link to check it. Tilt and rotation are not in the link, so the camera opens at the page's usual angle. Example: 3d.html#c=18.4400,-66.0900,14 opens near the centre of San Juan.
caveats: The tilt, rotation, open tab, switches and the clock settings are not saved in the address.

The r= part holds the exact coordinates of every point of a planned route, to about 11 metres. If a start, end or stop is your home or workplace, anyone with the link can see it. Remove the r= part before you share a link, or use points that are not private.

view.label: 3D view: San Juan

entries.plain_es: La vista 3D lee dos datos de la dirección de la página: el centro y el acercamiento de la cámara (c) y una ruta planificada (r). Las capas y los relojes no se guardan en la dirección.
entries.name_es: Enlace para compartir de la vista 3D
entries.how_to_read_es: Abra el enlace para verificarlo. La inclinación y la rotación no están en el enlace, así que la cámara abre con el ángulo habitual de la página. Ejemplo: 3d.html#c=18.4400,-66.0900,14 abre cerca del centro de San Juan.

entries.name: Shareable link of the Analysis tab
entries.plain: The Analysis tab writes its layers, year and base year into the page address. The 'Copy link' button copies the address, and opening it brings the same layers back.
entries.definition: The part e= holds the layers, in list order, separated by commas (written %2C in the address). Each layer is ten items joined by dots: <dataset>.<mode>.<show-as>.<ramp>.<classes>.<visible>.<fixed>.<inflation>.<opacity>.<colour>. For example poverty_pct.f.value.blue.q.1.1.0.85.0 is a shaded poverty rate, as published, in blue, with equal-count classes, visible, the same classes in every year, not inflation-adjusted, at 85% opacity. A link with an e= part opens the Analysis tab. These parts are read only when the page loads. If you change them in a page that is already open, reload it. To keep other map layers out of the way, add l=muni (see the 2D link entry). The first two shaded layers form the bivariate map.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: economy.js (ecEncode, ecRestore, ECON.extra). The button 'Copy link' (ecCopy) writes the address and copies it. If your browser blocks the copy, a message asks you to copy the address from the address bar.
entries.how_to_read: Build a link by copying one from the page and changing the year, rather than writing the layer codes by hand.
caveats: Settings of the workbench (open tab, chosen places) are not kept in the address.
A link names datasets by key. If a dataset is renamed or removed in a later version, its layer is dropped.

view.label: 2D map: poverty rate in 2022 as a shaded layer

values.<dataset>: The dataset key, for example poverty_pct or qcew_jobs. Unknown keys are ignored.
values.<mode>: f for a shaded layer, s for symbols.
values.<show-as>: One of the 'Show as' codes: value, per1000, perkm2, sharePR, shareJobs, lq, perCapita, index, diff, change, pctile. A code that the dataset does not offer becomes value.
values.<ramp>: blue, green, gold, red or gray.
values.<classes>: q for quantiles, e for equal intervals, j for natural breaks.
values.<fixed>: 1 for 'Same classes in every year', 0 for off.
values.<colour>: A number 0 to 4 for the symbol colour: 0 Red, 1 Blue, 2 Gold, 3 Green, 4 Charcoal.
values.ey: ey=<year>: the year. Left out when the year control is on 'Latest'.
values.eb: eb=<year>: the base year of 'Change measured from'. Left out when it is 2014.

entries.plain_es: La pestaña Análisis escribe sus capas, el año y el año base en la dirección de la página. El botón "Copiar enlace" copia la dirección, y al abrirla vuelven las mismas capas.
entries.name_es: Enlace para compartir de la pestaña Análisis
entries.how_to_read_es: Arme un enlace copiando uno de la página y cambiando el año, en lugar de escribir a mano los códigos de las capas.

entries.name: Shareable link of the Housing page
entries.plain: The Housing page keeps the municipality, the data year, the base year and an open dataset in the page address, so you can share the exact view.
entries.definition: The form is housing.html?m=<municipality>&y=<year>&c=<base year>&d=<dataset>#<section>. The page updates the address when you pick a municipality, a year or a base year. It adds d when a 'Full data' dialog is open and removes it when the dialog closes. A link with d opens that dialog after the page has loaded. A link with an anchor scrolls to that section.

coverage.frequency: Fixed in the page code. It changes only when the page is updated.

entries.method: housing.js (writeUrl, openDataset, init). The page reads the address once, when it loads.
entries.how_to_read: Use d to point a reader at one dataset's full table, and y to fix the year. Example: housing.html?m=Ponce&y=2020&c=2014&d=median_gross_rent#profile opens the profile of Ponce for 2020, with changes measured from 2014, and the full table of median gross rent.
caveats: The page does not check that y is in range. Years after the latest data show the latest available value with a note.
The id table2 is not a valid d value. Use population for the population table.

view.label: Housing page: Ponce, 2020, with the rent table open

values.m: m=<municipality>: the municipality of the profile. Matched ignoring accents and capitals.
values.y: y=<year>: the data year (2010 to 2025 in Snapshot 2026-10). Left out for 'Latest'.
values.c: c=<year>: the base year of 'Change measured from' (2010 to 2023 in Snapshot 2026-10). Left out when it is 2012.
values.d: d=<dataset>: opens a dataset's 'Full data' dialog. A series key such as median_gross_rent, or one of the published-table ids table6, t6live, table7, table10, grapilive, smocapilive.
values.embed: ?embed: hides the header bar and the contents bar, for use inside another web page.

entries.plain_es: La página de Vivienda guarda en la dirección de la página el municipio, el año de los datos, el año base y el conjunto de datos abierto, para poder compartir exactamente la misma vista.
entries.name_es: Enlace para compartir de la página Vivienda
entries.how_to_read_es: Use d para dirigir a quien lea a la tabla completa de un conjunto de datos, y y para fijar el año. Ejemplo: housing.html?m=Ponce&y=2020&c=2014&d=median_gross_rent#profile abre el perfil de Ponce para 2020, con los cambios medidos desde 2014, y la tabla completa del alquiler bruto mediano.

overture.name: Overture Maps Foundation — Places

more_links.label: Places theme: sources, licenses and monthly releases

overture.licence: Varies by contributor: CDLA-Permissive-2.0, Apache 2.0 or CC0 1.0
overture.credit: Source: Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org, Places theme, release 2026-09-23.1, accessed 1 October 2026 (Meta, Microsoft, Foursquare, AllThePlaces and others). Foursquare records: © Foursquare Labs, Inc., Apache License 2.0, transformed to the Overture schema
overture.access: The overturemaps command-line tool downloads the Places theme from Overture's public cloud-hosted files, cut to a box around Puerto Rico (west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57). The current snapshot is Overture release 2026-09-23.1, downloaded on 1 October 2026.
overture.cadence: Overture releases the Places theme every month. The observatory keeps one snapshot and renews it only when FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot).
overture.used_for: Every tourism place on the maps (name, category, location, address, website, confidence score and source dataset) and every count, density and exposure figure built from those places. Also the road distance from where residents live to the nearest supermarket, food store, pharmacy and bank or cooperativa, by barrio and municipio (essentials_series.json, essentials_barrio.json; only the distances, never the shops).
overture.terms_note: The license depends on who contributed the record: CDLA-Permissive-2.0 for Meta, Microsoft and others, Apache 2.0 for Foursquare and CC0 1.0 for AllThePlaces. In the 2026-10 snapshot the observatory publishes 32,541 places. The listed source is Meta for 31,945, Foursquare for 252, Microsoft for 241 and AllThePlaces for 103. Overture's other themes (Buildings, Divisions, Transportation) use ODbL; the observatory also uses Buildings, under its own source card (overture_buildings). Overture suggests citing 'Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org' with the access date. Foursquare's notice asks anyone who uses its records to keep attribution to Foursquare (including the full text of its NOTICE.txt), to give recipients a copy of the Apache 2.0 license and to mark any changes; Overture's attribution page carries Foursquare's copyright line. Listings are third-party business records, not an official register. FPR classifies and de-duplicates them. Phone numbers, emails and social-media links are not published.
overture.access_es: La herramienta de línea de comandos overturemaps descarga el tema Places de los archivos públicos de Overture alojados en la nube, recortado a un recuadro alrededor de Puerto Rico (oeste -67.97, sur 17.85, este -65.20, norte 18.57). El corte de datos actual es la versión 2026-09-23.1 de Overture, descargada el 1 de octubre de 2026.
overture.cadence_es: Overture publica el tema Places cada mes. El observatorio conserva un corte de datos y lo renueva solo cuando FPR reconstruye los datos (un nuevo corte de datos).
overture.used_for_es: Cada lugar turístico en los mapas (nombre, categoría, ubicación, dirección, sitio web, puntuación de confianza y conjunto de datos de origen) y cada conteo, densidad y cifra de exposición que se calcula a partir de esos lugares. También la distancia por carretera desde donde vive la gente hasta el supermercado, la tienda de alimentos, la farmacia y el banco o la cooperativa más cercanos, por barrio y municipio (essentials_series.json, essentials_barrio.json; solo las distancias, nunca los comercios).
overture.terms_note_es: La licencia depende de quién aportó el registro: CDLA-Permissive-2.0 para Meta, Microsoft y otros; Apache 2.0 para Foursquare, y CC0 1.0 para AllThePlaces. En el corte de datos 2026-10, el observatorio publica 32,541 lugares. La fuente indicada es Meta para 31,945, Foursquare para 252, Microsoft para 241 y AllThePlaces para 103. Los otros temas de Overture (Buildings, Divisions, Transportation) usan la ODbL; el observatorio también usa Buildings, con su propia ficha de fuente (overture_buildings). Overture sugiere citar 'Overture Maps Foundation, overturemaps.org' con la fecha de consulta. El aviso de Foursquare pide a quien use sus registros que mantenga la atribución a Foursquare (incluido el texto completo de su NOTICE.txt), que entregue a quienes los reciban una copia de la licencia Apache 2.0 y que indique cualquier cambio; la página de atribución de Overture incluye la línea de derechos de autor de Foursquare. Los listados son registros comerciales de terceros, no un registro oficial. FPR los clasifica y elimina los duplicados. No se publican números de teléfono, correos electrónicos ni enlaces a redes sociales.

fcc_bdc.name: FCC — Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability (National Broadband Map)
fcc_bdc.publisher: Federal Communications Commission (FCC), Broadband Data Task Force

more_links.label: BDC help center: data specifications and the public data API (an FCC account and API token are needed)
NTIA, BEAD program: served, underserved and unserved

fcc_bdc.credit: Source: FCC Broadband Data Collection, fixed broadband availability data, as of June 30 of each year (https://broadbandmap.fcc.gov/)
fcc_bdc.access: The FCC's public data API answers only with an account: the build reads FPR's FCC username and API token from the GitHub Actions secrets FCC_BDC_USERNAME and FCC_BDC_HASH and sends them only to broadbandmap.fcc.gov. It downloads Puerto Rico's state location files (one CSV per fixed technology, about 60 MB a release), keeps counts by census block in its cache, and publishes only counts and shares by area. The site never calls the FCC.
fcc_bdc.cadence: Providers file twice a year, as of June 30 and December 31; the FCC publishes each release a few months later and again as challenges are settled. The observatory keeps the June release of each year and checks for a new one every 30 days (refresh unit broadband).
fcc_bdc.used_for: Broadband serviceable locations, the shares served, underserved and unserved in NTIA's BEAD terms, the locations below 100/20 Mbps and the share where fiber is available, for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico, June 2023-2026 (broadband_series.json, broadband_barrio.json).
fcc_bdc.terms_note: Works of the US Government are not protected by US copyright. The location list behind the files (the Fabric) is licensed by CostQuest Associates and is not used: the public files give each location's census block, and the observatory publishes no location id, address or provider list. Availability is what providers report and can be challenged.
fcc_bdc.access_es: La API de datos públicos de la FCC responde solo con una cuenta: la compilación lee el usuario y la ficha de API de la FCC de FPR de los secretos de GitHub Actions FCC_BDC_USERNAME y FCC_BDC_HASH y los envía solo a broadbandmap.fcc.gov. Descarga los archivos de ubicaciones de Puerto Rico (un CSV por tecnología fija, unos 60 MB por publicación), guarda conteos por bloque censal en su caché y publica solo conteos y proporciones por área. El sitio nunca consulta la FCC.
fcc_bdc.cadence_es: Los proveedores informan dos veces al año, al 30 de junio y al 31 de diciembre; la FCC publica cada informe unos meses después y de nuevo cuando se resuelven las impugnaciones. El observatorio usa la publicación de junio de cada año y busca una nueva cada 30 días (unidad de actualización broadband).
fcc_bdc.used_for_es: Las ubicaciones con servicio de banda ancha posible, las proporciones servidas, subatendidas y sin servicio según BEAD de la NTIA, las ubicaciones por debajo de 100/20 Mbps y la proporción con fibra disponible, para los 78 municipios, los 901 barrios y Puerto Rico, junio de 2023 a 2026 (broadband_series.json, broadband_barrio.json).
fcc_bdc.terms_note_es: Las obras del Gobierno de EE. UU. no tienen derechos de autor en EE. UU. La lista de ubicaciones detrás de los archivos (el Fabric) tiene licencia de CostQuest Associates y no se usa: los archivos públicos dan el bloque censal de cada ubicación, y el observatorio no publica identificadores de ubicaciones, direcciones ni listas de proveedores. La disponibilidad es lo que informan los proveedores y se puede impugnar.

overture_buildings.name: Overture Maps Foundation — Buildings
overture_buildings.publisher: Overture Maps Foundation (OpenStreetMap contributors, Google Open Buildings, Microsoft ML Buildings and others)
overture_buildings.credit: © OpenStreetMap contributors, Overture Maps Foundation (overturemaps.org), Buildings theme, release 2026-10-21.0, ODbL 1.0
overture_buildings.access: The overturemaps package reads the Buildings theme from Overture's public GeoParquet files for a box around Puerto Rico (west -67.97, south 17.85, east -65.20, north 18.57), about 3.5 minutes. The build keeps, for each building, one point inside its outline, its footprint area, its first source and its height (cache/buildings/, not published). The site never calls Overture.
overture_buildings.cadence: Overture releases every month; the refresh checks every 30 days and rebuilds with the newest release (refresh unit buildings).
overture_buildings.used_for: The number of buildings, buildings per km², the land under roofs, the median footprint, the buildings in a FEMA Special Flood Hazard Area and the share traced by machine learning, for the 78 municipios, the 901 barrios and Puerto Rico (buildings_series.json, buildings_barrio.json).
overture_buildings.terms_note: ODbL 1.0 because the theme holds OpenStreetMap data: attribution as above, and share-alike for a derived database. The observatory's buildings files are counts and shares derived from it, so they are offered under ODbL 1.0 too. In release 2026-10-21.0, Puerto Rico's 2,157,363 buildings come from OpenStreetMap (1,500,399), Google Open Buildings (536,571) and Microsoft ML Buildings (120,393); 203,060 have a height. Footprints traced by machine learning can include sheds and miss buildings under trees. Most buildings are homes: nothing is published per building.
overture_buildings.access_es: El paquete overturemaps lee el tema Buildings de los archivos GeoParquet públicos de Overture para un recuadro alrededor de Puerto Rico (oeste -67.97, sur 17.85, este -65.20, norte 18.57), en unos 3.5 minutos. La compilación guarda, de cada edificio, un punto dentro de su contorno, el área de su huella, su primera fuente y su altura (cache/buildings/, no se publica). El sitio nunca consulta Overture.
overture_buildings.cadence_es: Overture publica una versión cada mes; la actualización revisa cada 30 días y reconstruye con la versión más reciente (unidad de actualización buildings).
overture_buildings.used_for_es: El número de edificios, los edificios por km², el terreno bajo techo, la huella mediana, los edificios en un Área Especial de Riesgo de Inundación de FEMA y la proporción trazada con aprendizaje automático, para los 78 municipios, los 901 barrios y Puerto Rico (buildings_series.json, buildings_barrio.json).
overture_buildings.terms_note_es: ODbL 1.0 porque el tema contiene datos de OpenStreetMap: atribución como arriba y compartir igual para una base de datos derivada. Los archivos de edificios del observatorio son conteos y proporciones derivados de ella, así que también se ofrecen bajo la ODbL 1.0. En la versión 2026-10-21.0, los 2,157,363 edificios de Puerto Rico vienen de OpenStreetMap (1,500,399), Google Open Buildings (536,571) y Microsoft ML Buildings (120,393); 203,060 tienen altura. Las huellas trazadas con aprendizaje automático pueden incluir cobertizos y omitir edificios bajo los árboles. La mayoría de los edificios son viviendas: no se publica nada por edificio.

nasa_firms.name: NASA FIRMS — VIIRS 375 m active fire detections (NOAA-20)
nasa_firms.publisher: NASA Land, Atmosphere Near real-time Capability for EOS (LANCE), Fire Information for Resource Management System (FIRMS)

more_links.label: FIRMS frequently asked questions (what a detection is, credit)

nasa_firms.licence: NASA open data, no restriction on use
nasa_firms.credit: NASA FIRMS (LANCE), VIIRS 375 m active fire detections, NOAA-20
nasa_firms.access: The build downloads FIRMS's yearly country files for Puerto Rico (NOAA-20, standard processing; public, no key) and, in GitHub Actions only, the last 12 months from the FIRMS area API for the Puerto Rico box with FPR's MAP_KEY, kept as the secret FIRMS_MAP_KEY. The detections stay in the build's cache; only counts by municipio are published. The site never calls FIRMS.
nasa_firms.cadence: FIRMS adds detections within hours of each pass; the yearly file of a finished year appears in the first months of the next. The observatory rebuilds monthly (refresh unit fires).
nasa_firms.used_for: Vegetation fire detections by municipio for each year since 2019, per 100 km² of land, and in the last 12 months (fires_series.json).
nasa_firms.terms_note: NASA's data are open with no restriction; FIRMS asks that published work credit 'NASA FIRMS'. A detection is a 375 m pixel that held one or more fires or other heat sources when the satellite passed, not a fire's outline or size. Suomi NPP stopped sending FIRMS data on 2026-11-02, so the observatory uses NOAA-20 for every year.
nasa_firms.access_es: La compilación descarga los archivos anuales por país de FIRMS para Puerto Rico (NOAA-20, procesamiento estándar; públicos, sin clave) y, solo en GitHub Actions, los últimos 12 meses del servicio de área de la API de FIRMS para el recuadro de Puerto Rico con la MAP_KEY de FPR, guardada como el secreto FIRMS_MAP_KEY. Las detecciones se quedan en la caché de la compilación; solo se publican conteos por municipio. El sitio nunca consulta FIRMS.
nasa_firms.cadence_es: FIRMS añade detecciones a las pocas horas de cada pase; el archivo anual de un año terminado aparece en los primeros meses del siguiente. El observatorio reconstruye cada mes (unidad de actualización fires).
nasa_firms.used_for_es: Las detecciones de fuegos de vegetación por municipio para cada año desde 2019, por 100 km² de terreno y en los últimos 12 meses (fires_series.json).
nasa_firms.terms_note_es: Los datos de la NASA son abiertos y sin restricciones; FIRMS pide que los trabajos publicados den crédito a 'NASA FIRMS'. Una detección es un píxel de 375 m que tenía uno o más fuegos u otras fuentes de calor cuando pasó el satélite, no el contorno ni el tamaño de un fuego. Suomi NPP dejó de enviar datos a FIRMS el 2026-11-02, así que el observatorio usa NOAA-20 para todos los años.

fema_nfhl.name: FEMA National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL)

more_links.label: Data service used by the build (for developers)
NFHL metadata: constraints and update frequency

fema_nfhl.licence: US Government work; FEMA's metadata lists no access constraints
fema_nfhl.credit: Source: FEMA, National Flood Hazard Layer (NFHL)
fema_nfhl.access: ArcGIS REST service (a public web service that returns map data on request) on hazards.fema.gov: NFHL MapServer, layer 28, Flood Hazard Zones. The build pages through the layer with the filter DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%' (Puerto Rico) and reads the fields FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF and STATIC_BFE. No key is needed.
fema_nfhl.cadence: FEMA says it adds new and revised data continuously, and its metadata gives a monthly update frequency. The observatory keeps one snapshot, downloaded on 1 October 2026, and renews it only when FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot).
fema_nfhl.used_for: The flood zone shapes on the maps (flood.geojson) and the flood-zone flags and shares for tourism places and municipalities. Also the roads that close in the estimate of residents cut off from hospitals by floods (cutoff_series.json, cutoff_barrio.json).
fema_nfhl.terms_note: FEMA's metadata says the printed Flood Insurance Rate Map, its database and the Flood Insurance Study are the official designation of Special Flood Hazard Areas and base flood elevations. The observatory draws a simplified copy for context. It is not a flood determination for any property.
fema_nfhl.access_es: Servicio ArcGIS REST (un servicio web público que devuelve datos de mapas cuando se le piden) en hazards.fema.gov: NFHL MapServer, capa 28, Flood Hazard Zones. La compilación recorre la capa por páginas con el filtro DFIRM_ID LIKE '72%' (Puerto Rico) y lee los campos FLD_ZONE, ZONE_SUBTY, SFHA_TF y STATIC_BFE. No se necesita clave.
fema_nfhl.cadence_es: FEMA indica que agrega datos nuevos y revisados de forma continua, y sus metadatos indican una frecuencia de actualización mensual. El observatorio conserva un corte de datos, descargado el 1 de octubre de 2026, y lo renueva solo cuando FPR reconstruye los datos (un nuevo corte de datos).
fema_nfhl.used_for_es: Las formas de las zonas inundables en los mapas (flood.geojson) y los indicadores y las proporciones de zona inundable de los lugares turísticos y los municipios. También las carreteras que cierran en el estimado de residentes incomunicados de los hospitales por inundaciones (cutoff_series.json, cutoff_barrio.json).
fema_nfhl.terms_note_es: Los metadatos de FEMA indican que el Mapa de Tasas del Seguro de Inundación (Flood Insurance Rate Map) impreso, su base de datos y el Estudio del Seguro de Inundación (Flood Insurance Study) son la designación oficial de las Áreas Especiales de Riesgo de Inundación y de las elevaciones de inundación base. El observatorio dibuja una copia simplificada como contexto. No es una determinación de inundación para ninguna propiedad.

padus.name: USGS — PAD-US 4.1 (protected areas)
padus.publisher: US Geological Survey (USGS), Gap Analysis Project

more_links.label: Data service used by the build (for developers)

padus.credit: Source: U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) Gap Analysis Project (GAP), 2024, Protected Areas Database of the United States (PAD-US) 4.1: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P96WBCHS
padus.access: ArcGIS REST FeatureServer layer 0 (a public web service) of a hosted copy of PAD-US 4.1 (layer PADUS4_1ProtMechCat, service Protection_Mechanism_Category_PADUS, on a USGS ArcGIS Online account). The build pages through it with the filter State_Nm='PR' and reads Unit_Nm, Mang_Name, Des_Tp, GAP_Sts, Category, Pub_Access and GIS_Acres. No key is needed.
padus.cadence: USGS publishes PAD-US in numbered versions. As of 3 October 2026 it lists version 4.1 (released March 2025, cited by USGS as a 2024 data release) as the most recent. The observatory keeps one snapshot, downloaded on 1 October 2026, and renews it only when FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot).
padus.used_for: The protected-area outlines on the maps (protected.geojson), the protected-area name and status for each tourism place, and the share of places inside protected areas.
padus.terms_note: USGS says its data are in the US public domain, and USGS and its data partners disclaim liability for misuse. PAD-US combines data from federal, state and local agencies and nonprofit partners. USGS recommends it for comparing agencies and advises asking the managing agency directly for authoritative boundaries. Proclamation boundaries (designation type PROC) are drawn but do not count a place as inside a protected area. The observatory draws a simplified copy.
padus.access_es: Capa 0 de un ArcGIS REST FeatureServer (un servicio web público) de una copia alojada de PAD-US 4.1 (capa PADUS4_1ProtMechCat, servicio Protection_Mechanism_Category_PADUS, en una cuenta de ArcGIS Online del USGS). La compilación la recorre por páginas con el filtro State_Nm='PR' y lee Unit_Nm, Mang_Name, Des_Tp, GAP_Sts, Category, Pub_Access y GIS_Acres. No se necesita clave.
padus.cadence_es: El USGS publica PAD-US en versiones numeradas. Al 3 de octubre de 2026, indica como la más reciente la versión 4.1 (publicada en marzo de 2025 y citada por el USGS como una publicación de datos de 2024). El observatorio conserva un corte de datos, descargado el 1 de octubre de 2026, y lo renueva solo cuando FPR reconstruye los datos (un nuevo corte de datos).
padus.used_for_es: Los contornos de las áreas protegidas en los mapas (protected.geojson), el nombre y el estado del área protegida de cada lugar turístico, y la proporción de lugares dentro de áreas protegidas.
padus.terms_note_es: El USGS indica que sus datos son de dominio público en los EE. UU., y el USGS y sus socios de datos declinan toda responsabilidad por el mal uso. PAD-US combina datos de agencias federales, estatales y locales y de socios sin fines de lucro. El USGS lo recomienda para comparar agencias y aconseja consultar directamente a la agencia que administra el área para obtener límites oficiales. Los límites de proclamación (tipo de designación PROC) se dibujan, pero un lugar dentro de ellos no cuenta como dentro de un área protegida. El observatorio dibuja una copia simplificada.

census_tiger.name: US Census Bureau — TIGERweb boundaries and counts

more_links.label: 2020 Census county subdivisions, the barrios (layer 20, full resolution)

census_tiger.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, TIGERweb (2010 and 2020 Census counts, 2020 Census blocks, 2023 generalized boundaries)
census_tiger.access: ArcGIS REST services (public web services that return map data on request) on tigerweb.geo.census.gov, no key, always filtered to STATE='72'. 2020 Census Counties (layer 82) give each municipio's population, housing units and area. Generalized_ACS2023 Counties 500K (layer 11) give the shoreline-clipped boundaries drawn on the maps. 2010 Census Counties (layer 100) give 2010 population. 2020 Census Blocks (layer 10) give block population. Generalized_ACS2023 County Subdivisions 500K (layer 7) give barrio outlines. 2020 Census Tracts (layer 6), Block Groups (layer 8) and County Subdivisions (layer 20) give each unit's name, land area, residents and housing units; the county subdivision outlines at full resolution place each census block in its barrio (geo.py). Layer 10 also gives each block's 15-digit id, housing units and land area.
census_tiger.cadence: The Census Bureau issues these layers by vintage (the 2010 and 2020 censuses, and 2023 generalized boundaries), so they do not change between vintages. The observatory keeps one snapshot, downloaded on 1 October 2026 (the tract, block group and county subdivision tables and the block ids on 6 October 2026), and renews it only when FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot).
census_tiger.used_for: Municipality and barrio boundaries, the 2010 and 2020 population and housing-unit counts per municipality, the block population behind the transit coverage figures, and the municipality of each place and stop. The 2020 geography crosswalk (units, parents, residents and housing units of each unit, barrio-to-tract weights) and the block ids and housing units behind it.
census_tiger.terms_note: The Census Bureau's TIGER/Line technical documentation says copyright protection is not available for works of the US Government and asks users to cite the Census Bureau as the source. The Bureau's citation page adds that conclusions drawn from any analysis of the data are the sole responsibility of the performing party. FPR's use of these data is not endorsed by the Census Bureau. The 2020 layer's legal boundaries include coastal water (they reach 3 nautical miles out), so the maps and point lookups use the shoreline-clipped generalized boundaries instead. Barrios are Census county subdivisions. The observatory does not use parcel (catastro) data from CRIM, the Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales (Municipal Revenue Collection Center).
census_tiger.access_es: Servicios ArcGIS REST (servicios web públicos que devuelven datos de mapas cuando se les piden) en tigerweb.geo.census.gov, sin clave y siempre filtrados con STATE='72'. 2020 Census Counties (capa 82) da la población, las unidades de vivienda y el área de cada municipio. Generalized_ACS2023 Counties 500K (capa 11) da los límites recortados a la costa que se dibujan en los mapas. 2010 Census Counties (capa 100) da la población de 2010. 2020 Census Blocks (capa 10) da la población de los bloques. Generalized_ACS2023 County Subdivisions 500K (capa 7) da los contornos de los barrios. 2020 Census Tracts (capa 6), Block Groups (capa 8) y County Subdivisions (capa 20) dan el nombre, el área de tierra, los residentes y las unidades de vivienda de cada unidad; los contornos de las subdivisiones de condado a resolución completa ubican cada bloque censal en su barrio (geo.py). La capa 10 también da el identificador de 15 dígitos, las unidades de vivienda y el área de tierra de cada bloque.
census_tiger.cadence_es: El Negociado del Censo de EE. UU. publica estas capas por edición (los censos de 2010 y 2020 y los límites generalizados de 2023), así que no cambian entre una edición y otra. El observatorio conserva un corte de datos, descargado el 1 de octubre de 2026 (las tablas de sectores censales, grupos de bloques y subdivisiones de condado, y los identificadores de bloque, el 6 de octubre de 2026), y lo renueva solo cuando FPR reconstruye los datos (un nuevo corte de datos).
census_tiger.used_for_es: Los límites de municipios y barrios, los conteos de población y de unidades de vivienda de 2010 y 2020 por municipio, la población por bloque en la que se basan las cifras de cobertura del transporte colectivo, y el municipio de cada lugar y cada parada. La tabla de equivalencias geográficas de 2020 (las unidades, las unidades que las contienen, los residentes y las unidades de vivienda de cada unidad, y los pesos de barrio a sector censal) y los identificadores de bloque y las unidades de vivienda en los que se basa.
census_tiger.terms_note_es: La documentación técnica de TIGER/Line del Negociado del Censo indica que la protección de derechos de autor no aplica a las obras del Gobierno de EE. UU. y pide citar al Negociado del Censo como fuente. La página de citas del Negociado agrega que las conclusiones de cualquier análisis de los datos son responsabilidad exclusiva de quien lo realiza. El Negociado del Censo no respalda el uso que FPR hace de estos datos. Los límites legales de la capa de 2020 incluyen aguas costeras (llegan a 3 millas náuticas mar adentro), así que los mapas y las búsquedas por punto usan en su lugar los límites generalizados recortados a la costa. Los barrios son subdivisiones de condado del Censo. El observatorio no usa datos de parcelas (catastro) del CRIM, el Centro de Recaudación de Ingresos Municipales.

census_cartographic.name: US Census Bureau — Cartographic boundary files, 2020 (1:500,000)
census_cartographic.licence: No license stated on the product pages; US Government work
census_cartographic.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, cartographic boundary files (2020 Census tracts and block groups, 1:500,000)
census_cartographic.access: Two zip files of shapefiles on www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2020/shp, no key: cb_2020_72_tract_500k.zip (0.6 MB) and cb_2020_72_bg_500k.zip (1.0 MB), last modified 19 May 2023 and read on 6 October 2026. geo.py reads them with pyshp and writes site/data/geo/tracts.geojson and blockgroups.geojson, keeping only the GEOID.
census_cartographic.cadence: A 2020 geography. The files are not revised within a decade except to correct errors. The observatory downloads them once and does not refresh them unless the build is run with its refresh option.
census_cartographic.used_for: The outlines of census tracts and block groups, for drawing only.
census_cartographic.terms_note: The Census Bureau describes these files as simplified representations designed for small-scale thematic mapping and says on its description page: "These files should not be used for: geographic analysis including area or perimeter calculation." The observatory uses them only to draw outlines; land areas come from the Census Bureau's own land-area field (AREALAND) and counts from the 2020 block table. The generalized files are clipped to a simplified outline of the coast and "some offshore areas may be excluded", so the 42 tracts and 42 block groups that are all water have no outline. The description page states no copyright or citation rule. The TIGER/Line documentation, which covers a related product, says copyright protection is not available for works of the US Government and asks users to cite the Census Bureau as the source. FPR's use of these files is not endorsed by the Census Bureau.
census_cartographic.access_es: Dos archivos zip de shapefiles en www2.census.gov/geo/tiger/GENZ2020/shp, sin clave: cb_2020_72_tract_500k.zip (0.6 MB) y cb_2020_72_bg_500k.zip (1.0 MB), modificados por última vez el 19 de mayo de 2023 y leídos el 6 de octubre de 2026. geo.py los lee con pyshp, escribe site/data/geo/tracts.geojson y blockgroups.geojson y conserva solo el GEOID.
census_cartographic.cadence_es: Una geografía de 2020. Los archivos no se revisan dentro de la década, salvo para corregir errores. El observatorio los descarga una vez y no los actualiza a menos que la compilación se ejecute con su opción de actualización.
census_cartographic.used_for_es: Los contornos de los sectores censales y los grupos de bloques, solo para dibujarlos.
census_cartographic.terms_note_es: El Negociado del Censo describe estos archivos como representaciones simplificadas diseñadas para mapas temáticos a pequeña escala y dice en su página de descripción: "These files should not be used for: geographic analysis including area or perimeter calculation." (estos archivos no deben usarse para análisis geográficos, incluido el cálculo de áreas o perímetros). El observatorio los usa solo para dibujar contornos; las áreas de tierra provienen del propio campo de área de tierra del Negociado del Censo (AREALAND) y los conteos, de la tabla de bloques de 2020. Los archivos generalizados están recortados a un contorno simplificado de la costa y "some offshore areas may be excluded" (algunas áreas mar adentro pueden quedar excluidas), así que los 42 sectores censales y los 42 grupos de bloques que son todo agua no tienen contorno. La página de descripción no indica ninguna regla de derechos de autor ni de cita. La documentación de TIGER/Line, que cubre un producto relacionado, indica que la protección de derechos de autor no aplica a las obras del Gobierno de EE. UU. y pide citar al Negociado del Censo como fuente. El Negociado del Censo no respalda el uso que FPR hace de estos archivos.

census_pep.name: US Census Bureau — Population Estimates (municipios)
census_pep.publisher: US Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program

more_links.label: Vintage 2025 age and sex, Puerto Rico (CSV)
Vintage 2025 state totals, Puerto Rico included (CSV)

census_pep.licence: US Government work; cite the Census Bureau as the source
census_pep.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program (Vintage 2020 for 2010-2019, Vintage 2025 for 2020-2025)
census_pep.access: Public CSV files on www2.census.gov, no key: PRM-EST2020.csv (totals) and PRM-EST2020-AGESEX.csv for 2010-2019 (Vintage 2020), and cc-est2025-agesex-72.csv for 2020-2025 (Vintage 2025). gii.py reads Puerto Rico's row of the newest state totals file (NST-EST2025-ALLDATA.csv) and keeps it in cache/gii/.
census_pep.cadence: The Census Bureau issues a new vintage every year (Vintage 2025 appeared in June 2026) and says the latest vintage replaces earlier estimates for the same dates. The observatory reads the newest vintage that has a Puerto Rico file when FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot).
census_pep.used_for: Resident population by municipality and the share of residents aged 65 and over, 2010 to 2025 in the 2026-10 snapshot (housing_series.json), shown on the Housing page and the Analysis tab; and Puerto Rico's population, the denominator of the FPR estimate of electricity output per million people (indicator 3.2.1 of the Global Innovation Index page, gii_profile.json).
census_pep.terms_note: Estimates are for July 1. The 2010 and 2020 values are census counts for April 1. Estimates for 2011 to 2019 were built on the 2010 census and were not revised to the 2020 count, so the series jumps at 2020. The product pages state no license. The Census Bureau's TIGER/Line documentation, which covers a different product, says copyright protection is not available for works of the US Government. The Bureau's citation page asks users to cite it as the source and says conclusions drawn from any analysis of the data are the sole responsibility of the performing party. FPR's use of these data is not endorsed by the Census Bureau.
census_pep.access_es: Archivos CSV públicos en www2.census.gov, sin clave: PRM-EST2020.csv (totales) y PRM-EST2020-AGESEX.csv para 2010-2019 (Vintage 2020), y cc-est2025-agesex-72.csv para 2020-2025 (Vintage 2025). gii.py lee la fila de Puerto Rico del archivo de totales por estado más reciente (NST-EST2025-ALLDATA.csv) y la guarda en cache/gii/.
census_pep.cadence_es: El Negociado del Censo publica una nueva edición (vintage) cada año (Vintage 2025 salió en junio de 2026) e indica que la edición más reciente sustituye los estimados anteriores para las mismas fechas. El observatorio lee la edición más reciente que tenga un archivo de Puerto Rico cuando FPR reconstruye los datos (un nuevo corte de datos).
census_pep.used_for_es: La población residente por municipio y la proporción de residentes de 65 años o más, de 2010 a 2025 en el corte de datos 2026-10 (housing_series.json), que se muestran en la página de Vivienda y en la pestaña Análisis; y la población de Puerto Rico, el denominador del estimado de FPR de la producción de electricidad por millón de habitantes (indicador 3.2.1 de la página del Índice Global de Innovación, gii_profile.json).
census_pep.terms_note_es: Los estimados corresponden al 1 de julio. Los valores de 2010 y 2020 son conteos censales del 1 de abril. Los estimados de 2011 a 2019 se basaron en el censo de 2010 y no se revisaron según el conteo de 2020, así que la serie da un salto en 2020. Las páginas del producto no indican ninguna licencia. La documentación de TIGER/Line del Negociado del Censo, que cubre un producto distinto, indica que la protección de derechos de autor no aplica a las obras del Gobierno de EE. UU. La página de citas del Negociado pide citarlo como fuente e indica que las conclusiones de cualquier análisis de los datos son responsabilidad exclusiva de quien lo realiza. El Negociado del Censo no respalda el uso que FPR hace de estos datos.

census_decennial.name: US Census Bureau — 2010 and 2020 Census housing occupancy
census_decennial.licence: US Government work; cite the Census Bureau as the source
census_decennial.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, 2010 and 2020 Census, PL 94-171 Redistricting Data (table H1, housing occupancy)
census_decennial.access: Two public ZIP files on www2.census.gov, no key: census_2010/01-Redistricting_File--PL_94-171/Puerto_Rico/pr2010.pl.zip and programs-surveys/decennial/2020/data/01-Redistricting_File--PL_94-171/Puerto_Rico/pr2020.pl.zip. The build reads each file's place-code table and the part that holds table H1 (housing occupancy), and keeps the island total and the 78 municipios.
census_decennial.cadence: A census is taken every ten years, on April 1 (2010 and 2020; the next is 2030), so these files do not change. The observatory reads them once and keeps the result.
census_decennial.used_for: Housing units, vacant units, vacancy rate and residents per housing unit on census day in 2010 and 2020 (housing_series.json).
census_decennial.terms_note: Census-day vacancy counts and American Community Survey vacancy estimates measure vacancy differently, so compare each source only with itself. The product pages state no license. The Census Bureau's TIGER/Line documentation, which covers a different product, says copyright protection is not available for works of the US Government. The Bureau's citation page asks users to cite it as the source and says conclusions drawn from any analysis of the data are the sole responsibility of the performing party. FPR's use of these data is not endorsed by the Census Bureau.
census_decennial.access_es: Dos archivos ZIP públicos en www2.census.gov, sin clave: census_2010/01-Redistricting_File--PL_94-171/Puerto_Rico/pr2010.pl.zip y programs-surveys/decennial/2020/data/01-Redistricting_File--PL_94-171/Puerto_Rico/pr2020.pl.zip. La compilación lee la tabla de códigos de lugar de cada archivo y la parte que contiene la tabla H1 (ocupación de la vivienda), y conserva el total de la isla y los 78 municipios.
census_decennial.cadence_es: El censo se realiza cada diez años, el 1 de abril (2010 y 2020; el próximo es en 2030), así que estos archivos no cambian. El observatorio los lee una vez y conserva el resultado.
census_decennial.used_for_es: Unidades de vivienda, unidades desocupadas, tasa de desocupación y residentes por unidad de vivienda el día del censo en 2010 y 2020 (housing_series.json).
census_decennial.terms_note_es: Los conteos de desocupación del día del censo y los estimados de desocupación de la Encuesta sobre la Comunidad Estadounidense (ACS) miden la desocupación de forma distinta, así que compare cada fuente solo consigo misma. Las páginas del producto no indican ninguna licencia. La documentación de TIGER/Line del Negociado del Censo, que cubre un producto distinto, indica que la protección de derechos de autor no aplica a las obras del Gobierno de EE. UU. La página de citas del Negociado pide citarlo como fuente e indica que las conclusiones de cualquier análisis de los datos son responsabilidad exclusiva de quien lo realiza. El Negociado del Censo no respalda el uso que FPR hace de estos datos.

acs5.name: US Census Bureau — American Community Survey 5-year
acs5.publisher: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey

more_links.label: Accuracy of the Data (margins of error)

acs5.licence: US Government work; cite the Census Bureau as the source
acs5.credit: Source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 5-year estimates, 2006-2010 through 2020-2024
acs5.access: Public summary files on www2.census.gov, no key. For the 2010 to 2020 vintages: per-sequence files under 5_year_seq_by_state/PuertoRico (and the 2012 Puerto Rico ZIP used for the 2008-2012 baseline). For 2021 to 2024: table-based files named acsdt5y{year}-{table}.dat. The build keeps the island and its 78 municipios. A second reader, acs_small.py, reads the tract, block group and barrio rows of the 2021 to 2024 table-based files by byte ranges (all five levels of a table cost 0.5 to 1.5 MB, against 18 to 121 MB for the nationwide file). small_area.py builds from it the files of barrios, census tracts and block groups (acs_barrio.json, acs_tract.json, acs_blockgroup.json) and the Population domain's series (population_series.json). The build also reads the Census Bureau's keyless table definitions at api.census.gov (the cell labels of each table, https://api.census.gov/data/{year}/acs/acs5/groups/{table}.json) to check that the cells it uses are the ones it means; no page of the site calls that host.
acs5.cadence: The Census Bureau releases a new 5-year vintage every year. In the 2026-10 snapshot the newest window the observatory holds is 2020-2024. The build checks for a newer table-based file and adds it when FPR rebuilds the data (a new snapshot).
acs5.used_for: Municipality housing, income, poverty, employment, education, cost-burden, commuting, vehicle and internet variables (housing_series.json and economy_series.json), plus the 2008-2012 baseline and the affordability figures. For 2021 to 2024, the same variables and the age, household, veteran and disability shares for 901 barrios, 981 census tracts and 2,555 block groups, with their margins of error. The age bands and age groups (population_age.json; the shares of the age groups also in population_series.json and, for 18 to 44 and 45 to 64, the barrio and tract files), from B01001 and B09001. Women's and men's labor force participation, unemployment and the counts behind them by sex and age group, for the 78 municipios and any group of them, in the three windows that share no year (2010-2014, 2015-2019, 2020-2024), from B23001, B23003, B98003 and B98001 (labor_sex_series.json and women_labor.json, women_labor.py).
acs5.terms_note: These are survey estimates. Each pools 60 months of answers, and the Census Bureau publishes margins of error at a 90 percent confidence level (see its 'Accuracy of the Data' document), which the observatory keeps where they exist. Windows are labelled by their last year. Dollar values are in the dollars of that last year, not adjusted for inflation. The product pages state no license. The Census Bureau's TIGER/Line documentation, which covers a different product, says copyright protection is not available for works of the US Government. The Bureau's citation page asks users to cite it as the source and says conclusions drawn from any analysis of the data are the sole responsibility of the performing party. FPR's use of these data is not endorsed by the Census Bureau.
acs5.access_es: Archivos de resumen públicos en www2.census.gov, sin clave. Para las ediciones de 2010 a 2020: archivos por secuencia en 5_year_seq_by_state/PuertoRico (y el ZIP de Puerto Rico de 2012 que se usa para la base 2008-2012).
